title: SSR safe-redirect accepts off-origin targets under relative-only and host allowlists
description:
Make safe-redirect classify browser network destinations before applying relative-only or host-allowlist policy. A Java URI parse with a nil host/authority is not sufficient evidence of a local destination. Two present fall-throughs let caller-untrusted locations redirect off-origin despite the caller's explicit restriction.

Remediation fence: this is the independent split of rf2-fzbj.10 Finding 1. Preserve the parent's existing hold until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj; this review authorizes filing, not implementation.

Ownership: impl_ssr; implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc:985-997,1220-1234,1275-1321. Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Concrete public reproduction in a source-loaded JVM started with -Dre-frame.debug=false:

    (rf/init! ssr/adapter)
    (rf/make-frame {:id :review/redirect :platform :server})
    (rf/reg-event :review/redirect
      (fn [_ [_ args]] {:fx [[:rf.server/safe-redirect args]]}))
    (rf/dispatch-sync
      [:review/redirect {:location "///evil.example/path" :relative-only? true}]
      {:frame :review/redirect})
    (ssr/peek-response :review/redirect)

Actual: status 302 and :redirect {:location "///evil.example/path" :status 302}. A fresh frame with :allow ["trusted.example"] also accepts that location. Java URI supplies nil scheme and authority, so relative? becomes true and the active allowlist's host guard is false. The original string, not a canonicalized local path, is stored for Location.

The installed Node WHATWG URL implementation resolves new URL("///evil.example/path", "https://trusted.example/login").href to "https://evil.example/path". The second confirmed input, "//evil_example/path", has a Java authority but no extractable host: :allow ["trusted.example"] again accepts it, and Node resolves the external host evil_example. The ordinary DNS-shaped triple-slash case alone establishes the bypass.

Controls from fresh registered-effect dispatches: /dashboard under relative-only is accepted; //evil.example/path under relative-only is rejected and leaves :redirect nil/status 200; https://trusted.example/path with that host explicitly allowed is accepted. This distinguishes the fall-through from a missing registration or wholly inactive policy. No HTTP request was sent. The neighboring Ring pipeline already emits the accepted original location; the prior rf2-c1b1 case-insensitive Location replacement repair does not classify URLs and is not the owner of this defect.

Expected: off-origin browser destinations cannot satisfy relative-only; a browser network target cannot waive an explicit host allowlist just because Java cannot expose its host. Spec 011's HTTP response contract deliberately provides this effect for caller-untrusted ?next= style locations. Application impact is an open redirect despite the declared restriction; authentication/token leakage is not asserted.

Suggested repair: conservatively reject ambiguous network-reference forms or normalize/classify them with semantics consistent with the destination the browser uses. At minimum, raw // prefixes must not turn relative through extra slashes, and an authority-bearing reference with no extractable host must not skip an active allowlist. Keep caller-trusted redirect, ordinary local references, and explicit allowed HTTP(S) destinations unchanged. A new URL abstraction or extra policy knobs are unnecessary.

Acceptance criteria:
- Public registered-event -> safe-redirect tests reject ///evil.example/path and repeated-slash variants under relative-only and an unrelated allowlist, preserving the previous accumulator and emitting the existing appropriate rejection.
- An authority-bearing hostless Java parse, including //evil_example/path, either fails closed or checks the actual destination host; it cannot silently bypass the allowlist.
- Keep local/explicitly allowed controls and existing protocol-relative, opaque-scheme, injection, and production rejection semantics.
- Run focused SSR tests through the real production JVM lane; compare the URL corpus with Node/browser destination parsing. Add a Ring Location assertion so the rejected input cannot reach the wire.

Validation performed: fresh Java 21/Clojure 1.12.4 production-mode public effect probe, ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_ssr/probe-impl-ssr-2.log and .exit, exit 0. Source resource URL prints this checkout. Node URL evidence probe-url-impl-ssr-1.log and .exit, exit 0. Attempt 1 independently reached the same redirect cases but exited 1 on a probe-only unavailable helper before the later hydration block; it is not counted as a passing run. No CLJS compilation/browser navigation or broad suite ran; source is unchanged.

Deduplication: current all-status safe-redirect search and all-status description search for ///evil return only rf2-fzbj.10, the two-finding aggregate. Read its newest three history entries: still open, no corrective notes. The aggregate does not substitute for this independent fix bead. No identical dedicated open issue found.
notes:
VERDICT (ssr-a worker, 2026-09-13): FIXED in PR #9747.

Re-verified at tip 601dee93cb before fixing: `///evil.example/path` under `:relative-only? true` and under `:allow ["trusted.example"]`, `////evil.example/path` under both, and `//evil_example/path` under `:allow` were all ACCEPTED. The new test was red on 5 of its 6 policy-by-location cases; `//evil_example/path` under relative-only was already refused.

Fix, in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc` `safe-redirect-fx`:
- A raw `//` prefix makes a target non-relative, whatever java.net.URI reports.
- Under `:allow`, every non-relative target must name an allowlisted host. A host URI cannot extract names none.
- The existing categories and reasons are reused (`:relative-only-violation`, `:not-in-allowlist`), so the always-on record vocabulary is unchanged.

Regression tests live in `re-frame.ssr-safe-redirect-production-test`. It runs in `jvm-ssr` and in `jvm-ssr-prod-gate` under `-Dre-frame.debug=false`.
- `a-network-path-reference-cannot-satisfy-either-policy`: `///`, `////` and `//evil_example` under both modes. Each asserts `:redirect` nil, `:status` 200, and exactly one `:rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed` record carrying the arm's reason.
- The control `each-policy-still-passes-its-legitimate-targets`: `/dashboard` and a relative path under relative-only; `/dashboard`, `https://trusted.example/path` and an upper-cased host under `:allow`.

Node 24's WHATWG URL, resolved against `https://trusted.example/login`, sends every refused location off-origin and keeps every passing control same-origin.

SKIPPED, with reason:
- The end-to-end Ring `Location` assertion. A refusal leaves `:redirect` nil on the accumulator (asserted), and ssr-ring `pipeline.clj` writes `Location` only from `:redirect`, so the accumulator assertion already covers the wire.
- Hostless network paths with NO policy supplied still pass. An unrestricted safe-redirect already accepts any http(s) or protocol-relative target, and the finding concerns the two restricting policies.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9747. safe-redirect-fx now treats a raw // prefix as non-relative, and under :allow it refuses any non-relative target without an allowlisted host, hostless java.net.URI parses included. The rejections reuse the existing categories and reasons. Regression and control tests are in re-frame.ssr-safe-redirect-production-test (jvm-ssr and jvm-ssr-prod-gate), shown red before the fix, and the Node WHATWG destinations agree. Skipped, with reasons: the Ring Location end-to-end test (the accumulator assertion covers the wire, since pipeline.clj writes Location only from :redirect), and hostless paths when no policy is supplied (unrestricted by design). The full verdict is in the notes.

title: [RED ON MAIN] spec/api-manifest.edn declares 496 vars but carries 495 rows; gen --check exits 1 on trunk (silent identical-edit merge via #9459's rebase-merge)
description:
RED ON MAIN, found by the mayor 2026-09-08 at trunk 27472063a1 while verifying a worker's rebase report. Trunk fails a required gate.

MEASURED, in the mayor checkout, exit code read off the runner's own command line:
  cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check
  -> exit 1
  -> "DRIFT: generated manifest differs from spec/api-manifest.edn."
  -> "(var set identical; :meta or formatting differs - regenerate)"

THE ARITHMETIC, three independent instruments agreeing against the declared field:
  declared        :var-count 496
  {:namespace     495
  , :tier         495
  :runtime-verified?  495
So the file claims one more public var than it carries. The var SET is correct; the count and formatting are not.

PROVENANCE: git log -1 -- spec/api-manifest.edn names c8fae0e8a8 "docs(hicasso): teach the client-root grammar; witness it; re-point spec + manifest", which is PR #9459 (rf2-kuky.59), merged by the mayor at 2026-09-08 ~12:05.

HOW IT GOT PAST CI, and this is the part worth keeping. It is the silent-identical-edit hazard on a GENERATED file, reached through a door nobody had covered: the MERGE ITSELF. Two changes each edited the same :var-count line to the same new value for DIFFERENT removals; git merges two identical edits without a conflict; the row deletions sat far apart so nothing forced them into contact. #9459's own CI graded ITS head, which was self-consistent. The rebase-merge then REPLAYED it onto a moved main and produced a tree that NO CI RUN EVER GRADED. Clause 5 of the merge criterion asks whether the check set was computed against the current matrix; it does not ask whether the MERGE PRODUCT was graded at all. That is a real gap, and it is why this reached trunk rather than a PR.

FIX: regenerate and commit, nothing more. The var set is already right.
  cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest
  clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen
  clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check   # must exit 0
Expect the declared count to land at 495 and the diff to be the count line plus formatting/:meta only. If the diff removes or adds a ROW, stop and report - that would mean the var set is not in fact identical and the diagnosis is wrong.

DO NOT hand-edit spec/api-manifest.edn; it carries the "GENERATED ... do NOT hand-edit" header. Regenerate.

WHY THIS GETS ITS OWN PR RATHER THAN RIDING A SIBLING: several in-flight PRs regenerate the manifest during their own rebases and would therefore CORRECT trunk as a side effect - one worker measured exactly that and flagged it rather than absorbing it. A trunk defect fixed invisibly inside an unrelated change is untraceable and teaches nobody. It gets its own commit with this bead's id in the message.

ACCEPTANCE: gen --check exits 0 on main; declared :var-count equals the independently counted rows; the diff touches spec/api-manifest.edn only; no row added or removed.
notes:
MAYOR 2026-09-08 12:20 AUSEST — INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, and one refinement to the account above.

A second worker (rebasing PR #9457, no knowledge of this bead) hit the same defect from the other end and BISECTED it. Its arithmetic did not balance — it expected 494 and got 493 — and rather than papering over that it chased the discrepancy to trunk. Its finding:

  c8fae0e8a8 (PR #9459) removed hydrate! and mount!, added client-root, and re-owned render! / unmount! — NET MINUS ONE ROW — without the :var-count header following.
  Every EARLIER revision is internally consistent: 498/498, 497/497, 496/496.

That last clause is what makes the diagnosis firm rather than plausible. The file was self-consistent at every revision up to and including the one before c8fae0e8a8, so the header/row divergence entered exactly there and nowhere else.

REFINEMENT: 'without the header following' describes the SYMPTOM; the mechanism is the one recorded above. #9459 was green on gen --check at its own head — that gate is required and it passed — so the tree its CI graded was self-consistent. The rebase-merge then replayed those commits onto a main that had moved, and the product is what carries 495 rows under a 496 header. The defect therefore lives in a tree NO CI RUN EVER GRADED, which is why a required, non-flaky gate did not stop it.

SECOND CORROBORATION OF THE PRACTICAL GUARD: that worker derived its expected count from main's ROW COUNT rather than main's declared header, and says outright that taking the header would have made it wrong by one. A third worker on PR #9455 reported the identical thing independently. Two workers arriving at the same guard from different branches is the strongest evidence available that 'count the rows, never trust the declared field' belongs in the standing method rather than in one brief.

RACE NOTE: at least two in-flight PRs (#9455, #9457) regenerate the manifest as part of their own rebases and therefore REPAIR trunk as a side effect. Both flagged it rather than absorbing it silently, which is the behaviour I want. If one of them lands before this bead's dedicated PR, that is acceptable — this bead then closes on the evidence rather than on its own diff, and the account above is the record. What is NOT acceptable is the repair going unremarked, which is the outcome the dedicated PR exists to prevent.
MAYOR 2026-09-08 — CORRECTION TO MY OWN CLOSE REASON ABOVE, raised by the worker on PR #9458 against a claim I made to it about its own work.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: my account says several workers "flagged rather than absorbed" the drift, and I told PR #9458's worker directly that it had "correctly declined to carry the repair". IT DID NOT DECLINE. It INCLUDED the regeneration, as commit c9904f981e, and said so in its report at the time. I conflated it with PR #9460's worker, which is the one that genuinely declined and gave the sequenced-hot-zone-holding reasoning. Two different workers, and I attributed one's judgement to the other while telling that other it had done something it had not.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE, checked rather than assumed: TRUNK's instance 1 was repaired by PR #9455, not by #9458. I measured the fast-forwarded trunk immediately after merging #9455 and read declared == counted == 493 with gen --check exit 0, and #9458 was — and still is — unmerged at that point. So the close reason's attribution for the TRUNK repair stands; what was wrong is the characterisation of #9458's worker's conduct.

WHY THIS IS WORTH THE CORRECTION rather than a shrug: the worker had to spend part of its context disputing a false statement about its own branch before it could get on with the rebase, and it was right to. A brief that misdescribes what a worker previously did is the same class of error as a brief that misdescribes the tree — and this session's whole finding is that briefs are where the errors are.
close_reason:
RESOLVED, and the fix came from a DIFFERENT PR than the one I dispatched for it — recorded that way deliberately rather than quietly attributed.

FIXED BY PR #9455 (rf2-kuky.13 item C + rf2-5op3), merged 2026-09-08. That PR's rebase regenerated spec/api-manifest.edn, and because its worker derived the expected count from main's TRUE ROW COUNT (495) rather than main's declared field (496), the regeneration corrected the drift as it went: 495 - 2 removals = 493, and the file now declares 493 against 493 counted rows.

VERIFIED BY ME ON THE FAST-FORWARDED TRUNK at 2fafa0a7a9, not inferred from the PR:
  declared :var-count 493 ; {:namespace rows 493   (equal)
  cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check
  -> exit 0, "OK: spec/api-manifest.edn in sync (493 public vars)"
The gate that was exit 1 on this bead's filing is exit 0 now.

THE DEDICATED FIX, PR #9464 (branch worker/manifix-a), IS THEREFORE A NO-OP and should be closed unmerged. It did its job correctly — it reproduced the defect independently, regenerated only, and confirmed the STOP condition did not fire (no row added or removed, the entire diff being the :var-count scalar 496 -> 495). It simply lost a race it could not see. Its evidence stands as the second independent confirmation.

WHY I DISPATCHED A DEDICATED PR ANYWAY, AND WHY THAT WAS STILL RIGHT: at least four in-flight PRs regenerate the manifest during their own rebases and would each have corrected trunk as a side effect. THREE of their workers (#9455, #9457, #9458) reported the drift explicitly rather than absorbing it, and #9460's worker declined to carry the fix at all on the grounds that the manifest trio is a sequenced hot-zone holding whose established repair is a dedicated regeneration chore. That is four independent workers refusing to let a trunk defect disappear into an unrelated diff. The dedicated PR existed to guarantee that outcome; the workers delivered it without needing the guarantee.

WHAT STAYS TRUE AND IS THE REASON THIS BEAD MATTERED: the causal account above is unchanged. A required, non-flaky gate did not stop a broken tree reaching trunk, because GitHub's rebase-merge produced a MERGE PRODUCT that no CI run ever graded, and clause 5 of the merge criterion asks whether the check set matched the current matrix but never whether the merge product itself was graded. The guard I have adopted, and now run: after merging anything that touches a generated file, check that file's own self-consistency on the fast-forwarded trunk before moving on. That is how this bead was found, and it is how the repair was confirmed.

title: bug(skill-reagent-migration): MIG-04/05 silently turn queued Reagent dispatches into synchronous Hicasso intents
description:
## Scope

Correct the scheduling contract taught by skills/reagent-migration/** for Reagent handler rewrites into Hicasso intents. Keep Hicasso's synchronous runtime semantics and data-first event API unchanged. The target is truthful, low-friction migration guidance: ordinary intents remain the default, while the rare ordering-sensitive handler gets one explicit preservation route.

## Correctness finding

The skill classifies its full M-tier, including MIG-04, MIG-05, MIG-06 and MIG-33 handler lifts, as unambiguous and observably identical. Its canonical rewrite turns a Reagent closure that calls rf/dispatch into a Hicasso intent vector.

Those two forms do not have the same scheduling contract. re-frame2 rf/dispatch appends to the router queue and returns immediately before the handler runs. A Hicasso intent closes over the frame API's dispatch-sync operation, drains the event and its synchronous cascade inside the browser callback's turn, and notifies the store before that turn ends. This is intentional Hicasso behavior, especially for controlled-input convergence, but it is a behavior change in an arbitrary migrated handler and the skill never names it.

## Exact evidence

- skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:107 calls the M-tier rewrites, expressly including dispatch lifting and keystroke maps, unambiguous and observably identical.
- skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:64-84 makes #(dispatch [:go 1]) -> [:go 1] a direct MIG-04 rewrite and performs the same lift for value/checked handlers in MIG-05. The MIG-33 rule at lines 397 onward likewise replaces conditional queued dispatch calls with a key map.
- skills/reagent-migration/evals/evals.json:38 and :51 grade the direct event-vector result. No expectation asks the agent to disclose or preserve queue ordering.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1167-1171 defines rf/dispatch as enqueue-and-return before the handler runs. Lines 1200-1207 distinguish dispatch-sync as an end-to-end fixed-point drain for tests, REPL and bootstrap.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs:85-96 mints Hicasso's frame dispatch from the captured :dispatch-sync operation. Lines 513-522 state that the event drains synchronously inside the caller's turn and store notification occurs before the turn ends.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:497-524 routes ordinary intent vectors through that captured dispatch.
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/callback_form_dom_cljs_test.cljs:8-17 and :101-108 are an existing real-browser witness: a returned intent reaches the synchronous door and produces its echo in the same turn.

## Concrete impact

A Reagent click handler that only enqueues an event returns before application handlers and effects run. After the prescribed migration, those handlers and their synchronous cascade finish before the Hicasso callback returns. Ordering can therefore reverse relative to later propagation listeners, browser default actions, imperative code outside the component, and observations made immediately after the callback. A coeffect or structural failure that used to occur during the queued drain can also surface on a different stack.

Most application events should still use the concise intent vector. The defect is not that Hicasso is synchronous; it is that the migration promises observational identity and gives an ordering-sensitive application no signal that it crossed this semantic boundary. Shadow comparisons that inspect settled DOM and intent streams can remain green while missing callback-turn ordering.

## Recommended bounded fix

1. State once in the mental model/procedure that Hicasso event intents dispatch synchronously, unlike rf/dispatch, and explain why controlled writes require same-turn convergence.
2. Remove the blanket observably-identical claim for handler-lifting rules. Keep ordinary dispatch-only closures as the idiomatic default rather than turning every handler into a decision ceremony.
3. Add one narrow detection/question for an explicitly ordering-sensitive site: code, tests or comments that require the event to remain queued until after the callback/propagation/default-action phase.
4. For that exceptional site, teach the existing preservation route: call rf/capture-frame during render, close a plain callback over the captured frame API's queued :dispatch function, and return nil. Do not call ambient rf/dispatch after the render extent; that is the separate no-frame-context failure already taught by MIG-26.
5. Add one behavioral eval that distinguishes queued-after-callback semantics from Hicasso's same-turn intent semantics and rejects an answer that calls the two observationally identical.

## Non-goals

- No Hicasso runtime change, async-intent variant, scheduler abstraction or new public API.
- No per-handler prompt, blanket refusal to use data intents, or compatibility mode.
- No weakening of synchronous controlled-input convergence.
- No redesign of event vectors, key maps, h/event, the reporter or the view migration tiers beyond the scheduling distinction.
- No attempt to enumerate every browser ordering edge; one clear invariant and one existing escape are enough.

## Duplicate and history research

Targeted all-status searches over .beads/issues.jsonl for reagent-migration, MIG-04, dispatch-lifting, Hicasso intent and dispatch-sync found no bead owning this async-to-sync migration seam. Closed rf2-90k4a covers three frame-context/refusal diagnostics, rf2-vpdrf covers SSR adapter boot, and rf2-qxca8 covers retired Hicasso read/navigation doors; none addresses event scheduling.

Git history strengthens the mismatch: the exact MIG-04 example originated in 819a2f68a7 for an earlier destination and survived the Hicasso retarget in 6cdc1979da unchanged. Hicasso's captured synchronous dispatch was established separately in 69e160e1d1. No later skill commit reconciled those two contracts.

## Uncertainty

No new runtime was launched in this review-only worker. The semantic mismatch is directly established by current public core docs, current implementation, and an existing real-browser Hicasso witness. What remains unknown is how many consumer handlers rely on callback-turn ordering; that uncertainty is why the repair should preserve the vector as the default and add one bounded exception rather than impose ceremony on every event.
acceptance_criteria:
- SKILL.md and the routed migration references no longer describe rf/dispatch-to-intent handler lifts as observationally identical without qualification.
- The skill states the exact scheduling boundary once: rf/dispatch queues and returns before the handler runs; a Hicasso vector, key-map branch, or vector returned from h/event drains synchronously inside the callback turn.
- MIG-04/05/06/33 remain concise defaults for ordinary application handlers. The guidance does not ask about every handler or introduce a new runtime form.
- The skill identifies only explicit queue-order dependencies as judgment work and gives a valid preservation spelling using a render-time rf/capture-frame and its captured queued :dispatch operation in a plain callback. It clearly distinguishes that captured operation from an ambient rf/dispatch invoked after render.
- Controlled input guidance continues to require same-turn synchronous writes and explains that this is intentional rather than accidental equivalence.
- A focused behavioral eval presents or states an ordering-sensitive Reagent handler and fails an answer that silently emits an intent while claiming equivalent timing; it passes either an informed semantic change accepted by the author or the captured queued-dispatch escape.
- Existing handler-lifting, no-frame-context, key-map and controlled-input eval expectations remain coherent; eval JSON and skill/package structural checks pass.
- No Hicasso/core runtime API or behavior changes.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9227 (worker/skmig-a). Premise VERIFIED at source, not taken from the brief: core.cljc's dispatch docstring reads 'Enqueue event-vec on the target frame's router; returns nil immediately, BEFORE the handler runs', while hicasso impl/collector.cljs mint-frame-dispatch closes over (:dispatch-sync ops) and its dispatch! docstring reads 'The event drains synchronously inside the caller's turn and the store notification runs before the turn ends'; impl/intent.cljs intent-handler routes ordinary intent vectors through that captured dispatch. So MIG-04/05 and MIG-33 did move every migrated handler from queued to same-turn with nothing said. Confirmed the fix did not already exist at tip: the only dispatch-sync mentions in the skill were boot-seeding (MIG-15/23), never handler scheduling. Delivered per the recommended bounded fix: (1) mental-model.md section 3 states the boundary once in both directions and explains controlled-input same-turn convergence as designed rather than accidental; (2) the blanket observably-identical claim removed from both assertion sites, SKILL.md line 107 and catalog-mechanical.md line 3, with 'mechanical' redefined as 'the destination shape is not a judgment call, not that timing is identical'; (3) one narrow check per converted VIEW (not per handler, no ceremony) keyed to a site that STATES a queue dependency; (4) the preservation route taught as render-time rf/capture-frame plus its queued :dispatch op in a plain callback, explicitly distinguished from the ambient rf/dispatch MIG-26 fails at click time with :rf.error/no-frame-context; (5) new behavioural eval 32 fails an answer claiming equivalent timing on an explicitly ordering-sensitive handler. MIG-33 got one sentence; intent vector remains the concise default; no runtime/API change. NOT a duplicate of PR #9209 (commit 51d6b7bdef): that fixed the reagent-slim ADAPTER's after-render firing before the React commit, a different subsystem and mechanism from the Hicasso intent lowering's dispatch scheduling. Gates green with exit codes captured from the runner: check_doc_slugs.py 0 and PROVEN LIVE by a planted broken anchor (exit 1 naming catalog-mechanical.md:104, restored byte-identical per cmp), check_skill_eval_docs.py 0 ([reagent-migration] eval identity unique), check_skill_description_budget.py 0 (1011/1032, no front-matter touched), check_skill_eval_packaging.py 0, api-manifest skills-check 0 (574 public-var references, validating the new rf/capture-frame reference). All re-run green post-rebase. HONEST LIMIT: the change is prose and no gate inspects prose content; neither link gate reads inside fences, so the Clojure examples were hand-checked against the shipped capture-frame docstring, and no eval RUNNER exists in CI so eval 32 is gated structurally rather than executed.

title: realworld-resources: the example's app-db never seeds in a development build (same boot-window defect as rf2-2xzc)
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 on worker/dispatchlater-a, not inferred. A dev build of
`:examples/realworld-resources` (shadow-cljs compile, served over HTTP, headless Chrome):
app-db is `{}`, zero article cards, `#app` is a 1698-character shell. Zero page errors.

SAME MECHANISM AS rf2-2xzc, whose full write-up is on that bead. examples/real-apps/
realworld_resources/schema.cljs registers four NON-NILABLE app-db path schemas against
:rf/default at ns-load:

    [:auth]                AuthSlice
    [:auth :login-form]    FormSlice
    [:auth :register-form] FormSlice
    [:settings-form]       FormSlice

app-db starts {} and the candidate validator walks EVERY registered path over the WHOLE
candidate app-db at EVERY :db commit (spec/010 §Per-step recovery row 4) with no exemption
for a path nothing has written yet. `:app/initialise` (core.cljs) fans out to
[:auth.login-form/initialise] and [:auth.register-form/initialise] as separate dispatches,
and `:auth/initialise` is its own :initial-events step - so each seed is its own commit and
each is rejected by the siblings still absent.

WORSE THAN THE SIBLING IN ONE RESPECT: [:settings-form] is never seeded at boot at all, so
that path reads nil forever. Every :db commit in that application is rejected permanently,
not only during the boot window. And because a rejected candidate does not walk :fx either,
nothing downstream of a :db-bearing handler fires.

DEV ONLY, for the same reason: validate-app-schema!'s whole body is inside
(if interop/debug-enabled? ... true), so a release build installs every candidate.

WHY NO TEST SEES IT: reg-app-schemas is frame-local to :rf/default and
realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs drives anonymous frames (it re-registers [:auth] against
its own frame by hand at line 550, which is the tell).

THE FIX is the one PR #9134 applied to the managed-HTTP sibling: wrap each registration in
:maybe for the boot window with the rationale written out (the idiom
examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs already documents), and name the registry as a value so a
harness can install it on its own frame. Then add the matching contract test in the framework
tree - examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm) - mirroring
implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs. Note that ns
cannot co-load both apps' auth/settings nses (duplicate ids under the image-assembly guard),
so the resources coverage needs its own ns.

P1 because it is the same class of failure as rf2-2xzc: total, silent, application-wide, and
only in the build every consumer develops against.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9143 (branch worker/resboot-a), open against main. examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/schema.cljs now wraps all four app-db path registrations in :maybe and names the registry as the value app-db-schemas so a harness can install it on its own frame. title: migration: path lowering misclassifies custom */path interceptors
description:
## Scope

Repair the v1-to-v2 event-registration migration path where the shipped M-73 scanner/codemod encounters interceptor-bearing reg-event-db or reg-event-fx calls. Scope includes migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod, its focused tests/README, the directly coupled re-frame-migration reference/eval, and one focused integration proof against the actual v2 reg-event contract.

## Correctness finding

The guide promises that M-73 composes with M-70, but the implementation performs a head/handler-only rewrite and deliberately preserves every middle slot. For the canonical path-interceptor example it emits an rf/reg-event whose metadata still contains the removed inline (rf/path ...) call; for historical positional chains it emits a reg-event with the retired vector middle slot. Both outputs are invalid v2 and hard-fail while the namespace loads. The codemod then reports the site as :rewrite/:rename rather than an unresolved M-70 finding, so its green unit suite certifies a broken migration.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md:482-505 tells users to prefer the shipped codemod and specifies the mechanical conversion from {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]} to {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]]]}.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:883-903 calls the codemod first-class/tested and gives the same positional [(rf/path :counter)] to metadata-ref conversion.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod.clj:31-33 instead states that path-interceptor metadata is preserved untouched. analyse-call at 301-342 classifies every reg-event-fx as a pure rename and simple reg-event-db solely by its last handler; it never analyses middle-slot shape or entries. apply-rewrite-at at 665-688 replaces only the registrar head and db handler.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/test/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod_test.clj:102-114 and 125-134 explicitly assert that {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]} survives while the call is renamed to reg-event, pinning the invalid output.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1962-1983 makes rf/path a throwing removal stub (:rf.error/path-removed). implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:71-82 and 126-165 require interceptor refs and reject inline values with :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed; 803-837 rejects a positional vector middle slot with :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the shipped codemod rewrite over this v1 source:

       (rf/reg-event-db :counter/inc
         {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}
         (fn [db _] (update db :value inc)))

2. Observe that it reports :action :rewrite and emits reg-event while preserving {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}.
3. Load/evaluate the emitted registration with the actual v2 re-frame.core namespace.
4. Observe the namespace-load hard failure :rf.error/path-removed before the handler registers. The positional-vector variant is also retained and is rejected as :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot; a custom inline value retained in metadata is rejected as :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The current successful rewrite is:

    (rf/reg-event :counter/inc
      {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}
      (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (update db :value inc)}))

Loading it against v2 calls the removed rf/path stub before the handler can register. A positional v1 chain is likewise left as the now-illegal vector middle slot, and a custom inline value carried into metadata is rejected by reg-event.

Invariant: every site the codemod reports as mechanically rewritten must be a valid v2 registration shape, or it must remain an explicit unresolved M-70 finding. A source transform is not successful merely because it parses and no retired registrar name remains.

## Recommended minimal fix

Teach the codemod one small middle-slot normalization that composes M-70 with M-73:

1. Recognize the standard path constructor in bare, positional-vector, metadata-interceptors, and metadata-plus-vector source shapes; lower each (rf/path p...) to [:rf.interceptor/path [p...]], create or merge the metadata map, and preserve chain order/comments.
2. Preserve entries that are already v2 refs.
3. For any other inline/bare interceptor whose stable registered id cannot be derived without author intent, emit an explicit M-70 Type-B finding and do not claim the event migration complete. Do not leave an invalid inline value hidden behind a successful M-73 result.
4. Scan both retired reg-event-* forms and already rewritten reg-event forms for these invalid middle-slot/inline survivors so a rerun can recover a partially migrated tree.
5. Replace the string-only preservation assertions with exact normalization tests plus a focused registration integration test using the actual v2 core.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A codemod test rewrites the canonical metadata source above to a reg-event containing exactly [:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]], with no executable rf/path call, and preserves the db-handler transformation.
- A codemod test rewrites a historical positional path vector and a metadata-plus-vector path chain into the one metadata-map :interceptors ref shape; multiple entries preserve declaration order.
- An executable integration test evaluates/registers the canonical transformed result against the actual v2 core and completes without :rf.error/path-removed, :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot, :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed, or :rf.error/unregistered-interceptor.
- Negative control: feeding the current preserved-inline output to that same integration harness deterministically throws :rf.error/path-removed (or the inline-value equivalent throws :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed), proving the test observes registration rather than only parsing/substring shape. Restoring the old preserve-middle behavior makes the positive test red.
- A custom inline interceptor with no stable id is surfaced as an unresolved M-70 Type-B finding and is not reported as a completed :rename/:rewrite; a rerun over an already-renamed invalid reg-event finds it.
- Non-vacuity controls show interceptor-free reg-event-fx still pure-renames, interceptor-free simple reg-event-db still performs its existing db wrap, already-canonical ref chains remain valid, and running the codemod twice is stable.
- Add a focused re-frame-migration eval fixture whose v1 event contains a path interceptor; its expected result uses the standard ref and the eval fails if the removed inline call or positional vector survives.
- The codemod unit suite and the focused runtime integration test pass.

## Non-goals

- No general Clojure analyser or arbitrary macro evaluation.
- No auto-naming or semantic re-authoring of custom interceptors; those remain M-70 Type B.
- No compatibility alias restoring rf/path, inline interceptor values, or positional reg-event chains in v2.
- No unrelated migration-rule rewrite, formatting cleanup, or broad runtime hardening.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title and description searches were run for: M-73 codemod, reg-event codemod, path interceptor codemod, inline interceptor migration, rf.interceptor/path, middle slot codemod, preserved metadata interceptor, M-70, M-73, reg-event-db, and codemod. A full all-status issue export was also scanned across title/description/notes for the same vocabulary. No existing open, in-progress, blocked, deferred, or closed bead owns this codemod-output/runtime-registration mismatch. rf2-0qzh covered CI discovery/classification for the codemod, not transform correctness; reagent/hicasso codemod beads are different tools and surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Canonical metadata, positional-vector, and metadata-plus-vector path-interceptor inputs lower to metadata :interceptors entries of [:rf.interceptor/path <path-vector>] while preserving handler semantics and chain order.
2. The canonical transformed output is executed against actual v2 reg-event and registers successfully.
3. A negative-control fixture containing the old preserved inline rf/path output throws the expected hard error in that same harness; reverting the normalization makes the positive test fail.
4. Custom inline interceptors without a stable id become explicit unresolved M-70 Type-B findings rather than successful M-73 rewrites, including when found in an already-renamed reg-event.
5. Interceptor-free fx/db rewrites, already-canonical ref chains, and a second codemod run remain successful and stable.
6. A focused migration-skill eval rejects any answer/output that leaves rf/path executable or a positional interceptor vector in reg-event.
7. Focused codemod and runtime integration suites pass.

AUDIT PR #8828 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness: path-call-info identifies the standard re-frame constructor only by (= "path" (name hv)). It therefore treats every qualified custom function named path as rf/path. A deterministic probe on merged main with (app.interceptors/path :tenant) inside a real rf/reg-event-db returned :action :rewrite and emitted [:rf.interceptor/path [:tenant]], silently replacing the custom interceptor's semantics instead of producing the promised unresolved M-70 :flag :interceptors. This contradicts the PR's central boundary that only the standard constructor is mechanical and every other custom inline call stays unchanged for author intent. Existing tests cover a custom var, rf/debug, and a dynamic rf/path arg, but not a custom qualified function sharing the simple name. Minimal repair: resolve the call head to re-frame.core/path from the namespace's require/refer aliases, or conservatively flag ambiguous qualified path symbols; add a custom/path negative test while retaining the standard qualified/alias/bare fixtures and idempotence.

Implementation-quality/completeness: the new :integration alias is not invoked by .github/workflows/test.yml or scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh. PR checks ran only clojure -M:test, so the real-v2 registration proof and all four negative controls are currently manual/orphaned. Add clojure -M:integration to the existing changed-surface codemod CI job (keeping it separate from the self-contained :test classpath).

Duplicate search across all statuses for custom path interceptor, symbol named path, path alias codemod, and M-70 custom call found no separate owner. Both residues are exact acceptance/quality gaps in rf2-8odvg.
AUDIT PR #8846 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness/completeness: the new namespace resolver still treats namespace-level availability as call-site resolution. In a file that refers re-frame.core/path, a lexically shadowing `let` binding named `path` is therefore silently lowered as the framework constructor. Deterministic probe on merge b38d2e0: `(ns app.events (:require [re-frame.core :refer [reg-event-db path]])) (let [path app.interceptors/path] (reg-event-db ... {:interceptors [(path :tenant)]} ...))` returned `[:rewrite nil true]` — a successful rewrite containing `:rf.interceptor/path` — even though the call denotes the custom binding. This contradicts the implementation comment at lines 344-350 and the README guarantee that a local/custom path function flags rather than changes semantics.

Minimal repair: for bare `path`, account for lexical bindings at the interceptor call site, or conservatively refuse lowering when an enclosing scope binds `path`; add one deterministic local-shadow negative fixture plus idempotence. This does not require a general analyser. The separate orphaned integration-CI residue remains owned by rf2-36u96 and is not duplicated here.
REPAIRED 2026-09-01 12:14:32 AUSEST (worker, PR #8857, commit ae9a7d7e59). The reopen's probe was reproduced verbatim at branch base 4e27fbbe49 BEFORE any edit and returned [:rewrite nil true] — premise confirmed at source, not assumed. Root cause exactly as the note stated: path-head resolution was a per-SOURCE fact derived from the ns form (path-head-context), with no call-site half, so ns-level AVAILABILITY stood in for what a bare head DENOTES.

FIX: reused the in-file machinery rather than adding a second mechanism. The free-occurrence analysis already carried a binding-form vocabulary (binding-vector-forms, seq-binding-forms, collect-binding-names); that vocabulary is hoisted into one shared section above both consumers, and a new enclosing-scope-binds? walks OUT from the registrar call over the same table. The two analyses now ask opposite questions in opposite directions over one vocabulary. Added the defn family (defn/defn-/defmacro), whose params scope over a registration in the body and which the downward walk had no reason to know. standard-path-head? consults the new :shadowed-bare-path? for BARE heads only — a namespace-qualified symbol names a var and cannot be shadowed by a local.

Conservative refusal, as the note permitted: an enclosing binder routes the site to the existing :flag :interceptors (unresolved M-70 Type B) and leaves the source byte-for-byte unchanged. Position-insensitive inside a binding vector, and an unreadable binding vector counts as binding the name — both errors can only produce a flag where a lowering was possible, never a silent semantic swap.

EVIDENCE (exits captured in the same shell as each run): probe [:rewrite nil true] -> [:flag :interceptors false] with the source byte-identical. clojure -M:test exit 0, 72/245 -> exit 0, 77/276. clojure -M:integration exit 0, 6/10 both sides. NON-VACUITY: one-line revert ((not shadowed-bare-path?) -> true) gives captured exit 1 with 25 failures falling in exactly the three new shadow deftests, at unchanged 77/276 totals so nothing was skipped; the two non-over-reach controls (qualified head inside a shadowing let still lowers; a sibling-form path binding does not suppress the site) stayed green. Restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff.

Tests added: shadowed-bare-path-flagged-not-lowered (the audit probe), shadowed-bare-path-flagged-across-binding-forms (let / if-let / fn / defn / letfn / doseq), shadowing-does-not-suppress-a-qualified-head, shadowing-elsewhere-does-not-suppress-a-referred-bare-path, shadowed-bare-path-idempotent. README's path-resolution guarantee updated to state the call-site half; its gate is check_doc_slugs.py, NOT check_readme_links.py (migration/ is in the latter's DOCS_GATE_ROOTS exclusion and in the former's DEFAULT_ROOTS) — established by planting a broken link: docs gate exit 1 naming file and line, readme gate exit 0.

The orphaned-integration-CI residue is rf2-36u96's, landed as the second commit of the same PR.
AUDIT PR #8857 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness: the lexical-shadow repair recognizes only unqualified binding-form heads. A valid qualified macro such as `clojure.core/let` is absent from `binding-vector-forms`, so `enclosing-scope-binds?` misses its local `path`. Deterministic probe at merge db8949e406: `(clojure.core/let [path app.interceptors/path] (reg-event-db ... {:interceptors [(path :tenant)]} ...))` returned `[:rewrite nil]` and emitted `[:rf.interceptor/path [:tenant]]`, silently replacing the custom interceptor. The same checkout evaluates `(clojure.core/let [path (fn [x] [:custom x])] (path :tenant))` as `[:custom :tenant]`, proving the source form is valid rather than synthetic.

Minimal repair: normalize recognized binding heads by simple name only when they resolve to clojure.core, or explicitly include their qualified clojure.core spellings; retain conservative refusal for ambiguous/custom macros. Add a qualified-let negative fixture plus the existing bare and sibling controls. All-status searches for `clojure.core/let`, qualified/namespaced binding forms, qualified binders, and `enclosing-scope-binds?` found no separate owner; this is the exact unresolved lexical-shadow acceptance boundary of rf2-8odvg.
REPAIRED 2026-09-01 (worker, PR #8896, commit b57bbac2f2). Scope: the AUDIT PR #8857 reopen only — the newest text-bearing mutation on this bead, established by walking bd history newest-first to the bead beginning (394 entries, 5 text-bearing changes, oldest entry notes-length 0 so the walk reached creation). The DESCRIPTION is historical: its central premise (head/handler-only rewrite, every middle slot preserved) was discharged by the three merged PRs #8828 / #8846 / #8857, and the two sibling acceptance items were confirmed present at tip — the migration-skill eval fixture in skills/re-frame-migration/evals/evals.json, and clojure -M:integration wired into .github/workflows/test.yml.

PREMISE CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED. The audit probe was reproduced verbatim at branch base a272031831 BEFORE any edit: the clojure.core/let form returned [:rewrite nil] and emitted the framework ref, while the bare-let control on the same run returned [:flag :interceptors] — isolating qualification, not shadowing, as the cause. The validity control evaluated the probe form to [:custom :tenant] in the same JVM, so it is real Clojure.

ROOT CAUSE: form-binds? asked the binding vocabulary whether it held a head VERBATIM. The vocabulary is keyed by unqualified symbols, so a qualified spelling of a binder was not a binder, and an unrecognised head bound nothing at all.

FIX — A RULE, NOT A ROSTER. Enumerating binder spellings one at a time is what reopened this bead three times, each on the next spelling of one hole, so the roster lookup is replaced by two rules that both fail CLOSED, towards the flag: (1) a recognised binder is matched by its SIMPLE name (binding-head), so clojure.core/let, cljs.core/let and an aliased c/let all count — the namespace is DISCARDED rather than resolved, deliberately, because resolving it is the fail-open choice that would leave an unrecognised my.macros/let binding nothing; (2) a head outside the vocabulary falls to unrecognised-form-binds?, where a vector child that binds the name — read as either a binding vector or a params vector — makes the form a binder, covering defmethod, when-first, dotimes, deftype methods and project macros without a general analyser (excluded by the non-goals). The catch-all is narrow: it fires only when a form enclosing the registration has a vector child that literally binds the name, and can only ever add a flag.

DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: the free-occurrence walk (free-in-form?) shares this vocabulary but consults it in the opposite direction, and a miss there fails SAFE — an unrecognised head falls through to free-in-children?, whose bare LHS occurrence reads as free, and referenced is the branch that keeps the name-preserving rebind. Normalising it would have been an unrelated behaviour change. The asymmetry is now stated at the shared vocabulary in-source.

EVIDENCE, each exit captured with the redirect and echo on one command line in one shell: clojure -M:test exit 0 at 77 tests / 276 assertions before, exit 0 at 82 / 310 after; clojure -M:integration exit 0 at 6 / 10 both sides; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. The probe flipped from [:rewrite nil] to [:flag :interceptors] with the source byte-identical. Doc-gate coverage was PROVEN rather than assumed by planting a broken link in the codemod README: exit 1 naming the file and line, restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object rather than by reading a diff.

TESTS ADDED (5): shadowed-bare-path-flagged-under-a-qualified-binder (the audit probe, plus cljs.core/let, an aliased c/let, clojure.core/fn); shadowed-bare-path-flagged-under-an-unrecognised-binder (defmethod, when-first, dotimes, a project macro); unrecognised-head-without-a-path-binding-still-lowers (NON-VACUITY for the catch-all: deftest/testing, comment, a defmethod binding another param, a doseq binding another name all still lower); qualified-binder-shadowing-does-not-suppress-a-qualified-head (over-reach control); qualified-binder-shadow-idempotent.

DOCS: migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/README.md carried this guarantee in two places and both now state that kin is a rule rather than a roster. The HOT-ZONE migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md was NOT touched — it does not state the shadow guarantee, so nothing in it became untrue.
close_reason: Lexical-shadow boundary closed by PR #8896 (commit b57bbac2f2). The AUDIT PR #8857 reopen — the newest text-bearing mutation, found by walking bd history to the bead beginning — was reproduced at source before any edit: a qualified binder such as clojure.core/let around a registration left a bare path head reading as the framework constructor, and the site lowered to the interceptor ref, silently replacing the custom interceptor. Cause: form-binds? matched heads VERBATIM against a vocabulary keyed by unqualified symbols. Repaired with two fail-closed rules replacing the roster lookup — binders matched by simple name, and an unrecognised head whose vector child binds the name treated as a binder — which also covers defmethod / when-first / dotimes / project macros without a general analyser. Five tests added including a non-vacuity control that unrecognised heads NOT binding path still lower. Gates, exits captured in-shell: clojure -M:test exit 0 (77/276 to 82/310), clojure -M:integration exit 0 (6/10), check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 with coverage proven by a planted broken link (exit 1) and restore verified by blob hash. The bead DESCRIPTION is historical — its original premise was discharged by merged PRs #8828 / #8846 / #8857, and both sibling acceptance items (the migration-skill eval fixture, and clojure -M:integration wired into test.yml) were confirmed present at tip.

title: surface-review(skill-setup): make one prompt produce one mounted SPA
description:
## Scope

Treat `skills/re-frame2-setup/**` as one installed product and make its unqualified greenfield request do one thing well: turn an empty directory into a running Reagent counter SPA in one pass. The default path owns the exact files, resolving dependency baseline, commands, verification, and handoff. Keep UIx and merge-into-an-empty-CLJS-project support only when the author explicitly asks for those routes. Align the emitted result with the reduced canonical scaffold owned by `rf2-zq34m`; do not maintain a second independent project template.

## Findings

1. The advertised six-step path is not a fast path. A brand-new Reagent run needs `SKILL.md` plus `deps-versions.md`, `shadow-cljs.md`, and `first-counter.md`: 75,697 bytes and about 9,942 words before the agent writes the project. If it follows the boot explanation pointer too, `entry-namespace.md` adds another 22,547 bytes. Four of the five reference leaves are over the family 16 KB ceiling, while `spec/design.md` says only `entry-namespace.md` is slightly over and that a typical session reads two leaves.
2. The default request is forced into an interview. `deps-versions.md` says the author must choose a pin and the skill must stop before editing if none was supplied. `SKILL.md` also forbids the skill from executing the repo's one-command generator and tells it to hand the command back to the author. Thus “Scaffold a re-frame2 app for me” cannot complete without a choice and a second actor.
3. The first-mount route carries decisions unrelated to mounting: schemas, Xray, `@xyflow/react`, `elkjs`, a right-side host column, CSP/production-hardening prose, publication-state branching, and substrate-specific devtools policy. Reagent is nominally the default, but UIx/Xray/Hicasso distinctions occupy cardinal rules, the main checklist, troubleshooting, and handoff before the default counter exists.
4. The copyable runtime code is currently sound: it uses the current `rf/init!` + explicit `frame-root` seed, frame-targeted schema attach, retained React root, and measured-correct `^:dev/after-load` mount path; the local-root compile cover exercises both Reagent and UIx. The gap is the product journey, not a need for more API explanation.
5. The strongest setup compile test does not materialise the documented dependency file. It synthesises a separate deps map with placeholder Maven versions, rewrites framework coordinates to monorepo `:local/root`, and proves only `compile app`. It neither proves that the exact default dependency command/coordinate resolves from an empty consumer project nor boots the page and clicks 0→1.
6. The 16 evals are explicitly trigger-only (`should_trigger`); none grades the response, resulting files, commands, no-question default, mounted DOM, or handoff. The 1,162-line structural suite instead locks Xray layout, CSP wording, publication branches, UIx routing, and the prohibition on executing the generator. It protects accumulated policy better than the outcome named by the skill.
7. History shows accretion. The initial skill commit shipped `SKILL.md` plus four references at 36,433 bytes and taught core + adapter as the day-one path. The current corresponding shipped corpus is 105,173 bytes after schema, Xray, UIx, CSP/release, troubleshooting, and parity rules accumulated. The useful hot-reload correction in `rf2-r0kk7` / `rf2-ms6r8` came from a real watch-and-browser measurement, demonstrating the kind of outcome proof this skill still lacks.

## Recommended Action

- Define a zero-interview default: an unqualified request in an empty directory chooses Reagent, a single reviewed resolving baseline appropriate to the current publication state, the conventional app namespace/build id/port, and the smallest runnable counter. A user-supplied pin or UIx request overrides the default; absence of either is not a reason to stop.
- Make the main skill a short executor and router. Put the entire default in one copy-complete shipped source (or an asset mechanically derived from the canonical reduced template) with exact filenames and commands. The skill should never reassemble one project from three large prose leaves or hand-maintain a second template.
- Execute the normal work under the explicit invocation: create the files, run `npm install`, run a terminating compile check, start the dev server, and report the URL. Broaden the routine command grants as needed; do not preserve the current user-run-generator prohibition as policy.
- Match `rf2-zq34m`'s small SPA contract. Keep only dependencies and source needed for the counter and selected adapter. Move schemas, Xray, Story, HTTP, production CSP/hosting, Pair, and other capabilities to a compact next-steps link instead of installing or explaining them on the default route.
- Keep explicit UIx and empty-project merge recipes as secondary leaves. They may share the substrate-neutral counter, but they must not introduce a wizard, option matrix, compatibility aliases, or questions into the default.
- Replace prose-lock emphasis with an exact-output behavioral contract: consume the same shipped source the skill uses, resolve its real deps, compile it, serve its real page, and assert the counter paints and advances 0→1. Keep small structural checks only where they prevent a false-green.
- End with a factual handoff: files created, command verified, URL, and the single next skill for application authoring. Mention optional tools only when requested.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From an empty directory, the positive prompt “Scaffold a re-frame2 app for me” takes no clarification round, writes a deterministic Reagent project with no `<VERSION>`/`<SHA>` placeholders, and uses one resolving baseline stored in one source of truth.
2. The default route requires `SKILL.md` plus at most one one-level-deep leaf/asset. Shipped leaves meet the family size discipline or have a demonstrated per-session token-saving exception; no default-path leaf routes onward to another required leaf.
3. The default direct dependency/file manifest matches the reduced runnable SPA contract from `rf2-zq34m`: no schema/Xray/Story/SSR/HTTP coordinate, no `@xyflow/react` or `elkjs`, no Xray host, and no generated policy/toolchain bundle unless the author explicitly requested that capability.
4. The skill executes file creation, install, and a terminating compile verification itself. Its handoff names the successful command and the actual local URL; it does not claim the browser mounted from compile success alone.
5. A black-box setup fixture consumes the exact shipped default source in a fresh temp project, resolves the documented coordinates, compiles, starts the real generated page, asserts the heading and initial `0`, clicks `+1`, and observes `1`. A red witness proves that breaking the adapter/init/build wiring or click path fails the fixture.
6. An explicit UIx prompt and an explicit merge-into-empty-CLJS prompt still reach complete focused routes, but the unqualified route contains no substrate/version/devtools questionnaire, option matrix, or compatibility mode.
7. Evals cover both routing and outcome: at least the start-from-nothing/minimum-wiring prompts assert no clarification, expected manifest/commands, successful verification, and concise handoff. Trigger-only fixtures may remain but are not the sole evaluation.
8. Root instructions, README/plugin metadata, references, internal design notes, and tests describe the same one-pass contract. Stale locks that require user-run generation, Xray/schema day-one wiring, or prose minutiae are removed rather than wrapped in compatibility wording.

## Non-goals

- No setup wizard, interactive questionnaire, `:minimal?` flag, profile system, deprecated aliases, or old-shape compatibility scaffold.
- No re-frame2 runtime, adapter, schema, Xray, Story, Pair, HTTP, SSR, CSP, or deployment redesign.
- No second generator implementation. Reuse or mechanically derive from the canonical reduced template contract; do not duplicate its variant machinery in the skill.
- No Hicasso substrate addition and no widening beyond the existing explicit UIx route.
- No authoring guidance beyond the mounted counter and concise next-step link.
- No Clojars group verification, coordinate rename, tag, repo split, or publication work; those remain with their existing owners.

title: websocket pattern trusts inbound correlation before validation
description:
## Scope

Align the canonical runnable WebSocket pattern across examples/patterns/websocket/, its external CLJS test wrapper, spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md, and the WebSocket skill so the code programmers and coding agents copy is safe at both trust boundaries: credentials leaving the app and frames entering it.

Preserve the example's existing lifecycle machine, mock transport, UI, queue/correlation semantics, and the repository's test-free-examples policy. This is a focused correction to one worked pattern, not a new WebSocket facility.

## Findings

The four pattern examples are generally current and copyable: they use the public reg-event/reg-sub/reg-view and reg-machine/defmachine idioms, explicit frame roots and initial events, machine data schemas, recordable durable coeffects, and external headless wrappers. Every declared pattern build is derived by the examples compile gate, including the Nine States story build.

The WebSocket example is also unusually well covered for reconnects, stale socket epochs, queueing, correlation, timeouts, subscription replay, loss semantics, and teardown. Its two trust boundaries nevertheless contradict the newer canonical guidance:

- connection.cljs persists the raw :auth-token in the connection machine's :data, accepts it on :ws/connect and :ws/refresh-token events, dispatches it to the child, and copies it into the socket actor's machine :data. schema.cljs and README.md teach the same shape, and the wrapper tests assert the token is present in snapshots.
- skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md now says raw bearer/cookie/refresh credentials must never enter machine :data or dispatch. Its canonical declaration carries only an opaque :cred-ref and resolves the bearer through an app-owned, client-only host seam.
- messages.cljs writes both pushes and correlated replies into app-db without an inbound message schema or :rf.schema/at-boundary. Its Message schema describes values after storage and is not a closed wire contract. The callback event :ws.app/request-reply is a second app-db-writing ingress with the same omission.
- spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md added the correct closed InboundMessage plus production boundary interceptor requirement, including the correlated reply path, but its main worked machine and re-authentication prose still carry raw :auth-token. The runnable example implements neither correction.

History explains the split rather than justifying it. Commit bc861c1d17 introduced the runnable WebSocket example on 2026-05-12. Commit ae12ce9b43 (historical bead rf2-x3u46) moved canonical credentials out of machine :data two days later, but changed the skill rather than the example. Commit d667871dae (historical bead rf2-096js) added the inbound-frame obligation to the spec on 2026-08-03, again without updating the runnable source or wrapper. The skill calls the runnable example ground truth, so this divergence makes the unsafe form the easiest one to copy.

## Recommended Action

Make the runnable example demonstrate the already-documented small seam:

- Carry only URL plus an opaque :cred-ref through connect, reconnect, rotation, connection :data, and spawned actor :data.
- Add the minimum app-prefixed, client-only host resolver needed by the demo. Resolve the real bearer immediately beside socket creation/authentication, retain it only in the private host closure for the necessary send, and discard it. Do not route it back through dispatch, app-db, machine snapshots, traces, or recorder data.
- Define one closed inbound wire schema for the demo's actual reply and push variants. Put that schema and :rf.schema/at-boundary on :ws/handle-message, and give the correlated reply-writing ingress an equally release-resident check. Keep locally synthesized connection-loss replies valid without presenting them as trusted server bytes.
- Update the README and companion spec to agree tersely with the runnable form. Reuse the current public APIs and current credential/inbound guidance; do not invent a generalized credential or protocol layer.
- Extend the existing external WebSocket wrapper to prove both boundaries while retaining its lifecycle coverage.

## Evidence

- examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:116-125 stores :auth-token in connection :data; lines 151-172 record and rotate it; lines 211-218 dispatch it; lines 344-351 copy it into spawned actor :data.
- examples/patterns/websocket/messages.cljs:253-269 stores the raw token in socket actor :data; lines 388-404 register :ws/handle-message with no schema/interceptor; lines 452-458 do the same for :ws.app/request-reply.
- examples/patterns/websocket/schema.cljs:36-39 declares :auth-token as connection data; its Message schema is a permissive stored-message shape, not a closed ingress union.
- examples/patterns/websocket/views.cljs:91-96 initiates the demo with :auth-token "demo-token".
- examples/patterns/websocket/README.md:93-102 teaches that reconnects carry the token through machine :data.
- skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md:28-36 requires opaque :cred-ref plus an app-owned client-only resolver; lines 174-181 identify raw machine credentials and skipped boundary validation as anti-patterns.
- spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md:429-458 specifies the closed inbound union, :rf.schema/at-boundary, and the second correlated-reply ingress, while lines 85-86, 121-130, 249-258, and 460-462 still teach raw token persistence.
- implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs has broad lifecycle coverage and explicit raw-token snapshot assertions, but no malformed/unknown inbound-frame rejection case.
- node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list derives examples/boot, examples/long-running-work, examples/nine-states, examples/nine-states-with-stories, and examples/websocket. examples/TESTING.md assigns behavior to the external wrappers and compilation to this derived gate.
- Fresh open/all-status title and description searches for the surface prefix, WebSocket, credentials, cred-ref, auth-token, bearer, inbound frames, and boundary validation found no duplicate. rf2-iacw2 and rf2-ujdn0 are adjacent launch-command tasks only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The connection and socket actor machine schemas/data carry an opaque :cred-ref, never a raw bearer, cookie, password, refresh token, or equivalent credential. Connect/reconnect/rotation event payloads and queued application events likewise carry only the reference.
2. A small app-prefixed, client-only host seam resolves the demo credential at the point of socket authentication. Initial connect, reconnect, and credential rotation still authenticate, while a distinctive raw credential sentinel is absent from inspectable machine snapshots and the exercised event/trace/recording surface.
3. The demo declares a closed schema for every accepted server push and correlated reply variant. :ws/handle-message applies that schema with :rf.schema/at-boundary, and the event that writes correlated server replies into app-db has the same release-resident protection.
4. External wrapper tests prove valid pushes and replies still land; malformed bodies and unknown :type values are rejected, produce the expected boundary-rejection observability, and do not change :messages or :last-reply. Locally generated connection-loss results remain supported.
5. Existing reconnect backoff, stale-epoch rejection, queue flush, subscription replay, request correlation, timeout, fail-in-flight, and teardown tests remain green.
6. The runnable source, its concise README, spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md, and skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md agree on the credential and inbound-frame contracts. No surface continues to call the raw-token form canonical.
7. npm run test:cljs and npm run test:examples-compile pass, along with the relevant documentation link/schema-policy checks for the touched files.

## Non-goals

- Shipping a managed WebSocket API, transport library, pattern framework, or compatibility layer.
- Building a general credential vault/resolver abstraction or prescribing an auth architecture.
- Cataloguing wire protocols or exhaustively documenting payload variants.
- Redesigning the connection machine topology, backoff, queue, subscription, correlation, timeout, or loss semantics.
- Adding tests under examples/ or a per-example browser matrix.
- Refactoring boot, long-running-work, or nine-states.
- Standardizing example launch commands; rf2-iacw2 and rf2-ujdn0 own that adjacent outcome.

## Related beads

- rf2-iacw2 - adjacent core-example launch-command correction; no overlap with this trust-boundary outcome.
- rf2-ujdn0 - adjacent capability-example launch-command correction; no overlap with this trust-boundary outcome.
- rf2-x3u46 - historical commit bead named by ae12ce9b43, which established the opaque credential-reference guidance.
- rf2-096js - historical commit bead named by d667871dae, which established release-resident inbound-frame validation in the spec.

Surfaces include spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md (HOT, no live toucher) and implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs (confirm the rf2-k5r9t fence is src-only). AUDIT PR #8821 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness/completeness, inbound boundary: validation occurs after untrusted bytes have already affected connection-machine truth. socket-actor-machine forwards every non-auth body to :ws/received. connection-machine :receive-message then treats mere presence of attacker-controlled :request-id as a correlated reply, immediately dissocs that in-flight slot, and dispatches the raw body to both :ws/handle-message and the stored reply event. The two schema-bound app events can reject the body, but they cannot undo the already-cleared correlation state. Thus the new malformed-correlated-reply test leaves app-db unchanged while silently consuming the pending request; it never asserts :in-flight remains.

RequestOutcome also admits LocalRequestFailure solely by data shape. A server that saw the wire request id can send {:request-id rid :ok false :error :ws/timeout} with no :type. InboundMessage rejects it, but the same raw body is dispatched to :ws.app/request-reply, matches the closed LocalRequestFailure arm, mutates :last-reply as if locally minted, and clears :in-flight. The test deliberately uses a malformed body carrying :type :reply and comments that :type prevents it posing as local, so it misses the exact provenance hole. Minimal repair: enforce the closed inbound wire contract before any request-id branching or runtime-state mutation, and keep server ReplyMessage delivery distinct from the machine's locally minted loss/timeout event (or otherwise encode trustworthy provenance); malformed/unknown frames must leave both app-db and :in-flight untouched. Add the local-failure-shaped hostile frame and pending-timeout/loss controls.

Implementation quality, credential boundary: mock-socket-for-actor resolves bearer in its outer let and the stored :send function closes over it. That handle remains in sockets-by-actor for the socket lifetime, so the bearer is not 'read once, then gone' or discarded after the auth send as the source/spec/README claim. The sentinel test cannot inspect lexical host closures. Resolve inside the :auth branch (or clear a one-shot cell immediately after forming the wire send) so the stored socket handle retains only cred-ref, then preserve connect/reconnect/rotation and unknown-ref tests.

All-status searches for websocket malformed reply in-flight, local request failure spoof, RequestOutcome websocket, and inbound boundary correlation found no separate owner. These are direct residues of rf2-iyjae's two trust-boundary outcome.
AUDIT RESIDUE ADDRESSED — PR #8856 (2026-09-01, branch worker/ws-boundaries-iyjae, based on f15d7ff332).

All three audit findings verified at source before acting, and all three HELD.

(1) Inbound boundary. connection.cljs :receive-message branched on (:request-id body) and dissoc'd that :in-flight slot before any validation, so a hostile frame naming a pending request consumed the correlation while the ingress downstream refused the body — caller never answered, and the scheduled timeout found nothing to settle. Fixed with a :trusted-frame? guard (connection epoch AND schema/valid-inbound-frame?, one named guard per 005 §No combinator data form) on a two-candidate :ws/received; the second candidate, :refuse-frame, returns no :data and forwards to :ws/handle-message so the ingress still emits the one canonical :rf.error/schema-validation-failure. Branching now reads the vetted :type, not presence-of-:request-id.

(2) Provenance. RequestOutcome admitted LocalRequestFailure by shape. Now a closed :multi dispatching on :origin, which the machine stamps AFTER receipt (:ws/server on a wire body handed to a reply event, :ws/local on fail-in-flight and :clear-request bodies). A frame off the wire cannot reach the :ws/local arm. Also closed both wire arms ({:closed true}); an OPEN push arm was a second route to the same in-flight consumption, since it accepted a :request-id under a :type unrelated to request-reply. Closing the push arm required declaring :at (the manual push button's timestamp) and changing one test's ad-hoc {:type :push :n N} frames.

(3) Credential closure. mock-socket-for-actor resolved the bearer in its outer let and the stored :send closure retained it for the socket's lifetime, contradicting the 'read once, then gone' claim in source, README and spec. Resolution moved inside the :auth branch; the stored handle now closes over :cred-ref alone. NOTE this repair is STRUCTURAL and not observable to the sentinel sweep — a lexical closure is on no serialisable surface — which is recorded in the test comment rather than papered over, since that blind spot is why the finding survived the first pass.

Tests: the audit was right that the old malformed-correlated-reply case never asserted :in-flight survived. Added that, the local-failure-shaped hostile frame ({:request-id rid :ok false :error :ws/timeout}, no :type), the :request-id-smuggling push, and a pending-timeout control proving the surviving slot still answers its caller. Added websocket-request-reply-ingress-rejection as a separate deftest, because the machine no longer routes bad frames to :ws.app/request-reply and that ingress must still hold its own contract. Provenance controls added to the drop, timeout and correlation tests.

Two prose drifts the audit implies but does not name were also corrected: the skill and README placed credential resolution 'at actor spawn' / 'as the socket opens', which is exactly the shape that retains the bearer. The skill's canonical declaration gained :trusted-frame? and the two-candidate :ws/received so the copied form is the vetted one.

Gates, captured exits on the final base: test:cljs 0 (11122 tests / 54598 assertions / 0 failures), test:examples-compile 0 (56 builds, zero warnings), check_readme_links.py --ci 0, check_doc_slugs.py 0. Each gate shown RED first: both doc gates against a planted fault at a line this change edits, and test:cljs against a payload-blind :trusted-frame? — which failed exactly 2 assertions, both the new ones, reproducing the audit's bug precisely. Every restore verified by git blob hash.

title: [MERGED #10123] Incomplete inspector width budget: long string leaves are still serialized in full
description: PR #10053 adds estimate-chars! to stop inline-fit work at the column budget, but its scalar branch in views/edn_inspector.cljs:1650-1653 calls pr-str on the entire scalar before comparing the accumulated length. A source-isolated probe intercepting pr-str records printed sizes [5 500002]; current origin/main retains this branch. This leaves repeated inline-fit decisions proportional to large raw text payloads even though their string length already proves they cannot fit. Check string length against the remaining budget before printing; preserve exact estimates for genuinely small values. Add a long nested string control that checks bounded work, not merely the returned infinity. Keep the existing small API and avoid a general-purpose serializer redesign. Source-isolated Babashka algorithm probe only; no timing/browser performance claim.
