`pr-str` and recording the size of every string it produced:

    {:body <500,000 chars>} at a 100px column   ->  printed sizes [5 500002]
    {:response {:body <same>}} at the ceiling   ->  printed sizes [9 5 500002]

The `[5 500002]` matches the item's own source-isolated Babashka probe exactly, so the
item's central claim holds and is now corroborated by a second, independent instrument.
Both cases returned `##Inf` — the RIGHT answer — before and after the fix. **The return
value was never the defect; the half-megabyte print was.**

## THE FIX — one branch, no API change

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:2026`. A string's `count` is
O(1) on this host and `pr-str` can only ever make it LONGER — two quotes, plus a character
per escape — so `(+ @total (count s) 2)` is a lower bound on where the running total lands.
When that bound ALONE already passes `cap`, printing cannot change the outcome, so the walk
charges the bound and skips the print.

Under budget nothing changes: the print still happens, so escapes are still counted.
`estimated-inline-px` (`:2046`) asks only whether `@total` passed `cap`, and both paths
agree on that, so **the value returned is identical either way — only the work differs.**

Scope held: no serializer redesign, no new API, `count-bound` (`:881`) and `bounded-vec`
(`:921`) untouched and not made unconditional, `children-of-pair` untouched (it is
`rf2-et4l0` / `rf2-t450s` territory), and no timing or browser performance claim anywhere —
the evidence is printed-size counts, which is a claim about WORK DONE.

## THE TEST WAS BUILT TO FAIL, AND WAS SHOWN RED ON THE GENUINE UNFIXED TREE

This was the whole risk in the item. A test asserting only that the function returns
`##Inf` PASSES on the unfixed tree. Committed first, run on the unfixed tree: **2
failures, both the `not-any?` assertions**, quoting the sizes above. Then green after the
fix with no test edited.

Two vacuity guards, both load-bearing:

1. **Positive control per case.** There was NO repo precedent for `with-redefs` on a
   `cljs.core` var — 0 occurrences tree-wide against a control of 346 on project vars — so
   a spy that silently failed to intercept would have left the recorded list empty and made
   "nothing large was printed" pass vacuously on a tree that still had the bug. Each case
   therefore asserts a SMALL leaf WAS recorded before the absence of the large one is
   believed. Those controls passed on the red run, which is what establishes the
   interception is live.
2. **Reachability control for the nested case.** Under a 100px budget the walk passes `cap`
   on the PREFIX and never reaches the nested leaf at all — so a nested test written the
   obvious way would have passed on the unfixed tree FOR THE WRONG REASON. The nested case
   uses the default ceiling and is paired against a short-string run proving that leaf
   position is printed.

`small-strings-are-still-measured-EXACTLY` pins the other half the item asked for: escaped
strings, the empty string, and a 4000-character string just under the ceiling are all still
measured by their own print, so exactness for genuinely small values is preserved.

## GATES — captured exits

- **`npm run test:cljs`** (node lane, held the shadow-cljs lane): baseline taken on my own
  base **12368 / 61999**; final **12371 / 62016, 0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0**. Delta
  **+3 tests / +17 assertions**, predicted from the diff BEFORE the log was opened and
  matched exactly — which is the evidence CI compiled this branch, a green log in this tree
  carrying zero `Testing <ns>` banners. Re-run after the rebase; both numbers held. Log
  integrity checked: 0 NUL bytes, exactly one summary line, so no orphan splice.
- **clj-kondo, PLAIN form** (not `--fail-level error`, which exits 0 on an unresolved symbol
  here): **0 errors, 2 warnings, exit 2**. Both warnings are pre-existing in committed code
  — confirmed against a baseline lint of the trunk copies, where they sit exactly 21 lines
  above their post-edit positions, which is precisely what this change adds. CI gate form
  `python scripts/lint_kondo.py`: exit 0, errors 0.
- **Relied on CI** for the other five surfaces the classifier arms when handed PATHS
  (controls: an arming path 6, a spec-only path 0): `cljs_browser`, `examples_compile`,
  `tools_jvm`, `mcp_conformance`, `story_xray_browser`.
- **Not applicable:** the two link gates and `mkdocs build --strict` do not grade this — it
  touches no markdown.
- **Docstring:** `estimate-chars!`'s "Scalars are measured by their own `pr-str` (exact)"
  was the stated design intent and would have become quietly false, so it is now qualified.
  Nothing grades whether a docstring is true; I read it against the code by hand.

Line endings, Python on the bytes, both files before and after: CR == CRLF and bare LF 0.
The source file's BEFORE numbers matched the dispatch fingerprint exactly, so the base is
confirmed.

## LANE

Granted exclusively and held continuously from 2026-09-20 22:38:42 to 23:07:47 AUSEST.
Verified free BY EFFECT before taking and after releasing — machine-wide census, NO path
filter, 6 rows / 0 lane-bearing / 0 empty command lines (the empty count is the control),
and 0 processes under this worktree at release. The two stray JVMs held under `rf2-azxt5`
were never touched, nor any Codex CLI or MCP server. Installed `node_modules` from the
lockfile in my own worktree rather than junctioning the shared tree; the coordinator's tree
read 103 entries before and after, counted with `find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1` rather than
a bare `ls`, which omits dotfiles.

## TWO THINGS THE NEXT READER SHOULD KNOW

**The item's `ai/` evidence log is gone and I did not look for it.** The dispatch stated
this up front, so no cycle was spent hunting. Nothing was lost: the item carries its
decisive measurement inline, which is exactly the property that makes a disposable
supporting path safe to lose — and this close reason carries its own inline too.

**One correction to the dispatch brief, offered as a finding.** Its fixed-string census
gave `inline-fit` as 16; at trunk `d631617b78` that is 16 MATCHING LINES but **17
OCCURRENCES** (one line carries two). `estimate-chars!` 6 and `pr-str` 40 both reproduced
exactly, as did every one of the six line numbers in its table — `count-bound` 881,
`bounded-vec` 921, `endless-candidate?` 945, `children-of-pair` 1517, `estimate-chars!`
1990, `leaf-diff-op` 3319 — and the scalar branch at 2008, against the item's stale
`:1650-1653`, a delta of +356. So the brief's table is sound; only the one count needed the
occurrences-versus-lines distinction the brief itself asks for.

title: review(xray/machines): senior-developer findings, 10 ranked, 3 spec chapters drift, trunk 9555881fe3 (2026-09-17)
description:
# Senior review: xray-machines

Reviewer persona: senior engineer who has built statechart tooling (visualisers, simulators, inspectors) and knows where they lie — a simulator that diverges from the runtime's transition semantics, a topology view that draws a transition the machine cannot take, an inspector that shows the previous instance's state.
Tree: xray-review-sep17 worktree, trunk 9555881fe3
Scope read: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector.cljs (1463), panels/machine_inspector_helpers.cljc (1058), panels/machines/trace_state.cljs (1194), panels/machines/topology_view.cljs (315), panels/machine_after_rings.cljs (626), panels/machine_after_rings_helpers.cljc (570), panels/machine_canvas.cljs (510), static/machines/{sim.cljs 862, sim_helpers.cljc 387, panel.cljs 472, definition_detail.cljs 450, browse_list.cljs 394, helpers.cljc 321, topology.cljs 219, persistence.cljs 187, instances_jump.cljs 113, cascade_dimmed.cljs 42} — 9,183 lines, every file in full; plus implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc (the Level 1 engine contract), parallel.cljc `build-initial-snapshot`, transition.cljc `state-path`/`initial-cascade`/`:rf.machine.timer/scheduled` emit, timer.cljc `:rf.machine.timer/cancelled` emit, machines-viz chart/overlays/after_rings.cljs + after_rings_geometry.cljc + chart/layout.cljc `highlight-id`; tests skimmed: sim_helpers_cljs_test.cljc, sim_cljs_test.cljs, machine_after_rings_cljs_test.cljs, machine_after_rings_helpers_cljs_test.cljc, machine_inspector_view_cljs_test.cljs (prev/next section).
Owning specs consulted: tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md (all 2,358 lines); 021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md §6 (:1270-1480), §Machine cascade (:1815-1904), §17.4 (:5784-6042); 014-Registry-Catalogue.md §Machine inspector (:700-726) + §Static mode (:746-791); spec/005-StateMachines.md §Transition table grammar through §Actions (:182-498), §Hierarchical compound states (:1382-1649), §Parallel regions intro/§Initial state/§Transition broadcast (:1650-1760), §Eventless `:always` (:1981-2106), §Delayed `:after` (:2345-2594).

## Findings, ranked

### 1. Static Sim silently records a guard-blocked (or unhandled) step as a self-transition  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/sim_helpers.cljc:285-318 (`step-sim`); sim.cljs:29-32 and :690-693 (docstrings promising the opposite); implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:138-164 (the engine contract)
- What: the sim folds every `:status :ok` result as a transition, but the runtime's Level 1 map returns `:status :ok` with the snapshot UNCHANGED for an unhandled or guard-blocked event, so a rejected step appends an audit row `#N :open → :open [:door/close]`, animates a from=to edge on the chart, and never shows the "Transition rejected" toast — the opposite of what the ns docstring, the SimChart docstring and spec 003 §UC1 ("LISTED but greyed… guard ✗ failed") promise.
- Evidence: `machines.cljc:147-149` — "An event no transition matched is `:status :ok` with the snapshot unchanged and `:fx []`"; `public-result` (:123-136) drops the engine's `handled?` flag, so the caller cannot tell a no-op from an action-only internal transition. `step-sim` (:306-316) takes the `:ok` branch unconditionally. The tests pin a fabricated contract: `sim_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:204-207` and `sim_cljs_test.cljs:163-165` stub the guard-fail case as `{:status :error … :no-matching-transition}`, a shape the engine never returns (control: the engine's only `:error` kinds are `machine-action-exception` and the two depth-exceeded ids, machines.cljc:150-155), and `sim_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:316-329` asserts "the chart keeps the prior edge lit while the guard error toasts" against that stub. Only a throwing guard/action or a depth trip ever reaches `record-error` in production.
- Action: in `step-sim`, when `:status :ok` AND `(= (:snapshot result) snapshot)` AND `(empty? (:fx result))`, stamp `:last-error` "no transition matched (unhandled, or every candidate's guard failed)" and append no row; rewrite the stub fixtures to the real shape. Decide: that cheap inference (S) vs adding `:handled? bool` to the Level 1 public map so an action-only internal transition is distinguishable too (M — one sentence in Spec 005 §Testing §Level 1). The engine is right; the sim is wrong.

### 2. Sim seeds a compound-`:initial` machine at the compound node, so hierarchical and parallel machines cannot be simulated  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/sim_helpers.cljc:171-189 (`initial-snapshot`), :142-167 (`available-transitions`); runtime seed: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/parallel.cljc:352-401 (`build-initial-snapshot`), transition.cljc:704-712 (`initial-cascade`)
- What: the sim's seed is `{:state (:initial definition) :data (:data definition)}` — the raw declared keyword — while the runtime descends the `:initial` chain to a leaf and, for `:type :parallel`, builds a region-map; so for `{:initial :auth :states {:auth {:initial :form …}}}` the sim sits at `:auth`, the picker lists the compound's own `:on` (usually nothing → "No outgoing transitions declared on this state"), every step resolves against `[:auth]` rather than `[:auth :form]` so the leaf's transitions never match and the machine is stuck at birth (and by finding 1 each attempt records a phantom `:auth → :auth` row); a parallel machine has no root `:initial`, so `initial-snapshot` returns nil, the rail shows `(none)`, and the first step hands `machine-transition` a nil snapshot (`state-path` throws `:rf.error/machine-bad-state-form`, transition.cljc:644-659, caught by `run-machine-transition` and reported as "transition failed").
- Evidence: `sim_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:286-291` PINS the wrong seed ("hierarchical-definition's :initial is :auth (a compound) — the seed snapshot keeps it as the declared :initial value"). Spec 005 :1397 — "A single-keyword `:K` read against a hierarchical definition is treated as the path `[:K]` (which must name a leaf at the root level)". Spec 003 :1413 says "the seed is the definition's declared `:initial` + `:data`", which is the sentence the code implements literally. Control: the flat fixture works and is what every other sim test uses. The runtime also runs `:entry` actions and settles `:always` at birth (Spec 005 :1419-1446); the sim skips both (docstring :176-183), so even a flat seed's `:data` diverges when an initial `:entry` writes it.
- Action: seed via the engine rather than by hand — `machine-transition definition <bootstrap-snapshot> [:rf.machine/start]` if the pure entry honours the start kick, else expose/`requiring-resolve` the artefact's `build-initial-snapshot`; at minimum descend `:initial` to the leaf (and build the region-map for `:parallel`) and say in the rail that entry actions were not run. Rewrite the pinning test. Spec 003 :1413's seed sentence should say "the runtime's initial snapshot".

### 3. The `:after` countdown rings project the wrong machine — and the wrong frame  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_after_rings.cljs:162-166; panels/machine_after_rings_helpers.cljc:298-311 (`project-timers`); panels/machine_inspector.cljs:1122-1132 (`:rf.xray/machine-inspector-data`) and :512-559 (the focused chart mounts the overlay with no machine-id); panels/machine_inspector_helpers.cljc:277-283 (`pick-selected`)
- What: (a) `:rf.xray/active-timers-for-focused-machine` reads `(:selected-id mi-data)` — the retired picker's `:selected-machine-id` slot or, when unset (always, in Dynamic mode), the alphabetically-first registered machine — while the chart it overlays renders the machine the focused event targeted (`record :machine-id`); with two machines registered the rings are folded for a different machine than the chart shows. (b) The fold filters by machine-id only, over a buffer that is the union of EVERY host frame's ring, so two singleton instances of one definition in two frames collide on the `(machine-id, state, epoch, delay)` key and one frame's schedule/cancel closes or replaces the other's ring on the inspected frame's chart.
- Evidence: (a) the only writer of `:selected-machine-id` is `:rf.xray/select-machine-id` (machine_inspector.cljs:1200-1202), dispatched solely from the Static JUMP (instances_jump.cljs:45-48); `project-data` → `pick-selected rows selected-id` → `(first rows)`, rows sorted by `(str machine-id)` (helpers :273, :277-283). Ring node-ids are `chart-layout/highlight-id state` (machines-viz layout.cljc:1442-1458), which carry no machine-id, and the overlay walks the DOM for `rf-mv-chart-node-<node-id>` (overlays/after_rings.cljs:76-84), so a `:loading` timer on `:auth/main` paints on `:checkout`'s `:loading` node when that is the chart on screen, and paints nothing when the names differ. (b) `trace_collector.cljs:166-172` — `snapshot-from-rings` "materialise[s] every registered HOST frame's flat trace events … into one oldest-first vector"; `project-timers` (:298-311) has no `:frame` predicate although both `scheduled` (transition.cljc:2185-2192) and `cancelled` (timer.cljc:293-301) traces carry `:frame`. By contrast the focused-event lens IS frame-scoped: `:epoch-history` is re-read per target frame (epoch.cljs:113, :140) and the section key includes `target-frame` (helpers :1050-1051). Control: every after-rings CLJS test registers exactly one machine (`:auth/login`) in one frame (machine_after_rings_cljs_test.cljs:66-142), so neither mismatch is visible to the suite.
- Action: make the sub take the machine id (`[:rf.xray/active-timers-for-machine mid]`, threaded from the focused record by `focused-event-section`) and filter the events on `(= target-frame (get-in ev [:tags :frame]))`; drop the `:selected-id` read. After this, `:selected-machine-id` has no Dynamic consumer left (see finding 7).

### 4. A cancelled `:after` ring is never evicted — every state exit leaves a permanent grey crossed ring, stacking one per visit  [CONFIRMED (retention) / PLAUSIBLE (visual stacking)] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_after_rings_helpers.cljc:313-348 (`active-timers-for-machine`), :116-144 (`timer-key` includes `epoch`); panels/machine_after_rings.cljs:449-491 (`overlay-tree` renders every spec); machines-viz chart/overlays/after_rings.cljs:209-214 (`^{:key node-id}`)
- What: the runtime emits `:rf.machine.timer/cancelled :reason :on-exit` for every armed timer of every exited state (timer.cljc:1121-1173), the helper keeps `:cancelled` records indefinitely ("the view decides retention" — :318-320) and the view decides nothing, so the ordinary "user event beat the timer" path leaves a grey crossed ring on the node until the trace ring buffer evicts the `:scheduled` event; each re-entry mints a new epoch and therefore a new record, so N visits to `:loading` that each exited early produce N cancelled rings on one node, all with the same React key.
- Evidence: `active-timers-for-machine` returns `:cancelled r` unconditionally (:346); `overlay-tree` maps all timers to specs and renders when `(seq specs)` (:467-469); the overlay's `for` keys each ring by `node-id` alone (:210), so two cancelled records at different epochs on one state collide. Spec 003 §M.2 (:2074-2075) promises "the old ring fades out (200ms)" and (:2072) a dashed/grey STALE ring, while `active-timers-for-machine` drops `:stale` outright (:347). Control: `machine_after_rings_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:273-286` pins that `:cancelled` records ARE returned; no test in either after-rings file pins any retention or a second visit (grep `retention|evict` in the helpers test: only the 5-second zombie rule for `:armed`, :287-289).
- Action: retain a cancelled ring for a short window keyed on `:closed-at` (reuse the existing `now-ms` arg — e.g. drop when `(- now-ms closed-at)` > 2000) and dedupe specs per node so the newest record wins; key the overlay's rings by `(str node-id "-" epoch)`. Then spec 003 §M.2 matches the code (fade → short retention).

### 5. Two per-trace hot paths re-fold the whole trace buffer — one for a ribbon nobody renders, one at 60 Hz  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: perf] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector.cljs:1122-1132; panels/machine_inspector_helpers.cljc:333-373, :404-418; panels/machine_after_rings.cljs:162-166; panels/machine_after_rings_helpers.cljc:292-311
- What: `:rf.xray/machine-inspector-data` has `[:rf.xray/trace-buffer]` as an input and runs `project-transitions` (filter + `sort-by` over the entire buffer) on every trace write while the Machine tab is mounted, to fill `:transitions` and `:chart-props` that no consumer reads since rf2-y9xmf removed the ribbon; `:rf.xray/active-timers-for-focused-machine` has `[:rf.xray/now-ms]` as an input, so while any timer is armed the rAF tick re-runs `project-timers` (filter + sort + fold over the whole buffer) about 60 times a second, when `now` is only used for the 5-second zombie drop.
- Evidence: consumers of the composite's `:transitions`/`:chart-props` — grep across `tools/xray/src` for `:transitions|:chart-props` finds only the helper's own docstrings and the composite itself (the two `:transitions` hits in `sim.cljs:852` / `definition_detail.cljs:441` are the sim's available-transitions, a different key); control: `:empty-kind` and `:selected-id` from the same map ARE read (machine_inspector.cljs:770-794, machine_after_rings.cljs:165). `cap-transitions` (helpers :365-373) likewise has no caller outside tests. The rings sub's input vector is at machine_after_rings.cljs:163.
- Action: delete `:transitions`, `:chart-props`, `project-transitions`, `cap-transitions` and the `trace-buffer` input from the composite (the composite then re-runs only on registry/snapshot/selection change); split the rings sub into a buffer-keyed fold sub and a tiny `now`-keyed filter sub. Same sweep: `machine_canvas.cljs:101-218` keeps the `chart-collapsed` slot, sub, event, fx, localStorage key (`xray.machine-canvas.chart-collapsed-by-id`) and boot-time hydrate for the collapse toggle rf2-g2axio removed — grep `chart-collapsed` in `tools/xray/src` hits only machine_canvas.cljs (31), one retirement comment in machine_inspector.cljs:262 and a key list in local_storage.cljs; no view subscribes `:rf.xray.machine-canvas/chart-collapsed-for` and nothing dispatches `set-chart-collapsed` — delete with its test; `:rf.xray/machine-chart-layout-pulse` (machine_inspector.cljs:1212-1214) is the same residue.

### 6. Prev/Next skips the birth and no-op epochs the panel itself renders  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector.cljs:1241-1245 (`epoch-touches-machine?`)
- What: the walker tests `h/transition-event?` only, so an epoch whose only machine activity is `:rf.machine/started` or `:rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op` — both first-class focused-event records per rf2-eldze / rf2-skmc7 and rendered by this panel — is stepped over; from the door's guard-blocked epoch (pink edge on screen) Prev lands on the last real transition and Next then skips the no-op you came from; a machine whose only history is its birth has a nav that never moves.
- Evidence: `project-focused-event-transitions` (helpers :893-956) folds `transition-event?`, `started-event?` and `no-op-event?`; `epoch-touches-machine?` folds the first only. Spec 003 :26-31 and :173-179: "walks the spine's epoch history to the prior/next epoch whose cascade ALSO touched the focused machine". Control: the only prev/next walk test (`machine_inspector_view_cljs_test.cljs:1113-1138`) seeds transition-only epochs and pins skipping a DIFFERENT machine's epoch; no test seeds a started/no-op epoch on the walk.
- Action: reuse the projection's predicate — `(seq (h/project-focused-event-transitions (:trace-events epoch) nil))` filtered to `machine-id`, or `(or transition-event? started-event? no-op-event?)` — and add one walk test with a birth epoch.

### 7. The Static → Dynamic JUMP's "pre-select this machine" is inert; `:selected-machine-id` is a vestigial slot  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/instances_jump.cljs:29-49; panels/machine_inspector.cljs:1108-1115, :1200-1206, :1253-1259
- What: the JUMP dispatches `:rf.xray/select-machine-id`, but the post-collapse Dynamic panel renders whatever the focused epoch targeted and never reads the slot for rendering, so the operator lands on the Machine tab looking at whichever machine the spine happens to be focused on (or the blank placeholder) — the only effects of the write are to mis-key the after-rings (finding 3) and to seed `scope-machine-id`'s fallback when nothing is focused.
- Evidence: readers of `:selected-machine-id` — `project-data` via the composite (rings only) and the nav fallback (:1258-1259); `focused-event-view` binds to `(h/pick-focused-transition records)` (:644) with no selection input. Spec 003 :1414 and :1421 promise "The user lands on the Dynamic Machines tab with this machine pre-selected"; the code's own comment concedes the panel "drives focus off the event lens, not the picker slot" (:1110-1112). Control: `:rf.xray.static.machines/select` (the Static list's own selection) works — it drives `:rf.xray.static.machines/data` (panel.cljs:268-277).
- Action: make the third dispatch do what the spec says — walk focus to the newest epoch whose cascade touched the machine (the `step-focus` loop already exists; expose it as `:rf.xray/machine-focus-latest mid`), or drop the third dispatch and the slot with it; either way retire `:rf.xray/select-machine-id` / `clear-machine-selection` / `:rf.xray/selected-machine-id` from 014.

### 8. Spec 021 §6.2 Case B contradicts spec 003's empty state, and the code that would render Case B is unmounted  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift] [size: L]
- Where: tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:1367-1390 vs 003-Machine-Inspector.md:549-586; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machines/topology_view.cljs:102-315 (`Topology`, `resolve-current-state-path`); panels/machines/trace_state.cljs:232-269
- What: 003 :3 names 021 §6 "the canonical content design layered onto the topology view", yet 021 §6.2 Case B says a registered machine with no transition this epoch STILL renders its topology with the last-known state annotated `current ●`, while 003 §Empty state (rf2-8og3k, Mike-ruled verbatim placeholder) and the shipped panel render only "This event does not target a state machine"; the Case-B renderer (`topology-view/Topology` with its 4-source current-state resolution and the walk-back helpers `current-state-from-epoch-history` / `from-state-from-traces`) exists and has no production caller.
- Evidence: grep `topology-view/Topology|\[topology-view/` across `tools/xray` — only the ns requires and `topology_view_cljs_test.cljs`; the three src requires call `static-context-shape` / `static-context-inferred?` only (machine_inspector.cljs:527, sim.cljs:728, static/machines/topology.cljs:122 — control). `current-state-from-epoch-history` / `from-state-from-traces` callers in src: `topology_view.cljs` only. `blank-state` (machine_inspector.cljs:677-705) is what the `:else` branch renders (:807-808).
- Action: decide — A) 003 stands (the ruled placeholder): delete `Topology`, `resolve-current-state-path`, the two trace-state walk-back fns and their tests, and rewrite 021 §6.2 Case B + §17.4.1's second "(no activity this epoch)" canvas to point at 003 (S once ruled); B) 021 stands: mount `Topology` for the no-transition case and retire 003's placeholder. description:
Shortlist item 9 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior-review wave (from rf2-pk4i6.1#2). Size L. **Mike ruled OPTION A: tombstone instead of dissoc.** That ruling is made; it is not yours to reopen.

## The defect

Optimistic REMOVE + owner release mid-flight + failed reply RESURRECTS THE DEPARTED OWNER, pinning the entry for the frame's life.

Delete a card, navigate away before the DELETE reply arrives, the reply fails: the rollback restores the full pre-apply entry **with a route owner that already released**. So the entry never GCs, refetches on every focus and reconnect, and polls forever.

The PATCH twin of this is already fixed and pinned. The REMOVE form has no entry for the revision bump to protect, which is why it survived.

## The ruled fix (option A)

Optimistic remove writes `:data nil :status :idle` IN PLACE — a tombstone — keeping owners, work and index. Then the ordinary `detach-owner` / `attach-owner` revision bumps protect it exactly as they protect the PATCH form, and the `:absent` special cases collapse. Touches `spec/016:1053` and the EP-0019 R6 wording.

Option B (filtering `:active-owners` in `restore-before` when `current` is nil) was considered and NOT ruled. Do not build it.

## The triage's citations — EVERY LINE NUMBER IS STALE, AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT CAUTIOUS

The reviewer re-verified these, and they were true when written:
- `mutation_events.cljc:510-512` dissoc's the entry
- `optimistic-conflict?` at `mutation_runtime.cljc:508-510` reads `(some? current-entry)`, so no conflict is detected
- `restore-before` at `:583-620` seats `before` unchanged when `current` is nil

**But PR #9895 (rf2-6gzdb) rewrote this artefact within the hour** — commit 7b927aac69, `mutation_events.cljc` alone moved +103/-20. Anchor every one of these to CONTENT. A line number here is now actively misleading rather than merely unreliable.

## THE INTERACTION WITH #9895 IS THE REAL RISK IN THIS ITEM, AND IT NEEDS DECIDING BEFORE YOU WRITE CODE

PR #9895 just landed a guarantee that the work ledger is BOUNDED, and part of how it achieves that is: **when an entry is REMOVED, its rows and its index bucket are dropped with it.**

Option A stops removing the entry. It writes a tombstone in place and deliberately keeps owners, work and index.

So the question you must answer first: **after the tombstone, does the optimistic-remove path still drop its ledger rows and index bucket — or has this item quietly re-opened the unbounded-growth axis #9895 just closed?**

Answer it by reading both changes at tip, and state the answer in the PR body either way. If the tombstone does re-open it, say so and propose the smallest thing that closes both — do not silently pick one guarantee over the other, and do not weaken #9895's pins to make yours pass. If it does not, say which code path drops the rows for a tombstoned entry and quote it.

This is the single most valuable thing you can produce here, above the fix itself.

## Pins

The item requires the remove-form twin of settle test `:416` — the PATCH twin already exists, so this is the missing half of a pair rather than a new idea. Find the existing PATCH pin at tip by content and mirror it.

Assert a PRECONDITION inside it: that the owner really did release before the reply failed. Without that the test can pass against a path where the owner never left, which is the case that was never broken. Three suites in this repo were found green-and-empty in the last two days by exactly that class of mistake, and the resources artefact supplied one of them.

## Surface and fences

Yours, exclusively: `implementation/resources/src/**`, the resources test tree, `spec/016-Resources.md`, and the EP-0019 R6 wording.

**Shortlist item 14 is sequenced behind this PR on exactly that surface** and will not be dispatched until it merges — the same fence this item waited behind for #9895.

Not yours: `implementation/core/**`, `implementation/epoch/**`, `implementation/schemas/**`, `implementation/http/**` and `spec/009` (a PR is open there awaiting merge); `implementation/fresco/**` and `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/**` (workers are live there). `spec/API.md` and its manifest sidecars are hot-zone: report, do not edit.

title: reagent-slim: render-to-static-markup drops the whole subtree under frame-provider, emitting one placeholder comment (rf2-pk4i6 item 17)
description:
Shortlist item 17 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior-review wave (from rf2-pk4i6.12#2). Mike ruled the whole shortlist as actioned; this is the filed follow-on. Size S.

## The defect

reagent-slim's own `render-to-static-markup` DROPS THE WHOLE SUBTREE under `frame-provider` and emits one placeholder comment.

The canonical slim mount `[rf/frame-provider {:frame f} [app]]`, rendered through the walker that `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:261` sells for HTML export, produces `<!--reagent-react-component-->` and NOTHING ELSE. No error. The comment at `server.cljs:41-45` claiming react-dom parity is FALSE — react-dom renders through Providers.

So the documented HTML-export path returns an empty document for the documented mount, and says nothing.

## The triage's citations (claims, to be opened at tip before editing)

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs` — `emit-hiccup-vector`, the placeholder path at `:1024-1030`, and the false parity comment at `:41-45`.
- `server_cljs_test.cljs:307` — where the provider case belongs.
- `ssr_keyword_head_contract_cljs_test.cljs:79-92` — the stock-Reagent contrast test.
- `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:261` — the page that sells this path.

Re-verified by the reviewer: NO. Both the placeholder path and the contrast test are line-cited only. Anchor to CONTENT, not line numbers.

## What the triage proposes (a proposal, verified before obeyed)

Recognise a React context Provider head in `emit-hiccup-vector` — `$$typeof` is the context symbol on React 19 — and walk its children. About ten lines. Frame scoping under the static walker already comes from `with-frame`, so this does not need to reimplement that.

Delete the false parity sentence at `:41-45`. Add the provider case beside `server_cljs_test.cljs:307`.

**THE SMALLER ALTERNATIVE IS EXPLICITLY ACCEPTABLE and the item says so: routing a Provider head to the existing bad-element throw.** That converts a silent empty document into a loud failure. It is a legitimate deliverable if walking the children proves harder than ten lines — a loud failure beats a silent wrong answer. Choose deliberately and say which you took and why.

## Two things the mayor measured at filing time

- `emit-hiccup-vector` is named in THREE places, not one: `server.cljs`, `IMPL-SPEC.md`, and `implementation/scripts/check-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation.cjs`. That last one is a GATE. Check whether your change moves what it grades before you open the PR — this project's ratchet gates grade the paths you touched, not the change you meant.
- `$$typeof` detection is a React-VERSION-dependent claim. The item says "on React 19". Verify what this tree actually pins before relying on the symbol's identity, and say in the PR body which version you verified against.

## Surface and fences

Yours: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/**`, `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/**`, `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md` if the change moves what it describes, and `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md` if the parity claim is repeated there.

**No live worker touches reagent-slim**, so the artefact is yours alone — but note that shortlist item 8 (the ratom dispose path) is QUEUED against `reagent-slim` and `reagent`, so keep your diff inside the static-rendering path and do not refactor shared adapter internals.

Not yours: `implementation/core/**`, `implementation/epoch/**` and `spec/002` (a worker is live there); `implementation/resources/**` and `spec/016` (a worker is live there); `implementation/http/**` and `spec/014` (a worker is live there); `spec/001` and `core.cljc` (a worker is live there); `implementation/fresco/**` (a worker is live there). `spec/006` is hot-zone: report, do not edit. `spec/API.md` and its manifest sidecars are hot-zone: report, do not edit.

title: story: login_form testbed machine, subs, events and variants become .cljc so story-mcp holds the flagship on the JVM (rf2-a1v8a idea 3, Mike ruled)
description:
RULING (Mike, in chat 2026-09-15: "rule A" on rf2-a1v8a's three Story ideas): all three are adopted, in the order 1, 2, 3. The parity re-run rf2-4gijz runs after them. This bead is idea 3.

MEASURED in rf2-a1v8a Journey 3 (advantage-measured-2026-09-14.md §4):
- story-mcp over stdio, with tools/story/testbeds on its classpath, cannot load the login_form testbed, because the testbed is .cljs only.
- Requiring login-form.events throws FileNotFoundException, list-stories returns {:stories []}, and get-variant :story.login-form/retry-to-success answers "Variant not found".
- So the agent journey could not run on Story at all, while Storybook closed it in 7 agent steps over its MCP addon.

WHAT:
- Split the login_form testbed so its machine, subscriptions, events and variants are .cljc and only the views stay ClojureScript.
- The docs/story tutorial copies this testbed verbatim: docs/story/index.md and 01-first-variant.md, whose ids and :script spelling must match the testbed. Update every doc reference to a renamed file in the same PR.

ACCEPTANCE:
- story-mcp on the JVM: list-stories returns the login_form stories, and get-variant :story.login-form/retry-to-success resolves.
- The testbed still runs in the browser at :8043.
- The examples compile sweep and the docs gates stay green.

title: docs(resources): correct and rebalance the TanStack migration page
description:
Correct two rows of `docs/resources/coming-from-tanstack-query.md` that are wrong at source, rebalance three competitor portraits that a TanStack user would call unfair, and put the two real divergences on the first screen. Docs only; not a hot zone.

Every claim below carries its own trunk file:line (verified at `f2f9ffd654b7`, 2026-09-15) or the exact experiment that produced it, so this bead needs nothing outside the checkout. (Provenance: the Resources parity study in the mayor checkout's gitignored `ai/findings/Resources/fable/`, report §3 and §6 H1/D2; a worktree does not carry it, and nothing here depends on it.)

## 1. Corrections (wrong at source)

- Line 194 says `:keep-previous?` sits "on the route/resource". It is a route-entry / `ensure` key, not a `reg-resource` key: Conduit uses it at five route sites in `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/routing.cljs`, and no registration in that example's `resources.cljs` carries it.
- Line 182 (Garbage collection row) says `:gc-after-ms` runs "after the last owner is released; timer re-checks owners before collecting". The source arms the timer after `:loaded-at`, and on fire removes the entry only if it is still owner-free and not in flight (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/timers.cljc:89`; default 300000 ms, `default-gc-after-ms` in `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc`). The re-check clause is right; the clock's basis is wrong.

## 2. Rebalance (unfair to TanStack as written)

- Fetch-on-render: TanStack Router loaders and `queryClient.query` (added in 5.102.0, deprecating `fetchQuery` / `prefetchQuery` / `ensureQueryData`) start reads before the view renders. The honest remainder: the default hook fetches from render, and a Resources subscription cannot fetch at all.
- Rollback: the documented context-rollback recipe does restore a stale snapshot under server drift. Measured on `@tanstack/query-core` 5.102.8 headless: two overlapping favourite mutations with `onMutate` snapshot + `onError` restore, the newer one settles and its refetch returns count 7, the older one then fails and `onError` restores count 1 over the refetched 7 until its own `onSettled` refetch repairs it. Keep that finding, but credit the two TanStack workflows the page omits: the `variables` pattern (the pending mutation's variables drive the UI, nothing is written to the cache, so nothing can clobber) and `mutation.scope` (a second mutation with the same scope id stays pending and issues nothing until the first settles).
- Declarative invalidation: RTK Query's `providesTags` / `invalidatesTags` is the same idea as `:invalidates` descriptors. Against RTK the row is a match; the extras are scoped descriptors and the event record, and the page should say so rather than claim the idea.

## 3. Lead with the two divergences a migrant meets first

Put on the first screen, beside a two-line migration profile:

- A resource with no `:stale-after-ms` is never time-stale (`spec/016-Resources.md:1213`; `registry.cljc` `default-gc-after-ms` docstring: "`:stale-after-ms` retains its separate infinite default"); TanStack's default is stale at once. The key is per registration; there is no frame-wide default.
- Focus/reconnect revalidation is off unless `:revalidate-on #{:focus :reconnect}` is declared on the frame (Conduit `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/core.cljs:406`); TanStack's is on by default.

The profile is two lines in two places: `:stale-after-ms` on each migrated registration (Conduit `resources.cljs:125`), `:revalidate-on` on the frame. Nothing is built for this.

## Gate, size, acceptance

- Gate: `mkdocs build --strict` (the page is under `docs/`, so the strict build covers it) and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.
- Size: S.
- Acceptance: lines 182 and 194 quote the source semantics above; the three portraits name loaders / `queryClient.query`, the `variables` pattern plus `mutation.scope`, and RTK tags; the first screen carries the two divergences and the two-line profile. No composite parity percentage is added anywhere.
- Removes nothing; corrects two rows and three portraits.

title: False: nested discovery can run a shadow .clj instead of the selected .cljc test
description:
Merged-PR audit #9778 (84328e4c1c4eb62b64872f447fa56b5b65b93683), against closed rf2-fzbj.8. The claim that the new resolution arm identifies the file require will actually load is false for mixed .clj/.cljc copies on the classpath. It can now clear a selected failing test file while the runner executes a different passing file and exits green.

Location: implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/runner.clj, resolved-through-classpath (777ff) and own-path-defect (819ff). The helper calls io/resource with the DISCOVERED file's extension. Clojure require searches the namespace's .clj resource before its .cljc resource across the classpath. Finding this exact .cljc resource therefore does not mean require will load it. collision-defects sees only files below the selected discovery directories, so a shadowing .clj in another classpath root is invisible to that check.

Reproduction executed against the actual landed runner, not a copied predicate:
1. Classpath roots, in order: selected, shadow. selected/probe/deep/mixed_test.cljc declares probe.deep.mixed-test and has a failing test. shadow/probe/deep/mixed_test.clj declares the same namespace and has a passing test.
2. Select only selected/probe with -d and probe.deep.mixed-test with -n. The discovered file is correctly located relative to its classpath root; the .clj shadow is outside the discovery directory.
3. discovery-defects returns []. The real re-frame.test-quiet.runner -main prints shadow-file-passes, runs 1 test / 1 assertion, and exits 0. The selected failing test never executes.
4. Remove only shadow from the classpath: the same command prints selected-file-fails, runs the selected .cljc, and exits 1 with one failure. This proves a real lost failure rather than a guessed resolution ordering.
5. The pre-fix runner source from the merge base reports the selected .cljc as a discovery defect under the same nested scan. The new extension-specific clearance opens this false-green case.

Required correction: before the real-classpath arm clears a file, determine the namespace load winner using Clojure's .clj/.cljc precedence, then compare that winner with the discovered canonical file. Refuse a selected file whose namespace will load a different source. Preserve the ordinary nested-directory repair, root-relative fixture compatibility, canonical same-file aliases, unreadable-form failures, and existing duplicate-file checks. No new allowlist or general policy layer is requested.

Add a subprocess regression with one selected failing .cljc and an unselected passing .clj on separate classpath roots. The runner must refuse it before reporting a green test tally, identify the selected file and actual winner, and still run the selected .cljc when the shadow is absent. Cover the selected root being first on the classpath: extension precedence still chooses .clj from the other root.

title: docs.yml detect job's PR case list is narrower than push.paths, so a scan gate can go red on trunk after a PR merged 87/87
description:
FAIL-OPEN CI GAP, measured 2026-09-13 while fixing rf2-yvmc.

docs.yml's `detect` job lights `docs_surface` unconditionally on any non-pull_request event, but on a PR only when `git diff --name-only origin/<base>...HEAD` matches its own INLINE CASE LIST. That list is deliberately narrower than the same workflow's `push.paths` filter, so a path on `push.paths` but absent from the case list is graded on the trunk push and NOT on the PR that introduces it.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: PR #9748 touched implementation/machines/** only. `detect` classified it non-docs, `MkDocs build` was SKIPPED, and the PR merged at a full 87/87 rollup. The merge's main push then armed on implementation/machines/** (on push.paths since rf2-tzy13, because the live-cell bundle bakes in core/reagent-slim/machines/flows) and ran `check_retired_image_keys.py` RED. Trunk was red across four main runs (ea7bb075d6, df6d1411cb, bcba9e61e5, and its successors) until PR #9760 landed the rename. PRs #9754 and #9759 inherited that red and could not merge.

SECOND INSTANCE IN THE SAME LIST, reported by the trunkfix worker: the case list also omits `scripts/check_retired_image_keys.py` and `scripts/_test_fixtures/check_retired_image_keys/**`, both of which ARE on push.paths. So a PR editing that gate itself — including one that loosens it until it matches nothing — also skips `MkDocs build`.

WHY IT MATTERS TO THE MERGE CRITERION: clause 2 grades the checks a PR actually has. A job `detect` skipped is not a failure and not pending, so the criterion is satisfied by a change the gate would refuse. This is the fail-open shape CLAUDE.md § Workflow catalogues, reached through a path filter rather than through a query.

THE FIX IS A JUDGEMENT CALL, NOT A MECHANICAL SYNC. Narrow-on-PR is presumably deliberate (the docs build is not cheap), so the options are: (a) bring the case list into line with push.paths for the paths the SCANNING gates read, keeping the heavy MkDocs build narrow; (b) split the scan gates out of `MkDocs build` into their own always-on job, which is what test.yml already does for the corpus scans under `verify-readme-links` (see rf2-v7fui, cited in docs.yml's own comments as precedent for exactly this move); (c) accept the gap and rely on trunk-push detection. Recommend (b): it removes the class rather than re-syncing two lists that drift, and the repo has already made that move once.

HOT ZONE: `.github/workflows/*` is sequential (CLAUDE.md § Workflow). One toucher at a time.

title: routing: strip deployment base before root query and fragment
description:
Recognize a deployment mount root followed by a query or fragment when stripping a history strategy's base path. with-base-path currently routes /app to the application root but treats /app?tab=all and /app#section as app-relative /app, causing a route miss.

Ownership / revision
- Surface impl_routing. Primary repair: implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc:260-277, strip-base-path. Its with-base-path shared ingress closure at :365-384 feeds both :decode and :install-listener!.
- history-decode at strategy.cljc:81-92 produces pathname + search + hash. history.cljc:160-164 feeds strategy decode into the initial sync; subsequent listener values use the same base wrapper.
- Tests: implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_url_strategy_test.clj and routing_url_strategy_cljs_test.cljs, with history lifecycle integration as needed.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; source rechecked at 9238907fec4e0cc708bc518aa7fa83db6c0182e7, no owned-path differences from baseline. New independent P2 finding; this review makes no source changes and dispatches no fixer.

Concrete trigger and actual behavior
Register (reg/reg-route :probe/home {} "/") and use (strat/with-base-path strat/history-url-strategy "/app"). A client at https://host/app?tab=all (or /app#section) initializes the URL-owning frame, or returns to that URL via Back/Forward. history-decode returns /app?tab=all; strip-base-path compares the WHOLE string with /app and accepts only /app/ as its other prefix. The ?/# boundary is omitted, so the wrapper returns /app?tab=all unchanged. match-url then misses the registered root route and routing commits not-found (or a distinct app route /app if one exists).

Process-local current-source reproducer:
(reg/reg-route :probe/home {} "/")
(let [strategy (strat/with-base-path
                 (assoc strat/history-url-strategy :decode (constantly "/app?tab=all"))
                 "/app")
      decoded ((:decode strategy))]
  [decoded (reg/match-url decoded)])
;; actual: ["/app?tab=all" nil]
;; expected: ["/?tab=all" {:route-id :probe/home ... :query {"tab" "all"} ...}]

Measured current-source controls:
- /app and /app/ -> / -> :probe/home.
- /app?tab=all, /app#section and /app?tab=all#section remain unchanged and miss.
- /app/?tab=all#section -> /?tab=all#section -> :probe/home, query and fragment preserved.
- /app/items/ok -> /items/ok -> registered item route.
- /application?tab=all stays unchanged (required sibling-prefix protection).
Node independently confirms /app?tab=all and /app#section survive host URL parsing without an inserted slash.

Expected / impact
The mount root denotes the same application route with or without an optional terminal slash, including query/fragment state. Current initial-load and browser-history behavior breaks root links carrying filters, auth callback/query state, or anchors specifically when the optional slash is absent. The existing tests explicitly accept the bare mount root, so query/fragment presence should not change whether the pathname belongs to the base.

Suggested repair
Keep one shared ingress rule. Determine base membership against the pathname, or accept end-of-string, slash, ? and # as the post-base boundaries while preserving the suffix verbatim. Strip the base and ensure an app-root slash before a query/fragment-only remainder. Retain strict rejection of prefix-sharing siblings (/application, /app-admin), the blank-base no-op and the hash-strategy rule that never strips an already app-relative fragment decode. No new public strategy or generic URL parser is needed.

Acceptance
- JVM pure wrapper tests cover /app?tab=all, /app#section and /app?tab=all#section, alongside slash-root, ordinary nested path, unrelated/sibling path and blank-base controls.
- CLJS tests drive the real history strategy's decode and listener callback with these URLs; assert app-relative root, preserved query/fragment, and the expected committed root route on initial sync and browser change.
- Existing hash-plus-base ingress/egress and sibling-prefix tests continue to pass.

Validation / limits / known references
Executed current-source JVM wrapper plus actual route matcher for eight inputs, with absolute source-resource checks; native Node URL witnesses passed. Evidence: ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_routing/probe-impl_routing-1.clj/.log/.exit and probe-impl_routing-2.cjs/.log/.exit (exit 0 for confirmed defect/control assertions). No browser was launched, no CLJS compilation/full suite was run, and no source was edited. Existing reply-envelope tests separately passed 9 tests/60 assertions.
Inspected Spec 012 URL strategies/with-base-path contract (spec/012-Routing.md:1969), existing mount-root/sibling tests (routing_url_strategy_test.clj:321-365), and the actual history producer/wrapper/consumer. Dedup searched current tracker for base path, with-base-path and routing, plus current prior aggregate rf2-fzbj.12 and its newest three histories. No dedicated open issue or prior aggregate finding covers this case. rf2-vuv84a is cited by the sibling-prefix test but no longer resolves in the current tracker; this repair preserves its positive protection and does not reintroduce the bare-prefix bug.

JVM: 18 failures, all in the two new JVM-visible deftests. CLJS: 36 failures, all in the three new deftests, with the ordinary-URL control rows green.

1. Raw navigate URL normalisation (rf2-fzbj.12 finding 1 = rf2-gwye.26). `navigate.cljc` now runs `rf.routing.url/request-url->app-url` once, after the external-URL refusal. 3. Base root followed by ? or # (rf2-gwye.29). `strip-base-path` now accepts `?` and `#` as post-base boundaries, alongside end-of-string and `/`. So /app?tab=all strips to /?tab=all and /app#section to /#section. Sibling rejection and the blank-base no-op are unchanged. The fix is in the one shared ingress rule, so the initial sync and the listener both get it. Spec 012 gained two sentences: the URL-string escape hatch resolves to the browser's location before matching, and a terminal splat slash emits as %2F.

title: Story: retain loader teardown owned by the active run across hot reload
description:
Retain loader cleanup with the run that opened its resources. Registered Story teardown currently reads the latest registry body, so editing/hot-reloading a mounted variant changes which cleanup runs for the already-active fixture. The original cleanup can be lost and a replacement cleanup invoked before its matching setup ever ran.

Surface and revision
- Ownership: tools_story, tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc and registered runtime lifecycle, under rf2-gwye.
- Reviewed source: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261, 2026-09-13. Owned paths unchanged from review baseline at verification.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Independently actionable split of rf2-fzbj.3 finding 2, freshly reproduced on destroy AND in-place rerun. No source edit is part of this review.

Source evidence
- frames.cljc:1015-1018: run-teardown-walks! calls registrar/handler-meta at teardown time and dispatches its current :loaders-teardown.
- frames.cljc:1020-1035 has the adjacent correct ownership precedent: allocation-time decorator stacks are captured and later consumed, explicitly to survive hot reload. The capture is written at :824.
- frames.cljc:1069 and :1117 use the same teardown walk for destruction and in-place reset; runtime.cljc:772-800 invokes reset before reallocation on a new run.
- tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md:518-545 specifies loaders-teardown as the symmetric cleanup of loader-owned resources, before decorator teardown.

Trigger and executed reproduction
Initialize Story with the plain-atom adapter and install-canonical-vocabulary!. Register three trivial events which append :opened-a, :closed-a, and :closed-b to an atom, then:

    (story/reg-story :story.review {})
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/reload
      {:loaders [[:review/open-a]] :loaders-teardown [[:review/close-a]]})
    @(story/run-variant :story.review/reload)
    (story/reg-variant :story.review/reload
      {:loaders [[:review/open-a]] :loaders-teardown [[:review/close-b]]})
    (story/destroy-variant! :story.review/reload)
    ;; Actual:   [:opened-a :closed-b]
    ;; Expected: [:opened-a :closed-a]

Repeat from a fresh registration but call run-variant after re-registration instead of destroy. Actual sequence is [:opened-a :closed-b :opened-a]; the reset closed B rather than the resource owned by the previous run. Replacing the cleanup with no cleanup follows the same current-registry read and would omit it entirely; that removal branch is source-confirmed, not separately executed here.

Impact and independence
Ordinary source editing while a story is mounted can leak the old socket, timer or subscription, or close an unrelated replacement resource. No real external resource was opened by the witness; the calls atom proves exactly which cleanup event was selected. This defect occurs on a direct variant with no extends or compose, so fixing inherited/composed loader resolution alone does not repair it.

Suggested repair
Capture the resolved :loaders-teardown belonging to the prepared/allocated registered run, alongside the existing decorator capture. Consume the old capture before reset overwrites it, then stash the next run's cleanup; evict it on destruction. Preserve loader-before-decorator ordering and current exception reporting/continue behavior. Reuse the existing normalized plan and lifetime boundary; a newly edited registry entry must not retroactively own a prior run's cleanup. No new public lifecycle API is necessary.

Acceptance
- Start cleanup A, re-register with cleanup B, then destroy: A runs exactly once and B does not.
- Repeat using in-place rerun: A runs once before the new setup; destroying the new run subsequently invokes B once.
- Re-register with cleanup removed: A still runs. Repeat with an inherited/fragment-supplied cleanup after the resolved-loader fix.
- Confirm cleanup order, no double teardown and no retained capture after destruction. In-process event call records are sufficient; real sockets/timers are unnecessary.

Validation and limits
Actual current-source JVM probe ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_story/probe-tools-story-1.clj reproduced both destroy and rerun sequences with assert checks, using cached Clojure 1.12.4/Malli 0.20.1 and plain-atom adapter. Resource URLs were printed and asserted to belong to the intended absolute tools/story/src; run derefs bounded to 10 seconds. Frame cleanup and shutdown-agents completed. Its own exit 0 is recorded in probe-tools_story-1.exit and log and means the counterexamples reproduced. No production edits, builds, dependency installs, persistent processes, external resources or browser tests. Real hot-module reload is represented by public re-registration; browser lifecycle timing was not exercised.

Deduplication and references
Read aggregate rf2-fzbj.3 including notes/status and newest three history entries. A current full issue-list scan and targeted Story/loader/cleanup searches found no dedicated nonclosed issue for this ownership failure; the aggregate is preserved. rf2-soie and rf2-5zgx are the separate completed exception-collector/bracket refactors and are not reopened. Source comments cite rf2-x76af2.19 for the existing decorator-capture rationale; that comment is corroborating implementation history, not proof of a current tracker owner. This issue deliberately addresses one resource-lifetime defect independently of the missing inherited-loader finding.

title: surface-review(reagent): activate direct derived listeners and repair async Form-3 ownership
description:
Recommendation: repair the stock Reagent adapter's direct derived-container observation path, and correct the asynchronous resource ownership in its Form-3 README recipe. Two confirmed P2 findings remain. The first has a shared ratom-spine cause; coordinate its implementation with reagent-slim rather than introducing a second subscription algorithm. Keep this review bead OPEN until both repairs are verified.

Scope and revision
- Assigned slice: adapter_reagent; exactly the tracked paths under implementation/adapters/reagent/** in ai/surface-review-20260912/partition.json.
- Owned production/documentation paths relevant to remediation: implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs; implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md; focused tests under implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/**. The common-helper fix for F1 also needs implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, explicitly outside this slice but the actual cause of the shipped adapter behavior.
- Reviewed source baseline: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. Observed shared HEAD: 5b89378c457e9997d7eff69b7dec56eec4e5307c. The root confirmed the intervening commit only changes .beads/issues.jsonl; a direct git diff of the adapter, relevant spine, and Spec 006 returned exit 0 (no differences).
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). No production edits, build output, installs, server startup, commits or pushes by this reviewer. Root owns the durable checkpoint/push.

Coverage and deliberate differences
Inspected the complete stock adapter namespace and its dependency/package declarations; traced guarded Reaction construction, source capture/activation, disposal dispatch, root create/render/hydrate/unmount wiring, client-root reuse, emitter wiring, and synchronous flush/after-render delegation into the shared ratom spine. Read the relevant Spec 006 observer, derived-value and disposal contracts and the pinned Reagent 2.0.1 ratom/batching/core implementations from the local Maven jar. Inspected focused tests for exactly-once disposal, rendering/root argument order, after-render deferral and copied-map routing, derived arities, synchronous DOM flush, and diamond recomputation; read the adapter smoke testbed and its browser assertion. Read the complete Form-3 README recipe and lifecycle guidance.

The native Reagent batching path is intentional: no eager :auto-run true and no React-hook epoch scheduler should be added to construction. Reagent's r/after-render is its own batching queue, not UIx's driver-root sentinel. Existing stock-adapter guard and teardown-drain fixes are present; this review does not re-file their old failures. The examples/testbed regression corpus was inventoried, not executed in full. No broad CLJS, browser, advanced-optimization, Maven publish, or real Vega integration gate was run, and no such green is claimed.

F1 — P2 confirmed: subscribe-container silently observes nothing on a fresh derived Reagent container
Source:
- implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:64-70 and 89-110: guarded stock Reaction construction is injected into make-ratom-spine; the guard adds disposal bookkeeping, never source capture.
- Same file:195 and 234-238: ratom/run activation exists, but is injected only into the adapter hook assembly, not the direct subscribe-container closure.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:510-518: make-subscribe-container merely add-watch/remove-watch.
- Same file:4049-4055: the ratom adapter exposes that helper beside its lazy make-derived-value.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:692-704 delegates subscribe-container without an activation step.

Contract: spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:189 says subscribe-container works on a derived container as on a base container; lines 199-201 explain why watchability alone is insufficient and require activation when the observer attaches. The separate activation hook fixes ViewCell consumers that call it; it does not make this adapter-owned listener entry point conformant by itself.

Trigger/reproducer, using the adapter slots outside a component/render context:
1. Create source s with value 1 and derived d with compute #(* 10 %).
2. read-container d returns 10. subscribe-container d records [old new] notifications.
3. replace-container! s with 2, then reagent.core/flush.
Expected: the observer receives [10 20] after the ratom flush. Actual: zero notifications; the derived compute has still run only once and d.watching remains nil. The last outward add-watch does not itself activate a stock Reaction.
4. Control: activate that same d through ratom/run, then change s to 3 and flush. Now [20 30] is delivered. The control proves the source, watch and flush are live; this is missing source capture, not a scheduling delay.
5. Cancel the listener and change s again. The control reports no further event and watching=nil.

Impact: tools or custom substrate consumers using the documented container listener API paint an initial value and then remain stale forever unless an unrelated Reagent render or explicit activation happens to capture the same node. Ordinary component-owned subscriptions already provide capture, which explains why the extensive mounted-view/diamond tests do not expose this direct-contract hole.

Repair recommendation: give the ratom subscribe-container path the same total, idempotent activation operation already supplied by the adapter; invoke it before installing the first observation watch/baseline. Factor the stock activation lambda so direct listener registration and the routed hook cannot diverge. The common helper may accept an injected activation operation with a no-op for eager/plain containers, or make-ratom-spine may wrap its observer registration; keep reagent namespaces out of the shared spine. Coordinate the same shared attachment path with reagent-slim. Do not activate at make-derived-value construction and do not set :auto-run true.

Acceptance:
- A focused test runs the actual current stock adapter :make-state-container/:make-derived-value/:subscribe-container/:replace-container! slots, with no component, ratom context, track!, or manual activate-derived-value! in the test body; source mutation plus the normal flush delivers the expected old/new pair.
- Cover a baseline read before attach and no baseline read before attach; multiple observers over the same live derived node must not force repeated activation recomputes, and removing one observer must leave the other working.
- Base-container listeners remain functional, cancellation is idempotent, final-detach cleanup releases the source watch, and multi-input derived changes retain native batching.
- A mutation/control that bypasses attachment activation makes the direct derived notification assertion fail. Run the focused stock-adapter lane, and coordinate a matching slim assertion if the common helper is changed.

F2 — P2 confirmed: the documented async Form-3 widget leaks results that settle after unmount or out of order
Source: implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:65-82, especially the unguarded promise completions at 68-69 and 75-76; the cleanup guarantee immediately below at 97.

Trigger/reproducer: let vegaEmbed return a controlled Promise. Invoke component-did-mount, then component-will-unmount before that Promise resolves; resolve it afterward with a result containing view.finalize. The unmount callback sees nil, clears vega-instance and el-ref, then the pending .then writes the newly created view back into vega-instance. Nothing can subsequently finalize it. A second ordinary trigger overlaps mount/update requests: resolve the newer request first and the older request last, then unmount. Only the older view is finalized; the newer view was overwritten without finalization.

Expected: each returned library instance is owned only while its request and mount remain current; every obsolete or post-unmount completion is finalized, and late work cannot replace the current owner. Actual controlled-Promise observations:
- completion-after-unmount: held="pending-at-unmount", finalized=[], hasElement=false;
- out-of-order completions then unmount: finalized=["older"] only, so "newer" is leaked.

Impact: copying the canonical lifecycle recipe leaks a real imperative widget on normal navigation with an in-flight initialization and during overlapping async prop updates. The code is specifically presented as the way to release library state/listeners, so teaching a recipe that only cleans up already-settled work defeats that guidance. This is a documentation/example defect, not a claim that the adapter can cancel arbitrary user Promises.

Repair recommendation: keep the recipe compact but make each async embed request carry a per-mount generation/token. Invalidate the token before teardown and before superseding a request; accept a completion only if it still owns the live mount/request, otherwise finalize its returned instance immediately. Retire the previous accepted instance exactly once. If the embed operation itself may perform late DOM writes to a shared target, serialize operations or give each request an isolated target so the example does not imply that guarding only the final assignment prevents those writes. A concise synchronous-library example with an explicit async-ownership note is also an acceptable simpler replacement.

Acceptance:
- Controlled completion after unmount finalizes the late result and leaves no retained widget.
- Two overlapping requests completed in reverse order keep only the latest live result; every superseded result is finalized once, and final unmount finalizes the retained result once.
- Normal mount/update/unmount still works; preserve per-mounted-instance frame capture and state ownership in the surrounding recipe.
- Verify the executable lifecycle logic explicitly; a markdown link check cannot validate promise ownership.

Runtime evidence and validation limits
The bounded process-local probe is ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-adapter_reagent-1.cjs, with matching .log and .exit, all ignored paths. Run command: node C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-adapter_reagent-1.cjs. Captured exit: 0, meaning its assertions successfully reproduced both defects and the activation/cancellation controls, NOT that the adapter passes a conformance gate. The process ended normally and leaves no server or probe session running.

For F1 the probe loads only the existing compiled stock Reagent dependency prefix, not the stale cached application adapter or full test runner. Embedded source maps for reagent/ratom.cljs, reagent/impl/batching.cljs, and reagent/core.cljs were compared byte-for-byte to the locally pinned reagent-2.0.1.jar entries; all three matched. Ratoms source SHA-256: b390644704d742223b7c58c6f5f627f5210d694b263c2be95cc75d87ffe0b1b7. The current adapter construction guard and current make-subscribe-container watch lifecycle are expressed faithfully in JS in the process-local probe; current source wiring was inspected separately. This is a real pinned-Reagent mechanism witness, not a freshly compiled end-to-end adapter test. Such a test is an acceptance requirement for the repair.

For F2 the probe expresses the README handlers' ownership algorithm in JS with controlled Promises. It executes the relevant asynchronous ownership sequence but does not mount React or load Vega, and makes no claim about Vega's internal DOM scheduling. The source defect is the unconditional completion assignment with no remaining owner after unmount; the broader late-DOM-write risk is unverified and must not be counted as a third confirmed finding.

Known history / duplicate check
- rf2-rzeko is CLOSED: its PR #8831 guard addresses double/re-entrant disposal. Its current source and newest history retain that disposition; F1 is missing observer activation, not the old double-disposal report. General throwing-on-dispose callback isolation was explicitly a non-goal of that bead and is not expanded here.
- rf2-ss8x is CLOSED: shared teardown drains now retain and rethrow failures; its final history also distinguishes the subsequently repaired UIx driver-root remnant from the stock ratom path. Neither old defect is re-filed.
- rf2-k5r9t is CLOSED and owns the reusable client-root API, not these findings.
- Source references rf2-8cnxg / rf2-jt8vz identify the existing activation mechanism, but direct bd show returned no surviving records for those IDs. The remembered entry substrate-fix-in-one-consumer-must-sweep-all-consumers explicitly records the same substrate trap occurring in another observer consumer; it supports looking for missed attachment paths, not claiming an extant duplicate.
- Searches across all statuses for subscribe-container, make-subscribe-container, activate-derived-value!, vegaEmbed and Vega found no bead owning these exact repairs. The returned rf2-k97c/.1/.2 records are the closed Xray substrate spike/decision, not this direct adapter observer contract or README recipe.
- The reagent-slim reviewer has been notified of the shared F1 helper and will cross-reference this bead rather than duplicate its remediation.

title: surface-review(examples-core): bound Cells evaluation and preserve Timer elapsed on duration changes
description:
Fix the Cells evaluator's repeated-subtree explosion and preserve Timer elapsed time when the duration is shortened. These are two confirmed P2 defects in ordinary, valid example interactions. Keep the existing examples small: no new framework API, no per-example browser suite, and no reversal of the test-free-examples policy.

Review identity

- Slice: examples_core; all 40 assigned tracked paths under examples/core/** are listed below.
- Revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f (HEAD verified; git diff against that revision for examples/core was empty after probing).
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review)
- Parent: rf2-fzbj; independent surface review, 2026-09-12 wave, performed 2026-09-13.
- Production source stayed unchanged. Root owns durable tracker checkpoint and push.

Finding 1 — P2: a short valid Cells dependency chain expands exponentially

Source: examples/core/seven_guis/cells/core.cljs:270-325, especially :285 (eager recursive evaluation of every argument), :280-281 (each cell reference directly calls evaluate-cell), and :319-324 (no completed-value cache). The public subscription at :383-393 starts a fresh evaluation for each displayed cell. The teaching claim that the small grid makes this cheap is at :15-20 and examples/core/seven_guis/README.md:32.

Trigger/reproducer: enter 1 in A1; in A2 enter =(+ A1 A1), in A3 enter =(+ A2 A2), and continue through A21. All references are in the supported A1..Z100 range; each formula is a routine addition. Change A1. No cycle, unusually long formula, malformed input, or large sheet is involved.

Expected: evaluate each distinct dependency once within an evaluation of the current immutable cell map, then reuse its settled value. The result for A21 is 1048576, with work bounded by the small dependency graph. The intentionally broad all-cells subscription may remain; it does not require repeated evaluation of an already-computed subtree.

Actual: the evaluator walks the same dependency twice at every level. For the one A21 result, evaluate-cell executes 2,097,151 times. Source-extracted process-local measurements were:

- 9 cells: 511 calls, value 256.
- 13 cells: 8,191 calls, value 4,096.
- 17 cells: 131,071 calls, value 65,536.
- 21 cells: 2,097,151 calls, value 1,048,576.
- Control: the same 21-cell depth with each formula adding one reference and literal 1 requires exactly 21 calls and yields 21.

The recurrence is T(n)=2*T(n-1)+1. All mounted cell value subscriptions run their own walks; the measurements above count only the final cell. Equality-based subscription deduplication occurs after this computation, so it cannot remove the duplicate recursion. A 31-cell version entails over two billion visits for one result by the same recurrence; that larger case was not executed.

Impact: an ordinary small sheet can monopolize the UI thread, preventing editing and correction, and the example teaches that final-value deduplication makes this evaluation strategy cheap. The measured 21-cell run took approximately 1.43 seconds in an instrumented Babashka process; that is not claimed as a browser benchmark. The portable evidence is the exact operation count and the source path that produces it.

Repair: keep the parser, sparse app-db, typed error values, and path-local cycle guard. Introduce a bounded completed-value cache scoped to one immutable cells snapshot/evaluation. A single pure derived value table for that snapshot is a straightforward option; an internal per-root memoized evaluator also removes the exponential defect. Distinguish currently visiting cells from completed cells so memoization does not replace cycle detection. Do not introduce a process-global cache keyed only by cell id, a second reactive framework, or an input-size cap that rejects valid formulas. Update the two teaching passages to describe the actual bounded evaluation rule.

Acceptance:

1. The 21-cell duplicate-reference chain returns 1048576 without exponentially expanding dependency evaluations; an operation-count regression must distinguish the old evaluator from the repair. Use deterministic work counts, not a fragile wall-clock timeout.
2. Changing A1 recomputes dependent results from the new snapshot; old snapshot results cannot leak through a global cache.
3. The equal-depth single-reference control remains correct. Existing two-cell/self-cycle, parse-error propagation, arithmetic, and empty-cell semantics remain correct.
4. Add the focused regression alongside the existing implementation/core/test/re_frame/seven_guis_cells_parser_cljs_test.cljs coverage, not beneath examples/.

Finding 2 — P2: shortening a running Timer rewinds elapsed and permits an incorrect restart

Source: examples/core/seven_guis/timer/core.cljs:132-152, especially :143 `(min (+ elapsed-ms observed) duration-ms)`; duration changes at :163-183 preserve elapsed but leave the pending generation accepted; restart eligibility at :166-170 then uses the rewound value.

This is distinct from intentionally clamping a FORWARD tick at the original deadline. The user already has 5000 ms of elapsed time before reducing the target to 1000 ms. The official 7GUIs Timer contract says e >= d stops the timer, increasing d restarts only if d > e, and Reset zeroes elapsed: https://eugenkiss.github.io/7guis/tasks/#timer (read during this review). The local namespace rules at :20-24 describe shrinking the target as making the bar full and reserve zeroing elapsed for Reset. The existing stopped-timer path also preserves elapsed when the slider is reduced.

Deterministic reproducer, times supplied as the existing recordable :rf/time-ms coeffect:

1. At t=0 dispatch [:timer/initialise], yielding elapsed 0, duration 10000, generation 0.
2. At t=5000 dispatch [:timer/tick 0], yielding elapsed 5000.
3. At t=5050 dispatch [:timer/set-duration 1000]. The bar is full and elapsed still reads 5000; the previously scheduled tick remains pending.
4. At t=5100 that [:timer/tick 0] arrives. Actual elapsed becomes 1000 and the chain stops.
5. At t=5200 dispatch [:timer/set-duration 3000]. Actual generation becomes 1 and a new tick is scheduled because 3000 > the rewound 1000.

Expected: shortening duration leaves elapsed at 5000 and stops progress. The already-pending tick must not move it backwards. Raising duration to 3000 remains stopped because 3000 < 5000. Raising it above 5000 may re-arm once with a new time baseline. Reset continues to zero elapsed.

Control: completing the 10000 ms timer first and then reducing duration to 1000 preserves elapsed at 10000, because no tick remains to execute the min. Thus the visible duration-edit semantics currently depend on whether a callback is still pending.

Impact: the elapsed label loses already-measured time, and subsequent slider movement resumes a timer that should remain complete. This is the competing slider/tick interaction that this canonical example is intended to explain.

Repair: make an accepted tick with elapsed-ms >= duration-ms preserve elapsed and stop scheduling, rather than running the downward min clamp. Keep the observed-time accounting, generation guard, and fresh re-arm baseline. A small explicit stop transition in set-duration is also valid if it preserves the same invariant. Do not turn this into a general timer abstraction or change the intentional forward-deadline clamp.

Acceptance:

1. The exact 0/5000/5050/5100 sequence above leaves elapsed 5000 after the pending tick, with no follow-up schedule.
2. Raising duration to 3000 keeps it stopped; raising above 5000 re-arms exactly one generation and measures from the re-arm event.
3. Mid-run and already-stopped duration reductions obey the same elapsed-preservation rule.
