title: surface-review(pair-mcp): preserve EDN query, path, signal and coeffect arguments as data
description:
Extend the existing literal-data emitter (`ef/rt-quote`) to the remaining query, path, signal, and scripted-coeffect arguments. One confirmed P2 correctness defect remains: several EDN inputs advertised as data are still printed into executable CLJS expressions. They can therefore address a different subscription/path, alter replay facts, or execute a nested list before the intended runtime operation. This requires a focused completion of the existing quoting repair, preserving full EDN expressiveness and the intentional internal source-composition API.

## Ownership, revision, and verdict

Owned slice: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/**` (source, tests, tool descriptor manifest/generator, package metadata, README, and spec). Reviewed revision: `1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f`; HEAD and tracked working-tree cleanliness were rechecked before filing. Parent: `rf2-fzbj`. Reviewer: `review_tools_pair_mcp`.

SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review)

Verdict: OPEN for remediation. Finding count: one confirmed P2 defect with six directly probed manifestations; the dispatch-dry-run cofx sibling is additionally confirmed by its identical source path, without a separate runtime execution. No production edits, builds, servers, dependency installs, commits, or pushes were performed by this reviewer. The coordinator owns tracker checkpoint/push.

## Coverage and exclusions

Inspected the server's lazy discovery, endpoint replacement and single-flight connection state, pre-dispatch refusals, handler-error conversion, stdin shutdown wiring, nREPL generation ownership/op settlement/eval unwrapping, and relevant existing lifecycle tests. Followed the tools dispatcher, registry, build selection, post-eval cache/cap ordering, cursor ownership, wire projection and result-envelope contracts. Examined the data argument parsers and actual emitted forms for dispatch, dispatch-dry-run, replace-app-db, read-sub, get-path, record, watch-until, and snapshot; sampled their tests and the emitter tests. Checked package.json, deps.edn, shadow-cljs.edn, installation prose, and documented unit/live test boundaries.

This was a focused review of those execution paths, not an assertion that every test or every tool implementation was exhaustively audited. Excluded implementation of the browser preload (skills/re-frame2-pair), shared mcp-base primitives, and the separate mcp-conformance/live fixture infrastructure except for contract/call-site context. No claim of CLJS compilation, browser execution, live nREPL behavior, npm packaging execution, or a passing module suite is made. Existing local compiled outputs predate this revision and were not used as evidence.

A considered cache-reconnect concern was not filed: current precheck-target returns nil for every tool, so this revision always evaluates before the result-hash cache decision; the historical cheap app-db-only precheck is not active. Existing frame ambiguity, cursor frame ownership, withheld-overflow cache entries, and quoted event/db repairs were inspected as current behavior, not re-reported as new defects.

## F1 — P2: data-only arguments remain executable in generated forms

Source locations (all relative to the owned slice):

- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/read_sub.cljs:51-91` accepts an arbitrary EDN vector; `:106-110` passes query-v directly to rt-call. An ordinary nested list is then evaluated as source.
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_path.cljs:98-105` binds an unquoted caller path; `:140-147` prints the plural paths collection directly into reduce. Both can read a different key from the requested one.
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/watch_until.cljs:81-88` passes parsed signals directly to sample-signals; `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/record.cljs:81-119` accepts EDN signal data and `:252-260` prints it directly into the start-recording! opts expression.
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch.cljs:467-496` quotes the event but puts parsed cofx into an unquoted opts-form; `:569` emits that map as an ordinary runtime-call argument. `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch_dry_run.cljs:323-334,361` does the same for simulated dispatch. The cofx contract explicitly says EDN data, not host source, in `spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:1097-1103`; owner-qualified fact values are otherwise preserved verbatim by the published contract.
- Shared emission behavior: `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/eval_form.cljs:135-161,219-238`. Bare data goes through pr-str (or tagged-node recognition), whereas rt-quote emits a literal datum without walking it as emitter instructions. The correct primitive already exists.

### Trigger and expected versus actual

A subscription accepting an EDN expression as a query parameter, a map keyed by an EDN list/symbol, or a scripted recordable fact containing such data is sufficient. These are legal values; no malformed request is needed.

Observed actual-source witnesses, with expected inputs on the left:

1. read-sub query `[:review/sub (inc 41)]` -> runtime-call argument `[:review/sub 42]`. Expected the second element to remain the list `(inc 41)`.
2. dispatch cofx `{:review/fact (inc 41)}` -> runtime opts `{:rf.cofx {:review/fact 42}}`. Expected the recorded fact to remain the original EDN value.
3. get-path `[(inc 41)]` against a mock db containing `{(list 'inc 41) :list-key, 42 :numeric-key}` -> `{:ok? true :path [42] :value :numeric-key ...}`. Expected `:list-key` and the original path.
4. get-path plural paths `[[(inc 41)]]` against the same db -> `:results {[42] {:exists? true :value :numeric-key}}`, again a successful answer about the wrong path.
5. watch-until signals `[{:sub [:review/sub (inc 41)]}]` -> sample-signals receives `[{:sub [:review/sub 42]}]`.
6. record with the same signals -> start-recording! receives `[{:sub [:review/sub 42]}]`.

Representative emitted source from the unchanged code:

`(re-frame2-pair.runtime/read-sub! [:review/sub (inc 41)])`

`(re-frame2-pair.runtime/dispatch-consequence! (quote [:review/event]) {:rf.cofx #:review{:fact (inc 41)}})`

Both expressions evaluate the nested list while preparing the runtime arguments. Symbols similarly resolve as program names instead of remaining symbolic data; the emitter's tagged-vector protocol makes some query-shaped vectors another source-splicing path. The ordinary `[:review/sub {:user/id 42}]` control preserves its value, and wrapping the list-bearing query with the existing rt-quote preserves it too.

Impact: read-only tools can observe the wrong target or perform effects while constructing a supposed data argument; dispatch/replay can use different causal facts from the caller's script. This is an argument-fidelity defect, not a request to sandbox programmer handlers or make dispatch read-only. A nested list can execute independently of the eval-cljs tool gate because it is embedded in a different tool's generated form.

### Validation and reproducibility

Executed an ignored, process-local Babashka probe against the unchanged source: `ai/surface-review-20260912/pair-mcp-data-arguments-review_tools_pair_mcp-3.clj`, invoked by its absolute path with `bb`. Exit 0. It loads actual eval_form.cljs; reads and evaluates the actual read-sub-form, single-path-form, batch-paths-form, watch-form, and start-recording-form definitions from their source files; and installs in-process mock runtime functions that report received arguments. It actually evaluates the emitted expressions rather than merely reading their syntax. The dispatch cofx witness uses the actual emitter with exactly the opts construction traced above. All six observed failures and both positive controls are asserted in the probe.

The BB witness exercises the common Clojure/CLJS expression semantics, not a CLJS compiler or browser. For get-path only, its reader maps the generated `#js {}` missing sentinel to a process-local ordinary map; the observed payloads are keywords, and the differing key chosen is independent of this sentinel representation. No generated browser-side mutation or real application handler was run. An initial attempt to send stdin via `bb -` failed because that bb invocation treats '-' as a filename; the corrected inline probe and then the saved actual-source probe both exited 0. No broad gate was run and no suite-green inference is made from these probes.

### Precise repair and acceptance

Quote complete data-valued query/path/signal collections and complete data-only dispatch opts maps at the point they cross into generated code. For record's intentionally mixed map, quote the :signals value while retaining the internally synthesized :pred-fn as source. Use rt-quote or its emitted equivalent consistently; do not globally quote internal emitter IR, ban symbols/lists, or add a generic validation/sandbox framework. Audit the neighboring parsed-data slots touched by the same composition functions, including parameterized interceptor override values, for the same distinction.

Acceptance: through real compiled tool/runtime calls, read-sub, singular/plural get-path, record/watch-until, and dispatch/dispatch-dry-run cofx preserve list and symbol values and emitter-tag-shaped data. Assert the receiving query/path/options, or handler-observed facts, equal the supplied datum; verify an inert marker expression is not evaluated. Include at least one data-only read or dry-run call with eval-cljs disabled, ordinary scalar/map controls, and an internal rt-raw control. Keep existing event and replace-app-db quoted-data cases green. Do not substitute source-string substring tests or read-back delimiter assertions for evaluated argument identity. Run the package's canonical npm test and applicable existing live/conformance lane from an isolated worktree when repairing.

## Existing issues and remaining uncertainty

Read current records/history for rf2-j2wz (closed: parsed event EDN quoting) and rf2-olqo (closed: replace-app-db quoting, including the corrected live witness). Their repairs remain present; this finding concerns different argument slots they did not repair. In particular, the previously documented list-to-vector normalization on egress is irrelevant here: the probe observes the arguments BEFORE any real runtime read or egress walk. Searched active and closed titles/descriptions for pair, cofx, read-sub, literal, and quotation; no existing owner for these remaining slots was found. Related known context inspected: rf2-gov3 (withheld-cap cache identity), rf2-q17a/rf2-yo4s (frame ambiguity/cursor ownership), and rf2-q774o (CWD port-file restart tracking).

No separate unverified risk is promoted to an actionable finding. Broader transport timing, cancellation behavior, packed-artefact execution, and unexamined per-tool edge cases remain outside the direct validation performed here.

title: False per-row isolation claim: Static Flows and Schemas inspector IDs omit the owning frame
description:
Merged-PR audit #9622 (21dfeb08fde333ef5e1032068264908765e5fc4d), correctness/completeness. The migration claims every inspector mount has its own identity, but the two row helpers omit the row's owning frame from edn/inspect-view node keys. With the documented nil observed-frame / browse-all projection, register :shared/flow in :app/a and :app/b, or an app-db schema at [:shared] in both frames. The catalogue produces two separately keyed rows inside the SAME :rf/xray render frame.

Flows panel.cljs:205,238-245 builds static-flows/<flow-id>/input/<index> and .../output; schemas panel.cljs:230-231,279 builds static-schemas/<kind>-<id>. Neither includes :frame, although each catalogue row key already does. edn_widget.cljs:139-143 turns these node keys into identical :mount-id and :panel-id values. The old edn/inspect head allocated a UUID per live mount; the new Fresco head instead trusts the explicit mount ID. edn_inspector.cljs:4253-4267 qualifies lifecycle identity with the RENDER frame, so both rows still share [:rf/xray mount-id]. Its memoized container-ref-for consequently shares one observer/ref entry, and detaching either row calls release-mount! for the surviving row too; expansion/width identity is shared as well. This is a caller identity defect, distinct from the already repaired cross-render-frame store key.

Evidence: independently evaluated the exact landed flow-row, schema-row, inspect-opts and inspect-view forms with Babashka, stubbing only presentation helpers. Two same-flow-ID/different-frame rows emitted 4 inspector forms but only 2 mount IDs; two same-schema-path/different-frame rows emitted 2 forms but only 1 mount ID. Distinct-ID controls emitted 4/4 and 2/2. This was a pure projection probe, not a DOM run; lifecycle consequences were traced in the shipped store code. New unit tests assert uniqueness only on single-frame/different-ID fixtures, and browser W5 removes differently named rows from one frame, so neither fixture exercises this supported case. CI otherwise passes on matching landed file blobs.

Keep the correction local: derive each inspector qualifier from the existing frame-inclusive row identity plus the input/output site. No new public API or general identity framework is needed.
acceptance_criteria: For both migrated panels, same-ID rows belonging to two different app frames render simultaneously under one Xray frame with distinct stable inspector mount IDs (and therefore distinct lifecycle/interaction state); ordinary rerenders preserve each row's identity. Add a bounded regression using two frames with the same flow ID and the same app-db schema path. Show that removing one row leaves the other's inspector state/observer alive and that expand/collapse does not affect the other row. Preserve the existing per-row key/removal witnesses and current public panel API.

title: fresco: a click inside an animating hosted ViewTransition lands on the DOM but writes nothing to app-db
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 by the rf2-6plj worker while witnessing a hosted `<ViewTransition>` around Fresco
children. It is the finding that BLOCKED the recipe that bead was conditionally going to publish, so read
rf2-6plj's close reason for the surrounding work before starting here.

THE DEFECT. A click inside a subtree that a hosted `<ViewTransition>` is animating LANDS ON THE DOM and
produces NO app-db write. Not late, not queued, not replayed — absent. And silent on every console channel.

FOUR READINGS FROM ONE ROW, which is what makes this a finding rather than a suspicion:
    the same click on a quiet document              -> app-db write in ~1 ms
    a native listener on the same node mid-animation -> FIRES (so the click really landed)
    a direct dispatch during the same live animation -> ~6 ms
    the intent's own write during that animation     -> ABSENT at 3 s, still absent after the animation settles

THE MECHANISM IS DELIBERATELY NOT ESTABLISHED, and four candidate causes are RULED OUT by their own controls
rather than by argument:
  * the browser — a native listener fires 4/4 during a live transition;
  * React's event delivery — `onClick` fires 4/4;
  * task scheduling — setTimeout, MessageChannel, microtask and rAF all resolve within a few ms;
  * the router.
So the write is being lost somewhere between a delivered event and app-db, under an active view transition,
and naming that place is the first job here.

WHY IT MATTERS: a UI that silently drops user intent during an animation is a correctness defect, not a
polish one, and it is invisible — no error, no warning, no console output. Anyone who adopts a hosted
`<ViewTransition>` around interactive Fresco children meets it and has nothing to go on.

A WRONG EXPLANATION WAS DRAFTED AND WITHDRAWN, and it is recorded here so nobody re-derives it: an earlier
draft claimed the intent CANCELS the transition, citing React's flushSync warning. That was FALSE — the
warning came from the row's own teardown, and the captured `console.warn` list is EMPTY at the moment of the
claim. Do not restate it.

A GOTCHA THAT WILL COST YOU A RUN IF YOU MEET IT COLD, measured twice each way: REACT'S ViewTransition
CALLBACKS ARE VIEWPORT-GATED. Below the fold, `onUpdate` never fires and far fewer animations run, while the
transition still starts and the DOM still commits. The witness lane mounts at the bottom of a long report,
which is why that worker's first run read a live mechanism as dead. Scroll the subject into view, or assert
the premise before the claim.

WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED AND MUST NOT BE REOPENED HERE: the CEILING. Ordinary dispatch activates no
transition; dispatch inside `startTransition` activates none; and `dispatch-sync` inside `startTransition`
also activates none — that third reading takes the router's queueing out of the argument entirely, which is
why it survives any future router work. All three read through the same instrument as a plain `useState`
transition under the same host, which DOES activate. That is the ceiling confirmed, not contradicted.

FIRST STEPS: reproduce the four readings above before changing anything, and keep the native-listener row as
the control that the click landed. Then instrument the path from the delivered React event to the app-db
write and find where it stops.

OUT OF SCOPE: any core wrapper, hiccup head, motion helper or `addTransitionType` work; the lane doc's
ceiling section; and publishing a `<ViewTransition>` recipe, which rf2-6plj correctly declined to do on
exactly this finding.

The observed click loss remains an investigation; its mechanism is not established by this audit. See rf2-hk8c for the focused witness correction. Existing criteria, notes, status and closure records are preserved.

close_reason:
CLOSED ON PR #9594, merged as f44bcaf43d. **THE MECHANISM IS NAMED, IT IS REACT'S, AND NOTHING IS FILED
AGAINST OUR CODE.** That was one of the three outcomes the dispatch declared acceptable, and it arrived with
controls rather than an argument.

=== THE MECHANISM ===

**IT IS REACT'S SUSPENDED COMMIT, NOT THE ANIMATION.** React gates its entire synthetic event system on one
module-level flag in `react-dom-client`: `commitBeforeMutationEffects` clears it, and only the mutation phase
restores it at the end of `flushMutationEffects`. Ordinarily those two sit microseconds apart inside one
task. Under a view transition, `flushMutationEffects` IS the `update` callback React hands to
`document.startViewTransition`, which the browser invokes only after capturing the old snapshot — so the flag
stays cleared across an ASYNCHRONOUS GAP, and `dispatchEvent`'s `if (_enabled)` discards everything delivered
in it. Not queued, not replayed, silent on every console channel.

=== THE CONTROL THAT MAKES IT UNARGUABLE ===

Two PLAIN React `<button onClick>` elements — one INSIDE the animating subtree, one OUTSIDE it in the same
root — are BOTH dropped in the window, while a native listener on the same node fires. Neither touches
Fresco, the collector or the router.

Two things follow, and the second corrects the bead's own framing: the loss is upstream of everything this
project owns, and **THE ANIMATING SUBTREE IS NOT THE BOUNDARY.** Any React event anywhere in that root is
discarded while the commit is suspended.

    :in-window     {:closed nil, :native 1, :inside 0, :outside 0}
    :after-window  {:before 1, :ms 0, :anims 8, :window-ms 32, :direct-ms 11}

The window measured 32 ms — about two frames. The identical clicks made after the `update` callback ran, with
EIGHT view-transition animations still running, all arrive. Determinism came from firing the clicks in a
microtask queued the instant `startViewTransition` is called: a microtask cannot be overtaken by the
browser's `update` callback.

=== THE MAYOR'S MID-FLIGHT CORRECTION WAS DISCHARGED, AND IT WENT THE OTHER WAY ===

I messaged this worker that one of the four eliminations I had briefed — a direct dispatch "during the same
live animation" — was unsupported, because the #9587 witness waited out a 3-second window against 240 ms
animations and never asserted the phase. The complaint was right; the conclusion survived anyway. Re-measured
with the phase taken at BOTH ends: a direct `rf/dispatch` from inside the suspended commit reached app-db in
1 ms with EMPTY `console.warn`/`console.error` for the window, and one with eight animations running at
dispatch and eight still running at arrival reached it in 11 ms.

**SO THE WINDOW STOPS REACT'S EVENT DELIVERY, NOT AN APP-DB WRITE** — the pair the original ~6 ms reading
could not separate. Those corrected timings are recorded on rf2-hk8c, which owns the witness repair.

=== WHAT LANDED, AND WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT ===

Two files: the browser-lane witness (+408/-14) and the fresco lane doc (+7/-1). The doc edit NARROWS the
previous warning rather than replacing it, and says so — including that the isolated-page `onClick` rule-out
holds only OUTSIDE the window. Verified by the mayor as a single hunk: the CEILING section the brief fenced
was not touched, and no `<ViewTransition>` recipe was published, per rf2-6plj's standing refusal.

The consumer guidance the doc now carries is the useful residue: the exposure is one to two frames at the
START of a transition rather than its whole length, it is not confined to the animating subtree, and React
DISCARDS the event rather than queueing it — so an interaction whose loss matters wants a native listener on
the node, or no view transition over it.

=== A GATE HAZARD FOUND IN PASSING, AND IT IS FILED ===

   nuisance.
3. NPM. Is `fresco` taken? (There is an old `fresco` package; confirm its state.) Does
   re-frame2 publish any npm package under this name — check implementation/package.json.
4. GITHUB. Is there a prominent `fresco` repo in the Clojure/ClojureScript space?
5. CLOJURE ECOSYSTEM SPECIFICALLY. Anything named Fresco on Clojars, in the Clojurians

   art term used by another company in a different product category is a much weaker problem
   than a one-letter miss on a personal name, which is the thing being fixed — but say so on

STEP 1. If `io.github.day8/re-frame2-fresco` is TAKEN on Clojars, or a Clojure/CLJS view

  classes by a party who would plausibly object to a CLJS library — CHOOSE ALTERNATE. The

STEP 3. Else if the only findings are (a) `com.facebook.fresco` under its own group and/or

silently. Close this bead with the evidence, set the epic to blocked, and surface it to Mike
with the finding plus at most three alternates that pass steps 1-3 — the runners-up already

the ONLY escalation path in this epic.

Each of the six checks with what you actually found and where you looked, which step fired,

child .2 reads this bead as its go signal and must not have to infer it.

   housewares, not software** — the class 009 entry was a kitchen thermometer and it is deleted.

   76035164 abandoned 2001-06-06. A live FRESCO DATA (registration 4495784, frescodata llc) is a

 * **CONCLUSION ON STEP 2: no party holds bare "FRESCO" in software or developer-tools classes.**
   Adobe holds ADOBE FRESCO for a consumer painting app. That is, on the evidence, exactly what
   the bead anticipated and expressly said is NOT a step-2 trigger.

   being retired. "Hicasso" is documented IN OUR OWN CHARTER as a deliberate one-letter play on

title: api(resources): reg-resource-scope takes one arity with :inputs required; delete the whole-db sugar and the :doc-only variant
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from resources.md (ref resources.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`reg-resource-scope` has two arities (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc:350–399`; the 2-arity at `:381` forwards `{}` metadata), and `canonical-spec` (`:248–347`) selects the "whole-db form" whenever the metadata map lacks an `:inputs` key (`:323`) — which includes a THREE-argument call carrying only `:doc` (codex's correction: deleting the 2-arity alone leaves the exception alive). In that form ALONE the resolver's first argument is the raw db rather than the inputs map — a documented "deliberate, cost-marked exception" and "first-arg meaning-shift" (`scope_registry.cljc:55–71`; `spec/016-Resources.md:192–203`, "a marked convenience, not a peer"). The implementation immediately wraps the sugar back into the canonical shape: a synthetic `:inputs {:db [:db []]}`, a wrapper `(fn [{:keys [db]} ctx] (f db ctx))`, and an authored flag `:whole-db? true` (`:342–346`). So the sugar buys one fewer map literal at the price of the one place in the resources grammar where a positional argument changes meaning.

The corpus never reaches for it: all 3 app/testbed registrations use the 3-slot form with `:inputs` (`examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/scope.cljs:106,135`; `testbeds/tenant_switcher/core.cljs:96`). The sugar's only occurrences are 2 test lines, one ns-docstring snippet, one spec snippet, one docs/api signature line and one historical EP snippet.

A second, related teaching fault: the same `{:from-db …}` reference is repeated at use sites that already inherit it from the registration. `realworld_resources/routing.cljs:97` repeats `resources.cljs:283` on the feed route entry; `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs:163` (`board-query`) repeats the `:rf.scope/global` claim at `:133` on the sub query; Spec 016's own worked example (`:1744–1790`) writes `{:from-db :realworld/session}` three times (registration `:1756`, route entry `:1770`, subscription `:1778`) and calls that "the one scope-resolution currency" (`:1789`). The runtime already inherits: a route entry with no `:scope` returns nil from `resolve-entry-scope` (`route.cljc:507`) and `resolve-scope-for-event` tier 3a resolves the spec's `{:from-db …}` against db (`registry.cljc:846–849`); the sub side resolves the spec policy per `016:115`, and `resources.cljs:263` states "no view ever passes a `:scope` payload". The other 7 route plans and every other sub in `examples/` omit `:scope` and inherit.

Folded drift: `spec/Ownership.md:64` still names the grammar `{:inputs … :resolve …}` — the pre-rf2-td8oe 2-slot shape the runtime rejects (`:rf.error/invalid-resource-scope-spec`, `scope_registry.cljc:300–310`).

## Evidence (HEAD `6445d0611b`)

- 2-arity / whole-db sugar sites (`git grep -n -A1 -E "reg-resource-scope +:[A-Za-z0-9./-]+\s*$" … | grep -B1 "(fn \[db"`): `scope_registry.cljc:57–58` (docstring), `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_scope_registry_cljs_test.cljc:189,282`, `spec/016-Resources.md:197–198`, `docs/EP/EP-0016-resource-mutation-completion.md:641` (historical record). Facade docstrings and arglists advertise it: `core.cljc:316–325` (fn alias), `core.cljc:558–575` (`defreg-macro`, `:arglists '([scope-id metadata resolve-fn] [scope-id resolve-fn])` at `:575`), `core_resources.cljc:164–186` (`:arglists` `:182`, the 2-arity delegate `:184`). `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:224–225,230`.
- `:whole-db?` exact-keyword consumers (`git grep -n -E ":whole-db\?"`): `scope_registry.cljc` ×11 (stored spec `:340,:345`; trace `:568`; egress `:473–510`; meta `:414`); `resources/tooling.cljc` ×1; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/resources_helpers.cljc` ×5, `panels/resources.cljs` ×2; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs` ×1, `descriptors_data.cljs` ×1, `tool-descriptors.edn` ×1, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` ×1; `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs` ×2, `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md` ×2; tests: `resources_scope_registry_cljs_test.cljc` ×7, `resources_from_db_scope_cljs_test.cljc` ×2, `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_scope_test.clj` ×1, pair-mcp `handler_meta_test.cljs` ×3, xray `resources_helpers_cljs_test.cljc` ×8, `resources_cljs_test.cljs` ×2, `skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/runtime/registrar_describe_test.clj` ×1; `spec/016-Resources.md:203`; `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:287,291`.
- Redundant use-site repeats: `realworld_resources/routing.cljs:97` ↔ `resources.cljs:283`; `linearlite/core.cljs:163` ↔ `:133` (`:157` `board-key` is a mutation `:optimistic` / `:patches` map-form target — only drop its `:scope` if 016 §Map-form exact resource targets (`:994`) inherits the registration policy; verify, else leave).

## Target API

```clojure
;; ONE arity. :inputs is REQUIRED. The callback's first arg is ALWAYS the inputs map.
(rf/reg-resource-scope :realworld/session
  {:inputs {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}}
  (fn [{:keys [username]} _ctx] (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}])))

;; whole-db, spelled as what it is
(rf/reg-resource-scope :app/everything
  {:inputs {:db [:db []]}}
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _ctx] …))
```

- `reg-resource-scope [scope-id metadata resolve-fn]` only. Metadata MUST be a map carrying `:inputs` (a map). A missing `:inputs`, a non-map metadata, or the old 2-arity spelling (which lands the fn in the metadata slot) all raise the existing `:rf.error/invalid-resource-scope-spec` with a message that names the whole-db spelling `{:inputs {:db [:db []]}}`.
- `:whole-db?` STAYS on the stored spec, on `scope-resolver-meta`, in the `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` trace and the egress projection — but DERIVED, never authored: true iff some declared input descriptor is the root path `[:db []]`. Every tool consumer above is unchanged (codex: "derive whole-db tooling information from the declaration instead of maintaining a second authored mode"). Do NOT add an unpacking flag to recreate the old callback convention.
- Teaching rule (codex + fable, adopted): registration-level `:scope` is the DEFAULT; a use-site `:scope` (route entry, sub query, event payload) is an OVERRIDE for the admin-reads-tenant-X case — never a required repetition. Delete the repeats that equal the registration; keep explicit overrides as worked examples where they differ.

## Corroboration (two-reviewer)

Codex: "For named scope resolvers, retain one callback contract: the first argument is always the declared inputs map. Require `:inputs` and remove the whole-db sugar, including the doc-only metadata variant … The whole-db case remains possible and honest about what it reads. Do not add an unpacking flag." And: "Teach registration-level scope as the default and use-site scope as an override. Remove needless repeated declarations in examples when they equal the registration." Grok Thoughts: "C. Do it." `fable/README.md` lists "one `reg-resource-scope` contract" under two-reviewer findings. rf2-td8oe (closed 2026-09-02, PR #8989) already moved the skill snippet to the 3-slot form; this bead removes the exception the skill still describes in prose.

## Deletion list

- The 2-arity of `reg-resource-scope` (`scope_registry.cljc:381`); the whole-db branch of `canonical-spec` and its wrapper (`:342–346`); the ns-docstring section "Whole-db function sugar — the ONE documented explicit alternative" (`:55–71`); the sugar clause in the fn?-check message (`:317–320`).
- Facade: the 2-arity delegate and arglist in `core_resources.cljc:182–184`; `:arglists` and the sugar sentence in `core.cljc:558–575`; the fn-alias docstring `core.cljc:316–325`.
- Authored `:whole-db?` (replaced by the derived value; the key itself survives).
- `spec/016-Resources.md` §Whole-db function sugar (`:192–203`); `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:225,230`; the redundant use-site `:scope` at `routing.cljs:97` and `linearlite/core.cljs:163`.

## Consumers to migrate

title: api(registry): add 5 missing CLJS registrar aliases, pin macro/alias concordance, fix table drift
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registration-and-testing.md (ref spellings.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`re-frame.core` emits its 15 `reg-*` registration macros from ONE generator — `defreg-macro` / `defreg-event-macro` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc:250` / `:311`), table at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:442-632` — but the Convention-A same-name CLJS value aliases (`#?(:cljs (def reg-x owning/reg-x))`) are a SECOND, hand-written list (`core.cljc:262-352`). The two lists have drifted:

- Aliases exist for 10 of the 15 registrars (`reg-event` :272, `reg-sub` :276, `reg-fx` :280, `reg-cofx` :287, `reg-interceptor` :295, `reg-route` :304, `reg-resource` :315, `reg-resource-scope` :325, `reg-app-schema` :339, `reg-app-schemas` :351). **Missing: `reg-flow`, `reg-mutation`, `reg-head`, `reg-error-projector`, `reg-http-interceptor`.** So on CLJS `(map rf/reg-resource …)` compiles and `(map rf/reg-mutation …)` does not, inside one artefact.
- `spec/Conventions.md:1481-1483` (Convention A) enumerates a DIFFERENT set: it names `reg-flow` (absent in code) and omits `reg-resource` / `reg-resource-scope` (present).
- `spec/API.md` rows four macros as **Fn**: `reg-flow` :108, `reg-resource` :459, `reg-mutation` :461, `reg-resource-scope` :463 — while `spec/api-manifest.edn:147,153,154,155` says `:kind :macro` (and the code is `defreg-macro` at `core.cljc:506/529/543/558`). The spec contradicts its own manifest.

Three more stale lines in the same tables, all true at tip:

- Conventions `*`-pair table (:1466-1469) tables `reg-machine` / `reg-machine*` as a current facade pair. `reg-machine*` left the facade under rf2-wad2fl (`core.cljc:391-394`); its home is `re-frame.machines/reg-machine*`. `spec/005-StateMachines.md` and `API.md:939` already say so.
- Conventions :1586-1587 shows `(rf/clear-flow :flow-id)` / `(rf/clear-flow :flow-id {:frame :session})`; `clear-flow` is `re-frame.flows/clear-flow`, off the facade (`core.cljc:1036-1048`).
- Conventions tear-down roster (:1376) lists six `clear-*` names; the facade carries nine — `clear-resource` (`core.cljc:1501`), `clear-mutation` (:1545), `clear-resource-scope` (:1573) are absent from the roster.

Nothing in the corpus trips on the alias gap today (no value-position `rf/reg-flow` etc. in code — only prose), which is exactly why a hand list drifts unnoticed.

## Evidence (re-run at tip)

```sh
grep -n -E 'defreg-(event-)?macro reg-' implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc     # 15 rows
grep -n -E '^\s+reg-[a-z-]+\s+rf\.' implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc          # 10 aliases (+ the 3 retired reg-event-* stubs at :416-430)
grep -n -E ':var "(reg-flow|reg-resource|reg-mutation|reg-resource-scope)"' spec/api-manifest.edn   # all :kind :macro
sed -n '108p;459p;461p;463p' spec/API.md | cut -c1-40                                 # all "| Fn |"
```

## Target

Codex's "smallest repair" (its cross-check: prefer missing aliases plus a concordance check over a generator unless one declaration can serve both hosts without new build machinery — the generator question is @spellings.3 Q1):

1. **Add the five aliases** to the CLJS block. Delegates are the same late-bind wrappers the macros splice to:
   - `reg-flow` → `rf.core-flows/reg-flow` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_flows.cljc:23`)
   - `reg-mutation` → `rf.core-resources/reg-mutation` (`core_resources.cljc:103`)
   - `reg-head` → `rf.core-ssr/-reg-head` (`core_ssr.cljc:65`)
   - `reg-error-projector` → `rf.core-ssr/-reg-error-projector` (`core_ssr.cljc:40`)
   - `reg-http-interceptor` → `rf.core-http/reg-http-interceptor` (`core_http.cljc:50`)

   Docstrings follow the existing pattern ("Fn-alias of the `reg-x` macro for HoF / programmatic registration (no source-coord capture) …", `core.cljc:267-352`) and say where the implementation ships (`day8/re-frame2-flows` etc., as the `reg-route` / `reg-resource` aliases do).

2. **Pin concordance so the list cannot drift again.** The rule, not a list: every `re-frame.core` `reg-*` macro that does NOT def a Var or walk a literal (`reg-view` :807, `reg-machine` :651, `defmachine` :699 are the only three — none are `defreg-macro` rows) has a same-named CLJS value. Mechanism: the api-manifest CLJS probe (`implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_probe.cljc`) already reconciles live CLJS publics against manifest rows in the consolidated `:node-test` build; extend it (or add a sibling probe for `re-frame.core`) so that for every `re-frame.core` manifest row with `:kind :macro` whose var starts with `reg-` and is outside `#{reg-view reg-machine defmachine}`, a same-named live CLJS public var exists. EXISTENCE only — the probe's docstring records why `:kind` is not reconciled on CLJS. Negative control in the PR body: remove one alias locally, watch it go red.

3. **Conventions.md** (HOT): replace the enumerated Convention-A list (:1483) with the rule sentence ("every `reg-*` macro that does not def a Var or walk a literal, plus `dispatch` / `dispatch-sync` / `subscribe`") and a pointer to the concordance check; the `*` table row for `reg-machine*` names `re-frame.machines` as its home; :1586-1587 → `re-frame.flows/clear-flow`; the tear-down roster lists all nine facade `clear-*` names (or defers to API.md §Clearing registrations). Do NOT touch the reserved-fx-id paragraphs (:474-486 — @spellings.2) or the `clear-*` DESIGN (@spellings.3).

4. **API.md** (HOT): rows :108 / :459 / :461 / :463 `Fn` → `M`.

5. **docs**: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:200` states the Convention-A pattern without a list — confirm; check `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md`, `re-frame.resources.md`, `re-frame.ssr.md`, `re-frame.http.md` for any "value position" sentence that names the alias set.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer (README). Codex's cross-check on this doc: "repair the alias/documentation drift; … fill genuine Convention-A omissions without reopening [the star-twin] work … Prefer the smallest repair — missing aliases plus a concordance check". This bead IS that repair; the generator is left to @spellings.3.

## Deletion list

None (additive). The three retired `reg-event-db/-fx/-ctx` throwing stubs at `core.cljc:416-430` are out of scope.

## Consumers to migrate

None. No value-position use of the five names exists in `examples/`, `tools/`, `testbeds/`, `implementation/**/test` (the gap was latent).

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/Conventions.md` (HOT-ZONE), `spec/API.md` (HOT-ZONE) as above.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn`: run `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/` — expect NO row change: the manifest's `re-frame.core` rows are JVM-derived and the new `def`s are CLJS-only values behind macros that already row as `:macro`.
- Skills: `git grep -n -E 'rf/reg-(flow|mutation|head|error-projector|http-interceptor)' -- skills` in value position → none expected; nothing to change.
- Tests: the probe extension (+ its JVM unit test if the probe has one), `npm run test:cljs` (the consolidated node bundle compiles the five defs).
- Migration README: no v1-era name changes.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Touches TWO hot-zone files (Conventions.md, API.md). Shares Conventions.md with @spellings.2 and, if ruled, with @spellings.3's implementation bead — the mayor serialises; this one goes first (the others edit adjacent paragraphs). Independent of @spellings.4 and of the testing beads.

## Risks

Low. Additive `def`s of wrappers the macros already delegate to; no change at the macro door; source-coord capture and production elision unchanged (the alias path never captured coords). The only trap is reconciling `:kind` in the probe — do not.

title: xray managed_http testbed: seeded handle carries no :frame, so its abort step is unreachable (rf2-o8ek fallout)
description:
The xray managed_http testbed's seed fx ignores its frame-ctx and records a
handle with no :frame stamp, so the handle keys under [nil <id>]. Since PR
#9195 the :rf.http/managed-abort fx is frame-scoped — managed-abort-handler
calls require-frame-stamp! and then abort-in-flight-in-frame! with the REAL
frame-id — so it cannot resolve a nil-frame handle at all. The testbed's
abort step (5) therefore resolves nothing.

Measured on this repo tip with a JVM registry probe reproducing the seed
shape, exit 0:

  {:keyed-under ([nil :xray/in-flight]),
   :any-frame-finds? true,
   :real-frame-finds? false,
   :managed-abort-hits? false}

Site: tools/xray/testbeds/managed_http/core.cljs — the seed fx binds
_frame-ctx (unused) and records {:url pending-url :abort-fn ...} with no
:frame; its :abort-fn also calls the one-arg clear-in-flight!, which #9195
redefined as an ANY-FRAME sweep, and its rf/dispatch carries no {:frame ...}.

The repair mirrors what examples/core/managed_http_counter/core.cljs now
does (rf2-o8ek audit fix): bind (:frame frame-ctx), stamp it on the handle,
pass {:frame frame} to the deferred dispatch, and clean up through
registry/clear-in-flight-in-frame! rather than the one-arg sweep.

Out of the rf2-o8ek fence (tools/** is owned by another peer this wave), so
filed rather than fixed. Not covered by any gate: examples/testbeds carry no
spec.cjs for this path.
notes:
REOPENED BY MERGED-PR AUDIT OF #9216. The frame stamps and frame-scoped selector landed correctly, but issue-as-actor still records every synthetic handle with a no-op abort-fn. abort-on-actor-destroy eagerly removes the actor slot, then delegates request-index cleanup to each handle abort-fn (registry.cljc documents that ownership). The testbed closure therefore fires and produces the two actor-destroy traces while leaving both actor-a request-id slots live. A deterministic probe of the landed shape returned {:aborts [[:managed-http/actor-a-1 :actor-destroyed] [:managed-http/actor-a-2 :actor-destroyed]], :requests (:managed-http/actor-a-1 :managed-http/actor-a-2 :managed-http/actor-b-1), :actors #:managed-http{:actor-b 1}}. The standalone request-id strip consequently retains two ghost actor-a handles after step 7, contradicting the described aborted-request lifecycle and retaining registry state until reset.

Minimal repair: give each synthetic actor handle an abort closure that removes its own request-id from the issuing frame, e.g. clear-in-flight-in-frame! frame request-id, while preserving actor B. Extend the guard or a reachable focused witness to prove that after frame-scoped actor A teardown both actor A entries are absent from both indexes and actor B remains in both. Keep this confined to the testbed; the distinct two-index publication race remains owned by open rf2-o8ek.

title: PR #9043 red: the derivation-egress bundle-isolation POSITIVE CONTROL lost its sentinel when rf2-g1vu replaced the keyword with an identity value
notes:
DIAGNOSED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-03 04:0x AUSEST from the failing job log. PR #9043 is converted to DRAFT (confirmed draft=true, state=OPEN) so it cannot be merged while red.

THE RED IS REAL, IT IS CORRECT, AND IT IS THE GATE DOING EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS BUILT FOR. Job: tests :: CLJS bundle isolation (counter, rf2-51x5), run 33661478278. The failure is not the negative check — it is the POSITIVE CONTROL:

  "Positive control FAILED - a sentinel is no longer PRESENT where it should be (rf2-e6qmxk). The sentinel string has DRIFTED ... so the negative counter-bundle check above has LOST ITS TEETH for that artefact: it would pass whether or not the artefact actually leaked."
  "  - derivation-egress: only 0/1 sentinels present in emitted module derivation-egress"

THE CAUSE, and it is a genuinely instructive one. Under rf2-g1vu the worker replaced dead-frame-sentinel in implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc — correctly, on my ruling, and having first REPRODUCED the raw-secret leak — changing it from the keyword ::no-egress-frame to #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)). A keyword literal compiles into the emitted bundle as a STRING. An identity value does not. So the literal the bundle-isolation script had pinned as its positive-control sentinel for the derivation-egress module simply stopped existing in the artefact.

SO A CORRECT SECURITY FIX SILENTLY DISARMED AN UNRELATED CONTROL, AND THE ONLY REASON WE KNOW IS THAT THE CONTROL CHECKS ITSELF. That is the same defect class this session keeps meeting — a control that cannot catch its own case — except here the control DOES catch its own case, which is why this is a red on a PR rather than a vacuous green on main for the next six months. rf2-e6qmxk built that self-check; it has now paid for itself.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE GATE PRINTS IT: "re-derive the sentinel from the artefact source and update the matching internalSentinels entry (keep it a live, unique literal)." The roster lives in implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs, with implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.test.cjs beside it.

AND THE GATE ALSO PRINTS THE ANTI-FIX, WHICH MUST BE HONOURED: "Never delete the sentinel to make this pass — that restores the vacuous-green hole this control exists to close." Deleting the derivation-egress entry would turn the job green and leave that artefact permanently unguarded. Do not do it, and do not weaken the positive control.

WHAT THE FIXER MUST DO: pick a LIVE, UNIQUE string literal that survives release compilation of the derivation-egress module — an error id or message literal is the shape the roster already uses — verify it actually appears in the emitted bundle, and prove the choice by the gate going red again if that literal is removed. A sentinel chosen by reading source and not verified in the EMITTED artefact is how this recurs.

DISPATCH SHAPE: a fix worker onto the EXISTING branch worker/code-a (the PR is already draft). Do not open a new branch; #9043 carries rf2-g1vu, rf2-rlrd and rf2-djqm, all three already closed, and none of that work is on main until this lands.
CLOSED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-03 05:3x AUSEST with a cross-reference, because the worker deliberately did not run bd from its worktree (to avoid dirtying .beads/issues.jsonl - the right call).

FIXED AND MERGED: PR #9043 at 23ef6f1684. The formerly-red CLJS bundle isolation (counter, rf2-51x5) now PASSES. Verified by the five-clause criterion, not by the merge line: rollup 86 (10 SKIPPED + 76 SUCCESS), four runs completed/success, job-key discriminator 0 against control 1.

THE SENTINEL CHOSEN: :rf.resource/opaque - the opaque resource-handle marker the projection MINTS AND READS BACK (opaque-handle emits it at egress.cljc:169, opaque-handle? compares against it at :145), both on the live path from project-graph, which is the fn the positive-control module references. A CLJS keyword interns its fully-qualified name as a string constant and Closure does not rename string literals.

VERIFIED IN THE EMITTED ARTEFACT, NOT IN SOURCE, which was the trap I named: 1 occurrence in out/bundle-isolation-positive-control/derivation-egress.js, 0 in the counter bundle (633,362 chars) and 0 in all five other example release bundles.

AND THE WORKER WALKED INTO THE TRAP AND OUT AGAIN, WHICH IS WHY THE NEXT ONE WILL NOT. egress.cljc:477 still carries defonce ^:private bundle-isolation-sentinel = "rf.derivation.egress/sentinel:...:do-not-rename" with a comment asserting the gate greps it and that it survives :advanced. MEASURED: ZERO occurrences in the emitted module - Closure drops the unused private var. Reading source alone picks exactly that string. Git archaeology confirms the comment is stale by design: commit 4e43784ec7 (Mike, 2026-07-15) had ALREADY moved this entry and its derivation-graph sibling off the planted strings when these controls became emitted-module greps. Both traps and that history are now recorded in the roster comment.

PLANT PROOF DONE PROPERLY: renamed to a NON-SUFFIX name deliberately, because the gate matches by SUBSTRING and ".../opaque-PLANTED" would have passed vacuously. Confirmed the runtime SAW the plant (emitted module: 1 planted, 0 sentinel) before trusting the red - the half a blob hash alone cannot prove. Gate exit 1 naming derivation-egress; restore blob-hash MATCH.

Test counts did not move: derivation-conformance 23 tests / 526 assertions, exit 0, including the rf2-g1vu collision regression.

title: ssr-node absence witness is RED ON MAIN: slice E broke both surviving absolute-zero rows in five places, and the surface-armed job was skipped on E's own PR so nobody saw it
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6) while discharging a red check on PR #9015. THE DEFECT IS THE TRUNK'S, NOT PR #9015's -- established by running the suite on the UNMODIFIED MERGE BASE, which is the discriminator the mayor asked for.

THE TWO RUNS, same command "node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs", exit code captured on the same line as the redirect:
- PR #9015 HEAD f6cbdbd411 -> exit 1
- MERGE BASE 7f6533dd0b, detached checkout, zero dirty files, my README change confirmed ABSENT (grep count 0) -> exit 1
IDENTICAL failure sets. Both fail exactly two rows of absence.test.cjs, and every other suite passes on both (8 of 9 green; the two 30/30 and 12/12 subtest blocks pass on both). So the base is red before PR #9015 exists.

WHY IT SURFACED ONLY NOW, and why this is nobody's carelessness: the node-ssr-node job is SURFACE-ARMED off implementation/ssr-node/**. Slice E touched none of that tree, so the job was SKIPPED on PR #8997 and could not report. PR #9015 edits .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh (a one-line comment), and a change to the classifier itself conservatively arms ALL 28 surfaces -- so #9015 is simply the first branch since E to arm a job that was already failing. The mayor confirmed independently: main skipped, five sibling branches skipped, this branch failed twice.

ROW 1 -- "the refusal-code namespace appears nowhere outside the package". Four sites spell the :rf.ssr-node/ namespace outside implementation/ssr-node/, all from slice E (git blame against origin/main):
  examples/substrates/hicasso/login/host.clj:58                 ae858bf329   build-identity-mismatch, in docstring prose
  examples/substrates/hicasso/login/server.cljs:34              ae858bf329   state-key-not-allowed, in docstring prose
  implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:252   bbc97a5678   service-saturated, in docstring prose
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/login_server_crossing_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:375   ae858bf329   a test ASSERTION on the literal wire string build-identity-mismatch

ROW 2 -- "no shadow-cljs build and no classpath entry reaches this package". One site:
  implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1629   ff6698f794   a ";;" COMMENT naming the implementation/ssr-node path
The assertion message reads "the package would be on a build's source path", which here is FALSE IN FACT -- it is a comment, not a :source-paths entry. This row greps the whole file rather than loader positions, so it is stricter than Reading 1 (correctly loader-position-scoped since rf2-6ovv).

THIS IS A CONTRACT JUDGEMENT, NOT A TYPO -- do not let a fix worker simply delete words. The witness was written when NOTHING outside the package could legitimately name the refusal vocabulary. The crossing now exists, and an application that HANDLES refusals has honest reasons to name them. Two coherent repairs, and choosing between them is Mike's / the mayor's call:

(a) NARROW THE WITNESS. Say the surviving absolute zero is about code that could DISPATCH on the vocabulary, and let prose and a contract-pinning test assert the wire strings. DANGER: absence.test.cjs's own header argues at length that an allowance mechanism with nothing in it is the first entry of an allowance list, and it calls this row "the absolute zero that survives, and the reason the narrowing above is safe rather than merely smaller". Narrowing it a second time needs that argument answered, not bypassed.

(b) STOP SPELLING THE VOCABULARY OUTSIDE THE PACKAGE -- which is what the programme's OWN ruling already requires of the adapter. S5: "the adapter classifies by the transport's status contract and never spells that vocabulary." The three docstrings can say "the sidecar's build-identity refusal" and so on at no cost. The TEST at :375 is the hard one: pinning the exact wire string is legitimate contract-testing, and whether that assertion moves inside the package, or reads the constant from protocol.cjs rather than restating it, is the real design question.

For ROW 2 the likely repair is different again: either reword the shadow-cljs comment so it does not spell the path, or fix the row to read loader positions the way Reading 1 does, since a comment genuinely is not a source path.

ALSO WORTH FIXING, and arguably the most valuable part: THE JOB CANNOT SEE ITS OWN BREAKAGE. The absence witness makes claims about the WHOLE repo (implementation/, examples/, tools/, scripts/, .github/) but is armed only by changes to implementation/ssr-node/**. Any change ANYWHERE ELSE can break it silently, which is exactly what happened -- three commits, five sites, zero signal. Consider arming ssr_node on the surfaces the witness actually reads, or running it unconditionally: the suite is seconds and needs no build and no node_modules, as the classifier comment beside the arm already says.

NOT FIXED ON PR #9015 DELIBERATELY: that PR is a docs/manifest slice fenced from code, the defect predates it, and the mayor's instruction was to report the merge-base result rather than grow the diff. Fold this into rf2-8arzr.5 instead if preferred -- .5 is already reopened for slice E's example-host defects, and this is more slice-E fallout.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-02 23:34:30 AUSEST. Dispatched off MAIN (worker/ssrnode-red), not onto PR #9015's branch — the merge-base run established the defect is the trunk's, so the fix belongs on its own branch and #9015 stays untouched.

ON THE CHOICE THE BEAD PUTS TO ME: option (a), narrowing the witness, is REFUSED. Two independent reasons, and neither is taste. First, absence.test.cjs's own header argues at length that an allowance mechanism with nothing in it is the first entry of an allowance list, and calls this row 'the absolute zero that survives, and the reason the narrowing above is safe rather than merely smaller' — narrowing it a second time requires answering that argument, and nothing in the five broken sites answers it. Second, and decisive: option (b) is not a new decision at all. The programme's OWN S5 ruling already requires it of the adapter — 'the adapter classifies by the transport's status contract and never spells that vocabulary.' Applying an existing ruling to three docstrings that violate it is work under a decision already made, not a fresh call.

SO THE RULING IS (b), and the two residual questions resolve by precedent rather than by preference. The test assertion at :375 reads the constant from protocol.cjs instead of restating the literal — that keeps the contract pinned (which is legitimate and stays) while removing the second spelling, so it satisfies the witness without weakening the test. Row 2 fixes the ROW rather than the comment: a ';;' comment genuinely is not a source path, the assertion message 'the package would be on a build's source path' is false in fact, and Reading 1 was already scoped to loader positions under rf2-6ovv — so this is the same repair applied to the sibling reading, with precedent.

ARMING: also authorised, and it is the most valuable part. A witness that makes whole-repo claims while armed only by its own directory is a control that cannot catch its own case — the defect class this project keeps finding — and it is exactly why three commits and five sites produced zero signal. The suite is seconds and needs no node_modules, so it runs unconditionally. This is CI hygiene under the project's own stated defect class, not a product call; I am recording it as MY call so Mike can reverse it cheaply if he disagrees.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: PR #9015 cannot merge until this lands. Clause 2 admits only passing or skipped checks and a FAILURE is neither, so 'the defect is the trunk's' does not make the check pass — it only says where the fix belongs. #9015 waits.
FIXED 2026-09-03 on worker/ssrnode-red, PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9024. Three commits off main, rebased onto 8931e1a1fb: 60957146f0 (Row 1), 0c1777ae63 (Row 2), bfb15b379e (arming).

THE CONTROL HELD. Base run at merge-base 58efa988ed, before any edit: exit 1, the same two rows the bead measured, 8 of 9 suites green. Final run after all three commits: exit 0, 9 suites green, 18 rows in absence.test.cjs. So the bead's premise reproduced exactly and the trunk red is cleared.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern resources — reg-resource-scope shown as a 2-slot {:inputs :resolve} map the runtime rejects; canonical form is 3-slot (id metadata resolve-fn)
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md` §Named scope resolvers — `reg-resource-scope` (L104-107):

```clojure
(rf/reg-resource-scope :session
  {:inputs  {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}    ;; declared inputs — names ↦ source descriptors
   :resolve (fn [{:keys [username]} _ctx]
              (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}]))})
```

L118 then describes the `{:inputs … :resolve …}` **form** as the canonical declaration ("The `{:inputs … :resolve …}` form **declares** which app facts decide identity") and offers the whole-db bare-fn as the sugar. `resources-mutations.md`, the mutation descriptors and every `{:from-db :session}` reference in both leaves build on this registration.

## TRUTH AT TIP

`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc:15-23` — "## The `{:inputs …}` metadata + resolver-fn grammar (the ONE canonical form) … The 3-slot shape is `(scope-id metadata resolve-fn)`: the resolver is the THIRD (value) slot, not a `:resolve` key inside the metadata map." L289-300: the registration fn is `[scope-id metadata resolve-fn]`, throws `:rf.error/invalid-resource-scope-spec` with the message "the :inputs / :doc reflection-config metadata map is the SECOND slot, the :resolve fn is the THIRD", and the comment at L299-300 is explicit: "A `:resolve` left INSIDE the metadata map is a mislocated key; reject it". `spec/016-Resources.md:169,586` states the same 3-slot grammar; `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/scope.cljs:105+` registers `:realworld/viewer` / `:realworld/session` in the 3-slot form. The whole-db bare-fn sugar the leaf mentions (L118) does exist (`scope_registry.cljc:55-68`) — that part is right.

## IMPACT

The one registration the whole Resources scope story hangs on is written in a shape the runtime rejects loudly (2-slot with `:resolve` mislocated). An agent copying it gets `:rf.error/invalid-resource-scope-spec` at boot; every `{:from-db :session}` downstream then fails closed (unresolved scope → `:rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope` on subs, dropped targets on mutations). Loud rather than silent, but it is the leaf's headline snippet and it contradicts the spec, the implementation and the canonical example at once.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, `patterns/resources.md` only)

Rewrite L104-107 to the 3-slot form (lift from `scope_registry.cljc:17-20` or `scope.cljs`):

```clojure
(rf/reg-resource-scope :session
  {:inputs {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}}     ;; metadata: declared inputs
  (fn [{:keys [username]} _ctx]                           ;; resolver: THIRD slot, first arg = resolved inputs map
    (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}])))
```

and reword L118 ("The `{:inputs …}` metadata + third-slot resolver …"). Optionally add the one-line "first arg is ALWAYS the resolved inputs map; the bare-fn sugar is the only form whose first arg is the whole db" since that is the trap the grammar exists to prevent (`scope_registry.cljc:26-33`).

## GATE

No gate compiles skill code fences; `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` still run. Verify by hand against `scope_registry.cljc` §grammar and `realworld_resources/scope.cljs`, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

Every `reg-resource-scope` call in `skills/re-frame2/patterns/*.md` is 3-slot `(id metadata resolve-fn)` with no `:resolve` key in the metadata map; the prose names the resolver as the third slot.

title: WebSocket teaching surfaces disagree on timeout delivery and reply-envelope shape
description:
Audit finding from PR #8907 across completeness, correctness, and implementation quality.

The PR correctly synchronizes the three active-exit doors with the runnable WebSocket example, but the request-outcome contract is still internally contradictory on the same edited teaching surface.

At merged commit 9445bfeb3c:
- spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md's worked :clear-request action only dissocs the slot. Item 4 says the caller's reply event never fires on timeout.
- The canonical runnable example examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs does the opposite: action-clear-request reads reply-event, clears the slot, and dispatches one machine-stamped :ws/timeout failure. Existing rf2-b2jpr acceptance and tests explicitly require a live-socket timeout as an explicit terminal outcome.
- Two lines after the stale item 4, the spec says a locally minted loss/timeout failure reaches the caller's reply-event. Thus the page contradicts itself and copying its worked machine restores the caller-hang that the canonical example already removed.
- The edited skill still emits the runnable example's bespoke {:origin :ws/local :request-id ... :ok false :error ...} outcome, while its correlation guidance on the same page mandates the uniform reply envelope with closed :status and :rf.reply/work-id. The runnable schema/RequestOutcome and spec use the bespoke shape. A programmer or AI cannot tell which contract is canonical.

No existing Bead owns WebSocket timeout documentation or this reply-envelope conflict; all-status searches covered websocket timeout, clear-request, reply-event, RequestOutcome, uniform reply, and rf.reply/work-id. rf2-0g60h owns only the fatal-door listing drift, rf2-b2jpr the already-fixed clean-disconnect runtime leak, and rf2-iyjae the already-fixed inbound trust/provenance boundary.

Keep this small: rule the one callback contract and align the runnable example, spec, and skill. Do not build a generalized WebSocket facility or a new reply abstraction.
acceptance_criteria: The spec worked :clear-request, its request-reply sequence, the runnable example/test, and the skill agree whether a live timeout invokes reply-event; no copied canonical form can silently clear a request while leaving its caller waiting. The WebSocket RequestOutcome uses one documented envelope shape across source schema, spec, and skill (either the uniform managed envelope or an explicitly justified pattern-local contract). Loss and timeout remain machine-stamped, server outcomes remain unforgeably distinct, and existing exactly-once/stale-epoch controls stay intact. No new abstraction or compatibility layer.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-01 22:07 AUSEST — THE UNIFORM REPLY ENVELOPE IS CANONICAL. Settled from the page's own normative text, not by preference.

BOTH HALVES OF THIS BEAD ARE REAL, and neither is a taste call once you read the sources.

HALF 1 — THE SELF-CONTRADICTION. spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md's item 4 says the caller's reply event never fires on timeout. Two lines later the same page says a locally minted loss/timeout failure DOES reach the reply-event, and the runnable example (examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs) dispatches one. So item 4 and the worked :clear-request action are the wrong side of the contradiction: the example and the page's own later text already agree with each other, and rf2-b2jpr's acceptance requires a live-socket timeout as an explicit terminal outcome. RULED: correct item 4 and the worked action to fire the reply-event. Copying the current worked machine restores the caller-hang the canonical example already removed, which is the whole cost here.

HALF 2 — THE ENVELOPE. skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md:200 already states the rule, with its reason and a citation: 'Because this is the completion of an async request, model it on the uniform reply envelope (Managed-Effects property 9), not a bespoke ack: dispatch the :reply-event with a reply map carrying a closed :status {:ok :partial :error :cancelled :stale} and the request id as :rf.reply/work-id ... so your socket replies read the same as every other async completion in trace/Xray.' Line 64 of that same file, and spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md at 181/505/575, emit {:origin :ws/local :ok false :error :ws/connection-lost} — the bespoke ack the page forbids. RULED: the envelope is canonical and the bespoke shape is the drift. A page carrying its own rule plus worked examples that violate it is worse than either alone, because the reader cannot tell which is the contract.

:origin :ws/local IS NOT DROPPED — it is carried INSIDE the envelope. The same paragraph demands that two producers reaching one reply-event be told apart 'by a provenance key the machine stamps after receipt, never by the body's shape'. That is exactly what :origin is for, and it is the reason the two shapes must not remain alternatives: provenance belongs as a field, never as a rival envelope.

SCOPE, measured rather than assumed: seven files carry the bespoke spelling — spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md, skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md, examples/patterns/websocket/{connection,schema,messages}.cljs and its README, plus implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs. No framework source depends on it, so this is a teaching-surface correction plus one test, not a runtime migration.

NOT WANTED: any change to the reply-envelope contract itself; a WebSocket-specific exemption from it; a new outcome abstraction; a Playwright spec. Do not widen beyond the WebSocket surface.

---

WORKER VERDICT 2026-09-01 (rf2-i3og0, PR #8936, branch worker/wsenvelope-i3og0)

HALF 1 — IMPLEMENTED. Both premises confirmed verbatim at tip before acting.
Item 4 read: "The :clear-request action removes the in-flight entry; the
caller's reply event never fires." Two paragraphs later the same page reads:
"A correlated wire reply and a locally minted loss/timeout failure both arrive
at the caller's :reply-event." The runnable example already agreed with the
second. Fixed in spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md only: :clear-request now reads the
:reply-event, clears the slot and dispatches the :ws/timeout failure (guarded
for a nil reply-event); item 4 states the reply-event fires and why a silent
clear strands the caller; and the local-failure body is factored into a helper
as connection.cljs already does, so the lost-wire and elapsed-deadline
producers cannot drift into two shapes again. The example, the test and the
README needed no change — they were already on the correct side.

HALF 2 — STOPPED. THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD, AND THE DRIFT RUNS THE OTHER WAY.
skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md:200 does say what the ruling quotes, but
it is the residue, not the rule. Four independent sources say the opposite:

1. spec/Managed-Effects.md:281 — the envelope contract's OWN owning spec: "A
   WebSocket connection is a long-lived synchronous surface rather than a
   one-shot async request, so property 9 (the uniform async-reply envelope) is
   exempt — the eight synchronous properties are the ones the pattern is
   graded on."
2. spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md:8 — the page's own header blockquote states the
   same property-9 exemption independently.
3. spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md:511 — normative note: "This correlation shape is
   APP-LEVEL — NOT the uniform reply envelope ... the recommended worked shape
   is the app-level :in-flight map."
4. Commit 6fb1223396 (2026-06-17, rf2-eygytk) "pin the WebSocket request/reply
   path as app-level, outside EP-0011" — THIS EXACT FINDING was raised then
   ("could read as a second, competing reply vocabulary alongside the EP-0011
   uniform reply envelope") and resolved the other way on a recorded Mike
   ruling that re-frame2 ships no managed WebSocket. It states: "Rewriting it
   to :rf/reply-to + reply-map would contradict the spec." That commit planted
   a CANARY, live at tip: websocket_cljs_test.cljs:1150-1159, five assertions
   that the reply carries none of :rf/reply-to, :status, :work/id, :work/kind,
   :completed-at, commented "a canary if a future ruling ever folds this into
   the envelope."

TIMELINE SETTLES WHICH SIDE DRIFTED. The skill's uniform-envelope sentence
entered 2026-06-11 (208c7e281d, a general EP-0011 sweep across managed-async
guidance). The pinning fix landed 2026-06-17, six days LATER, and corrected the
spec, the example and the test — but never reached the skill. PR #8907 carried
the stale sentence through unchanged today.

WHY THIS STOPPED RATHER THAN PROCEEDED. Implementing Half 2 as ruled would
require withdrawing the property-9 exemption in spec/Managed-Effects.md —
outside the dispatch fence, and the brief's explicit STOP condition. It would
reverse a recorded Mike ruling and turn the five canary assertions red.
