title: http: capture the interceptor chain at request issue (both walks + retries) and state the timing contract in Spec 014 §Middleware
description:
RULED 2026-09-08 — see NOTES for the full ruling, which is what to brief from. This bead is a SPEC-CONTRACT DECISION PLUS ITS IMPLEMENTATION, NOT a bug: Spec 014 §Middleware is SILENT on chain-resolution timing (verified independently by two reviewers), so nothing is in breach of a contract. Re-typed from BUG and re-prioritised P2 -> P3 on measured severity — documented and in-repo usage registers interceptors at BOOT, where the window is empty.

FOUND BY worker httpfix-a, 2026-09-07/08, while diagnosing an intermittent CI red on after-less-interceptors-are-transparent. That CI symptom was a TEST-ISOLATION FLAKE and is SEPARATELY FIXED on the test side, already on main; the runtime asymmetry underneath it is what this bead covers. PR #9434 (c905e8dbb1) only reshuffled ns-interns test order and exposed it — trigger, not cause.

THE ASYMMETRY. The `:before` chain is resolved ONCE at issue (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc:411); the `:after` chain is resolved AGAIN from the live process-global registry at response time (:455 — re-measure, lines move, and note the source is whitespace-aligned so an exact-string grep of the old quoted spelling finds nothing). The middleware-ctx IS carried forward for the request; the CHAIN IS NOT. A response landing after the registry changed therefore walks a chain its request never had, and an `:after` can be handed a ctx its own `:before` never touched.

WHAT WAS RULED. A managed request CAPTURES its frame's interceptor VECTOR (function-bearing slots, not ids) once, immediately BEFORE the `:before` walk is entered — i.e. before handlers.cljc:343, NOT at the handlers.cljc:383 ctx-capture site, which is measurably too late — and that same captured vector drives the `:before` walk, the `:after` walk and every retry attempt. Registering, replacing or clearing an interceptor mid-flight affects only requests that capture their chain afterwards. No live-registry fallback anywhere; an empty snapshot is a real snapshot; the captured vector rides the INTERNAL normalised ctx, never the user-visible middleware-ctx. Rejected: live resolution (option B), id-only capture with live fns (C1), clear-filtering (C2).

ACCEPTANCE. The chain is captured at issue and used by both walks and by retries; a test that registers an interceptor AFTER a request is issued — and one that registers from INSIDE a `:before` — shows the response walking the ORIGINAL chain; Spec 014 §Chain order and frame scope states the timing contract explicitly.

The "DO NOT dispatch until the ruling lands" hold is DISCHARGED. Scope, the two implementation traps, the measured blast radius on existing tests, the file:line map and the deliberate out-of-scope list are in the NOTES — read them before starting, and do not re-run the analysis: it has been done twice.
notes:
--- MAYOR 2026-09-08 16:2x AUSEST — PREMISE RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE; RULING STILL OWED AND STILL MIKE'S ---
I applied the "which of these actually need Mike" test to this bead this tick and it PASSES. Unlike
rf2-hu69, which I took off the ruling list and dispatched because its acceptance began with a
MEASUREMENT, this bead's mechanism is already measured at source and its own text says "DO NOT dispatch
this bead until that ruling lands". There is no worker-shaped half to send. So the only useful thing a
coordinator can do is make sure the citation still resolves before you rule on it, and that is what this
note records — measured on origin/main at cac4089a22.
THE DEFECT SITE IS AT :455, NOT :454 — one line of drift since filing, and the bead already warned to
re-measure. `run-after-chain!` opens at :434, and the offending form reads:
    :chain      (reverse (get @interceptors frame-id))
Aligned with whitespace, which is worth knowing because an exact-string grep for the unaligned spelling
the bead quotes returns NOTHING — a false zero of exactly the kind this project keeps recording. Match
the construct (`reverse (get @interceptors frame-id)`), not the quoted line.
THE DOCSTRING PROMISE THE BEAD LEANS ON IS STILL THERE and still says what the bead says it says: `:after`
receives the middleware-ctx the `:before` chain produced for THIS request, and a following comment
repeats that `:after` always sees the fixed middleware-ctx. So the ctx really is captured and the chain
really is not — the asymmetry the bead names is intact at tip. Control: `:chain` reads 2 in that file, so
the grep is live rather than matching one lucky line.
NOTHING HAS CHANGED THAT WOULD ALTER THE RECOMMENDATION. It remains: yes, the `:after` chain should be
the one in force when the request was ISSUED. What is owed is a Spec 014 §Middleware contract statement,
which is a spec change and therefore yours.

--- MAYOR §3 CHECK 2026-09-08 22:4x AUSEST — THE SPEC DOES NOT RULE THIS, BUT ITS OWN WORKED EXAMPLE ONLY WORKS UNDER THE PROPOSED CONTRACT ---
I did NOT dispatch this — the bead says "DO NOT dispatch until that ruling lands" and I am honouring that.
What I did was read spec/014-HTTPRequests.md §Middleware to see whether the contract is already stated,
and the answer sharpens Mike's question considerably.
WHAT THE SPEC ACTUALLY SAYS, twice and precisely, at :1455 and again in the ctx row at :853:
    ":before runs in registration order, :after in reverse, and the :after sees THE SAME CTX the :before
     chain produced for that request — so request-correlated response handling (e.g. a start-mark stamped
     by :before, read by :after) is a single-interceptor concern."
    "ctx | The SAME ctx the :before chain produced for THIS request ... Carrying the request ctx forward
     is what makes request-correlated handling expressible: a :before that stamps ::started-at lets the
     SAME INTERCEPTOR'S :after read the start mark and compute a wall-clock delta without app-level state."
SO THE SPEC IS EXPLICIT ABOUT THE CTX AND SILENT ABOUT THE CHAIN. That is exactly the gap this bead
found — the ctx is captured, the chain is not — and it means the spec does not literally answer the
question. I am not going to pretend it does.
BUT ITS WORKED EXAMPLE IS UNSOUND WITHOUT THE PROPOSED FIX, and that is the finding. The spec's stated
purpose for carrying the ctx forward is that ONE interceptor can stamp in :before and read in :after. If
the chain is resolved live at response time, an interceptor unregistered between request and response
DOES NOT RUN ITS :after AT ALL — so the start-mark it stamped is never read, and the single-interceptor
concern the spec promises silently becomes a no-op. The ctx survives; the reader of the ctx does not.
Capturing the ctx without capturing the chain protects half of one mechanism.
WHAT THAT DOES TO THE RULING: it narrows it from "is this the intended contract?" to "ratify what §Middleware's
own example already assumes". The bead's recommendation — capture the :after chain at request time — is not
a new contract; it is the condition under which the contract already written is true. I agree with
httpfix-a and with the bead, now on spec evidence rather than on plausibility.
STILL MIKE'S CALL, because it IS a Spec 014 behavioural change and the acceptance names a spec edit
("Spec 014 §Middleware states the contract explicitly"). Nothing is blocked by waiting — the CI flake was
separately fixed on the test side, as the bead records.
--- RULING 2026-09-08 23:03 AUSEST (HEAD 379c73da97) — DECIDED: CAPTURE AT ISSUE. Re-typed BUG->TASK, P2->P3. Two independent analyses weighed (original dossier + Codex review); dossier consumed and deleted. ---

THE DECISION, in two sentences. A managed HTTP request CAPTURES its frame's interceptor vector ONCE, immediately BEFORE the `:before` walk runs, and that same captured vector drives BOTH walks — `:before` at issue and `:after` at response — and survives every retry attempt. Registering, replacing or clearing an interceptor mid-flight therefore affects only requests that capture their chain AFTERWARDS; Spec 014 §Middleware gains one bullet saying so. That is the whole change: internal threading inside `implementation/http/`, one spec bullet, focused regression tests. Both reviewers independently landed on this option; there is no live-resolution reading left to preserve, so do not re-litigate it.

RE-TYPED BUG -> TASK, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT CONTRADICTS THE BEAD'S OWN PREMISE. The bead was filed as a runtime defect against a contract. THERE IS NO SUCH CONTRACT: **Spec 014 §Middleware is SILENT on chain-resolution timing**, verified independently by both reviewers. §`:after` (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:847-856`) pins WHICH CTX an `:after` sees ("The SAME ctx the `:before` chain produced for THIS request") and says nothing about WHICH CHAIN runs; §Chain order and frame scope (`:865-871`) has five bullets — registration order, reverse order, skip-when-absent, clear-then-re-register, per-frame isolation — and no timing bullet; §Clearing (`:883-887`) covers hot-reload of the REGISTRY, not of in-flight requests. A regex sweep of the whole 1500-line page for `in.?flight|snapshot|at issue|issued|registration time|request time|response time` returns no hit inside §Middleware. So this is CHOOSING WHAT THE CONTRACT SHOULD SAY, not repairing a violation. Type it and brief it that way.

RE-PRIORITISED P2 -> P3. Measured severity is LOW and the two reviewers split on what to do about it; the original's position wins because it is the one carrying evidence. The documented, exemplified and ONLY in-repo usage registers interceptors at BOOT, before any request can be in flight — `docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md:160` says so in a comment ("Register at app boot, before the first authenticated request can fire"), and both RealWorld examples do exactly that inside `run` before `mount!` (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/core.cljs:445-447` and its `realworld_resources` twin). Under that shape the window is EMPTY and the defect unreachable. Confirmed harm to date: one flaky CI test, ALREADY FIXED on the test side and on main; zero production reports. Codex's counter — "the evidence does not justify changing the bead's priority" — concedes in the same sentence that it establishes no production urgency, so it is an argument from inertia against an argument from measurement. P3. It is still worth doing: the defect is silent in three of its four symptom shapes, and the fix is small.

=== WHERE THE TWO REVIEWERS CONFLICTED, AND WHO WON ===

1. **CAPTURE POINT — CODEX WINS, AND THIS CHANGES THE CODE.** The original proposed capturing beside `:middleware-ctx` on the internal normalised ctx at `handlers.cljc:383-384`. THAT IS TOO LATE. The `:before` walk is entered at `handlers.cljc:343` (`ctx (rf.http.middleware/run-interceptor-chain! frame-id ctx0)`) and derefs the registry at `middleware.cljc:411`; `normalised0` with `:middleware-ctx` is only assembled at `:383-384`, AFTER that walk has returned — re-verified at source in this checkout while landing this ruling. Codex measured the arm that proves it: registering a new interceptor FROM INSIDE the original `:before` gives the new `:after` a nil mark, with NO asynchronous interleaving needed at all. A snapshot taken at :383 would therefore differ from the vector `:before` actually ran, reintroducing the same disagreement one step earlier. CAPTURE ONCE BEFORE `run-interceptor-chain!` IS CALLED AND PASS THE VECTOR INTO BOTH WALKERS. The defect window opens at `:before`-chain SELECTION, not at network send.

2. **THE NO-SNAPSHOT FALLBACK — CODEX WINS.** The original flagged this as an open question for the implementer ("skip, or fall back to a live deref — state it"). Codex answers it, and its answer is the right one: if an internal caller supplies a middleware ctx but no captured chain, MIGRATE THAT CALLER. Do NOT add a live-registry compatibility fallback — that would leave the defect alive on exactly the path nobody tests. Corollary: an EMPTY captured vector is a REAL SNAPSHOT, not a signal to consult the live registry.

3. **RETRY HANDOFF — CODEX WINS (stronger evidence).** The original flagged `transport.cljc:1483-1496` as untraced. Codex traced it: the handoff transforms the existing ctx with `dissoc`/`update`/`assoc` (`transport.cljc:1194`) and `run-attempt!` removes only `:rf.http/retry-handoff` (`transport.cljc:1586`), so an additional top-level key survives the handoff without further plumbing and without re-running `:before`. Still needs one regression assertion; it is no longer a design risk.

4. **"ALL FOUR SPEC USE CASES DEPEND ON PAIRING" — CODEX'S CORRECTION WINS; it does not change the ruling.** The original overstated. The 401 example is `:after`-ONLY and ignores ctx (`http_interceptors_test.clj:1294`), and the auth how-to DISPATCHES LOGOUT rather than merely tagging for refresh (`docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md:187`). Use case 2 — `:before` stamps `::started-at`, `:after` reads it — genuinely does depend on pairing and IS spec-pinned (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:861`, test `motivating-response-time-telemetry` at `http_interceptors_test.clj:1202-1234`). One sound motivating case is enough to decide; do not repeat the four-case claim in the spec bullet.

5. **"FOUR FILES, ZERO TEST CHURN" — CODEX'S QUALIFICATION WINS.** Nothing PINS the current live-resolution semantics (that half of the original's claim held up), but the canned helper `run-request-chain` has a consumer outside `implementation/http/` that reads `(:request ctx)`: `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_request_decoration_cljs_test.cljc:102`. Changing that helper's return shape means updating this caller or preserving its existing return contract. Budget accordingly; "zero churn" was an estimate, not a verified compatibility proof.

6. **CLJS ARITHMETIC DIVERGENCE — DROPPED, both agree it is not load-bearing.** Codex measured JVM `(- ended nil)` throwing NPE; the original's CLJS prediction (null coerces to 0, silently bogus delta) is unmeasured and unnecessary to decide. Do not spend time on it.

=== LOAD-BEARING ANALYSIS, PRESERVED ===

THE ASYMMETRY, one file, forty lines apart — same expression, two different moments (re-verified at source):
  `middleware.cljc:411`  `:chain      (get @interceptors frame-id)`            — `:before`, derefed ONCE at issue, synchronously
  `middleware.cljc:455`  `:chain      (reverse (get @interceptors frame-id))`  — `:after`, derefed AGAIN at response, asynchronously
INSTRUMENT NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: an exact-string grep for the bead description's quoted spelling returns NOTHING — the source is whitespace-aligned as `:chain      (reverse …)`. Match the CONSTRUCT, not the quoted line. Control: `:chain` reads exactly 2 in that file, lines 411 and 455, so the instrument is live.

THE WINDOW. The registry is one process-global `defonce` atom keyed by frame-id (`middleware.cljc:84-85`); `reg-http-interceptor` swaps a slot on (`:189-197`), `clear-http-interceptor` removes one (`:222-224`), `clear-all-http-interceptors!` resets the whole map (`:295`) — all callable at any moment. The ctx is captured and carried (`handlers.cljc:383-384`, threaded to the transport at `:424`); the CHAIN is not. Default per-attempt timeout is 30 000 ms (`handlers.cljc:204-205`) and `:retry` adds attempts plus backoff on top, and `:before` is NOT re-run per attempt — so one managed request holds one ctx across that whole window while the chain floats free. Response side: platform completion callback -> `dispatch-reply!` (`transport.cljc:208-228`) -> `run-after-then-dispatch!` (`middleware.cljc:499-502`) -> `run-after-chain!` (`:453-455`), the second deref.

THE PROMISE THE CODE ALREADY MAKES — for the CTX only. `run-after-chain!`'s docstring (`middleware.cljc:440-443`) and a comment in its body (`:458-460`) both say the `:after` sees "the middleware-ctx the `:before` chain produced for THIS request". The runtime went to real trouble to freeze the CTX and then resolves the CHAIN THAT CONSUMES IT live. That mismatch is the substance: an `:after` fn can be handed a ctx its own `:before` never touched, because it was not registered when that `:before` ran.

CODEX'S MEASURED DISCRIMINATOR — bounded probe in a separate JVM, loading the real middleware namespace from this checkout and printing its resolved source URL, invoking the existing walkers directly with controlled intervening registrations; no transport, shared build or repo file involved; exit 0. Clojure on the cached classpath was 1.12.4 while the declared core dep is 1.12.0 (`implementation/core/deps.edn:35`) — measurements are on the former.
  - control, no intervention                     -> original `:after` read its original `:before` mark
  - register a NEW paired interceptor            -> new `:after` ran FIRST with its own mark NIL; original `:after` followed
  - REPLACE the original id                      -> new `:after` read the OLD implementation's mark
  - CLEAR the original id                        -> original `:after` did not run at all
  - register the new one INSIDE the original `:before` -> new `:after` received a nil mark, no async interleaving needed
The last arm is the one that moved the capture point (conflict 1 above).

THE MEASURED CI REPRODUCTION (from `httpfix-a`, commit `9180cfe3bd`, 20 trials per arm; both reviewers inspected the record rather than re-running it). Leaker `clear-then-reg-appends-to-end-of-chain` (`http_interceptors_test.clj:669`) registers `:before`-only `:a` `:b` `:c` and — pre-fix — returned with its own HTTP response still on the wire, because those `:before` fns fire synchronously inside `dispatch-sync` so the first wait probe succeeded immediately. The fixture's post-dispose hook then fires `:http/clear-all-http-interceptors!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:474-475`), victim `after-less-interceptors-are-transparent` (`:1108`) registers `:before-only` then `:after-only`, and THEN the leaker's response lands and walks the VICTIM's chain — running an interceptor belonging to a different request, a different frame-lifetime and a different registry generation, handed a middleware-ctx produced by a `:before` chain it had never met. Observed order `[:after-only-fired :before-only-fired :after-only-fired]`, the exact CI signature: 2 of 20 leaker/victim pairs before, 0 of 20 after the TEST-SIDE fix. WHY IT HID FOR MONTHS: almost every interceptor test registers `:before`-only interceptors, under which the `:after` walk is a no-op under its own chain. TRIGGER vs CAUSE: PR #9434 (`c905e8dbb1`) deleted three tests, reshuffling `ns-interns` hash order and moving leaker and victim from positions 16/20 (with the deleted tests acting as an accidental drain window) to 15/16, adjacent. THAT IS THE TRIGGER. The race is the cause and is still in the runtime; the test-side fix (every test awaits the reply landing in app-db before asserting and before `stop-server!`) is on main and changed no runtime code.

BLAST RADIUS ON EXISTING TESTS — MEASURED, and the answer is that NOTHING PINS THE CURRENT SEMANTICS. Every `deftest`, `dispatch-sync`, `reg-http-interceptor`, `clear-*` and reply-wait line was listed across `http_interceptors_test.clj` (27 deftests), its CLJS twin (11), `http_reply_tail_test.clj` (4), `http_reply_tail_cljs_test.cljs` (1) and `http_managed_test.clj` (68). EVERY registration precedes its `dispatch-sync`. Exactly two tests mutate the registry between two requests inside one test — `clear-http-interceptor-unregisters` (`:438`) and `clear-all-http-interceptors-empties-every-frame-chain` (`:788`) — and BOTH ALREADY AWAIT THE FIRST REPLY BEFORE MUTATING (`:461`, `:826`), so both pass identically under either semantics. Codex confirmed independently that the reverse-order and ctx-correlation tests register first (`:1014`, `:1042`). No test registers or clears mid-flight. The ONLY in-flight registry mutation anywhere in the suite is the fixture's post-dispose `clear-all-http-interceptors!` — the leak vector, not a pin. The two conformance fixtures that covered interceptors (`spec/conformance/fixtures/http-interceptor-before-transforms.edn`, `…-clear.edn`) were DELETED in `c905e8dbb1`; nothing under `spec/conformance/` references http interceptors now. Control: a search for `interceptor` under that tree still returns 11 files, so the instrument works — the http ones are genuinely gone.

TRAP 1 — THE CAPTURED CHAIN MUST NOT RIDE ON THE `middleware-ctx`. That map is USER-VISIBLE: it is the `ctx` argument every `:after` receives, and Spec 014's ctx table (`:836-843`) enumerates its keys. Putting a `:chain` key there leaks runtime internals into a public contract. It belongs on the INTERNAL normalised ctx (`handlers.cljc:383-384`) — the same map that already carries `:issuance`, `:request-id` and `:middleware-ctx` and is threaded to the transport at `:424`. (Note the interaction with conflict 1: the value is CAPTURED before `run-interceptor-chain!` at `:343` and STORED on the internal ctx at `:383-384`; those are two different moments and both matter.)

TRAP 2 — THE SYNTHETIC-CALLER GUARD. `run-after-then-dispatch!` currently keys the entire `:after` walk off the presence of `middleware-ctx` (`middleware.cljc:500-502`: `(if middleware-ctx (run-after-chain! …) reply-payload)`). Synthetic and test-path callers legitimately arrive with no ctx and are skipped — keep them transparent. For a caller with a ctx but no captured chain, see conflict 2: migrate the caller, no fallback.

TWO CORRECT PREMISES WORTH KEEPING, from Codex, that stop the implementer over-reaching. (a) SNAPSHOTTING DOES NOT FREEZE THE WORLD — a captured fn can still read current app-db, deref an atom, or call a redefined var, and that is programmer-controlled behaviour we want. The guarantee is stable MEMBERSHIP, ORDER and STORED FUNCTION VALUES across the two walks; it is not request determinism and not isolation from logout. (b) FRAME ISOLATION ALREADY HOLDS for distinct frame-ids — both walks select by `frame-id`, so mutating frame B cannot touch frame A. The real hazard is REUSE OF THE SAME ID, which is what fixtures do. Also: a captured vector needs NO deep copy and NO lock — the atom holds an immutable persistent value and updates install a new one, so retaining the selected vector preserves its slots by structural sharing. The only cost is holding those function references for the request's lifetime.

HISTORY, since `rf2-uheqq` (cited throughout the code comments as the origin bead) IS NOT IN THE TRACKER — treat those citations as historical code comments, not resolvable references. Codex recovered the record: commit `264dc7b352d076749ddaf0e3ed52e2a06fd0b2eb` (PR #2333) introduced the paired-ctx contract, AND ITS DESCRIPTION DOES NOT CHOOSE LIVE RESPONSE-TIME RESOLUTION. That supports the reading both reviewers reached independently: live `:after` resolution was never a design decision, it is the obvious spelling of "get the chain" written without the timing question being asked.
=== DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE — DO NOT GOLD-PLATE THESE BACK IN ===
  - NO id-only capture with live fn resolution (rejected option C1) and NO clear-filtering / "honour mid-flight clears" (rejected C2). Both trade a clean statable rule for a convenience nobody asked for. If "a cleared interceptor stops acting immediately" is ever wanted, it goes on top of this as a deliberate documented exception.
  - NO registry generation counter, NO public option or flag, NO cancellation protocol, NO hot-reload policy, NO logout/teardown machinery. Request cancellation and app session logic keep their own responsibilities.
  - NO defensive rewrite of the `:after` docs or of the §Middleware use cases telling authors to write `(when-let [started …])`. That was the price of the REJECTED option B and is exactly the ergonomic tax on every `:after` author that this ruling avoids paying.
  - NO nag diagnostics or warnings when a chain changes mid-flight. The contract makes it a non-event.
  - NO restoration of the deleted conformance fixtures, and no new test framework.
  - Do NOT re-derive the `ns-interns` ordering, re-run the 20-trial reproduction, or measure the CLJS arithmetic divergence.
  - Do NOT chase frame-teardown clearing: verified that no production caller of `clear-http-interceptor*` exists beyond the two public arities of `clear-http-interceptor`, so teardown does not currently clear a frame's interceptors despite what the seam's docstring implies (`middleware.cljc:211-215`). Out of scope here; file separately if it ever matters.

=== NEXT STEPS — one worker, one PR ===
  1. Capture the resolved frame's interceptor VECTOR (function-bearing slots, not ids) immediately before `run-interceptor-chain!` at `handlers.cljc:343`; pass it explicitly to the `:before` walker in place of the `middleware.cljc:411` deref, and store it on the INTERNAL normalised ctx beside `:middleware-ctx` (`handlers.cljc:383-384`, threaded at `:424`).
  2. Take it as an argument in `run-after-chain!` / `run-after-then-dispatch!` in place of the `middleware.cljc:455` deref; thread it through `dispatch-reply!`'s destructure (`transport.cljc:208-210`, `:218`) and the canned path (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:140-145`; the canned entry points and route stub share the before-helper at `:252`, `:266`, `:415`). Migrate the resources consumer at `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_request_decoration_cljs_test.cljc:102` or preserve `run-request-chain`'s return contract. Empty snapshot = real snapshot; no live fallback; synthetic no-middleware callers stay transparent.
  3. Confirm the key survives the retry handoff (`transport.cljc:1194`, `run-attempt!` at `:1586`) and that `:before` is not re-run per attempt.
  4. Spec 014 §Chain order and frame scope gains ONE bullet. Suggested wording, tightened from both reviewers: "Chain resolution is at issue time. Each managed request captures its frame's HTTP interceptor chain immediately before running `:before`, and its response walks the SAME captured registrations in reverse; retries retain it. Registering, replacing or clearing an interceptor affects only requests that capture their chain afterwards, including changes made from inside an interceptor. This is what makes the ctx-carried-from-`:before` contract above sound: an `:after` only ever runs for a request whose `:before` chain it was part of." It does not promise an `:after` for a response already suppressed by the existing failure, cancellation or stale-reply rules — leave those untouched. Fix the `run-after-chain!` docstring (`middleware.cljc:440-443`) and body comment (`:458-460`) to say chain as well as ctx.
  5. TESTS — the minimum that DISCRIMINATES, nothing more. (i) Issue request A under the old chain; register/replace/clear; issue B under the new chain; release both; assert A walked its original functions, ctx and order and B the new ones — this is the bead's acceptance criterion, and it must use a controlled outstanding response, NOT sleeps and NOT fixture ordering. (ii) Register from INSIDE a `:before` and assert it does not join that request — this is the one that distinguishes real capture from late capture at `:383`. (iii) Start from an EMPTY chain, which defeats a live-fallback bug. (iv) One retry-handoff assertion. (v) One canned-path case, since that path changes. Put them in the shared contract where the existing tests already run on both CLJ and CLJS rather than building a new matrix; keep the reply-tail exception tests as they are.
  6. SEQUENCING: `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` is not on the hot-zone list but this PR touches it — check for a concurrent Spec 014 worker before dispatching. The code side is confined to `implementation/http/`, which is isolated.
  7. NOT DISPATCHED by this ruling. The "DO NOT dispatch until the ruling lands" hold in the description is now DISCHARGED — this note is the ruling. Dispatchable at P3.
close_reason:
Delivered by PR #9502, merged as trunk cb1f5a07f6 — 7 files, +529/-64. Verified on the merged trunk myself, and I had to rebase before believing my own greps: the local fast-forward aborted with "Not possible to fast-forward" (the racing-audit-push case, where the .beads remedy is inert), so my first verification read a STALE tree and returned zeros. After rebasing: capture-chain reads 3 hits in middleware.cljc, the live-registry "reverse (get @interceptors" resolution reads 0, and spec/014 carries the "Chain resolution is at issue time" bullet at 1. Recording the sequence because a stale-tree grep is a false zero that looks exactly like a failed merge.

THE SABOTAGE PROOF IS THE PART THAT MATTERS, and it is the strongest verification anyone produced this session. The worker committed first, then planted the OLD live-registry resolution back into run-after-chain! with the anchor match count read as 1 beforehand and the blob hash moving, so not a no-op. All four shared-contract tests went red at exit 1 WITH PREDICTED VALUES rather than merely failing: test (i) returned [[:three nil] [:two :marked]] against an expected [[:two :marked] [:one :marked]], which is exactly what "A walked the LIVE chain and an interceptor that never ran a :before for it got a nil mark" looks like. Restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object.

AND THE BLAST RADIUS CORROBORATED THE RULING'S OWN CLAIM: of 29 live-transport tests, exactly TWO reddened under the plant — the two the worker added. That is independent evidence for the ruling's "nothing pins the current semantics", measured rather than asserted.

TEST (ii) CANNOT PASS BY TIMING, which was my explicit requirement because this bead exists BECAUSE a timing-shaped flake hid a real defect. It is entirely synchronous — no transport, no timer, no async. A :before registers an interceptor mid-walk and the assertion is on the :after log's VALUE: a capture at the wrong point puts the joiner in the snapshot, so its :after runs with a nil mark. The failure is a wrong value, never a slow one, and elapsed time cannot change it. Every test clears the frame chain itself and names its frame explicitly, so nothing depends on test order either.

THE RULING'S file:line CITATIONS WERE RE-MEASURED WITH ONE NIT FOUND: the test_support.cljc call the ruling gives as 140-145 actually spans to 147. Everything else matched exactly, including the ruling's own control that ":chain reads exactly 2 in middleware.cljc".

THE CAPTURE SITS WHERE IT HAD TO: on the line immediately before run-interceptor-chain!, NOT at the :383 ctx site — capturing at the ctx site is the "late capture" bug test (ii) exists to catch. The registry deref is removed from both walkers with no fallback, and run-request-chain's return contract is preserved so the resources consumer needed no change at all.

ONE ADDITION TO THE RULING'S SPEC WORDING, which I endorse: a final sentence making explicit that this fixes WHICH chain a response walks, not WHETHER a response is delivered — a reply already suppressed by the failure, cancellation or stale-reply rules stays suppressed. The ruling said that in its prose; the worker put it in the normative bullet.

title: [implementation/ssr-ring] Replace Location case-insensitively when materializing redirects
description:
Source snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:225-239 folds application headers case-insensitively, then inserts redirect target with a case-sensitive (assoc "Location" target). headers.clj preserves the first spelling. response.cljc:864-882 records a redirect without clearing existing header pairs. Thus an ordinary event with {:fx [[:rf.server/set-header {:name "location" :value "/old"}] [:rf.server/redirect {:location "/new"}]]} yields both "location" -> "/old" and "Location" -> "/new" in the Ring response. Uppercase-first spelling happens to be replaced; lowercase-first is not.

Expected: the documented redirect precedence yields one logical Location header containing /new, independent of header casing. Actual: duplicate conflicting singleton headers leave redirect choice to the HTTP adapter/client and can navigate to stale /old. Both ssr-handler and stream-handler use this shared materializer. docs/ssr/response.md:15 explicitly promises case-insensitive header names; :42 describes status plus Location.

Smallest repair: remove existing Location spellings using the existing case-insensitive strip helper before adding the redirect target. Preserve unrelated headers/cookies/status/body behavior. This is not new validation or safe-redirect policy.

Validation: source-only exact public-fx-to-materializer trace; no HTTP/runtime/suite run. Active+closed title/description and redirect memories searched, no matching repair. Existing redirect tests assert the normal empty-header case only. Latest mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d has no relevant materializer drift.
acceptance_criteria: Materializer and public-handler coverage with existing location, LOCATION, and Location spellings plus a new redirect yields exactly one case-insensitive Location entry set to the new target. Unrelated headers/cookies retained; streaming and non-streaming redirect bodies remain empty.
close_reason: PR #9377, commit 015abf53b7. Premise re-verified at tip before acting: pipeline.clj really did (cond-> target (assoc "Location" ...)) after the case-insensitive fold. ssr-response->ring-response now strips every casing with the existing rf.ssr.ring.headers/strip-header helper — the same rule headers->ring-map+content-type-override already applies to the :content-type override — before associating the canonical Location. Scoped to the arm that HAS a target: the no-target branch adds nothing so it removes nothing, or an app-set Location would become a 3xx with no target at all. Both ssr-handler and stream-handler share this materialiser. Tests in pipeline_materialiser_test.clj: lowercase, LOCATION, Location and LoCaTiOn spellings each yield exactly one case-insensitive Location entry carrying the new target with no stale value surviving under any key; a repeated-Location vector fold is cleared rather than conj'd onto; unrelated headers, a multi-valued Vary fold, cookies, status and the empty body are all retained; a target-less redirect leaves an app-set Location alone; and public-handler coverage drives the documented fx sequence ([:rf.server/set-header {:name "location" :value "/old"}] then [:rf.server/redirect {:location "/new"}]) through ssr-handler and asserts one Location on the wire at /new. Red before: 16 failures. Green after. implementation/ssr-ring JVM suite 240 tests / 1211 assertions, exit 0. docs/ssr/response.md already promised case-insensitive header names, so no doc change was needed.

title: [implementation/ssr] Preserve a leading newline in preformatted hiccup text
description:
Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; relevant source unchanged at mayor HEAD a7b6793a0d6a0614a1cc64d5988afa93d1e4c490. Ordinary supported input: (ssr/render-to-string [:pre "\ncode"]) (equally, a shared .cljc view returning that form). Expected browser textContent is "\ncode", matching the authored single string and the client Reagent/React rendering. Actual emitted markup is "
\ncode
", whose first LF is consumed by the HTML parser, leaving "code". [:textarea "\ntext"] has the same content loss. This is text preservation, not a request for the hiccup emitter to adopt the separate semantic-tree prop vocabulary. Exact source trace: - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:752-779 emits a native start tag, emit-children, and end tag with no leading-LF compensation. emit-element:592 escapes the original text but does not compensate for the surrounding element. - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:368-404 has a parallel walk-dom-tag branch with the same omission, affecting progressive shell/continuation markup too. - The same artifact already implements and documents the required browser rule in ui_tree.cljc:520-583: pre/listing/textarea discard one initial LF; leading-newline-compensation prefixes one for a single leading-LF string. Its semantic-tree emission applies that helper at 946/957 and focused tests at test/re_frame/ssr/emit_ui_tree_cljs_test.cljc:484-536 pin it. Neither hiccup path uses it. - Spec011:229-254 describes the hiccup emitter as text-preserving per-position HTML output and supports shared .cljc Reagent/server views (177-193). The structural render hash is computed from authored data rather than parsed HTML, so a correct equal tree hash does not detect this dropped character. Impact: a server-rendered preformatted/code or text-area string loses its authored initial blank line until client rendering, with a text hydration mismatch on an otherwise identical tree. Smallest repair: share the bounded newline compensation rule with BOTH hiccup emitters for the ordinary single-string content case. Preserve raw-text rules and the existing semantic-tree distinction for multi-child bodies; no general DOM normalizer or API change is needed. Dedupe: active+closed searches newline/description newline and relevant memories; no matching current record. Historical rf2-0spji/rf2-ib4fd are not present in bd; their source comments concern sole trusted-HTML semantic-tree content, which is not the plain hiccup path here. Validation limits: source-only exact emitter and HTML-parser-contract trace, cross-checked against the artifact's existing semantic-tree helper and tests. No JVM/CLJS build, browser, or suite execution.
acceptance_criteria: For one LF-leading string under pre/listing/textarea, parse emitted non-streaming and streaming HTML and assert textContent matches the original string and the client rendering. Cover no-leading-LF as a control, preserve raw-text handling and the existing multi-child rule, and share the compensation rather than creating divergent rosters.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #9377 (2026-09-07), landed 0f3f7c9fdc1606760b359b2120c9aa2b9a1d038d: the shared leading-LF runtime repair is delivered; reopen this exact owner for its outstanding observation-level acceptance and the repair's incorrect spec carry. Preserve original acceptance unchanged. The acceptance explicitly says to parse emitted non-streaming AND streaming HTML and assert textContent matches the original string and client rendering. New implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_hiccup_newline_test.clj:54-78 instead strips tags with a regex, reads the production newline-eating-tags roster, manually drops one LF, and manually unescapes five entities. It never invokes an HTML parser or a client renderer. Its docstring honestly calls this a parse model, but assertions labelled DOM/textContent and PR's 'parses emitted ... HTML' summary overstate what the witness observes. A model built from the production roster cannot independently establish the browser/parser boundary this owner's acceptance names. Keep useful byte/unit controls, and add the bounded existing adapter/browser or HTML-parser-backed test that actually parses both emitters' output and compares the real node textContent with the authored/client string. Include uncompensated markup as a negative control; no general parser implementation or new framework API is requested. Also correct spec/011-SSR.md:260's new leading-LF paragraph: it says React neither patches nor reports this TEXT divergence, calling it the same blind spot as attributes. The linked section at :864-866 says exactly the opposite for text: text-content mismatches are recoverable divergences delivered via onRecoverableError; attribute-only mismatches are the omitted class. Keep the valid point that hashing the authored tree alone cannot see an emitter/parser text change, but do not erase the existing React-native text-adoption detection claim. This is an internal contradiction at the exact landed revision, independently checkable without assuming an untested browser result. All fifteen changed head and CI blobs match landed. Actual SSR, production SSR, Ring and ssr-node CI passed; no additional runtime defect is claimed and no new full/browser suite was run in this audit. The three other owners rf2-8v89, rf2-c1b1 and rf2-kirm are delivered. Original title/description/criteria and previous notes are retained; no duplicate Bead. Merged-PR audit #9391 (4f08f642f9f0a63c0949155b3d61f04158c6b36c): the misleading DOM/parser labels and Spec 011 text-versus-attribute contradiction are corrected, and the model no longer reads the production element roster. Those improvements are accepted. Reopen this same owner only for its still-undelivered original acceptance: parse both non-streaming and streaming output and compare real textContent with authored/client rendering, with uncompensated markup as the negative control. The original criteria and #9377 audit note explicitly require that observation; the note did not offer renaming the model as an alternative completion. The new test namespace instead explicitly says it invokes neither parser nor client renderer and closes the residual on the rename. Correctly labelling a model does not execute the specified acceptance. Retain the byte pins and literal-roster improvement, add the bounded parser-backed or existing browser/adapter witness in the framework test tree, and remove the claim that this observation was completed by relabelling. No production behavior change, shipping dependency or new API is required by this note; a test-only dependency or existing browser lane can be chosen within the original scope. Original description, criteria and prior note remain authoritative and unchanged. PR #9403 (worker/ssrfix-a, branch head bcfbfaef04) delivers the reopened observation-level acceptance by PARSING, not by relabelling. Route chosen: (a) a test-only HTML parser on this artefact's own :test and :slow-test aliases -- nu.validator/htmlparser 1.4.16, one 417 KiB jar, no transitive deps, nothing under src/ requires it. :paths and the top-level :deps are untouched, so no shipping dependency and no production behaviour change. Both aliases, because :slow-test does not compose onto :test (unlike :prod-gate) and the runner loads every test namespace before it filters vars. NOT jsoup, and this is a measured finding worth keeping: jsoup 1.22.1's HtmlTreeBuilderState consumes the leading LF for pre and listing but NOT for textarea, so parses to "\n\nt". A textarea witness written against jsoup would have pinned jsoup's conformance gap as the browser's behaviour -- the exact class of error this bead was reopened for, reached through a different door. nu.validator/htmlparser is a port of the HTML5 tree-construction algorithm (the parser behind the W3C/WHATWG validator), gets all three roster elements right, and yields an org.w3c.dom tree, so the witness reads Node.getTextContent() -- the browser contract's own vocabulary. modelled-text-content is gone; parsed-text-content replaces it at every site. New deftest server-parse-matches-authored-and-client-text states the acceptance once: for pre/listing/textarea the non-streaming emitter, the streaming shell walk AND react-dom/server's own measured bytes all parse to the authored string, with the uncompensated pre-repair markup as the negative control. The client-rendering leg reduces to the authored string because React's client path sets a lone string child as a DOM text node (no HTML parse on the client), which the test states explicitly. Held: the roster literal stays a literal (the namespace still does not read rf.ssr.html-helpers/newline-eating-tags; one-roster-one-rule still pins production against it from the other side, and the parser shares a roster with neither). Raw-text and multi-child rules preserved, and now OBSERVED through the parser rather than only pinned as bytes. Compensation still shared -- one roster, one rule, three paths; no second roster created. Two React-parity divergences the parser exposed, now pinned as such rather than left implicit: a leading CRLF loses both characters (React tests charAt(0)==='\n'; the parser normalises CRLF->LF in input preprocessing and then eats it, so 
\r\ncode
parses to "code"), and a multi-child body loses its LF (
\na\nb multi-child parses to "ab"). Both pre-existing, both react-dom parity, neither changed here.

title: xray: rename facade load-theme -> load-theme! under §Naming, no roster row (ruled A; gates the alpha tag)
description:
RULED 2026-09-06 17:26:59 AUSEST (option A; delegated ruling on the decision dossier — the full RULING note and the dossier itself are in this bead's notes): RENAME `day8.re-frame2-xray.core/load-theme` -> `load-theme!` under spec/Conventions.md §Naming bucket 3. No `load-*` roster row, no spec/Conventions.md edit, no alias or stub. This bead is the implementation work item; rf2-kmqx3 (the first alpha tag) depends on it. The RULING note carries the touch list (about ten files, census with line numbers at ruling time), the sequencing (spec/API.md is hot-zone; the manifest EDNs are shared with rf2-kuky.* PRs; PR #9314 has MERGED so docs/xray/api/mount-control.md is free), the gates by path and the acceptance. Options (b) roster-it and (c) fold-into-configure! below are REJECTED. Everything below this line is the original question, preserved verbatim.

---- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION (filed 2026-09-04, preserved verbatim) ----

RULING NEEDED: the Xray facade's `load-theme` is the only export on any of the three facades that mutates without a `!`, and the repair is ambiguous between two shapes. Raised by the rf2-ar67 facade sweep (Xray slice), which recorded it `:keep` with the uncertainty in its `:justification` rather than choosing — per the CONTESTED clause, and the same posture rf2-i6kh took for canonical-hash / make-run-artifact / run-artifact?.

PLACEMENT IS NOT IN QUESTION. `load-theme` belongs on the facade: tools/xray/spec/API.md §Canonical rows it, and editor-driven palette sync is an ordinary host workflow reached in one call. This bead is about the SPELLING only.

## The measurement (2026-09-05, at tip 42f2c8f89a)

day8.re-frame2-xray.core has 16 public exports. Eleven mutate and are banged
(init!, open!, open-overlay!, close!, toggle!, popout!, set-target-frame!,
focus!, configure!, set-auto-open!, set-editor!, set-egress-profile! -- twelve
counting focus!). Three are reads and correctly carry no bang (status,
target-frame, valid-focus-panels). `load-theme` is the ONE outlier: it mutates
and carries no bang.

The mutation is real, not incidental. `load-theme` calls
`global-styles/set-host-theme-css!`, which installs or replaces a dedicated
<style> block appended last to <head>. The OWNING fn carries the bang; the
facade alias drops it. By spec/Conventions.md §Naming: when does a surface
carry `!`? that mechanism is bucket 3 -- "process-level state mutation outside
the registrar" -- which mandates the bang.

## Why the sweep did not just rename it

Because `load-*` appears on NO row of the closed lifecycle-verb roster
(spec/Conventions.md §Lifecycle-verb law). The roster is clear+ / unregister-
/ destroy- / reset- / unsubscribe / watch- / attach!-detach! / mount!-unmount!
/ open!-close! / configure! / describe-config-current-config. That section
says in terms:

  "The roster is CLOSED: a surface that fits none of these is evidence the law
   is missing a verb -- file a bead against this section rather than coining
   dispose- / teardown- / shutdown- / a fresh un-*. Adding a verb is a Spec
   change to this table, not a per-author call."

So there are at least two defensible repairs and the choice is explicitly not
a worker's to make:

  (a) BANG IT -- rename to `load-theme!`. Minimal, mechanical, closes the
      inconsistency, and treats `load-*` as an unrostered-but-acceptable verb.

  (b) ROSTER IT -- add a `load-*` row to the §Lifecycle-verb law table stating
      what the verb owns and its bang posture, then spell the var to match.
      Heavier, but it is what the section's own escape clause prescribes, and
      it would cover future sibling surfaces.

  (c) FOLD IT INTO configure! -- a CSS string is plain data, and
      §Configuration surfaces bucket 1 routes "a global runtime knob with a
      plain-data value" to configure!. Weakest of the three (the call is an
      immediate runtime override rather than boot config), listed for
      completeness.

## Why it is worth settling before the tag

A rename after the first meaningful external alpha is a consumer-visible
break, and that is precisely the cost spec/Conventions.md §Facade policy's
audit obligation exists to avoid ("The audit is the one cheap window to settle
placement; after it, moves cost consumer breakage"). rf2-ar67 deliberately did
NOT add a blocking edge onto rf2-kmqx3, because its own discriminator says a
contested row is kept and does NOT hold the tag. If Mike wants the spelling
settled first, the edge is `bd dep add rf2-kmqx3 <this-bead>`.

## Blast radius if (a) or (b) is chosen

Small, but it crosses two fences, which is the other reason rf2-ar67 did not
execute it:

  - tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs  (the def + its docstring)
  - tools/xray/spec/API.md                        (2 sites: the §Canonical
                                                   code block, the §Wider
                                                   public surface table row)
  - tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/core_cljs_test.cljs (4 call sites)
  - spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn + spec/api-manifest.edn (the row; the
    justification text already discusses this question and would be rewritten)
  - docs/xray/api/reference.md and docs/xray/api/mount-control.md -- OUTSIDE
    the rf2-ar67 fence, which is why the rename was not executed there.

SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FOUND WHILE MEASURING THIS, worth its own bead if
Mike wants it fixed independently: docs/xray/api/mount-control.md still says
the runtime CSS-swap surface "is not yet wired" and that calling load-theme
emits `:rf.warning/xray-load-theme-not-yet-implemented`. That is STALE --
rf2-ee38b.2 wired it through global-styles/set-host-theme-css!, and
tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/core_cljs_test.cljs asserts that NO such
warning fires. The doc contradicts a live test today, independently of how the
spelling question is resolved.

## Gates for whichever repair lands

implementation/scripts/api-manifest: `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen
--check` then `clojure -M:test`; `clojure -M -m
re-frame.api-manifest.xray-spec-check`; tools/xray `clojure -M:test`;
implementation `npm run test:cljs` (the CLJS probe now holds
day8.re-frame2-xray.core FULLY-ROWED in both directions per rf2-ar67, so a
rename without the matching row edit goes RED -- which is the safety net that
makes this rename cheap to attempt).

DECISION: Option A — rename `day8.re-frame2-xray.core/load-theme` to `load-theme!` under spec/Conventions.md §Naming alone (bucket 3, "process-level state mutation outside the registrar"). NO `load-*` row is added to §Lifecycle-verb law's roster and spec/Conventions.md is NOT edited. No alias, no throwing stub, no deprecation window: pre-alpha, zero consumers outside tools/xray, spec/ and docs/xray, a redundant spelling is deleted. Behaviour unchanged.

THIS BEAD IS THE WORK ITEM. It is a task, not a decision: it stays OPEN, its title is amended to the imperative form, and a RULED header is prepended to its description (the original description is preserved verbatim beneath it). No separate implementation bead is filed. rf2-kmqx3 (the first v0.0.1.alpha tag) now DEPENDS ON this bead (`bd dep add rf2-kmqx3 rf2-7nk1`) so the tag cannot be cut on the old spelling — the tag is already blocked on rf2-uelji and rf2-fo4ng, so the edge costs nothing today.

REASONS, anchored in the posture and the dossier's evidence:
1. The mechanism decides, and it is unambiguous. The facade delegates to `global-styles/set-host-theme-css!` (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/global_styles.cljs:1656), which does createElement/appendChild on document.head, or set!s an existing node's textContent, or .remove()s it — and the OWNER already carries the bang. §Naming calls itself "principled, not stylistic", decides "by mechanism, not by feel", and says its four buckets are exhaustive for API.md surfaces. Posture: a minimal, ergonomic, low-hidden-context API — on a facade where 15 of 16 vars teach "no bang = read", the one silent exception taxes every reader (human or AI) who learned the rule from the other fifteen.
2. The roster objection proves too much. Eight of this facade's twelve banged mutators (init!, toggle!, popout!, focus!, set-target-frame!, set-auto-open!, set-editor!, set-egress-profile!) use verbs on no roster row and nobody proposes unbanging them; and the on-record precedent at spec/API.md:1017 (register-trace-listener -> register-listener!, "bang form matches the side-effecting nature of listener registration") settled the identical no-bang-to-bang question with no roster row added. The roster governs WHICH lifecycle verb a surface takes; §Naming governs WHETHER it carries `!`. Adding a bang to an existing verb creates no new operation family.
3. The alternatives fail the posture. B (rename + a `load-*` roster row) is a Conventions change for one var whose row would restate set-*'s mechanism — over-engineering — and by the mayor's routing it would wait on rf2-kuky.4 and rf2-uimu. C (keep, document the exception) is not free: three documents currently advertise an open question and would have to be rewritten to say the spelling is settled the wrong way, and the only rationale available ("named while a stub", fae8d54d2e) is historical, which §Naming's mechanism wording does not admit. D (fold into configure!) relocates a working one-liner into a new config key plus a key-to-DOM apply path, for zero callers.

SECOND REVIEWER (Codex): also recommends A — FOLLOWED. Two qualifications, both accepted, both narrowing the ruling rather than changing it. (i) The roster does call itself complete and explicitly includes facade APIs, so the dossier's "the roster has never been read that way" is too strong. The ruling is therefore the NARROW one Codex proposed — keep the established `load-theme` verb; spell this DOM mutation `load-theme!` under §Naming — and is NOT a licence to coin new lifecycle verbs; rf2-uimu's and rf2-kuky.4's roster and boot questions are not redesigned here. (ii) Folding into configure! is technically viable (tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md allows post-mount rebind), so "boot-only" is not the objection to D; the objection is that it needs a new accepted key and a key-to-DOM path where the existing call already does the whole job. D stays rejected. Codex also reported, and I re-verified with `gh pr view 9314` at ruling time, that the dossier's scheduling obstacle has cleared: PR #9314 is MERGED (2026-09-06T06:27:42Z, commit cf8d8beeb6) and rf2-fwf5 is closed.

CROSS-REFERENCE rf2-uimu (open, held by the mayor until rf2-kuky.4 is ruled; NOT edited by this ruling — a sibling agent is ruling it). Its dossier says one Conventions edit answers both beads. Recorded here: THIS ruling needs NO roster change and NO Conventions edit, so rf2-uimu's eventual Conventions PR and this rename cannot collide, and this bead does not wait on rf2-uimu or rf2-kuky.4. # rf2-7nk1 — Spell the Xray facade's `load-theme` as `load-theme!`, or write down why it is the one unbanged mutator

**Decision needed from Mike:** does `day8.re-frame2-xray.core/load-theme` — which installs a `<style>` block into `<head>` — take the `!` that Conventions §Naming bucket 3 gives every other process-level mutator, and if so, does the Lifecycle-verb roster need a `load-*` row first?
**Recommendation:** **A** — rename to `load-theme!` under §Naming alone; the roster does not govern the bang axis and needs no new row.
**Bead:** rf2-7nk1 (task, P3, open) · **Epic:** none — `discovered-from` rf2-ar67 (closed, PR #9210) · **Written:** 2026-09-06 16:28:23 AUSEST at tip 6d513ba07f

## The problem

The Xray facade has 16 public vars (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs:71-303`). Twelve mutate and carry `!`; three are reads and do not (`status`, `target-frame`, `valid-focus-panels`); one mutates and does not:

```clojure
;; core.cljs:259-271 — the facade today
(defn load-theme
  "... installs a dedicated <style> block appended LAST to <head> ... Idempotent:
   successive calls REPLACE the override in place; nil / blank clears it ..."
  [css-string]
  (global-styles/set-host-theme-css! css-string)   ; the OWNER is banged (global_styles.cljs:1656)
  nil)

;; what a host writes today                          ;; under option A
(xray/load-theme editor-palette-css)                 (xray/load-theme! editor-palette-css)
```

The mutation is real: `set-host-theme-css!` (`theme/global_styles.cljs:1656-1687`) does `createElement` / `appendChild` on `js/document.head`, or `set!`s an existing node's `textContent`, or `.remove`s it. That is §Naming bucket 3 — "process-level state mutation outside the registrar" — verbatim, and §Naming calls itself "principled, not stylistic".

**How it got this way.** The name predates the mutation. At `fae8d54d2e` (rf2-13bx9, Causa era) `load-theme` took `[_css-string]`, emitted `:rf.warning/causa-load-theme-not-yet-implemented` and returned nil — a stub whose only effect was a trace, so no bang was warranted. `e4d5cafb84` (rf2-ee38b.2) wired the DOM mutation, banged the new owner, and left the facade spelling untouched. The spelling itself comes from the UX finding (`tools/xray/spec/findings/xray-ux-design.md:407`: "Settings → Theme → Load CSS … `(rf.xray/load-theme css-string)`"). Nobody decided the bang off; it was never decided on.

**Who it hurts.** The reader who infers the rule from the other fifteen: on this facade "no bang" has meant "read" every time. An AI agent or host author writing boot code sees `(xray/load-theme css)` beside `(xray/set-editor! :cursor)` and reads the first as pure. That is hidden context in a facade whose whole job is to be legible without opening the owner.

**Why the sweep left it (the case for not renaming, stated fairly).** rf2-ar67 recorded `:keep` because `load-*` is on no row of §Lifecycle-verb law's closed roster, whose escape clause says "adding a verb is a Spec change to this table, not a per-author call". Two further pieces of counter-evidence Mike should weigh:

1. **The mayor already routed this jointly.** rf2-uimu's notes (2026-09-05, mayor verification): "rule kuky.4 first, then uimu+7nk1 together on whatever survives … one amendment to the Lifecycle-verb law answers both". rf2-uimu is HELD on that release condition, and rf2-kuky.4 (open, P3 RULING) is unruled. Coupling this bead to that chain means it waits.
2. **The bead's uniqueness claim is Xray-true, not repo-true.** `re-frame.core/init-platform` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2806`, "Set the host-wide active-platform marker", delegating to `interop/set-platform!`) has the identical shape — banged owner, unbanged facade — on the `:advanced` tier. It sits in rf2-kuky.4's prune table with 0 consumers, so its fate is decided there; but an "exception" written here would have to cover it or explain why not.

Against the roster argument, one measurement. The roster's nine rows (`spec/Conventions.md:1265-1275`) are:

    clear-*  unregister-*  destroy-*  reset-*  unsubscribe  watch-*  attach!/detach!  mount!/unmount!  open!/close!

plus `configure!` in its own subsection. Of the twelve banged mutators on this same facade, **eight** use verbs on no roster row either — `init!`, `toggle!`, `popout!`, `focus!`, `set-target-frame!`, `set-auto-open!`, `set-editor!`, `set-egress-profile!` — and nobody has proposed unbanging them. The roster has never been read as an exhaustive facade-verb list; it governs *which teardown/lifecycle verb* a surface takes.

*Whether* a surface takes `!` is §Naming's axis, and §Naming says its four buckets "are exhaustive for the surfaces in API.md". The precedent is on record at `spec/API.md:1017`: `register-trace-listener` (no bang) → `register-listener!`, "bang form matches the side-effecting nature of listener registration" — and no `register-*` roster row was added then either.

## The decision

**Which one:** **A** rename to `load-theme!` under §Naming, no roster change · **B** rename AND add a `load-*` row to the roster · **C** keep `load-theme` and record it as a documented exception · **D** fold it into `configure!` as a `:rf.xray/*` key.

The decisive evidence is the current [facade](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs) and [style owner](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/global_styles.cljs): the facade immediately delegates to `set-host-theme-css!`, which creates a style node, replaces its text, or removes it. It adds a clear effect signal to the existing one-call editor-palette workflow without making the trusted host programmer learn another namespace or configuration key. Second, folding into `configure!` is technically viable: [Xray Configuration](../../tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md) explicitly allows post-mount calls for live rebind. The practical objection is that CSS application would need a new accepted key and a path from that key to the DOM, while the existing call already performs the entire job. The strongest case for keeping the design is proportionality: `load-theme` already sounds imperative, its docstring explains the effect, and no failing host workflow was found. The missing bang is not a runtime bug or a promise of purity being enforced by ClojureScript. I still favour the rename because the current public surface supplies a consistent local convention and the pre-alpha correction is small. I would not turn this into a new release campaign merely to enforce punctuation.

title: hic: pilot workspaces 404 on every deep link - no :push-state fallback in the shadow-cljs template, and workspace.md never mentions RealWorld's /realworld base path
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 ~17:45 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. Two defects with one cause; filed
together because the fix is one change to workspace.md's project-file templates.

(1) THE REALWORLD EXAMPLE IS SERVED FROM A SUB-PATH AND workspace.md NEVER SAYS SO.
routing.cljs:254 wires (routing/with-base-path routing/history-url-strategy
"/realworld"), and its own docstring says "this example is served from a sub-path".
The workspace serves app/public at the ROOT of :dev-http, and step 5 tells the
operator to open http://localhost:8080 - a URL outside the app's own base path.
The consequence is visible the moment anything is clicked: the app's links
navigate to /realworld/tag/clojure, /realworld/login and so on, which is a
different address space from the one the page was loaded at.

(2) NEITHER PILOT'S :dev-http HAS A PUSH-STATE FALLBACK, so every one of those
URLs 404s on reload. Measured on the assembled workspaces:
  http://localhost:8080/realworld       404
  http://localhost:8080/realworld/      404
  http://localhost:8081/board           404
  http://localhost:8081/index.html      200
  http://localhost:8081/nope            404
shadow-cljs' :dev-http takes :push-state/index for exactly this; workspace.md's
template is {:dev-http {8080 "public"}} with nothing else, and the published
installation page (00-installation.md:83) prints the same bare line, so a pilot
reading the documentation finds no answer either.

WHY A PILOT MEETS THIS EARLY AND MISREADS IT. Outcome 4 is hot reload - "change a
migrated view with the build running and record what survived". Reloading the
browser after navigating anywhere inside either app lands on a 404 from the dev
server, which reads as the framework's routing being broken rather than as the
dev server lacking a fallback. rf2-nvcp's own investigation hit the same wall
from the other side: linearlite's /index.html falls through to not-found-page
because index.html is not a route.

SCOPE OF THE FIX. Add :push-state/index (or the equivalent) to workspace.md's
app/shadow-cljs.edn template for both pilots, and say in one sentence that
RealWorld carries a /realworld base path so its links live under that prefix.
Whether 00-installation.md's own :dev-http line should carry the same is a
judgement for whoever owns that page - it is the published documentation, and a
pilot on outcome 4 reads it.
close_reason:
WITHDRAWN BY ITS OWN AUTHOR, ~20 minutes after filing, because the instrument was wrong. NOT A DEFECT.

The 404s in the description were measured with curl, which sends Accept: */*. shadow-cljs' :dev-http serves index.html for ANY path when the client accepts HTML, so it already does the push-state fallback the bead asked for. Re-measured on the same live server, same URLs, one header apart:

  /             accept */* -> 404    accept text/html -> 200
  /board        accept */* -> 404    accept text/html -> 200
  /nope         accept */* -> 404    accept text/html -> 200
  /index.html   accept */* -> 200    accept text/html -> 200

A browser sends the HTML Accept header, so no pilot and no user ever sees the 404. The tell was that playwright had already loaded a page at a URL curl called 404 — two instruments disagreeing about the same request. That disagreement is the whole finding, and it is the "a search that returns zero is not a check that passed" hazard reached through HTTP: curl answered a question I did not ask.

The second half - that workspace.md never mentions RealWorld's /realworld base path (routing.cljs:254 wires with-base-path ... "/realworld") - is TRUE but is not a defect either, and falls with the first half: because the fallback works, /realworld/tag/clojure reloads to index.html, the base path strips, the route matches, and the app is correct at both / and /realworld/*. Nothing to fix, nothing for a pilot to trip over.

rf2-2xzc (the empty Global Feed) is UNAFFECTED - it was measured through the browser throughout, never through curl, and reproduces at /, at /realworld, and after an in-app navigation to /realworld/tag/clojure.

title: Repo-wide syntax-aware require-alias dialect ratchet (scripts/ + lint.yml)
description:
Both parent beads of the rf.* require-alias migration (rf2-6r9j.161 core, rf2-6r9j.167 routing, rf2-j5or machines) list a syntax-aware CI ratchet in their acceptance criteria, and all three deliberately did not build it: scripts/ and .github/workflows/ are hot-zone and the ratchet should be ONE repo-wide instrument, not one per artefact. Per-artefact is exactly what let machines go unowned — .161 and .167 each fenced their own tree and nothing covered the third.

The full design, with the four textual traps measured on the machines sweep, the derived (not listed) exemption rule, the per-surface floor shape and the positive-fixture requirement, is written up in the notes on rf2-j5or (PR #9114). Read it there rather than re-deriving; every trap in it was hit for real, and one of them silently rewrote 42 late-bind keys on a first pass.

Summary of the design:
- scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py (Python, no JVM start-up) + one job in .github/workflows/lint.yml, which already owns lint_surface gating. Not a new workflow file.
- Find libspec vectors by BALANCED BRACKET scan, never by line: a multi-line [re-frame.machines.result :as result / :refer [...]] defeats any single-line regex and the miss is silent (116 use sites skipped on a clean-looking run).
- Distinguish ::alias/key (auto-resolved, MUST move) from :alias/key (a literal keyword, MUST NOT); machines alone carries 179 of the latter against 7 of the former.
- Skip fully-qualified re-frame.x/y and quoted 're-frame.x/y; do NOT skip #'alias/y var-quotes. Skip repo-relative paths whose first segment collides with an alias (spec/conformance/..., docs/machines/...).
- Exemption is DERIVED: an alias bound to 2+ distinct namespaces within one file is the host-conditional reader-arm shape and is exempt. No path allowlist, which would go stale on the first rename.

scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK B reads every :rf.* keyword NAMESPACE out of implementation/**/src and demands a matching `:rf.<ns>/*` row in spec/Conventions.md's reserved set. Its extractor (_RF_KEYWORD_RE = r":(rf(?:\.[a-z][\w.-]*)?)/[\w.*+!?<>=-]+") CANNOT TELL `::rf.x/y` FROM `:rf.x/y`.

That matters because the canonical `rf.<tail>` require alias TEXTUALLY SHADOWS the `:rf.<area>` reserved keyword root. An auto-resolved `::rf.machines.result/depth-abort?` denotes `:re-frame.machines.result/depth-abort?` and reserves nothing at all, but the checker reads it as a literal reserved-root keyword and demands a Conventions row that would be a FALSE reservation.

Machines is the first artefact to produce one: `git grep '::rf\.' -- implementation/*/src` returned NOTHING on main before PR #9114, which is why the core and routing sweeps never met it. Every remaining artefact with an auto-resolved keyword in src will meet it — schemas, flows, epoch, resources, ssr, ssr-node, security, adapters.

PR #9114 resolved its one instance INSIDE its fence, by spelling the sentinel fully-qualified (`:re-frame.machines.result/depth-abort?`) with a comment recording why, rather than by editing scripts/. That is defensible on the merits — a fully-qualified literal says the same thing to a reader and to a scanner — but it is a per-site remedy, and the scanner gap is still open.

The one-line correction, when a lane owns scripts/: add a negative lookbehind for the second colon, `(?<!:):(rf(?:\.[a-z][\w.-]*)?)/...`. It is strictly safe — `::x/y` ALWAYS resolves through an alias, and every framework namespace is `re-frame.*`, so no `::` form can ever denote a literal `:rf.*` value. Pair it with a self-test fixture asserting that `::rf.foo/bar` does NOT fire CHECK B while `:rf.foo/bar` still does; the checker already carries a self-test suite in the same shape.

Worth deciding at the same time whether the ratchet should simply FORBID `::rf.<tail>/key` in framework source, which is the stronger and simpler rule: the fully-qualified spelling is unambiguous to every consumer (Xray, the MCP catalogues, this checker and any future one), and the auto-resolved form buys only brevity.

(2) --write-baseline IS NOT MONOTONIC. title: Clarify private locals in reply vocabulary conformance matrices
description:
## Finding
The reply vocabulary conformance suite uses one-letter or abbreviated private lexical bindings in its EDN helper, family matrix loops, correlation helper, and time-pair loops.

## Evidence
implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:51 defines edn-roundtrip [x]; lines 467, 492, 619, 849, 862 bind family specs as :as f; lines 619-622 and 849-864 bind descriptor keys as with-k/no-k; lines 746-804 bind projected replies as out in correlation helpers and stale-row loops. These names are lexical only and do not alter vocabulary keys.

## Impact
The suite has a large cross-product of reply families and situations. Abbreviated bindings make it harder to distinguish family descriptors, key names, and projected outcomes while reviewing conformance failures, increasing maintenance and review ambiguity.

## Recommendation
Rename only lexical bindings to role-revealing names (value, family-spec, with-key/no-key, outcome or equivalent), updating local references mechanically. Keep all descriptor map keys, test names, statuses, payloads, and control-flow predicates byte-for-byte semantic equivalents.

## Compatibility and exclusions
No public API, namespace, file, operation keyword, wire/storage key, or behavior change. Do not change the matrix predicates or coverage owned by rf2-6r9j.88/.90, nor stale descriptor/inventory/path targets owned by rf2-6r9j.91 (including :error-work-status and the phantom filename); docs and files outside this bounded surface are excluded.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. All identified abbreviated locals at lines 51, 467, 492, 619-622, 746-804, and 849-864 are renamed consistently with no missed references.
2. Matrix cardinality, predicate semantics, test names, reply keys, statuses, and assertion counts remain unchanged.
3. Focused CLJS/JVM test and lint gates pass, and git diff --check is clean.

title: Disambiguate Event Conformance reply and correlation values
description:
## Finding

The two retained reply/event integration cases use generic locals at the boundary where four distinct values coexist: the reply target, the completed event vector, the reply envelope delivered on that vector, and carried/current correlation state. `observe-stale-reply!` destructures a local named `reply` beside the `reply` namespace alias, yielding `reply/complete target reply`; the success row similarly calls both the source envelope and delivered envelope `reply`, while `completed` omits that it is an event. The observer row uses `pool`, `img`, `target`, `carried`, `current`, `outcome`, and `delivered`, obscuring image setup and suppression roles.

## Evidence

- `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_reply_envelope_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:74-76` visually overloads the `reply` namespace alias and local envelope in one expression.
- Lines 83-114 distinguish observed event/coeffects, completion, and delivered envelope using `seen-cofx`, `target`, `reply`, `completed`, and `delivered`.
- Lines 130-196 build an explicit image-loaded frame and a stale-suppression correlation pair under `pool`, `img`, `target`, `carried`, `current`, `outcome`, and `delivered`.
- Managed-Effects names these concepts reply target, completed event, reply map/envelope, carried/current correlation facts, and stale-suppression outcome. EP-0023 names registration sets and image values.
- History shows the observer helper replaced an older delivery gate; its current local names were inherited through that semantic shift.
- No all-status bead owns these naming changes. Phase-1 bead `rf2-6r9j.97` owns the separate vacuous stale non-delivery row, which is excluded entirely.

## Recommendation

Rename retained-case locals to `seen-coeffects`, `reply-target`, `completed-event`, `delivered-reply`, `stale-reply`, `dispatch-options`, `image-registrations`, `event-image`, `carried-correlation`, `current-correlation`, `suppression-outcome`, and `handler-call-count`. Update the observer helper's destructuring explicitly so the namespace alias is never shadowed. Preserve all registered ids and reply/correlation map keys.

## Risks / contracts

This is test-private naming only. Do not change the canonical reply envelope, `:deliver?`, correlation data, reply target shape, registered event/image/frame ids, dispatch options, handler routing, assertions, or namespace/file names. Do not edit the `rf2-6r9j.97` deletion/replacement target or its namespace prose.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The retained success and observer paths clearly distinguish target, completed event, delivered/stale reply, image setup, correlation inputs, and suppression outcome.
2. No local reply envelope shadows the `reply` namespace alias in retained code.
3. The Phase-1-owned stale non-delivery test remains unchanged.
4. Event-conformance JVM and consolidated CLJS Node suites, focused lint, exact searches, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified role-bearing private naming in event-conformance fixtures, event-model observations, and reply/correlation integration cases; JVM/CLJS focused suites and pinned clj-kondo pass.

title: mcp-conformance: remove the zero-consumer transport handle from the runner contract
description:
Evidence
- tools/mcp-conformance/test/_runner.cjs:15-29 constructs a StdioClientTransport, gives it to client.connect(), then returns { client, transport }.
- runWithWatchdog at lines 55-90 retains a transport local solely to call body(client, transport).
- Repo-wide call-site inspection found 11 runWithWatchdog bodies and the direct connectServer consumers; every body uses only client, direct callers destructure only { client } or read aux.client, and no consumer reads .transport or a second callback argument.
- The extra parameter dates to d16cf18641, which centralized the old per-test ceremony and documented async (client, transport), but no current test exercises that part of the private contract.
- The pinned @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0 contract says Protocol assumes ownership of the Transport. Its close() calls this._transport?.close(), matching _runner's existing closeQuietly(client) teardown.

Impact
The runner advertises and threads a second teardown handle that callers must not own under the SDK contract. This widens a private harness API, obscures the single owner, and creates needless destructuring/local state without providing any current capability.

Recommendation
Keep transport local to connectServer long enough to wire stderr and call client.connect(transport), but return only the connected client handle (or { client }, whichever minimizes call-site churn). Remove runWithWatchdog's transport local and invoke body(client). Update the private contract comments.

Risks and contracts
Preserve onClient publication before the initialize await, AUX_CLIENTS registration, prefixed stderr, connect-failure closeQuietly(client), watchdog behavior, and all 0/1/2 exit grading. Do not close the transport separately: Client owns it. This package is private and _runner.cjs is not a published API, but all in-repo direct callers must update atomically.
acceptance_criteria:
- connectServer no longer exposes transport to callers, while still passing it to client.connect().
- runWithWatchdog calls bodies with only client and carries no transport-only local/destructuring.
- Every direct connectServer and runWithWatchdog caller remains green.
- npm --prefix tools/mcp-conformance run test:unit passes, including connect-hang and auxiliary-client watchdog coverage.
- Repo-wide search finds no stale documentation claiming body receives transport.
close_reason: PR #9086 (head 79b2ee56a6). connectServer now returns { client } only; runWithWatchdog calls body(client) with no transport local. Proved zero consumers two ways: fixed-string census of 'transport' across tools/mcp-conformance (every hit outside _runner.cjs is transportSpec or prose; 'client, transport' appears nowhere else in the repo) plus enumeration of all 12 runWithWatchdog sites — the 11 bodies are async (client) x7, async (rawClient) x2, async () x2, none taking a second arg — and all four direct connectServer callers destructure { client } or read aux.client. Control: the same method over 'client, called' returned 3 files. Returning { client } kept call-site churn at zero. Gates: mcp-conformance node unit cluster exit 0 (124 tests, 0 fail), wire-vocab clojure -M:test exit 0 (94 tests / 1031 assertions).
