title: Prune ssr-node zero-consumer internal and test residue
description:
## Evidence

A whole-repository identifier/import census found seven internal or test-only residues with no consumer:

- src/isolate.cjs initializes this.renders at :54 and increments it at :134, but no code ever reads the counter.
- src/isolate.cjs exports WORKER_PATH at :241. The constant remains live inside that file at :38/:65, but no caller imports the export; tests import only Isolate.
- src/protocol.cjs exports KEY_TEXT and refuse at :523/:525. Both remain live implementation details inside protocol.cjs, but no caller imports either name. The package exports map does not expose protocol.cjs as a public subpath.
- test/_support.cjs exports boot at :75. boot is used only locally by withService at :12/:20; all suite destructuring imports omit it.
- test/observations.cjs exports ATTR at :70. ATTR is used only locally to build RE and encode; the three consumers import encode or observationsIn, never ATTR.
- test/fixtures/reference.cjs allowlists :bytes at :67, but that fixture neither reads :bytes nor receives it in any repository request. Every byte fixture request uses test/fixtures/bytes.cjs (bytes.test.cjs:109,138,168).

The render counter and internal exports date to the initial package; the test exports/allowlist survived later witness changes. No existing bead found by the exact identifiers, zero-consumer export, render counter, or ssr-node searches owns them.

## Impact

The unread counter looks like operational telemetry but can never inform health or scheduling. The extra exports imply supported seams that do not exist. The unused allowlist member weakens the reference fixture's fail-closed role by accepting state it never reads. Together they create false surface area and misleading future maintenance choices.

## Disposition

Remove the renders state and increment; narrow the isolate/protocol/test module export objects to names actually consumed; keep WORKER_PATH, KEY_TEXT, refuse, boot, and ATTR as local implementation details where still used; remove :bytes from the reference entry allowlist.

## Risks

Do not delete the live local helpers merely because their exports are dead. Do not touch the documented package entry points or their named Service/statusFor/STATUS exports in this cleanup: absence of an in-repo importer is not enough to prove those public API names unused outside the checkout. Keep the separate bytes fixture and byte tests intact.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Isolate has no unread renders property or increment.
2. WORKER_PATH, KEY_TEXT, refuse, boot, and ATTR remain available locally where needed but are not exported from their internal/test modules.
3. The reference fixture no longer allowlists :bytes; all requests accepted by its app/root entry use keys the fixture actually reads for behavior or observations.
4. Whole-repository import searches find no broken consumer.
5. ESLint and all 9 ssr-node suites remain green with no test-count drop.
close_reason: PR #9099. All six residues confirmed dead with two independent instruments (fixed-string git grep -F over tracked files excluding .beads, plus a reading of every require of the four modules and the names each destructures) and removed. Isolate.renders init+increment gone. WORKER_PATH, KEY_TEXT, refuse, boot and ATTR dropped from their module.exports and kept as live locals where still used. reference.cjs no longer allowlists :bytes (every byte request goes to chunked.cjs/bytes.cjs, which carry their own); the documented mirror of that table in envelope.test.cjs moved with it. Public entry points and Service/statusFor/STATUS untouched. Census proven live rather than vacuous: ATTR returns 50-odd hits repo-wide, renders 27 in-package. eslint exit 0 (control fired: a planted unused const reds no-unused-vars), suite 9/9 green at 108 rows vs a 107-row baseline, so no test-count drop.

title: Remove ssr-node compatibility guards below its Node 24 floor
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/package.json declares engines.node >=24, a deliberate crossing requirement recorded by closed feature rf2-8arzr.2.
- The code still treats four much older core APIs as optional: bootTimer.unref?.() at src/isolate.cjs:81, render timer.unref?.() at :154, waiter.timer.unref?.() at src/pool.cjs:148, and server.closeAllConnections?.() at src/http.cjs:250.
- Node's official API history records Timeout.unref() since v0.9.1 and http.Server.closeAllConnections() since v18.2.0. Both methods are unconditional under the supported Node 24+ floor:
  https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/timers.html#timeoutunref
  https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/http.html#servercloseallconnections
- Every call receives a real Node Timeout or http.Server; no repository test double omits these methods.
- These guards predate the package manifest/floor: isolate/pool came from b2b35bf6e9 and HTTP from 939d439ad9, while the Node >=24 package contract landed later in rf2-8arzr.2.
- No existing bead found by ssr-node, unref, closeAllConnections, or Node-floor searches owns these compatibility remnants.

## Impact

The impossible fallback paths imply that failure to detach lifecycle timers or force-close active HTTP connections is an accepted runtime mode. That obscures the actual shutdown/timeout guarantees and leaves below-floor compatibility code after the project chose a firm runtime floor.

## Disposition

Call unref() and closeAllConnections() directly. Preserve the calls themselves and their ordering; only retire the optional compatibility branches. Keep this separate from any redesign of graceful shutdown.

## Risks

server.closeAllConnections() is still needed for active connections even though modern server.close() also reaps idle connections. Do not remove it. Direct calls intentionally make an unsupported or malformed runtime fail loudly rather than degrade lifecycle behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No optional call remains for Timeout.unref or Server.closeAllConnections in implementation/ssr-node.
2. The three timers are still unrefed and HTTP shutdown still force-closes active connections before completing.
3. The Node >=24 engine floor remains explicit.
4. Timeout, admission, shutdown, serve, and full ssr-node tests are green.
close_reason:
Confirmed and removed in PR #9078. THE FLOOR WAS RE-VERIFIED FIRST, since it is the whole justification: implementation/ssr-node/package.json declares engines.node '>=24' at my tip, unchanged; every .github/workflows/*.yml that pins a runtime pins node-version '24'; and the node running these gates is v24.13.0. Probed both APIs on that runtime directly rather than trusting the docs: typeof setTimeout(...).unref === 'function' and typeof http.createServer().closeAllConnections === 'function' both true. Timeout.unref() has existed since v0.9.1 and http.Server.closeAllConnections() since v18.2.0, so both are unconditional under the declared floor.

All four sites were exactly where the bead said, re-derived at my tip: src/isolate.cjs:81 (bootTimer.unref?.()), src/isolate.cjs:154 (render timer.unref?.()), src/pool.cjs:148 (waiter.timer.unref?.()), src/http.cjs:250 (server.closeAllConnections?.()). Each patch was anchored to a single line with its match count read first (=1 in every case). AC1: a repo-wide grep for 'unref?.' and 'closeAllConnections?.' under implementation/ssr-node now returns nothing.

AC2: the calls and their ordering are untouched — the three timers are still unrefed at the same points, and closeServer still calls closeAllConnections() before server.close(), which the bead's risk note is explicit about keeping (server.close() reaps idle connections only; active ones still need the force-close). Only the branches that could never be taken are gone, so an unsupported or malformed runtime now fails loudly instead of silently degrading shutdown behaviour, which was the stated intent.

AC3: the >=24 engine floor is untouched and still pinned by test/serve.test.cjs's row 'the manifest points its bin at this launcher, exports the two entry points, and pins the Node CI runs'. package.json was not edited — this bead reads the floor, it does not move it.

AC4: timeout, concurrency (admission), serve and all 9 ssr-node suites green — 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0 on the final rebased base. Note the shutdown paths are genuinely exercised rather than merely compiled: serve.test.cjs spawns bin/serve.cjs as a real process and stops it on SIGTERM, and timeout.test.cjs drives real render deadlines and isolate termination, so the unrefed timers and the force-close both ran.

title: Finish schema-implies-validation migration in schemas tests
description:
## Finding

The schemas test surface did not complete the `schema implies validation` migration. Twelve test namespaces that already require the public `re-frame.schemas` facade still separately require `re-frame.schemas.malli`, and two CLJS suites continue to describe that direct adapter require as the canonical application opt-in. One test named `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` models an application posture that the facade deliberately made impossible; what it actually exercises is the supported defensive missing-hook/substitute-port fallback.

## Evidence

- Current source and Spec 010 state that `re-frame.schemas` itself requires `re-frame.schemas.malli`; requiring the artefact automatically publishes the Malli validate/explain hooks. Commit `d0b95fdc54` made this Ruling A specifically to eliminate the "schemas loaded but adapter not required" posture.
- A line-oriented census finds 12 direct `[re-frame.schemas.malli]` requires under `implementation/schemas/test`; every one of those namespaces also directly requires `re-frame.schemas`. No test calls an adapter var (the adapter is load-side-effect-only). The dedicated `schemas_implies_validation_test.clj` intentionally requires only the facade and already proves the transitive wiring contract.
- `schemas_cljs_test.cljs` (currently lines 18-25 and 96-111) still says direct adapter require is the "canonical opt-in" and that omitting it soft-passes. Its `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` test (currently around lines 136-161) manually clears late-bind hooks; because the same namespace requires the facade, this is not an app-without-adapter scenario.
- `schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs` (currently lines 48-55) repeats the obsolete instruction that CLJS apps must require the adapter at boot, despite also requiring the facade on line 58.
- Spec 010 currently says there is "nothing extra to opt into" (around lines 652-660) and reserves the soft-pass for a cross-port default-absent posture or an explicitly installed substitute validator. The stale test prose contradicts that normative contract.
- Blame dates the obsolete CLJS comments/direct requires to `80119fc1a9`, before Ruling A. The June 15 vestigial sweep `2980649a9c` edited the same file but only repaired a retired event-registration spelling, leaving this older posture untouched.
- All-status title/description searches for `adapter require`, `schema implies validation tests`, `canonical opt-in`, and `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` found no owning issue. Closed `rf2-tiymn` covers production elision of Malli's humanizer, not test import/posture cleanup.

## Impact

The redundant requires make broad schemas tests bypass the public load contract they are ostensibly exercising and stale comments teach consumers the exact extra boot step Ruling A retired. The no-adapter test name/text presents a reachable consumer configuration that cannot occur after loading the facade, obscuring the real reason the soft-pass branch remains: alternate ports or deliberate hook invalidation.

## Proposed disposition

Remove redundant direct adapter requires from schemas tests that already load the facade, leaving the dedicated facade-only regression as the authority. Rewrite the two CLJS comment blocks to state automatic facade wiring. Keep the missing-hook behavior test, but rename/reword it around deliberate hook absence/substitute-port fallback rather than an app forgetting a separate require.

## Risks

Do not remove `re-frame.schemas.malli` from the facade or change the default validator. Do not delete the defensive soft-pass branch/test: alternate ports and deliberate unbinding still need it. Preserve the production boundary build's validator/humanizer assertions and the matched bundle probes.
acceptance_criteria:
- No schemas test namespace that already requires `re-frame.schemas` separately requires `[re-frame.schemas.malli]`; the facade remains the single default-adapter wiring boundary.
- `schemas_cljs_test.cljs` and `schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs` no longer describe a separate Malli adapter require as canonical or omission as a normal application posture.
- The former `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` test is named and documented as a deliberate missing-hook/substitute-port fallback and still proves the default validator soft-passes when that hook is explicitly absent.
- `schemas_implies_validation_test.clj` still proves that requiring only the facade binds validate/explain hooks and makes a bad registered value fail.
- Schemas JVM, ordinary CLJS, production-boundary CLJS, and bundle A/B gates pass; a negative control removing the facade's adapter require makes the facade-only regression fail.
- Public schema registration, custom-validator installation, nil-validator opt-out, and production boundary semantics are unchanged.

title: http privacy: retire inert origin-event and frame-opts compatibility arguments
description:
## Finding

The HTTP privacy orchestrator retains three compatibility inputs after both of the features they carried were removed: `request-sensitive?` still accepts an origin event it ignores, and `prepare-emit-tags` / `prepare-emit-failure` still accept an opts map whose frame is ignored.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy.cljc:421-437` defines `[args-map _origin-event]`; the body reads only the two per-call flags in `args-map`. Commit `dd7c1f0df5` removed handler-registration `:sensitive?`, deleted `handler-sensitive?`, and changed the parameter to `_origin-event`, explicitly stating that origin metadata is no longer consulted.
- All production callers still manufacture/pass that retired provenance: `handlers.cljc:227,333,363`, `test_support.cljc:93`, and `privacy.cljc:465` (nil). Unit tests at `http_privacy_test.clj:165-206` also pass differing origin values only to prove they do nothing.
- `privacy.cljc:477-546` defines two/three-arity `prepare-emit-tags` and `prepare-emit-failure`; both three-arity bodies bind `_opts` and never read it. Their docs explicitly say the third argument is “kept for call-site compatibility”.
- Commit `e4c9b11341` moved carrier lookup from frame policy to process-global `:rf.http/managed` registration metadata. The composers now call `managed-carriers` with no frame. Eleven source call sites across `middleware.cljc`, `registry.cljc`, `transport.cljc`, `transport_cljs.cljc`, and `transport_jvm.cljc` nevertheless still build/pass `{:frame ...}`; several adjacent comments describe that frame as attribution even though the composer cannot use it.
- The generated API manifest exposes only the `re-frame.http` verb facade; none of these orchestrator helpers is a manifested user API. Spec 014 names the operations conceptually but does not promise these obsolete arities. Repo-wide consumer and bead searches found no external-in-repo caller or existing issue requiring compatibility.

## Impact

The signatures and call sites carry false dataflow: readers can reasonably conclude handler provenance or frame identity influences redaction when neither can. Every emit site allocates a throwaway frame map, and future privacy work could mistakenly rely on values the callee discards.

## Proposed disposition

Use the current contracts directly: make `request-sensitive?` a one-argument function and make both composers canonical two-argument functions. Update every caller, focused test, docstring, and stale frame-attribution comment. Do not change carrier lookup or sensitivity semantics.

## Risks / retained contracts

These vars are public Clojure vars despite being artefact-internal and unmanifested, so an unpublished downstream direct-require could depend on the old arities. Confirm the project’s pre-release compatibility posture; if an arity must be retained, document it as an intentional public contract instead of leaving anonymous `_...` compatibility. Preserve handler-metadata non-participation and process-global carrier resolution.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `request-sensitive?` has one canonical input and all callers/tests stop passing origin-event solely for retired handler metadata.
2. `prepare-emit-tags` and `prepare-emit-failure` have canonical two-argument call paths; no source caller constructs an inert `{:frame ...}` opts map for them.
3. Privacy docs/comments state that sensitivity is per-call and carriers come from the process-global `:rf.http/managed` registration, without implying these composers consult frame attribution.
4. Existing request-privacy, carrier-extension, middleware-failure, abort, retry, and JVM/CLJS warning tests preserve redaction and stamping behavior.
5. HTTP JVM and consolidated CLJS suites pass, and source lint reports no compatibility placeholder introduced by this cleanup.
notes: Audit of PR #9081: acceptance criterion 3 remains unmet in implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc. The comment beside check-cljs-only-keys! still says "The frame is threaded for the warning-path trace stamp", but this PR removed the frame argument and the live call now passes only args-map and sensitive?. Remove or correct that false dataflow sentence; behavior is otherwise sound.
close_reason: PR #9109 (b4238a79c5). title: Collapse vestigial duplicate source-id branch in machines tooling
description:
## Evidence

`machine-instance-algebra-view` in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/tooling.cljc` computes `source-id` with three `cond` arms (currently lines 393-396): keyword `machine-type` returns that keyword, `spawned?` returns `actor-id`, and `:else` also returns `actor-id`. Splint reports the adjacent `spawned?` / `:else` arms as identical (`tooling.cljc:395:35 [lint/identical-branches]`). The equivalent expression is `(if (keyword? machine-type) machine-type actor-id)`; `spawned?` continues to serve its real uses in spec resolution and the emitted `:spawned?` field, but cannot discriminate `source-id`.

`git blame` shows all three arms have been unchanged since the tooling view was introduced in commit `85379652c5f` (2026-06-12). The function's documented contract confirms the two non-keyword cases intentionally share identity: an inline-definition spawn uses `actor-id`, and a singleton is its own `actor-id`. Tests and downstream graph consumers observe the resulting node, not this private branch structure.

Bead searches for `machine-instance-algebra-view source-id`, `tooling source-id spawned actor-id`, `spawned source-id conditional`, and `identical branches machines tooling` found no existing issue covering the redundant branch.

## Impact

The redundant arm suggests a semantic distinction between inline-definition spawned actors and singletons at the source-id boundary even though both deliberately use `actor-id`. That false branch adds cognitive load in a tooling projection whose main job is to make identity rules explicit, and it leaves a standing identical-branches lint warning.

## Proposed disposition

Collapse `source-id` to a two-way expression: use the keyword `machine-type` for registered-type spawns, otherwise use `actor-id`. Preserve the separate `spawned?` binding because it still selects spec resolution and is emitted on the node.

## Risks

This projection feeds Xray and derivation-conformance tooling. Keep the change expression-only; do not alter `spec`, `spawned?`, registrar lookup, source form, owner, or state projection.
acceptance_criteria:
- `source-id` has exactly two outcomes: keyword `machine-type` when present, otherwise `actor-id`; no identical conditional arms remain.
- `spawned?` still selects spawned-vs-singleton spec resolution and still appears in the output node.
- Splint no longer reports `lint/identical-branches` at `tooling.cljc` for this expression.
- Machines algebra-view tests and derivation-conformance JVM/CLJS tests pass, covering registered-type spawns, inline-definition spawns, and singleton nodes.
- Xray derivation-graph consumer tests pass and node output is unchanged for all three identity cases.
close_reason: PR #9150: collapsed machine-instance-algebra-view's three-arm source-id cond to (if (keyword? machine-type) machine-type actor-id) in tooling.cljc; the spawned? and :else arms both yielded actor-id. spawned? deliberately kept — it still selects spawned-vs-singleton spec resolution and is still emitted as the node's :spawned? field. Re-measured at branch tip: my own splint run over tooling.cljc went exit 1 with tooling.cljc:395:35 [lint/identical-branches] to exit 0 with 0 style warnings. Machines JVM suite exit 0 (1241 tests/4495 assertions) and npm run test:cljs exit 0 (11173/55748), so node output is unchanged for registered-type spawns, inline-definition spawns and singletons.

CI (.github/workflows/test.yml:511) and scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:942 both invoke the gate WITHOUT --include-tests. description:
## CLAIM (file:line, quoted)

`skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md` — the on-demand leaf SKILL.md:81 tells the retro to consult so "a match raises the finding's priority" — lists, under "Typical improvements", behaviours the current 29-tool Pair-MCP catalogue already ships:

1. §Frame ambiguity :91-94 — "require an explicit `:frame` opt where ambiguity is possible, or surface the implicit choice prominently in the result" / "list `(rf/frame-ids)` and recently-active frames at session start".
2. §Wrong listener for the question :106 — "short prose in SKILL.md naming the two streams and when each wins".
3. §Time-travel restore failures :116-118 — "structured presentation of the seven named failure modes ... with a next-best-action per mode" / "preflight check before restore" / "surface `:history-size` and `:schema-digest-recorded`/`:current` in the tool's output".
4. §Production-elision confusion :130-131 — "preflight check that reads `re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?` and reports the answer" / "make 'I am attached to a production-elided build' a first-class result state".
5. §Error observability :147 — "prefer a recipe over a doc paragraph when the friction is 'I didn't know how to pull recent errors at the REPL'".

## TRUTH AT TIP

Registry: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs` — 29 `:name` entries, including `get-operating-frame`, `set-operating-frame`, `reset-operating-frame`, `discover-app`, `restore-epoch`, `trace-window`, `watch-epochs`.

1. Frame: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:169-173` — the four-tier operating-frame cascade; "every other frame-targeted op refuses with `:ambiguous-frame` rather than guess"; `discover-app` returns `:frames [...]` (descriptors_data.cljs:186). The "explicit `:frame` or surface the choice" improvement IS the shipped design.
2. Streams: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:216` — "Use the assembled epoch stream by default; reach for the raw trace stream when you need detail the projection drops." The prose already exists.
3. Restore: the dedicated `restore-epoch` tool returns a structured refusal `:reason :restore-rejected` (`tools/restore_epoch.cljs:50`); the seven failure ops and their `:tags` (`:history-size`, `:schema-digest-recorded`, `:schema-digest-current`) are pinned at `spec/Tool-Pair.md:116-126`.
4. Elision: `tools/discover_app.cljs:191-194` — `discover-app` returns `:debug-enabled?` and a hint "re-frame.interop/debug-enabled? is false ..." (descriptors_data.cljs:186 shows `:debug-enabled? true` in the example result). The preflight exists.
5. Errors recipe: `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md:22` — the `(re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer :rf/default {:flat true :op-type :error})` recipe for surfacing `:rf.error/handler-exception`.

## IMPACT

A retro that pattern-matches a session onto one of these classes is told to propose, as the "smallest credible product change", a surface that already ships — and §Issue drafts then emits a draft asking `day8/re-frame2` for it. That is the wrong owner AND the wrong finding: when the session had `discover-app`'s `:debug-enabled?` or the operating-frame trio available and did not reach for them, the friction is discoverability in the pair skill's wording/recipes (tool-shaped), not a missing surface. The leaf's own inputs.md:56 update rule ("a new structured op ships → check whether known-frictions has a 'missing op' pattern that this resolves") was not applied when these landed.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR against `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md` only. For each of the five entries, replace the shipped-behaviour bullet with a one-line "check first" that names the shipped tool/leaf (e.g. "check whether the session called `discover-app` and read `:debug-enabled?` — if it existed and was not reached for, the friction is tool-shaped: pair-skill recipe/wording; if it was used and still fell short, name the framework surface"). Keep bullets whose improvements are genuinely unshipped (e.g. §Frame ambiguity's "current operating frame indicator in retrospective output" is a retro-output idea, fine to keep). Do not grow the leaf: it is 195 lines / 12.7 KB against the 250 / 16 KB ceiling.

No gate — verify by hand: every tool named must appear in the `descriptors_data.cljs` `:name` list; every pair-skill line cited must exist at the PR's merge-base. `bb tests/duplicate_search_test.clj` (reads SKILL.md only) stays green as a smoke.

title: skill(re-frame2): xstate-translation.md has no row for three shipped transition-grammar features — :ns/* and :* wildcards, :reenter? self-transitions, cross-region :tags/:all-state guard ctx (the stateIn analog)
description:
CLAIM
- `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/xstate-translation.md:11-37` — the translation table; `reg-machine.md:20` calls it "The full 27-row translation key — every concept, convergence and divergence"; SKILL.md cardinal rule 3 names it the standing mental model ("think in xstate, then map onto re-frame2 … a handful re-frame2 renames or omits, and those divergences are the trap").
- `xstate-translation.md:7` lists `stateIn` among the v5 helper creators v6 "removes … which re-frame2 never had" — with no row saying what re-frame2 ships for the cross-region-coordination *concept*.
- `reg-machine.md:118-132` (§Transition shape): the `:on` value forms — bare target / map / guarded vector. Nothing on event-descriptor tiers.
- `reg-machine.md:153-155` (§Guard/action contract): "Every callback receives one context map — `{:keys [data event state meta] cofx :rf.cofx}` … the runtime always delivers the full context map".
- `regions.md` has no section on how one region's guard reads a sibling region's state.
- `git grep -nEi "reenter|wildcard|:ns/\*|all-state|stateIn" skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/ skills/re-frame2/decision-trees/` hits only the L7 preamble above.

TRUTH AT TIP — three shipped transition-grammar features with no row and no leaf
1. Wildcard / partial event descriptors. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:289-330` (§Wildcard transitions, §Namespaced (partial) event descriptors — `:ns/*`): `:on` resolves three tiers, exact → `:ns/*` → `:*`, least-priority *enabled* candidate at each level. `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:800` (`:event-key <matched :on key, else nil> ;; exact / :ns/* / :* key`). XState spelling: `'*'` and `'mouse.*'` wildcard keys — a v4/v5/v6 constant an xstate-trained agent will reach for.
2. `:reenter?` self-transitions. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:332-360` (§Self-transitions — internal default vs external `:reenter?`): four geometries — targetless (action only, children preserved), self/ancestor target without `:reenter?` (re-resolves descendants to `:initial`), descendant target from a compound (re-enters the child), `:reenter? true` (exit + entry, timers restart, `:spawn` children respawn). `transition.cljc:1512-1522` implements the opt-in. XState spelling: `reenter: true` (v5/v6), `internal: false` (v4).
3. Cross-region coordination — the `stateIn` analog. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:1750-1836` (§Cross-region coordination — tags as `stateIn`): a guard/action running inside a parallel region gets two extra ctx keys, `:tags` (machine-wide tag union — "**the** documented `stateIn` equivalent") and `:all-state` (region-name → active-state map, `(= :valid (:form (:all-state ctx)))`), frozen at the start of the selection round; flat/compound ctx stays exactly `{:data :event :state :meta}`. `transition.cljc:284-333` (`callback-ctx`: "additionally receives `:tags` + `:all-state`" for region callbacks).

IMPACT
These are precisely the "xstate-trained intuition steers you wrong" cases the leaf exists for, and today each ends in a hand-roll: duplicating a transition per event id instead of `:mouse/*`; exiting-and-re-entering via an intermediate state to get `:after` timers to restart, or writing an action that resets `:data` because "self-transition re-resolves children" is unknown; coupling regions through shared `:data` flags because the guard contract paragraph says the ctx is *exactly* `{data event state meta}`. Item 3 is also a correctness bug in `reg-machine.md:153-155` as written for parallel machines.

FIX SHAPE (one PR, three files)
- `xstate-translation.md`: three rows — **wildcard transitions** (`'*'` / `'ns.*'` → `:*` / `:ns/*`, convergence, note the enabled-fallthrough rule); **`reenter`** (`reenter: true` → `:reenter? true`; default = xstate "internal" geometry; targetless = action-only); **`stateIn` / `In()`** (→ read `(:tags ctx)` or `(:all-state ctx)` inside a region guard; flat machines use their own `:state`). Fix L7 so `stateIn` points at its row rather than reading as "never had".
- `reg-machine.md` §Transition shape: one line naming the three descriptor tiers; §Guard/action contract: "flat / compound: exactly `{data event state meta}`; inside a parallel region also `:tags` and `:all-state` — see regions.md". Fix "27-row" to the real count (the table has 25 rows today; 28 after).
- `regions.md`: a short §Cross-region coordination (the `:submit`-guarded-on-sibling-validity example from spec §1772, ~10 lines) and one gotcha on the frozen-config rule.
Watch the byte ceiling: reg-machine.md is already 19.8 KB (separate size bead); keep the additions to one line each there.

GATE
No gate validates this prose. `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py --verbose` must stay green. Verify the new fences by hand against spec/005 §289/§332/§1750 and `transition.cljc` `callback-ctx`, and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE
`git grep -nE ":ns/\*|:reenter\?|:all-state" skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/` hits xstate-translation.md, reg-machine.md and regions.md; the row-count sentence in reg-machine.md matches `grep -c '^| ' xstate-translation.md` minus the two header rows; drift script exits 0.

title: method: the mayor carried a disposition across four ticks instead of re-deriving it - the rule that refutes it was cited in the same sentence that got it wrong
description:
FOUND 2026-09-17 by the §5 METHOD-REREAD LOOP on its own named axis — checking a rule the mayor has
been ENFORCING against what the tree actually does. The rule was fine. **The mayor was carrying a
conclusion instead of re-deriving it, and the method has no sentence about that surface.**

## THE INSTANCE, AND IT COST FOUR TICKS

`subargdel-r4m8k` was reported as NOT REAPABLE in four consecutive loop reports, on the stated
ground that its transcript file read 0 bytes so no completion sentence could be quoted.

**The rule that refutes it was already written, in the section being executed.** §4 Reaping says,
in terms: *"The id buys the TRANSCRIPT, not a live conversation, and may key several locations. An
empty file keyed by the id is a fact about THAT LOCATION, never about the id."* And it prescribes
the remedy in the next bullet: *"With no id, the report is unindexed rather than missing. Search
transcripts for the worktree's path... the report's own stated root is the decisive test."*

Running that search, once, took a single command and found:

    file keyed by the agent id, in the tasks dir     0 bytes
    <session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl         1,546,110 bytes, 119 hits
    quotable sentence                            "Done. PR #9909 is ready for review."
    stated WORKTREE_ROOT                         /c/.../re-frame2-worktrees/subargdel-r4m8k
    branch it states                             worker/subargdel-r4m8k

So the report was UNINDEXED, exactly as §4 says, and the worktree was reapable the whole time. It
was reaped this tick along with three others.

**The cost was not the four ticks.** It was that the disposition was converging on permanence: the
tree was being described as §4 "residue", which is the category explicitly reserved for trees that
can only be cleared on operator authority. A correct tree was being routed into a bucket that would
have kept it for ever.

## WHAT MADE IT SURVIVE FOUR RE-READINGS

Each tick re-read the PREVIOUS TICK'S REPORT rather than re-running the test. The report said "no
quotable report; the transcript file reads 0 bytes, which §4 names as a fact about that location,
never about the id" — which **cites the rule that refutes it, in the same sentence**, and still
concludes the wrong way. Citing a rule is not applying it. That is what makes this worth an item
rather than a shrug: the text looked maximally rigorous, named the right authority, and was wrong.

## THE GAP, MEASURED

The mechanism IS documented — but every statement of it points at ITEM content, never at the
coordinator's own serial output. `re-deriv` reads 4 times in `loops.md` (0 in CLAUDE.md, 3 in the
template, 1 in bootstrap), and read in full they are:

  1. §2 — an item's LIST OF SITES drifts in membership; re-derive it at tip.
  2. §2 — treat a parent's remainder table as stale until re-derived.
  3. §4 — walk the export's history for an unresolvable ruling id before re-deriving the ruling.
  4. Tracker mechanics — *"a note repeating a figure some later note retracted re-derived instead
     of re-checking. Cite the check you made, or say you are summarising and from what."*

Number 4 is the closest and states this exact mechanism — for NOTES ON ITEMS. Nothing states it
for the mayor's own tick-to-tick reporting, which is the mayor's primary output and the surface
where this happened. Controls over the same four files, so a zero means absence: `worktree` reads
25/46/50/8, `fence` reads 12/13/24/0, a nonsense token reads 0/0/0/0. Probes for the idea in other
words — "carried forward", "carry forward", "last tick", "previous tick", "without re-checking" —
read **0** in every file.

## THE SHAPE OF THE FIX

One bullet. Something of the form: **a disposition you have now reported more than once is a rule
you are enforcing, so re-derive it rather than re-reading your own last report — and a report that
CITES the rule which would refute it is the dangerous case, not the safe one.**

§5 is the natural home, because §5 already says its own axis is "check the rules you have been
ENFORCING against what the tree actually does" and a repeated disposition is precisely such a rule;
the gap is that "rules you are enforcing" currently reads as rules from the documents, not
conclusions of your own. A reader could also argue for §3, where dispositions are reported. **Pick
one and defend it; do not put it in both.**

## NOT ESTABLISHED

  * **Whether any OTHER carried disposition is currently wrong.** This was found by accident, not by
    sweep. The obvious candidates are the ones this session has repeated: that `restoregc-9nlg1` is
    operator residue (partly refuted already this tick — its branch reads CONTAINED, so its work
    landed), that `rf2-lect` is fenced, that the two retained branches' release conditions are
    unmet. None was re-derived today. **A sweep of the mayor's own repeated claims is the obvious
    follow-up and is NOT part of this item.**
  * Whether the failure is frequent or was a one-off. n=1, and the base rate is unmeasured.
  * Whether a sentence changes anything. The refuted rule was already present and cited; this
    proposes adding a second sentence to catch a reader who ignored the first, which is exactly the
    kind of thing CLAUDE.md warns usually is not the repair. **Whoever takes this should weigh
    writing nothing** — the honest alternative is that the method is fine and the operator simply
    erred, in which case the correct output is a recorded decision not to write.

## SCOPE

  * **Do NOT add a gate.** Nothing mechanical distinguishes a re-derived disposition from a copied one.
  * **Do NOT add a lettered instrument item** — no instrument misreported; the 0-byte file was an
    honest fact about an empty location.
  * **Do NOT rewrite §4's existing bullets.** They are correct and were correct throughout.
  * **P4.** The stance applies with force: the gate guidance and the loops are already long, and one
    measured instance is thin evidence for new text.

title: ci(test.yml): the jvm-uix job comment still says the UIx artefact has no JVM-runnable tests — it has two, and one reddened trunk this week (the reagent sibling comment is still TRUE)
description:
Flagged by the rf2-q4s8 worker while sweeping the classifier, and verified at source by the mayor at
trunk `2e28be9bc6`.

## The stale claim

`.github/workflows/test.yml`, the `jvm-uix` job's header comment (around `:1852`; RE-MEASURE, this is
a hot file):

> The UIx artefact's `:test` alias has no JVM-runnable tests of its own (the adapter ns is
> `:cljs-only` — UIx is a CLJS-only library). The job exists so the artefact's deps + classpath
> wiring stay green. The empty case needs no `|| echo` fallback: the cognitect test-runner returns 0
> when there are no test namespaces matching...

**Both halves are now false.** `git ls-files 'implementation/adapters/uix/test/**/*.clj'` returns
TWO files at tip:

- `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_component_recipe_docs_pin_test.clj`
- `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj`

So the job does not merely keep classpath wiring green — it runs real tests, and one of them
(`uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test`) reddened trunk under rf2-v37n this week. The "empty case" reasoning
about the test-runner returning 0 is also no longer the situation being described, though the code it
justifies is harmless either way.

## DO NOT TOUCH THE REAGENT SIBLING — it is still TRUE

The near-identical comment on the `jvm-reagent` job (around `:1762`) makes the same claim for Reagent,
and it still holds: `git ls-files 'implementation/adapters/reagent/test/**/*.clj'` returns **0**. That
job really does exist only to keep deps and classpath wiring green.

The two comments read almost identically, which is exactly why a careless sweep would "fix" both and
make the Reagent one wrong. Change the UIx block only, and say in the PR that you checked Reagent
separately and left it alone deliberately.

(For completeness, measured the same way: `reagent-slim` has 1 `.clj` test file. It is not the subject
of either comment.)

## Why this is worth a bead rather than nothing

It is a comment, and comments are cheap to leave wrong — but this one misleads about WHY a CI job
exists, in the file that defines the CI matrix, and it does so in the direction that invites deletion:
a reader trimming "jobs that only check wiring" would take out a job that runs the recipe test.

## AN INSTRUMENT NOTE, because it cost a search

The phrase is LINE-BROKEN in the file — `:1852` ends "...has no JVM-runnable tests of its" and the
next line begins "own (the adapter ns is...". A line-oriented search for the full sentence reads
**0**, which is the reassuring answer. It was found only by flattening. If you census this file for
other stale claims, use the flattened and comment-marker-stripped passes too, and take a control that
bites (`jvm-uix` reads 3).

## Scope

One comment block. `.github/workflows/*` is HOT-ZONE ONE-TOUCHER — sequence, never parallel. No job
key is added or removed, so the check count must not move; say so in the PR.

The cheapest correct shape is ONE panel action owned by ONE data owner (the Epoch panel's selected record), reusing the projector that already exists: `egress.cljs:86` delegates to `rf/project-egress`, which recognises a stamped `:rf/epoch-record` and invokes the epoch projector at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc:654`. Reopening `021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §10.1/§10.5 and updating `skills/re-frame2-xray/references/shared-components.md` in the same PR is still required.

**The one pre-sanctioned escape that needs NO B.9 reopen** is copy-cascade-id, `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:478` — explicitly value-free, explicitly outside the lock, simply unbuilt. **Copy-PATH in panel chrome is NOT pre-sanctioned**: `018-Event-Spine.md:954-956` calls that "an open reading, not settled here". And a copied path is navigation, not a snapshot — the palette reads the LIVE app-db (`palette/events.cljs:156`) while the popup renders the FOCUSED EPOCH's state (`panels/app_db_segment_inspector.cljs:77`), so a pasted path can return a different value from the one on screen. See the notes field for the full ruling and the demand evidence.

---

## Original filing (design record, preserved)

DEFERRED DESIGN BEAD, filed 2026-09-04 by the delegated ruling agent for rf2-6r9j.24 (Mike's delegation of 2026-09-04). NOT dispatchable as filed: it exists so the design analysis two reviewers produced is not lost when the dossier is deleted. It becomes live only if Mike says there is demand for per-value copy in Xray AND agrees to reopen the B.9 lock; either signal alone is not enough.

## What was decided upstream

rf2-6r9j.24 RETRACTED the dead universal value-copy affordance (the edn-widget copy-affordance glyph, its CSS, the :copy? no-op, and the dispatcher-less :rf.xray/copy-value-to-clipboard and :rf.xray/copy-path-to-clipboard events) and honoured tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md sections 10.1 and 10.5 (LOCKED per B.9: no copy-path, no copy-value on the canonical renderer; re-proposals must reopen the lock with the mayor first). The published skill (skills/re-frame2-xray/references/shared-components.md:22-26) carries the same contract. This bead is the ONLY sanctioned route back.

## Why a universal root glyph was wrong, so the next design does not repeat it

The retracted event received only [_ value] with no absolute path, origin, partition or record kind. Xray's egress.cljs:53-58 and spec/API.md (Off-box egress section) say a slice egress'd in isolation must pass its absolute app-db :path or the path-keyed :sensitive / :large declarations cannot match. The canonical inspector is handed: app-db slices at a path (panels/app_db_segment_inspector.cljs), raw managed-fx request/response/handler values (panels/managed_fx_template.cljs) which spec/Security.md section Epoch privacy posture says are NOT app-db-rooted and MUST be default-redacted off-box, raw trace before/after (panels/trace.cljs), registry values (static flows/routes/schemas), and runtime-db machine snapshots. Those do not share one projection rule; a shared renderer cannot infer provenance from a naked value. The old tests proved only app-db-root-shaped fixtures through direct dispatch.

## What is lost without it (the case FOR building this, kept honest)

Browser text selection copies the render projection: collapsed nodes give their {N keys} / [N items] preview, diff annotations come along, and the app-db path is lost. Snapshot app-db is the whole focused-frame db, much coarser. There is no route for "paste this event's :fx vector / this exception's ex-data / this sub's value into a bug report or REPL". Demand evidence is nil either way: the glyph was user-reachable four days (2026-05-21 to 05-25) and nobody asked for it in the ~100 days after.

## Design sketch (from the Codex review, corrected at tip)

- Design from the DATA OWNER outward. Each enabled call site supplies a typed copy projection rather than a value: an app-db slice with its absolute :path; a projected trace/epoch record (record-aware, fx :args redacted by default, per Security.md); a runtime-db projection under its own axis; registry/static values that are value-free by contract and may ride the fx directly (the Copy Mermaid pattern at static/machines/panel.cljs).
- Opt-in per call site where such a projection exists; never default-on from the renderer root. App-DB stays OUT unless Mike changes it (his rf2-ilubp ruling, 95d92180bb).
- Precedent: re-frame-10x (upstream a3c309430d, src/day8/re_frame_10x/popup.cljs) exposes copy CONTEXTUALLY as Copy Path and Copy Subtree in the inspector popup, derived from the selected data path. The natural home here is therefore the edn-inspector popup (views/edn_inspector_popup.cljs), which at tip has only a close button — an action strip would be new chrome, not existing chrome. Do not stack a second absolute-positioned button at right: 2px beside the popup affordance.
- Egress: every value-bearing projection goes through day8.re-frame2-xray.egress/egress-value naming :frame (the fail-closed gesture; nil / destroyed / colliding-id frames egress :rf/redacted — pinned by the re-pointed rf2-7htk7 proofs in test/.../panels/app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs) and passing :path for slices. The clipboard fx :rf.xray.fx/copy-to-clipboard already offers :on-success / :on-failure; use them for honest Copied / Copy failed feedback.
- Acceptance for that future bead: a REAL rendered click through frame routing (N parallel shells isolated; captured dispatch-fn pattern of popup-affordance-button in views/edn_inspector.cljs), each privacy axis, stale/nil frame, clipboard rejection (NotAllowedError), keyboard focus, and browser user-activation — the current suites stub the fx or run on node, and nobody has established that queuing rf/dispatch from the click before writeText keeps activation in supported browsers.
- Spec: reopen B.9 explicitly in 021 section 10.5 (and 10.1) with the narrow form chosen; update the skill's shared-components.md in the same PR; correct spec/API.md's Off-box egress inventory and README.md to enumerate the new sink; any PR touching tools/xray/ updates tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR or states why the spec is unchanged.

## Not this bead

The 007-UX-IA long-keyword click-to-copy glyph on elided keywords is a separate design. The 018-Event-Spine Copy path / Ctrl+click copy cascade-id items are tracked separately (see the sibling bead filed from rf2-6r9j.24).

Keeping those identifiers avoids disturbing existing citations. There is no need to renumber history, introduce another classification system, or create a validation tool for the labels. The long physical line is a readability and editing concern, but restructuring the whole instruction file is outside this decision.

The substantive guidance needs narrower wording than the bead supplies. Clojure's [reader reference](https://clojure.org/reference/reader#_reader_conditionals) specifies that unselected expressions are read and skipped. In the version declared by [core/deps.edn](../../implementation/core/deps.edn), Clojure 1.12.0, [`LispReader.ConditionalReader.readCondDelimited`](https://github.com/clojure/clojure/blob/clojure-1.12.0/src/jvm/clojure/lang/LispReader.java#L1490) calls `read` with `RT.SUPPRESS_READ` bound; `StringReader.invoke` still rejects an unterminated string. Consequently, a JVM reader can reject malformed text while ordinary Clojure compilation never compiles the discarded ClojureScript expression. A syntax failure is therefore an unsuitable demonstration that a JVM suite exercises that expression.

There is a second correction worth preserving: **clj-kondo is not generally blind to `:cljs` branches.** Its [official configuration documentation](https://github.com/clj-kondo/clj-kondo/blob/master/doc/config.md#only-lint-specific-dialects-in-cljc-files) says it lints all understood dialects in `.cljc` files by default. An unchanged finding count for one historical defect does not establish universal blindness. Neither should “runs on the JVM” be confused with “only analyzes Clojure”: the relevant distinction is what the particular tool selects and checks.

The local example is concrete: [`config.cljc`](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/config.cljc) defines `drain-suppressed-counts!` inside `#?(:cljs ...)` at lines 890–918. [shadow-cljs.edn](../../implementation/shadow-cljs.edn) includes Xray's source and test roots and selects `cljs-test$` for `:node-test`; [package.json](../../implementation/package.json) makes `test:cljs` compile that target and run its output. That supports this compact instruction beside the existing [Build & Test](../../CLAUDE.md#build--test) lane guidance:

> When changing a `:cljs` reader-conditional branch, select a ClojureScript build and relevant tests that actually include the namespace. A green Clojure JVM suite does not validate the branch's ClojureScript behavior, even though its reader may reject malformed text. A green linter is supplementary evidence, not a replacement for that coverage.

verified by blob hash against the committed objects, and the tree is clean
(`git diff --quiet HEAD` exit 0).

The fourth row is the one that matters: it isolates the cause to the four gated files
specifically, and away from the rest of that commit (a core.cljs docstring, a spec page,
and a test namespace).

## 3. THE MECHANISM — full call path, read off the pseudo-names bundle

    re-frame.story.ui.state/swap-state!            (user clicks a variant in the sidebar)
      -> reagent.ratom notify-w
        -> day8.re-frame2-xray.core/seat-and-set-target-frame!   (core.cljs:114)
          -> day8.re-frame2-xray.mount/ensure-seated!            (mount.cljs:518)
            -> panels.image-view-reads/seat-xray-frame!
              -> re-frame.live-frame/make-frame
                -> re-frame.live-frame/resolve-generation!
                  -> re-frame.image-assembly/assemble-cached -> assemble* -> mapv
                    -> select-and-lower-image
                      -> re-frame.image/select-descriptors
                        -> re-frame.image/select-by-include-ns
                          -> re-frame.error/throw-error!   <-- THROWS HERE

The entry door on the Story side is `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs:469`,
`(xray-core/set-target-frame! now)` — the per-variant re-orientation gesture.

WHY IT BROKE:
- `:story-static/counter-with-stories` is an `:advanced` release build, so `goog.DEBUG` is
  false and `re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?` is false.
- Story's RHS embeds ONE Xray panel per variant, so
  `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/xray_embed.cljs` `:require`s
  `day8.re-frame2-xray.mount` and `day8.re-frame2-xray.panels`. Xray's namespaces are
  therefore IN the static bundle even though no preload runs.
- BEFORE 58bd56635b, four top-level `rf/reg-view` forms fired at namespace load
  UNCONDITIONALLY, so the registrar carried at least four descriptors stamped with
  `day8.re-frame2-xray.*` provenance. That is all the `:include-ns` glob needed.
- 58bd56635b wrapped all four in `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? ...)`. In release they no
  longer fire, so Xray's load-time registration footprint in an advanced build is now ZERO
  — which is exactly what the commit INTENDED (production elision, rf2-y8doi.60).
- But the Story static export still MOUNTS an Xray panel in release, and that mount path
  seats `:rf/xray` by ASSEMBLING Xray's own image over the now-empty pool. Core's
  deliberate fail-loud zero-match guard fires, the throw aborts the canvas render, and the
  smoke's `:story.counter/empty` assertion times out.

The core guard is CORRECT and must not be weakened — that was already ruled during the
rf2-atecy premise check, and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/image.cljc` says so in its
own docstring under EP-0023.

## 4. THIS IS rf2-atecy's ERROR THROUGH A SECOND, UNGUARDED DOOR

rf2-atecy / PR #9809 fixed this exact error, same glob, by teaching
`mount.cljs`'s `boot-on-runtime-ready!` loop to seat only while Xray's instruction set is
still registered (it probes for `:rf.xray/set-target-frame`). That guard sits on the BOOT
POLL. `core/seat-and-set-target-frame!` -> `mount/ensure-seated!` is a DIFFERENT entry
point into the same seat, and it carries no such check: `ensure-seated!` guards only on
`(rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter)`. So the earlier fix's shape is the precedent, and
the earlier fix's coverage is the gap.

## 5. WHAT WAS REFUTED

- THE CORPUS HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. `spec/findings/**` on the CLJS classpath is not
  implicated at any point. The break is 35 commits and ~9 hours EARLIER than the top of the
  suspect window, and the isolation run in section 2 pins the cause to four Xray source
  files. The reasoning that made the corpus a weak suspect by symptom was right.
- PREMISE 5 IS REFUTED AT SOURCE, and it is why the window was wrong. At `a4e90ebaee` the
  step `Run the Story static-export gate (direct-gate change, rf2-9n2cv)` reports
  conclusion `skipped`, not `success` — that run never executed the step either. So
  `a4e90ebaee` was not "the last run that ACTUALLY EXECUTED the step and passed"; it is
  just the last main run before the vacuity was noticed. Measured locally it is RED.
- THE VACUITY FINDING IS RIGHT, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN STATED. `story_static_gate` arms only
  on `implementation/scripts/check-story-static.cjs` and `story-build.cjs`, so on PRs the
  step is almost always skipped. What DID arm it for PR #10139 is that
  `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` is the classifier itself, and a change to it
  hits the arm-everything block at `report-changed-surfaces.sh:253-265`. Two comment lines
  in the classifier armed all 29 surfaces. That is the gate working as designed.

## 6. BUT THE NIGHTLY IS NOT VACUOUS, AND IT IS REPORTING GREEN ON A RED TREE

`expensive-tests.yml` runs `npm run test:story-static` UNCONDITIONALLY under
`if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`. Its step `Gate — Story static export (test:story-static)` reads
conclusion `success` on EVERY nightly checked, including run 35519398372 at `c98567fa89`
(2026-09-20 15:22Z) — which is BEFORE the break — and also on the three nightlies whose
runs failed for an unrelated `Gate — Xray feature matrix` step. The last nightly predates
58bd56635b, so no nightly has yet graded the broken tree; tonight's should go red. Worth
watching, because if it does NOT, the nightly's green is vacuous in some further way and
that is a second finding.

## 7. THE FIX IS A DECISION, NOT LANDED (fence honoured)

No file in the repository was changed. Three candidate shapes, cheapest first:

(a) Guard the seat the way rf2-atecy guarded the boot poll — `mount/ensure-seated!` (or
    `core/seat-and-set-target-frame!`) seats only while Xray's own instruction set is
    registered, and is otherwise a no-op. Smallest diff, matches existing precedent
    exactly, touches `tools/xray/src` only, no hot-zone file.
(b) Have Story's static mode not mount the Xray embed at all. `static-mode?` already drops
    the other dev-time affordances, and an Xray panel in a published docs export is
    arguably in that set. Touches `tools/story/src`.
(c) Make `image_view_reads/xray-image` refuse to assemble when Xray is unregistered.

(a) and (b) are not exclusive and answer different questions: (a) makes the seat safe for
every host that elides Xray in production, which is the general case that rf2-y8doi.60
deliberately created; (b) decides what a published static export should contain. The
general case is (a).

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: 58bd56635b's own commit message says its new regression guard
in `registry_cljs_test.cljs` "cannot discriminate the production claim". That is accurate,
and this is the failure it could not see. The one lane that WOULD have seen it is the
story-static gate, which does not arm on `tools/xray/src` changes. Arming
`story_static_gate` on Story/Xray runtime source would have caught this at the PR — but it
is a release compile plus a browser drive, so that is a cost decision, not a free one.

## 8. GATES AND INSTRUMENTS

Every exit code above was captured with the redirect and the `echo $?` on ONE command line
in ONE shell, and quoted from that file — never from a pipeline through a filter and never
from a harness report. No gate was sabotaged: the deliverable here is a diagnosis, and the
control ran the other way — a local GREEN was established at `17820adc57` before any red
was believed.

The shadow-cljs lane was taken for this work (a machine-wide census of node/java processes
before taking it showed no build running) and has been released.
Merged-PR audit #10140 forward pointer: rf2-n440v (open) records the incomplete static-mode boundary: mount-time Xray presets and evidence focus links still drive the omitted Xray surface. Corrective work is tracked separately there; this closed source remains unchanged in status and closure fields.
Merged-PR audit #10140 (2d86a04fa1c8063bfbba9c3b995f5d82cc714a8e; merged 2026-09-21T04:38:12Z). Completeness: Both intended release guards are present and the spec removes its unsupported inspector promise. Coverage is incomplete at mount-time preset application and retained-evidence Xray links; separately actionable open finding rf2-n440v was created, linked discovered-from, forward-pointed, and verified in bd ready. Existing open rf2-cljo6 and rf2-1t0d5 cover different decisions/defects. Correctness: The new static-mode selection branch skips Xray calls while retaining variant setup and autorun, and the entire Xray band is omitted. Exact merged CLJS source-form probe on JVM reproduced remaining preset calls and three active evidence links under static=true; actual focus returned dispatches with no Xray frame. Captured exit 0 with worktree root verified, positive dev control. No browser/pageerror claim from this probe. GitHub browser job 106210043374 succeeded but its static-export step was skipped, consistent with the disclosed local-only release smoke. Implementation quality: The two compile-time guards are small and keep Xray/core contracts intact. Imports remain bundled as documented; no larger API/build refactor is required. The material issue is incomplete coverage of existing Story entry points, not the choice to omit the release inspector. No additional actionable quality defect found. Actionable findings: rf2-n440v. Existing finding updates: none.
close_reason:
FIXED. PR #10140 merged 2026-09-21 at trunk `2d86a04fa1` — "fix(story-static): don't drive or mount Xray in a release export". Two files, +113/-40: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs` and `tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md`. Merged on the five clauses at band 88 (0 pending, 0 failed, aggregator present by NAME, 4 runs completed at the full 40-character head, matrix unmoved).

## THIS BEAD'S OWN DESCRIPTION IS PARTLY WRONG AND IS LEFT STANDING AS THE RECORD OF A WRONG DIAGNOSIS

Read the description as history, not as instruction. Two of its premises were refuted by the workers it dispatched, and both refutations changed what happened next.

**The suspect window was wrong.** The description says the break is in `a4e90ebaee..765c370308`. It is not. The first red commit is **`58bd56635b`** (rf2-y8doi.60, "gate the four top-level reg-view sites under debug-enabled?"), which the mayor verified is an ANCESTOR of `a4e90ebaee` by exactly 7 commits — outside the stated window entirely. A bisect obedient to this bead would have searched a range not containing the bug, found nothing, and left the corpus hypothesis exonerated-but-unexplained.

**The corpus hypothesis was REFUTED.** `spec/findings/**` on the CLJS classpath (the rf2-nup2n corpus, 316 files) is not implicated anywhere. It was a strong suspect by timing and mechanism-opportunity and a weak one by symptom, which the bead said at the time; the symptom won.

**Premise 5 was wrong.** The description calls `a4e90ebaee` "the last run that ACTUALLY EXECUTED the step and passed". At that commit the step reads `skipped`. That error is what produced the wrong window.

## WHAT IT ACTUALLY WAS — TWO INDEPENDENT BREAKAGES, NOT ONE

`qj` is **`cljs.core/ExceptionInfo`** — the minified CONSTRUCTOR name, build-specific (`qj` in CI, `Ri` locally), never an identity worth chasing. The tell is that Playwright's `.stack` is empty, which a real JS Error never is. It hid `rf/image: :include-ns pattern "day8.re-frame2-xray.**" matched no loaded registration [:rf.error/image-zero-match]`.

1. **The zero-match**, as diagnosed.
2. **`reg-view` carries its `def` INSIDE the gate.** `58bd56635b`'s own commit message says so: *"the macro both registers the view AND `def`s the symbol to `(rf/view id)`… with the whole form inside the gate so the `def` travels with its registration"*. Under `:advanced` with `goog.DEBUG` false the four symbols never bind, and `views/edn_widget.cljs:116` renders `ei/edn-inspector` unconditionally, giving `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`.

Breakage 2 was PROVED rather than reasoned: making the seat self-sufficient moved the failure from `check-story-static.cjs:274` to `:282`, carrying the TypeError. **So no repair confined to the image-assembly path could have worked** — which eliminated the two options that reshape Xray's guards, on the merits and not merely on precedent.

## WHY THE FIX WENT WHERE IT DID

Story-side: neither mount nor DRIVE Xray under `static-mode?`. Both halves were required, and the mayor's own framing of this option was incomplete — it aimed only at the embed mount, but the throw enters at `shell.cljs:469` in the VARIANT-SELECTION WATCHER, and `shell.cljs:69` requires `day8.re-frame2-xray.core` directly, independently of `xray_embed`. Unmounting the embed alone would have left the gate red.

The two rejected options both reshape a deliberate fail-loud contract and neither can reach breakage 2: guarding the seat reverses rf2-atecy's recorded decision (*"The guard itself is untouched and still fails loud for every explicit seat"*) and would trade a loud crash for silently dropping the host's target frame — the `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` failure rf2-88f1/rf2-bitb built that seam to fix; refusing assembly weakens a guard `image.cljc` says under EP-0023 must not be weakened. **Correction to the dispatch brief: that second option lives in `image_view_reads` under `tools/xray`, not in core, as the brief claimed.**

## THE GATE, BOTH DIRECTIONS, ON COLD BUILDS

`test:story-static` BEFORE: captured exit **1**, `[browser:pageerror] Ri`, locator timeout at `:274`. AFTER: captured exit **0**, "Story static smoke passed.", 0 pageerrors. Both runs cold (`.shadow-cljs` and `out/` removed), so the stale-macro-cache trap is excluded by construction. Gate provenance verified by effect: the green `main.js` sat in the worker's own worktree, written 23s before the check, with no such artefact in the mayor checkout. `npm run test:cljs` exit 0 at 12,407 tests / 62,289 assertions.

## WHAT THIS BEAD LEAVES BEHIND

- **rf2-cljo6** — the ruling this fix forces: `tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md` promised in three places that the published shell "can retain its inspector", a promise `58bd56635b` silently falsified. This fix rewrites that promise. Mike rules whether to accept the loss or restore the capability.
- **rf2-1t0d5** — `set-target-frame!` is documented as behaving like `init!` but seats without ensuring registration.
- **rf2-5dihy** — the observability gap: a path-gated gate went ungraded on trunk and only the 24-hour nightly would have caught it.
- **PR #10139 is unblocked** and is the first change that will actually exercise the fixed gate, because #10140 does not arm it (`story_static_gate=false` for its own paths, so CI never ran the fixed gate on the fixing PR — the local cold-build exit 0 is the whole of that evidence).
- **A live prediction:** tonight's nightly runs `test:story-static` unconditionally and its last run predates the break. If the fix is right it goes green; if it had run before this merge it should have gone red.

description:
Filed from the review wave under epic rf2-ikbgk (report re-frame2-pair.md). The report below is the reviewer's, verbatim.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## Worker rules

- Every path:line below was read at the FROZEN review tree named in the report header. Re-verify each cite at the current trunk before editing; the review wave's earlier beads found premises that had moved.
- Act on the findings under the stance: a finding you would not spend a morning on yourself is not one to implement. Where a finding says "decide: A or B", it is Mike's call; hold it and say so in the PR body rather than choosing.
- Fences are full repo-relative paths. Hot-zone files (CLAUDE.md § Workflow) are sequential; if a finding lands in one, say so and wait for the mayor's sequencing.
- The shadow-cljs build lane is a machine-wide exclusive granted by the mayor: ask before any build, and prefer static checks and the JVM lanes.
- Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). Skills gates live in scripts/check_skill_*.py; run the ones that name your surface and say which.
- No AI attribution trailers; the PR body carries a "## Quality gates" section naming what ran and its exit codes.

---

# Senior review: skills/re-frame2-pair

Reviewer persona: read-only senior reviewer on the MCP tool-contract axis — does what the skill tells the agent to call, expect and interpret match the Pair MCP server SOURCE (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src) and spec/Tool-Pair.md at this tree?
Tree: skills-review-sep21 worktree, trunk b60a20abca
Scope read: skills/re-frame2-pair in full — SKILL.md (245), references/ (8 leaves, 1,515 lines, each read end to end), spec/ (3, 356), docs/ (4, 808), README (221), STATUS (91), RELEASING (19), package.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, agents/openai.yaml, .gitignore; preload/runtime.cljs (ns form, sentinel, machine door, DOM bridge read; full `defn` roster of the 4,114 lines) and pure.cljc (roster + operating-frame/envelope section); tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj (1,163, read); tests/runtime/*.clj (4 read, 11 by deftest roster); tests/fixture (shadow-cljs.edn, README, src/counter/core.cljs, both CLJS test rosters). ~9,000 lines.
Surfaces the skill teaches, consulted: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src — tools.cljs, tools/registry.cljs, tools/eval_cljs.cljs, tools/result_envelope.cljs, nrepl.cljs (cljs-eval bridge), tools/handler_meta.cljs, tools/get_re_frame2_pair_instructions.cljs, tools/reserved_frame_guard.cljs, tools/descriptors_data.cljs (grep), roots_discovery.cljs (port-file order), server.cljs (flags) — plus tool-descriptors.edn and test/fixtures/tool-names.json; implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc (register-listener! vocabulary, with-frame), trace/tooling.cljc (trace-buffer opts), router/diagnostics.cljc (unknown-event op-type), epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc (epoch-history order); spec/api-manifest.edn (facade roster); spec/Tool-Pair.md (§Time-travel table, Artefact home, replay contract, §Pair-tool writes), 002-Frames, 009-Instrumentation, 006, 005, 001, 014, Conventions, Spec-Schemas (heading census); tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc + story/{args,determinism,frames,plan,recorder,ui/state,ui/view_state,ui/a11y} (fn/atom roster, lifecycle/status vocab, make-frame shape); tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md, 017-Testing-Story.md (existence); docs/skills/re-frame2-pair.md (mirror).
Gates run (frozen worktree root, PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8): check_skill_mcp_drift.py exit 0; check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py 0; check_skill_description_budget.py 0; check_skill_eval_docs.py 0; check_skill_eval_packaging.py 0; check_skill_package_refs.py 0; check_skill_redirect_anchors.py 0; check_doc_slugs.py 0 (silent on success; no summary flag).

## Findings, ranked

### 1. Nine `eval-cljs` forms in the leaves use the `rf/` alias that the skill itself says the eval namespace does not have  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S]
- Where: references/ops.md:186 `(rf/epoch-history :rf/default)`, :187 backstop `(rf/restore-epoch! :rf/default <epoch-id>)`, :189 `(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:depth 200}})`; references/recipes.md:208 `(rf/reg-event :exp/probe …)`, :244 backstop `(rf/restore-epoch! …)`, :247 `(rf/reg-event …)` / `(rf/reg-sub …)` / `(rf/reg-fx …)`, :248 `(rf/reg-machine …)`, :393-394 `(rf/app-db-value …)`; README.md:121 (worked example). Root in the skill's own spec: spec/authoring-prompt.md:327 tells a re-author to cite `(rf/epoch-history :rf/default)` "verbatim — these are the contract".
- What: These are copy-paste `mcp__re-frame2-pair__eval-cljs {form: "(rf/…)"}` invocations — the throwaway-probe registration, the Experiment-loop hot-swap step, the ring-depth bump and the time-travel backstop — and every one of them comes back `:rf.error/eval-cljs-compile-error` because the server evaluates the form verbatim in shadow's default namespace and refuses any analyzer warning.
- Evidence: nrepl.cljs:762-763 builds `(shadow.cljs.devtools.api/cljs-eval :<build> "<form>" {})` — empty opts, no `:ns`, no alias rewrite; eval_cljs.cljs:234 wraps only in the fully-qualified `(re-frame.core/with-frame …)` and result_envelope.cljs `wrap-form` adds a `try`; nrepl.cljs:836-845 rejects a non-blank shadow `:err` (an unresolved alias is one) as `:rf.error/eval-cljs-compile-error`. The skill states the rule: SKILL.md:80 "spell it fully qualified … because the eval namespace carries no `rf` alias"; errors.md:27 "there are no ambient aliases". Every server-side example spells `re-frame.core/subscribe` (tool-descriptors.edn eval-cljs example 1). Control for the zero: `git grep -l '(ns cljs.user'` over the tree = 0 files (nothing gives the REPL ns an alias), while the same instrument finds `(ns re-frame2-pair.runtime` = 1; the live e2e fixture spells its one eval form `re-frame2-pair.runtime/…` and uses `(rf/` 0 times. The rest of the leaves' forms are correctly qualified (`re-frame2-pair.runtime/…`, `re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer`, `re-frame.story/…`), which is why nothing caught this: tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj pins that recipes NAME `reg-event` / `restore-epoch` (rows :experiment-loop, :trace-explain-dispatch) but nothing pins that a published `form:` string is fully qualified. Prose citations of `rf/…` (SKILL.md:80-81, STATUS.md, capabilities.md) are contract references, not invocations, and are fine.
- Action: In the nine sites replace `rf/` with `re-frame.core/` inside the `form:` strings (recipes.md:208 becomes `(re-frame.core/reg-event :exp/probe …)`, etc.). Amend spec/authoring-prompt.md:327 with "as contract citations; inside an `eval-cljs {form: …}` spell `re-frame.core/`". Add one deftest beside `experiment-loop-names-the-handler-fn-hash-wire-key`: no leaf may carry `form: "(rf/` (control in the same test: the regex must find `form: "(re-frame2-pair.runtime/`). One worker, one PR.

### 2. The docs-site mirror `docs/skills/re-frame2-pair.md` describes a skill that no longer exists (runtime injection, `scripts/` shims, `{:ok? false :missing :re-frame2}`, a 2-arity listener verb, npm install, eval as escape hatch)  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: packaging] [size: S]
- Where: docs/skills/re-frame2-pair.md:12, :21, :33-35, :41, :47-50, :65.
- What: The site page teaches (a) `(rf/register-listener! id listener)` where the facade verb is stream-parameterized `(rf/register-listener! :trace id cb)` (core.cljc:2350 vocabulary `#{:trace :epoch}`); (b) that `discover-app` "injects the runtime namespace" and fails as `{:ok? false :missing :re-frame2}` — there is no inject step and no `:missing` reason; (c) that "`scripts/` shims … exist only for the project's own e2e harness" — deleted; (d) `register-epoch-listener!` as a trigger term — not a facade export (core.cljc:2601-2602; api-manifest.edn:159 `:namespace "re-frame.epoch" :facade? false`); (e) "Install via `npm install -g @day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp`" — not published (README.md:5, mcp-transport.md:17); (f) "rather than ad-hoc `repl/eval` — the escape hatch" — SKILL.md:211 makes eval-cljs first-class.
- Evidence: the mirror lines vs README.md:5/:18/:154, STATUS.md:67, SKILL.md:211. Control for the `:missing` zero: `git grep -F ':missing :re-frame2'` over tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src + preload = 0 files, while `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing` = 2. No gate reads this page's prose: `git grep -l docs/skills -- scripts` = 0, and all seven skill gates were green with this drift present.
- Action: Rewrite §What it does / §Kickoff / §Transport from the current README (stream-parameterized verb, preload-not-inject, the diagnostic-ladder reasons, build-from-clone install, eval-cljs first-class), or replace the body with README §Install / §How the connection works verbatim. S.

### 3. errors.md and the error recipe name a dispatch-time op-type, `:rf.error/no-such-event`, that the framework never emits — the real one is `:rf.error/no-such-handler`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S]
- Where: references/errors.md:57 ("e.g. `:rf.error/no-such-event`"); references/recipes.md:144 ("e.g. `:rf.error/no-such-event` because the registered id is misspelt").
- What: An agent following "Explain this error" step 4 looks in the `:op-type :error` buffer for `:rf.error/no-such-event` and finds nothing, so a misspelt-id dispatch reads as "no error fired"; the framework emits `:rf.error/no-such-handler` for an unknown event id (the same op-type Tool-Pair.md:125 shows with `:kind :frame` for an unknown frame, and the one `dispatch`'s own validator pre-empts as `:unknown-id`).
- Evidence: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router/diagnostics.cljc:32-62 — "Emit `:rf.error/no-such-handler` when a dispatched event has no handler", emitted through `:error-emit/emit-error-both`. `git grep -l no-such-event` over spec/ and `implementation/*/src/**` = 0 files (the six hits in implementation/core/test are event-vector NAMES such as `[:no-such-event-handler]`, not op-types); control: `:rf.error/no-such-handler` = 19 src files, a nonsense id = 0.
- Action: Replace `:rf.error/no-such-event` with `:rf.error/no-such-handler` at both sites and say the agent's own `dispatch` never reaches it (validated as `:unknown-id` first) — it appears only for app-issued dispatches. Optional pin: a prompt-regression deftest that every `:rf.error/*` / `:rf.epoch/*` keyword in errors.md exists in `implementation/*/src/**` or tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src (this is the only one of the 26 framework ids the leaves cite that fails it). S.

WHAT THE BEAD REPORTED: `spec/Construction-Prompts.md`'s CP-3 row still taught the removed Flight Booker `:notify` effect. MEASURED AT TRUNK, both directions:
