title: Examples review: core small apps, counter/flows/notebook/managed_http_counter/login (8 findings: login README routes the success reply into the machine the model deliberately bypasses; login-with-stories promises an Xray host its live surface lacks; flows declares :schema but its build never loads re-frame.schemas)
description:
Filed from the review wave under epic rf2-fn0kx (report core-small.md). The report below is the reviewer's, verbatim. ## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md) > Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece. > But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer. > We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a > library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every > last fine detail and drown in the minutiae. ## Worker rules - Every path:line below was read at the FROZEN review tree named in the report header. Re-verify each cite at the current trunk before editing; the review wave's earlier beads found premises that had moved. - Act on the findings under the stance: a finding you would not spend a morning on yourself is not one to implement. Where a finding says "decide: A or B", it is Mike's call; hold it and say so in the PR body rather than choosing. - Fences are full repo-relative paths. Hot-zone files (CLAUDE.md § Workflow) are sequential; if a finding lands in one, say so and wait for the mayor's sequencing. - The shadow-cljs build lane is a machine-wide exclusive granted by the mayor: ask before any build, and prefer static checks and the JVM lanes. - Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). Skills gates live in scripts/check_skill_*.py; run the ones that name your surface and say which. - No AI attribution trailers; the PR body carries a "## Quality gates" section naming what ran and its exit codes. --- # Senior review: core-small (counter, flows, notebook, managed_http_counter, login) Reviewer persona: senior re-frame2 reviewer reading the five smallest core examples the way a first-time programmer and the AI beside them would: every dataflow traced event -> handler -> effects -> db -> subs -> view, every name checked against implementation/ and spec/, every README sentence checked against the code. Tree: skills-review-sep21 worktree, trunk b60a20abca (git status --porcelain: 0 lines) Scope read: all 20 tracked files under the five directories (git ls-files; the slice brief's "27" does not match the tracked count), ~3,500 lines: counter (core.cljs 121, README 120, index.html 31), flows (337/71/31), notebook (408/164/130), managed_http_counter (413/60/21 + api/inc.json), login (core.cljs 163, model.cljc 767, stories.cljs 408, stories_host.cljs 127, README 94, two index pages); plus examples/README.md and examples/TESTING.md in full. Surfaces the examples teach, consulted: spec/013-Flows.md (Sequencing, Lifecycle effects settle, clear-flow cleanup, direct reg-flow does not settle), spec/014-HTTPRequests.md (Reply addressing, Decoding/:auto, Aborts, canned stubs/:after-ms), spec/010-Schemas.md (Production builds, :where :machine-data, :boundary? true), spec/005-StateMachines.md (extras folded onto the inner machine event, :meta {:terminal? true}), spec/API.md name census; docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md, docs/core/introduction.md, docs/core/flows.md, docs/core/glossary.md and docs/machines/glossary.md anchors; skills/re-frame2-setup/references/first-counter.md and entry-namespace.md; implementation/core: core.cljc (dispatch/dispatch-sync/with-frame/reg-view macros, make-frame record-config), views/provider.cljs (frame-root vs frame-provider), router.cljc validate-event!, core_schemas.cljc; implementation/flows: flows.cljc, flows/registry.cljc (:rf.fx/reg-flow route, vacate-output-path!); implementation/http: handlers.cljc (managed-abort-handler), encoding.cljc (reply-target exclusivity), test_support.cljc (canned stubs), registry.cljc (record-in-flight!, clear-in-flight-in-frame!, abort-in-flight-in-frame!), json.cljc (keywordize); implementation/machines/machines.cljc (:rf/machine, :rf.machine/has-tag?); implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs (client-root, adapter); tools/xray mount.cljs, preload.cljs, keybinding.cljs, config.cljc; tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc (:network, reg-fragment, force-fx-stub-id, :variants-grid); tools/testbed-support story_host.cljs; implementation/shadow-cljs.edn build blocks for all six ids; headers of implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/flows_example_cljs_test.cljs and implementation/core/test/re_frame/managed_http_counter_cljs_test.cljs. Checks run: `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` exit 0, 58 builds listed, all six slice ids present (examples/counter, examples/flows, examples/notebook, examples/managed-http-counter, examples/login, examples/login-with-stories); `node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs` exit 0 (33 pages, _shared intact); `node examples/scripts/check-reagent-slim-boundary.cjs` exit 0 (74 sources); no clj-kondo, no JVM test, no build, no browser (none was needed to confirm a finding). ## Findings, ranked ### 1. login README and stories docstring teach the success reply landing in the machine; the model deliberately routes it elsewhere [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: readme-drift] [size: S] - Where: examples/core/login/README.md:37; examples/core/login/stories.cljs:41-46, :85, :331 (and :25-27, see below); against examples/core/login/model.cljc:604-623 and :626-678 - What: README §Managed HTTP says "that reply lands back inside the machine as just another event — `[:auth.login/flow [:auth.login/success]]`, with the reply payload appended", but `:auth.login/submit-form` sends `:on-success [:auth.login/succeeded]` (model.cljc:622), and `:auth.login/succeeded` persists the token and then nudges the machine with a bare, credential-free `[:auth.login/flow [:auth.login/success]]` (model.cljc:673-678); the model spends 40 lines explaining that appending the reply to the machine event would ship the session token as an unclassifiable positional arg (model.cljc:604-614, 633-643). - Evidence: traced submit-form -> :rf.http/managed (:on-success [:auth.login/succeeded], :on-failure [:auth.login/flow [:auth.login/failure]]) -> demo stub -> canned-success -> [:auth.login/succeeded {:status :ok :value {...}}] -> :auth.session/store + dispatch [:auth.login/flow [:auth.login/success]]. Only the FAILURE branch lands in the machine with the envelope appended (spec/005 §folding, lines 944-964, confirms the fold). Control: `auth.login/succeeded` appears 9 times in model.cljc and 2 in stories.cljs, 0 times in README.md. stories.cljs is internally inconsistent: lines 98-106 and 341-368 describe `:auth.login/succeeded` correctly, while the header cascade at 41-46, the driver comment at 85 and the success-variant comment at 331 still say `:auth.login/success` receives the reply. Same file, line 25-27: the variant roster says `:story.login/invalid-credentials` is "rejected at the schema boundary; lights Xray's Issues ribbon", while the variant itself (262-279) and the paragraph at 55-58 say it is caught by submit-form's pre-submit `Credentials` validation with nothing dispatched — the second is what the code does (model.cljc:587-624). - Action: rewrite README.md:37's last two sentences to say the success reply lands on `:auth.login/succeeded` (the token owner) which then signals the machine, and that the failure reply is the one that rides the machine event with the envelope appended; fix the three stories.cljs comments to name `:auth.login/succeeded`, and change the line 25-27 roster entry to "a bad draft caught by pre-submit validation; nothing dispatched". No code change. ### 2. login-with-stories promises Ctrl+Shift+C on the live surface, but its host page has no `[data-rf-xray-host]`, so Xray's default launch refuses [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: packaging] [size: S] - Where: examples/core/login/stories.index.html:17-20 (body is `
` + script only); examples/core/login/README.md:94; examples/core/login/stories_host.cljs:13-25, :110-114; implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:2010-2018 (build carries `day8.re-frame2-xray.preload`) - What: The README says "Press Ctrl+Shift+C on either surface to open Xray", but on the live `#/` surface the chord goes keybinding -> `mount/toggle!` -> `open!` -> `create-inline-mount-node!`, which returns nil when `layout-host` finds no `[data-rf-xray-host]` and reports `:missing-layout-host` via console.error; nothing mounts. - Evidence: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:404, :437 (chord routes to `mount/toggle!`); mount.cljs:1137-1140 (first toggle calls `open!`), :1068-1072 (`open!` -> `create-inline-mount-node!` or `@diagnostic-state`), :306-320 (needs `layout-host`), :218-231 (`:missing-layout-host`, "Xray default launch requires an app-provided true-inline layout host"); the overlay is only reachable through the explicit `open-overlay!` ("Debug/fallback launch path ... Not the default developer experience", mount.cljs:1074-1076). `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/story_host.cljs` injects no host (grep for xray/aside/createElement: 0 hits, control `defn ` 1 hit). Control the other way: examples/core/counter/index.html:25-28 carries the aside for the same preload, and `git grep -l data-rf-xray-host -- 'examples/**/*.html'` lists counter, flows and realworld_resources only. On `#/stories` Story renders its own host slot (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs:641), so the claim holds there and fails on the live surface. Not run in a browser; what would settle it beyond the trace is opening the showcase on `#/`, pressing the chord and reading the console for `:missing-layout-host`. - Action: add the counter page's `
` shell to stories.index.html (check-examples-assets already scans showcase pages, exit 0 today), or narrow README.md:94 to "on the `#/stories` surface". Cross-example: examples/patterns/nine_states/stories.index.html has the same shape and README.md:195 makes the same promise; the tool-owned tools/story/testbeds/*/index.html pages also lack the aside, so this may be one sweep rather than one page. ### 3. flows declares `:schema` on two events, but nothing in its build loads the schemas artefact, so the tripwire is silently inert in the runnable example [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S] - Where: examples/core/flows/core.cljs:36-41 (ns requires: re-frame.core, re-frame.flows, re-frame.adapter.reagent), :128 and :139 (`:schema [:cat [:= :cart/inc-qty] :string]`, `[:cat [:= :cart/dec-qty] :string]`) - What: The example teaches "add `:schema` to your event" without the opt-in require that makes it do anything; in the standalone `:examples/flows` build the router skips validation because the `:schemas/validate-event!` hook is never published. - Evidence: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:791-840 — `validate-event!` "Defaults to true when the schemas namespace hasn't been loaded" (`(if-let [validate! (rf.late-bind/get-fn-cached :schemas/validate-event!)] ... true)`); the hook's producer is `re-frame.schemas` (late_bind/directory.cljc:314-315). `re-frame.flows` requires no schemas ns (flows.cljc:14-26), the Reagent adapter requires reagent.core/ratom/dom.client + re-frame.substrate.spine + re-frame.views (adapter/reagent.cljs:4-8), `re-frame.core` reaches schemas only through `defwrapper` late-binding (core_schemas.cljc:16-18), and the build block (shadow-cljs.edn:1657-1661) carries no preload. Control: of the 8 files under examples/core carrying `:schema`, the other 7 (login/model.cljc:86, cells, circle_drawer, crud, temperature, timer, flight_booker) all `[re-frame.schemas]` explicitly, several with a comment saying why ("Pulling in `re-frame.schemas` switches on schema validation"); flows is the only one that does not. The node-test wrapper co-loads login's model, so `flows_example_cljs_test` cannot see the difference. - Action: add `[re-frame.schemas]` to the ns with the one-line comment the login model uses, or drop the two `:schema` keys (the example's subject is flows, not schemas). Either is under an hour; the first keeps the idiom the sibling examples teach. ### 4. counter's view comment names `frame-provider` in `run`; the code stands the frame up with `frame-root` in `mount!` [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S] - Where: examples/core/counter/core.cljs:52-55 ("`reg-view` hands them to you as locals, already wired to the frame in scope at render time — the `frame-provider` in `run` below is what puts this tree in a frame") - What: The first explanation a reader gets of where injected `dispatch`/`subscribe` find their frame names the wrong component and the wrong function, on the file every doc and the setup skill point at first. - Evidence: core.cljs:105-112 mounts `[rf/frame-root {:id app-frame :initial-events ...}]` inside `mount!`, and the later comment at 83-90 says so correctly. `frame-provider` is the SCOPE-only sibling that fails loud given `:id` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:118-142, "Given an `:id` ... FAILS LOUD naming `frame-root`"); docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:92 and skills/re-frame2-setup/references/entry-namespace.md:21 both teach "roots ensure; providers scope". Control: `frame-provider` 1 hit in the file (this comment), `frame-root` 5. - Action: change the comment to "the `frame-root` in `mount!` below". Comparison against the teachings asked for: the skill's first-counter.md and the boot how-to spell the same boot shape as the example (defonce client-root, `init!` then `mount!`, `frame-root {:id ... :initial-events ...}` under `^:dev/after-load`); the divergences are cosmetic (skill seeds 0 with `:counter/increment` only and names the entry `init`; docs/core/introduction.md:53 uses an unprefixed `[:initialise 3]` under `{:id :app1}`) and are not findings. ### 5. notebook's seed "Patterns" document names a spec that does not exist and an example directory that has no HTTP example [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: readme-drift] [size: S] - Where: examples/core/notebook/core.cljs:52-54 (`:patterns` seed body: "Pattern-Managed-HTTP — declarative HTTP with cancellation" ... "Each has a worked example under `examples/patterns/`") - What: This is the third document in the sidebar and renders in the preview pane, so it is prose the running app shows a reader; it points at a `Pattern-Managed-HTTP` spec and an `examples/patterns/` HTTP example, neither of which exists. - Evidence: `git grep -c Pattern-Managed-HTTP -- spec docs examples` hits only this file; `git log --oneline --all -- spec/Pattern-Managed-HTTP.md` is empty (never existed), control `git log -1 -- spec/Pattern-Boot.md` returns a commit and `Pattern-Boot` appears in 12 tracked files; `ls examples/patterns` is boot, long_running_work, nine_states, websocket. Managed HTTP is spec/014-HTTPRequests.md and lives at examples/core/managed_http_counter/. - Action: replace the fourth bullet with a real pattern (e.g. "Pattern-NineStates — the nine canonical UI states") and keep the closing sentence true; or drop the sentence. ### 6. login's Story host re-spells `model/frame-config` by hand instead of merging the one owner [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: consistency] [size: S] - Where: examples/core/login/stories_host.cljs:78-81 (`install-live-frame!` writes `:fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :auth.login.demo/managed-stub}` and `:initial-events [[:auth.login/initialise-form]]` as literals) - What: The model exists so the frame config lives once (model.cljc:745-767, "The one piece of frame config the three mounts share"); the showcase's live surface carries a second copy that will drift the day `frame-config` gains a key. - Evidence: examples/core/login/core.cljs:153-155 merges `model/frame-config`; grep `frame-config` in stories_host.cljs: 0 hits (control: 3 hits in core.cljs). `make-frame` accepts `:fx-overrides`/`:initial-events`/`:doc` as record-config (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1030-1036), so `(rf/make-frame (merge {:id :rf/default :doc "..."} model/frame-config))` is a drop-in. - Action: merge `model/frame-config` in `install-live-frame!` (two lines); keep the surrounding comment, which already describes exactly those two keys. ### 7. managed_http_counter teaches `(nil? reply)` as the initiation guard three times, then uses `:else` for it in the fourth handler [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: consistency] [size: S] - Where: examples/core/managed_http_counter/core.cljs:313-315 (`:http-counter/start-long` initiation arm is `:else`); against :117-122, :161-163, :190-191 (the rule) and :123, :164, :192 (the three handlers that follow it) - What: The file argues at length that the initiation arm must test for the ABSENCE of a reply so an unenumerated status can never re-issue the request; a copier pattern-matching the four handlers sees 3:1 and the wrapper test docstring already calls the odd one out "the REAL handler's `:else` branch" (implementation/core/test/re_frame/managed_http_counter_cljs_test.cljs:52). - Evidence: grep `(nil? reply)` 3 hits (lines 123, 164, 192), `:else` initiation 1 (313). Reachability today: only the seeded `:abort-fn` dispatches to `:http-counter/start-long`, always with `:status :cancelled` (core.cljs:285-292), so no live re-seed occurs; this is a teaching inconsistency, not a bug. - Action: reshape `:http-counter/start-long` like its siblings: `(nil? reply)` seeds, `:else` settles to `:idle`. ### 8. managed_http_counter's Start long/Cancel pair depends on a registry seam that is not on any public surface and hand-builds a framework-owned envelope [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics] [size: L] - Where: examples/core/managed_http_counter/core.cljs:46-50 (requires `re-frame.http.registry` because "the write seam (`record-in-flight!`) isn't on the public facade"), :250-292 (`record-in-flight!`, `clear-in-flight-in-frame!`, hand-built `{:status :cancelled :cancelled? true :rf.reply/cancel-reason ... :error {:kind :rf.http/aborted ...}}`) - What: A core example — the one examples/README.md:88 calls "the compact complement to RealWorld for Spec 014" — shows app code reaching into an internal registry namespace and re-spelling the uniform reply envelope; the framework's own regression test exists because that envelope "can drift from the uniform reply contract silently" (managed_http_counter_cljs_test.cljs:12-22). - Evidence: `record-in-flight!` has 0 hits in spec/014-HTTPRequests.md and 0 in spec/API.md; control: `:rf.http/managed-abort` appears in both (spec/014 lines 659-673, API.md:420, :507). title: core-instrumentation: trace ring :run-order subvec spine retains every evicted dispatch-id (unbounded growth behind a 50-slot ring)
description:
## Defect

The per-frame trace ring's `:run-order` is meant to be bounded at `:events-retained` slots. Eviction does `(subvec o 1)`, and the next run then `conj`es onto that SubVector. `SubVector.cons` appends to the UNDERLYING vector, so the backing vector gains one element per run and is never trimmed. Every evicted dispatch-id stays reachable for the life of the ring. The `:runs` map (the event payloads) is bounded correctly; the leak is the dispatch-id spine, a boxed Long plus a trie slot per event run for every frame. It is dev-only, but it is exactly the kind of growth the "bounded ring" contract says cannot happen, and a long-lived dev session or a JVM soak with tooling loaded pays it without limit.

## Where

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:279-296` — `push-to-ring!`: `order' (conj order dispatch-id)` onto the previously `subvec`-ed order, and the eviction loop `(recur (subvec o 1) …)` at `:290`.
- The same `subvec` pattern at `:176-183` (`resize-ring`) and `:701-709` (`configure-trace-buffer!`).
- Public entry: any dispatch with `re-frame.trace.tooling` loaded (Xray / Story / pair preloads, test fixtures, `rf/register-listener! :trace`).

## Failure scenario

With the default cap of 50, `(dotimes [_ 5000] (rf/dispatch-sync [:ping]))` leaves 50 retained slots whose `:run-order` is a `SubVector` over a 5000-element backing vector. Retained memory grows linearly with total runs rather than with the cap.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — a bounded JVM probe from the reviewer scratch dir against the frozen tree at `034d0c8fc8` (nothing written to the tree). Reading the private ring atom after 5000 `:ping` dispatches on `:rf/default` gives:
- `(count run-order)` = 50 and `(count runs)` = 50;
- class `clojure.lang.APersistentVector$SubVector`;
- backing vector count (`.-v`) = 5000.

CLJS (inspected): `cljs.core/Subvec` `-conj` builds on `(-assoc-n v end o)` over the backing vector, so the same growth applies. A tracker full-text search finds no bead on this.

## Smallest fix

Keep the spine a plain vector after eviction — for example `(into [] (subvec o drop-n))` once per push or resize, or a `clojure.lang.PersistentQueue` / `cljs.core/PersistentQueue` for `:run-order`. Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc`, plus an assertion in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/trace_buffer_test.clj`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM core artefact: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/core` (the `^:requires-debug` trace-buffer tests). The touched forms are plain cljc. `npm run test:cljs` covers the CLJS lane.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fix — rf2-3x7nj.4.7 (2026-09-23, worker/instr-elision-3x7nj, PR #10279)

Reproduced at trunk 2c8b8847a3 with a bounded JVM probe: after 5000 `:ping` dispatches on `:rf/default` at the default cap of 50, `(count run-order)` 50 and `(count runs)` 50, class `clojure.lang.APersistentVector$SubVector`, backing vector (`.-v`) count 5000.

Fix in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc`, at all three sites the description names: `push-to-ring!` copies the survivors into a fresh vector when eviction happened (`(if (identical? o order') o (into [] o))`, so a push that evicts nothing copies nothing), and `resize-ring` and `configure-trace-buffer!` keep `(into [] (subvec order drop-n))`. `vec` would not do: on both hosts `vec` of a subvec returns the same subvec view. `:run-order` stays a vector, so no reader changes. After the fix the probe reads class `clojure.lang.PersistentVector`, 50 elements.

Regression in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/trace_buffer_test.clj`: `run-order-spine-stays-bounded-by-the-cap` (`^:requires-debug`), reading the spine's backing size rather than its count through a private-var read of the ring store (the precedent `frame_upsert_linearization_jvm_test.clj` uses), one block per site: 200 runs at cap 3, a `configure!` trim from 23 runs to 2, and a per-frame override resize from 20 to 4, each beside a `trace-buffer` count control. Control: with all three sites reverted the namespaces went 3 failures, one per block (spine 200 vs 3, 220 vs 2, 20 vs 4), controls green; restored, blob hash equal to the committed object.
Merged-PR audit #10279 (950a0cba74f4ba056b1ae5b0a523cf4e7d6a702a; merged 2026-09-23T13:30:43Z). The existing open pagination-contract question rf2-ealv5 is reused with concrete measurement, not silently treated as resolved. Correctness: Independently ran exact merged core sources at 950a0cba74f4ba056b1ae5b0a523cf4e7d6a702a: elision and trace-buffer suites 113 tests/306 assertions, zero failures/errors, exit 0. Additional indexed-batch large-offset probe 1 test/3 assertions passes and records marker/default versus explicit-large behavior. Verified worker root and loaded source identities. Existing policy follow-up remains separately trackable and ready. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: rf2-ealv5.

title: machines-lifecycle: :final? auto-destroy never drops the actor's :sensitive/:large elision claims - the finalize commit re-installs the pre-drop registry
description:
## Defect

A machine that declares `:sensitive` / `:large` classification and ends by reaching a `:final?` state (the D4 auto-destroy) never loses its per-actor elision claims. `finalize-machine` drops them out of band (`drop-at-destroy!`, a live `swap-elision-slot!`). It then returns `{:rf.db/runtime db-after-destroy}`, built from the `:rf.db/runtime` COEFFECT captured before that drop, which still carries the pre-drop `:rf.runtime/elision` registry. The router's `reconcile-runtime-db-effect` treats an effect-carried `:rf.runtime/elision` as an explicit full-frame install and honours it verbatim, so the commit writes the dropped claims straight back. Every classified actor that finishes via `:final?` leaves a permanent `{:source :machine :actor-id <dead-id>}` claim in the frame's registry: unbounded growth for spawned `<type>#n` actors, and a registry that every trace/SSR egress lookup walks. This is the mirror image of rf2-dr0pfi, which fixed the same stale-coeffect clobber for the BOOT lowering (`registration.cljc:1068`, "a machine snapshot commit never re-asserts it"). The finalize path was not given the same guard. Explicit destroy is unaffected, because its drop runs in an fx after the event's commit.

## Where

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:717`: `(rf.machines.classification/drop-at-destroy! frame-id machine-id machine owner-token)` is the live drop.
- `finalize.cljc:662-666` and `:833`: `db-after-destroy` derives from the `runtime-db` argument and is returned as `:rf.db/runtime`.
- `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:769` / `:830-831`: `new-runtime-db (assoc-in runtime-db path next-snapshot)`, where `runtime-db` is the coeffect (`:976`) still holding `:rf.runtime/elision`. Only the boot path dissocs it (`:1068`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:320-323`: an effect carrying `:rf.runtime/elision` is "honour[ed] verbatim". Called from `core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1575-1577`.
- Public entry: any `reg-machine` with `:sensitive`/`:large` whose actor reaches a top-level `:final?` leaf on a non-birth event (singleton or spawned).

## Failure scenario

`(rf/reg-machine :pb2/child {:sensitive [[:data :token]] :initial :idle :data {:token "t"} :states {:idle {:on {:finish :done}} :done {:final? true}}})`. Spawn three via `[:rf.machine/spawn {:machine-id :pb2/child}]`, then send each `[:finish]`. Every snapshot is gone, yet the registry still holds `[:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :pb2/child#1/#2/#3 :data :token]` claims owned by the three dead actors, and it grows by one entry per future classified completion.

## Evidence

Executed with a bounded JVM probe (`probe_a.clj`, frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`):
- Singleton, finish via `:final?`: registry after boot `{:sensitive-declarations {[... :pb/m :data :token] #{{:source :machine, :actor-id :pb/m}}}}`; snapshot after finish `nil`; registry after the auto-destroy is UNCHANGED (the claim survives).
- Three spawned children finish: `snapshots left: nil`, while the registry still holds all three `child#1..#3` claims.
- Control, explicit `[:rf.machine/destroy :pbc/m]` of an identically classified machine: registry after destroy `nil`. That rules out the drop logic and points at the finalize commit path.

Tracker searched (`drop-at-destroy`, `rf.runtime/elision`, `classification … final`): no bead.

## Smallest fix

Omit `:rf.runtime/elision` from every `:rf.db/runtime` a machine handler returns (the rf2-dr0pfi move), at least on the finalize return. Simplest is to dissoc it from the coeffect `runtime-db` once in `make-machine-handler` rather than only when `boot?`. The router then carries the live, post-drop registry forward. Fence: `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc` (and/or `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc`), plus a test in `machine_data_schema_redaction_test.clj`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`.cljc` shared code, no reader conditional: `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` (`implementation/machines` `clojure -M:test`) and `npm run test:cljs`.

## Decision needed

no
notes:
== FIXED in PR #10286 (worker/machines-life-3x7nj, head 4b7dc79d95), 2026-09-24 00:27 AUSEST ==
Premise held at trunk 51494841d9. The regression was red before the fix: final_auto_destroy_elision_drop_cljs_test.cljc had 2 failures (the singleton's claim survived its :final? auto-destroy; all three spawned child#1..#3 claims survived).

This is the rf2-dr0pfi move generalised; its boot-only cond-> dissoc is removed as redundant. title: machines-core: a machine-root :on targeting the active leaf or an active ancestor does not re-enter it (root excluded from the declaring-compound descendant rule; :after not restarted)
description:
## Defect

A transition declared on the MACHINE ROOT's own `:on` (flat/compound machine), whose target is the active leaf or an active ancestor, does NOT re-enter the target. It runs action-only for a leaf target, or "re-resolve descendants" for an ancestor target. So the target's `:exit` / `:entry` do not run, its `:after` timers do not restart, and its `:spawn` children are not respawned. The reason is that the declaring-compound descendant rule is gated off for `decl-path []`, so the root falls into the self/proper-ancestor arm.

By its own definition, that arm covers a target "at or above the declaring state" (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:340`). A child of the root is BELOW the root. The only geometry row whose definition fits is the proper-descendant row (`:341`), and spec 005 calls the root a compound: "Every compound root — including the parallel root — honours its `:on` as the ancestor fallback" (`:1752`). XState v5 (`getTransitionDomain`, where the domain is the source when every target is a descendant of it and `reenter` is false) re-enters a root-targeted child.

The canonical "global reset" idiom, root `:on {:reset :idle}`, is therefore a silent no-op while the machine sits in `:idle`, which is exactly when a reset is meant to restart `:idle`'s timeout.

## Where

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:3097-3103`, where `(pos? (count decl-path))` excludes the root. The rationale comment is at `:3087-3091`: "a root-`:on` or the birth cascade is the standard external geometry". In fact the root does not get the external geometry; it gets the target-on-active-path arm at `:3185-3186` (`lca-len = (count target-base)`), which is an empty exit and entry set for a leaf.
- `transition.cljc:1490-1493`: `pick-transition` stamps `:decl-path []` for the root `:on` fallback.
- Public entry points: `re-frame.machines/machine-transition`, and `rf/dispatch` to a registered machine.
- All citations are at `034d0c8fc8`.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
{:initial :idle
 :on      {:reset :idle}                       ;; root-level reset
 :states  {:idle {:entry … :exit … :after {1000 :busy} :on {:go :busy}}
           :busy {}}}
```

At `:idle`, `[:reset]` fires. `:idle`'s exit/entry do not run and the 1000 ms timer is not restarted: its epoch stays 1 (executed), so the still-live timer keeps its ORIGINAL schedule (inferred from the unchanged epoch and the absence of any cancel or schedule fx). The same root transition fired from `:busy` works, because that is the disjoint geometry. So the reset behaves differently depending on where the machine happens to be.

## Evidence

EXECUTED. A scratch JVM probe calling `re-frame.machines/machine-transition`, with no writes to the frozen tree:

| Case | callbacks | fx | after-epoch |
|---|---|---|---|
| ROOT `:on {:reset :idle}` at `:idle` | `[]` | `[]` | `{[:idle] 1}` (unchanged) |
| CONTROL: same shape one level down, `:p :on {:reset [:p :idle]}` at `[:p :idle]` | `[:exit-idle :entry-idle]` | `[:rf.machine/after-cancel :rf.machine/after-schedule]` | `{[:p :idle] 2}` |
| ROOT with `:reenter? true` at `:idle` | `[:exit-idle :entry-idle]` | `[:rf.machine/after-cancel :rf.machine/after-schedule]` | `{[:idle] 2}` |

So the identical authored shape re-enters on a compound and not on the root, and `:reenter? true` is the workaround.

INSPECTED. The exclusion is deliberate in the code, but no ruling is recorded for it: a scan of the tracker export for the rationale and its ids found none. `machine_decl_path_default_test.clj:18-21` describes the root exclusion as the property that keeps a ROOT-declared deep disjoint target correct. ## Smallest fix

Keep the bootstrap excluded, but let a real root `:on` in. Gate condition (a) on `(or (pos? (count decl-path)) (pos? (count src-path)))`, or pass an explicit "root-declared `:on`" marker from `pick-transition` instead of overloading `[]`. This depends on the descendant-arm clamp from the sibling bead. Without it, a root-declared deep disjoint target would take `lca-len = (dec (count target-base))` and inherit that bug.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## Shape

44 slices: 21 under implementation/, 17 under tools/, 6 under examples/. Distinct surfaces are one slice each; the five trees too large for one reviewer (core/src, resources/src, machines/src, xray/src, story/src) are split by explicit ordered rules with a remainder bucket, and every source file in those trees is asserted to land in exactly one slice. The per-slice scope files and the partition script live in the mayor's session scratchpad (review-wave/partition.py) and are supporting detail only.

Each slice gets ONE child bead of this epic (the SURFACE bead, created at dispatch and claimed so it stays out of the ready pool). The reviewer appends its report to the surface bead and files ONE grandchild bead per actionable finding under it, labelled review-wave:<this epic> and surface:<slug>. title: story-ui-evidence: stacked focus-traps all close on one Escape (same-target window listeners), so Escape in the recorder export dialog also closes the save dialog, which cannot be reopened, and the recording is lost
description:
## Defect

Every `a11y-dialog/focus-trap` installs its own window-level, capture-phase `keydown` listener that calls `(.preventDefault) (.stopPropagation) (on-close)` on Escape. Listeners on the SAME target all fire, and `stopPropagation` does not stop the others; only `stopImmediatePropagation` would. So when two trapped dialogs are stacked, one Escape closes both.

The recorder deliberately stacks them: the save-recording dialog's "export" button opens the export dialog ON TOP, without closing the parent. Pressing Escape in the export dialog also closes the save dialog. That dialog resets to its idle state, dropping its captured-events snapshot, and it cannot be reopened in v1. The recording the user just made is lost, and they must re-record.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/a11y_dialog.cljs:110-198`: `focus-trap`. The Escape handler at `:151-158` is added to `js/window` with capture `true`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/review_dialog.cljc:446-459`: the recorder save dialog is wrapped in `focus-trap {:on-close on-close}`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/recorder.cljs:811-819`: `:on-export` opens the export dialog, with the comment "We DON'T close the parent dialog; the export dialog stacks on top".
- `:336-337`: `close-dialog!` resets to `review-dialog/initial-state` (via `recorder.cljc:781-786`).
- `:313-316`: "re-open is a v1.1 polish".
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/recorder_export_dialog.cljs:308-309`: the export dialog's own `focus-trap {:on-close close-dialog!}`.
- Entry point: recorder REC, then stop (the save dialog auto-opens), then "export", then Escape.

## Failure scenario

1. The user records a flow and stops; the save dialog opens with the captured snippet.
2. They click "export"; the export dialog opens on top.
3. They press Escape to dismiss just the export dialog.
4. Both dialogs close. The save dialog's state is `initial-state`, so its events snapshot is gone, and there is no affordance to reopen it. The recorded flow must be recorded again.

## Evidence

INSPECTED only. These are `.cljs` files, and the brief allows no browser.

- Both traps register on `js/window` with capture, and both are mounted at once in this flow (the parent is explicitly not closed).
- DOM dispatch semantics: `stopPropagation` does not prevent other listeners on the current target from running, while `stopImmediatePropagation` does. The listeners fire in registration order, so the parent's `on-close` runs first.
- The other `focus-trap` users (`ui/recorder.cljs:580` assertion picker, `ui/share.cljs:754`) were checked. None stacks on another trapped dialog in the flows read.

Dedup: rf2-3x7nj.25.5 is an Xray focus-trap bug in a different module and a different defect. rf2-p1ai7 added the trap to the review dialog. There is no bead on stacked traps.

## Smallest fix

Keep a module-level stack of open traps in `a11y_dialog.cljs`, and have only the topmost trap handle Escape (push on mount, pop on unmount). Alternatively, call `stopImmediatePropagation` and register newer traps so that they run first; the stack is simpler and deterministic.

Fence: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/a11y_dialog.cljs`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

This is a `.cljs` file, compiled only by the CLJS lane: `npm run test:cljs`, plus a DOM test that mounts two traps and dispatches one Escape, expecting only the top trap's `on-close`. A JVM green says nothing about it.

## Decision needed

No.

title: examples-capabilities: the flagship ssr example ships the RAW runtime-db partition as its hydration payload (bypasses project-runtime-db); copied into a routed app it puts a :sensitive route value and the elision registry in the HTML
description:
## Defect

The flagship SSR example builds its hydration payload by hand and ships the frame's RAW runtime-db partition, `(:rf.db/runtime (rf/frame-state-value f))`, as `:rf/runtime-db`, labelling it "the runtime-db partition (serializable)" and "serializable runtime-db projection". It is not a projection. Spec 011 says only the serializable projection rides the payload and that it "MUST NOT carry transient runtime state" (spec/011-SSR.md:398), and the framework's own projector, `re-frame.ssr.payload-policy/project-runtime-db`, exists precisely to redact route / machine `:sensitive` values and to OMIT the `:rf.runtime/elision` declaration registry (rf2-ybn1yb, rf2-4xut98, rf2-jm2u63). The example's own run leaks nothing, because its runtime-db happens to be empty; the defect is the idiom. The docstring invites the copy in terms ("This example has no machines and doesn't hydrate a route, so its runtime-db slice is empty here — but the shape is the same one a richer app fills in", core.cljc:207-208), and docs/ssr/tutorial.md Step 3 teaches the identical line as "the framework's (route, machines)". The sibling `resources_ssr` example does it correctly (`project-runtime-db`, `apply-policy`, `build-payload`), so the two SSR examples teach opposite answers to the same question.

## Where

- `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:379` — `final-runtime (:rf.db/runtime (rf/frame-state-value f))` ";; the runtime-db partition (serializable)"
- `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:417-420` — the hand-built payload `{... :rf/app-db final-db :rf/runtime-db final-runtime ...}` ";; serializable runtime-db projection"
- `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:207-208` — "the shape is the same one a richer app fills in"
- `docs/ssr/tutorial.md:153` — the same idiom in the tutorial that cites this file (`cf. examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc — the render + payload half`); its disclaimer at the end of Step 3 covers the whole-app-db half only, not runtime-db.
- Contrast, correct: `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:422-429` (`apply-policy` + `project-runtime-db` + `build-payload`).
- Entry point: `ssr.core/handle-request` (the `:clj` server path a reader copies).

## Failure scenario

A programmer copies `handle-request` into an app with a route declaring `{:query [:map [:token {:optional true} :string]] :sensitive [[:query :token]]}` at `/reset` (the textbook password-reset case). A request for `/reset?token=SECRET-RESET-TOKEN` serves an HTML page whose `__rf_payload` carries `{:rf.runtime/routing {:current {... :query {:token "SECRET-RESET-TOKEN"} ...}} :rf.runtime/elision {:sensitive-declarations {[:rf.runtime/routing :current :query :token] #{{:source :route}}}}}` — the raw token in cacheable HTML, plus the classification registry the framework deliberately never ships. The framework projection of the same frame ships `{:query {:token :rf/redacted}}` and no registry. The same holds for a machine snapshot's classified `:data`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED, bounded JVM probes from `implementation/core` at the frozen tree `034d0c8fc8` (classpath from `clojure -Spath -A:test`, scripts and output in the reviewer's scratch dir; tree porcelain 0 before and after):

- The example as written: `ssr.core/handle-request` with a canned article stub returned 200; payload keys `(:rf/app-db :rf/render-hash :rf/runtime-db :rf/version)`, app-db keys `(:articles :articles/load-state)`, runtime-db keys `()` — so the example itself leaks nothing (control that the probe reads a real payload: status 200 and the two app-db keys).
- The idiom in a routed frame (`:platform :server`, route above, `:initial-events [[:rf.route/handle-url-change "/reset?token=SECRET-RESET-TOKEN"]]`): RAW `(:rf.db/runtime (rf/frame-state-value f))` keys `(:rf.runtime/elision :rf.runtime/routing)`, carries the token `true`, carries the elision registry `true`; `(project-runtime-db raw fid)` keys `(:rf.runtime/routing)`, carries the token `false`, carries `:rf/redacted` `true`. Both directions read off the same frame, so the zero on the projected side is the projector working, not a probe that cannot see.
- Tracker: no bead names this idiom (searched titles and full text for `frame-state-value` with the ssr example / tutorial, `project-runtime-db`, `ssr.core payload`); prior-wave rf2-fn0kx.6 traced the payload for frame-id only.

## Smallest fix

Build the ssr example's payload the way `resources_ssr` does: project runtime-db through `rf.ssr.payload-policy/project-runtime-db` under the explicit request frame (two-arity, while the frame is live), and pass app-db through `apply-policy` with an explicit policy (`{:payload [:articles]}` is the honest allowlist here; `:rf.ssr.payload/whole-app-db` if the demo prefers), assembling with `build-payload` and a nil wire frame id (or dissoc `:rf/frame-id`). Correct the two comments and the docstring sentence. Make the same one-line change in the `docs/ssr/tutorial.md` Step 3 snippet (inside a fenced block, so no link gate reads it — check by hand) and widen its closing disclaimer to runtime-db. Fence: `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc`, `docs/ssr/tutorial.md`. No hot-zone file. The static `index.html` stand-in needs no change (its runtime-db is a hand-written sample and the README already says so). `project-runtime-db` of an empty runtime-db returns nil and `build-payload` then omits the optional key, which the existing ssr deftests do not pin.

## Gates

The payload code sits inside `#?(:clj …)`, so the JVM lane grades it: from `implementation/core`, `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.examples-test` (the `ssr-example-*` deftests drive `handle-request` and hydrate its payload). A green there does not prove the redaction — plant a `:sensitive` route in a scratch probe as above if you want the positive control. The tutorial edit is prose in a fence: verify by hand.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT (examples-3x7nj, PR #10329, 2026-09-24 AUSEST): FIXED ==

ssr.core/handle-request now builds its payload the way the Ring host does: apply-policy with {:payload [:articles]}, then project-app-db-egress, and project-runtime-db (two-arity) under the live request frame fid, assembled by build-payload with a nil wire frame id. The example's empty runtime-db projects to nil, so the payload omits :rf/runtime-db. The comments and docstring were corrected.

docs/ssr/tutorial.md Step 3 now uses build-payload plus project-runtime-db, not the bead's "one-line change". Measured on the JVM: a hand-built payload carrying a PRESENT nil :rf/runtime-db is refused by hydrate! (it returned nil and left app-db {}), while an absent key hydrates. So swapping the value alone would break the tutorial's own empty-runtime demo. The closing disclaimer now covers runtime-db. spec/011-SSR.md needed no edit.

CONTROL. A process-local JVM probe (not committed) drove the SHIPPED handle-request with a :sensitive /reset route activated in the frame:
- At trunk (pre-fix) the payload runtime-db keys were (:rf.runtime/elision :rf.runtime/routing), and the raw SECRET-RESET-TOKEN was in the HTML.
- Fixed: the keys were (:rf.runtime/routing) only, the token read :rf/redacted, and there was no elision registry.
- With the projection planted out (the raw partition passed through), the payload leaked again. Restored, the default-form blob hash matched the committed blob.

The key the projection strips is :rf.runtime/elision, and it redacts the route's :query :token. JVM gate: clojure -M:test -n re-frame.examples-test from implementation/core read 24 tests, 174 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0. A planted wire frame-id made it exit 1, which proves it read this tree.
Merged-PR audit #10329 (757ece5afd0823976c0d02eb965f2a4a8e94671a; merged 2026-09-24T01:16:52Z). title: story: (story/run (story/variant-plan id)) silently recompiles the normalized plan as an authoring body and drops its :world (seed, stubs, loaders) - refuse a map carrying :world
description:
## Defect

`(story/run (story/variant-plan :some/variant))`, and likewise `story/is`, `story/explain` and `variant-plan` handed a map, silently treat an already-normalized variant plan as an inline AUTHORING body and recompile it. The map branch of `re-frame.story.plan/variant-plan` reads authoring keys (`:setup`, `:script`, `:db-seed`, `:decorators` ...) and ignores `:world`, so everything the compiled plan carried under `:world` is dropped with no error: the seed, the decorator stubs, loaders, the network routes. The run returns an ordinary `:pass` for a run the variant never makes.

It is the obvious thing to try once the rf2-3x7nj.31.2 ruling refuses plans at the determinism gate and the golden family ("run the variant instead"), so the trap now sits on the recovery path.

## Evidence (EXECUTED)

Bounded JVM probe by the rf2-3x7nj.31.2 ruling agent, tools/story `:test` classpath, trunk 779281870b (tools/story byte-identical to trunk 7fc78b7b72). Variant `{:db-seed {:count 10} :script [[:dispatch [:probe/inc]]]}`:
- `run-variant` / `(story/run :id)`: `:pass`, count 11.
- `(story/run (story/variant-plan :id))`: `:pass`, count **1**.
Codex's independent probe for the same ruling measured the same (ending at 1).

## Where (trunk 7fc78b7b72)

- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc `variant-plan` (:1889), map branch: "a map — an inline plan body".
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc `run-inline-plan` (:1723), which compiles the map with `plan/variant-plan`.
- `:world` is not an authoring key: the variant-body schema (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc) names `[:world ...]` only as a lowering target in comments.

## Smallest fix

Refuse a map carrying `:world` at the map branch of `plan/variant-plan` (the one chokepoint `run`, `is`, `explain` and `render-variant` share) with a structured `:rf.error/story-*` error whose message says: this is a compiled plan, not an authoring body; run the variant by its id. Through `run`, it surfaces as the ordinary plan-construction error result (runtime `plan-error-result`), with no frame allocated. Do not add a "run a compiled plan" path: a compiled plan is an output, and ids and bodies are the run inputs.

Check first that no caller legitimately hands `variant-plan` a map carrying `:world`: promotion's `materialize-variant-plan` compiles a BODY built by `artifact->variant-body`, which carries no `:world`.

## Gates

- `cd tools/story && clojure -M:test`. RED first: `(story/run (story/variant-plan id))` over the seeded variant reads `:pass` at count 1 today and must read the structured error after. Control: `(story/run id)` still reads count 11, and an inline authoring body still runs.
- plan.cljc is `.cljc`; if the change touches a `#?(:cljs` branch, also run `npm run test:cljs` (a shadow-cljs lane: take it from the mayor, or declare reliance on CI).
- tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md §Inline plan: one sentence saying a normalized plan is refused.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
MAYOR (2026-09-24 10:53:19 AUSEST): QUEUED SPEC SENTENCE — rf2-nt9f1 needs one sentence in tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md §Inline plan (compiled-plan refusal, :rf.error/story-compiled-plan-target). 017 is held by the story-doc worker's open draft PR #10331. The story-ui2 worker adds the sentence in ITS PR after #10331 merges; if its PR publishes first without it, the mayor routes the sentence as a follow-up. Clears when the sentence lands on trunk.
## Worker verdict (story-ui2-3x7nj, PR #10335): FIXED

- Reproduced first. The variant `{:db-seed {:n 10} :script [[:dispatch [:inline/inc]]]}` gives:
  - `(run id)`: `:pass`, `:n 11`;
  - `(run (variant-plan id))`: `:pass`, `:n 1`.
- The fix: the map branch of `re-frame.story.plan/variant-plan` refuses any map carrying `:world`, with `:rf.error/story-compiled-plan-target`.
  - The ex-data carries `:recovery :run-by-id` and `:variant/id`.
  - The message says it is a compiled plan, not an authoring body, and to run the variant by its id.
  - It is thrown via `fail!`, so it carries `:where 'rf.story/variant-plan`. Through `run` / `is` it therefore surfaces as the ordinary plan-construction error result (`plan-error-result`), with no frame allocated.
  - There is no "run a compiled plan" path.
- Caller check: no legitimate caller hands `variant-plan` a map carrying `:world`.

title: xstate-parity dim C: interpretation and actors (lifecycle, persistence, children, errors, inspection)
description:
Dimension C of the XState 6.0.0-alpha.59 parity campaign (epic rf2-2n6uv): interpretation and actors. It grades the RUNTIME GUARANTEES around the pure transition in each system rather than the objects that carry them — snapshot status (active/done/error/stopped) and how an app learns a machine finished; the create/start/stop/restart lifecycle and whether exit actions run on stop; persist/restore (what is and is not persisted, entry actions not replayed, children restored, timers on restore graded as a RECORD only under rf2-ry7x); child lifecycle (invoke-on-entry/stop-on-exit, stop-when-parent-stops, stop-when-parent-errors per alpha.59, onDone/onError delivery, sendParent); error propagation (sync action throw, async action rejection per alpha.55, guard throw, child error, unhandled error reporting); addressing (registryKey/system.get/address versus fixed ids and generated addresses); event delivery (mailbox deferral, events to a stopped actor, dead letters); observation (subscribe/on/inspection events/SimulatedClock versus the :rf/machine sub and the :rf.machine* trace family); the pure API (transition/initialTransition/getMicrosteps/getNextTransitions versus machine-transition); durable execution (graded and handed off, not filed unless a small aligned capability falls out); and the waitFor/toPromise test affordances.

Method: for every dynamic row the SAME machine is written in both systems and driven through the same event sequence — XState through node scripts under xs/C-*.mjs against the installed xstate@6.0.0-alpha.59 dist, re-frame2 through JVM scripts under jvm/C/ against implementation/machines at trunk fe8de195bd — and the state/data/effect/trace records are compared. Static rows take "what happens when you try it" at createMachine/first send versus reg-machine. Each row is classified exactly once as MATCH, LEAD, GAP, DIVERGE-RULED, DIVERGE-SUBSTRATE or N-A; the execution-model split (actor objects and mailboxes versus one router queue and runtime-db snapshots) is settled as DIVERGE-SUBSTRATE and is not re-litigated. Only GAP rows and stale records become child beads (cap eight); the matrix lives in ai/findings/xstate-v6-parity/C-actors.md and is appended to this bead on close. No tracked file is edited and no git write is made.

description:
PR #10361, merge 3bde45c576db1f0899915c5c6d57d47b1483d4e4. The source sweep correctly reports this pre-existing runtime defect; rf2-tv5ac.81 records it only as a possible defect and explicitly forbids a behavioral repair. This open finding owns that repair.

Evidence: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/tooling.cljc:505-548 promises one node per concrete entry. live-node-for sets :id to the projected scoped key (471-475), and resource-cache-algebra-view assoc's the node under key-id of that projected key (570-577). ssr.cljc:312-333 and 404-410 deliberately replace sensitive values with content-free shape tokens. Thus two live keys [{:tenant "a"} :app/profile {:id 1}] and [{:tenant "b"} :app/profile {:id 2}] under one sensitive resource produce the same projected key: two one-entry maps have the same shapes. The second assoc silently overwrites the first node, losing its status, owners and work attribution. This follows directly from the code; no runtime reproduction was executed. Partial scope/params redaction can cause the same kind of collision.

Required correction: prevent silent loss when distinct live entries project to equal keys. Use the smallest privacy-preserving representation consistent with the tooling consumers, preserving every entry or explicitly representing a lossless collision group. Keep content-free sensitive projection: do not restore a raw key or enumerable content digest just to gain identity. Align the one-node/distinctness claims with the chosen representation. This is not a request for a new public API or identity framework.
acceptance_criteria: A focused regression with two same-shaped sensitive entries retains both entries and their different metadata; raw sensitive values/content digests do not escape. Cover an ordinary non-sensitive pair as a control and the affected tooling consumers.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT (resaudit-15, PR #10385, branch worker/resaudit-15, rebased on trunk 9d41cf3dfa) — FIXED ==

Reproduced at source before fixing. New deftest `live-view-keeps-same-shaped-sensitive-entries-distinct` (resource_algebra_view_cljs_test.cljc) installs two live entries of one `:sensitive? true` resource, scopes {:tenant "tenant-alpha-SECRET"} / {:tenant "tenant-beta-SECRET"}, params {:account "acct-alpha-SECRET"} / {:account "acct-beta-SECRET"} (same shapes), one :loaded, one in flight. On the unfixed tooling.cljc (blob 2e7241268a) the first JVM run of that namespace read 7 failures, and 8 once the in-flight assertions were added: view count 1 not 2, ids 1 not 2, statuses #{:fetching} only, owners of one entry only, live-derivation-graph 1 resource node not 2, egress project-graph 1 node not 2. With the fix: 0 failures. The fix was then removed (tooling.cljc restored to the pre-fix blob), the namespace went red again (8 failures), and the fixed file was restored and verified by blob hash (default-form hash = committed blob 34e0bc7fd4).

Representation chosen (the mayor's "ordinal within its collision group" steer): `resource-cache-algebra-view` projects every entry's key once, groups entries by the byte key-id of the PROJECTED key, and
- a group of one keeps its projected key (byte-identical output to before for every non-colliding entry);
- a larger group gives each member a `collision-key`: the same 3-tuple `[scope resource-id params']` with params wrapped as `{:rf.resource/collision <ordinal> :rf.resource/params <projected-params>}`.
Every identity position of that node (`:id`, `:output`, work-ledger work-id and record `:resource/key`, `:host-transient`) carries the collision key; `:inputs` carry the plain projected scope/params.

Why it is content-free: ordinals are assigned by sorting the group on the nodes' already-visible axes (`:status`, `:lifecycle`, `:work-ledger`, `:host-transient`, via canonical-bytes, pr-str fallback). Members that tie show identical content, so which gets which ordinal is unobservable. Raw-key-id ordering was rejected because it would let an observer who knows the candidate identities pair each node with its identity. No raw key, no digest.

Consumers checked, none broken: `re-frame.derivation.graph` keys nodes `[:resource (:id node)]` — distinct ids now give distinct graph nodes (the old collapse also happened there). `re-frame.derivation.egress/scoped-resource-key?` needs a 3-tuple with a keyword at 1 and a map at 2 — the collision key keeps both, so project-graph still mints opaque handles (distinct ones). Spec-Schemas says resource node ids reuse `:rf/scoped-resource-key` = [:tuple :any :keyword :any] — conforms. Xray's derivation graph panel labels by pr-str. tools/ not edited. No public API added. New keywords live in the reserved `:rf.resource/*` namespace (keyword-catalogue drift gate exit 0).

Regression also covers: no raw value and no `:omit` digest of any of the four values anywhere in the view, the live graph or the shipped graph; the in-flight node's work-ledger positions equal its own id; control deftest `live-view-keeps-distinct-plain-entries-verbatim` (non-sensitive pair keeps verbatim ids in view and graph).

Gates (final base 9d41cf3dfa): implementation/resources `clojure -M:test` 924 tests / 8083 assertions, 0 failures (merge base measured 922 / 8062; predicted delta +2 / +21, got +2 / +21). implementation/derivation-conformance 29 / 576 green; implementation/core 2380 / 12445 green. Pinned clj-kondo 2026.04.15 without --fail-level error: warning counts identical to base on every changed file, 0 errors. Reader conditionals: every changed form is unconditional except the `catch` class selector in `visible-order` (`#?(:clj Throwable :cljs :default)`); the CLJS lane (`CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)`) is CI's.

Out of fence, reported not changed: `re-frame.derivation.graph/collect-nodes` keys by `=`, so two NON-sensitive entries whose params differ only by list vs vector (distinct byte key-ids, Clojure-=) still collapse to one graph node, although the tooling view keeps both. spec/Derivations.md §The live resource cache view says nothing about egress projection or the collision key; now accurate as written, optionally worth one sentence.

Completeness: Reviewed all nine changed files against four closed audit findings and their acceptance criteria. Sensitive projected-key collisions now retain every live node; hydration-GC rationale, the any-site scope trigger and registered poll-cancellation documentation are corrected. The remaining two timer-description contradictions already have explicit open correction scope on rf2-tv5ac.81, which was reused and linked. Correctness: The view groups by projected canonical-byte key, adds ordinals only on collision and updates node/output/work/host identities consistently. Ordering uses already-visible axes rather than raw secrets; ordinary noncolliding keys stay unchanged. The graph egress projection handles the resulting tuple/map identity consistently. Source confirms GC rearm exceptions, the any-site normative trigger and three-kind cancellation. No additional material runtime defect established; the reported pre-existing list/vector graph equality edge does not justify broadening this repair. Implementation quality: The change uses local helpers and existing graph/egress consumers without a new public API or tools change. title: FALSE: engine and visualization agree on choice-state allowed keys
description:
Recovery of prior merged-PR audit work, explicitly requested by Mike on 2026-09-25.

Source: rf2-7thjw; status at recovery: in_progress. No original Bead has been reopened or claimed. This is a new, independently trackable record.

Audited PRs: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10409

Outstanding correction recorded by the audit. Re-check the latest trunk before editing and coordinate any active work on the source; do not duplicate a fix that has since landed.

Evidence and scope
The engine accepts :on-done and unknown keys on a :type :choice state, while the visualization grammar refuses those keys. This makes accepted machine definitions depend on which surface reads them.

Original bounded source record:
## What

Worker mviz3-4v2t6 reported this while mirroring the leaf `:on-done` refusal into tools/machines-viz (rf2-xnbyt, PR #10409). It is an engine gap, and `implementation/` was outside that worker's fence. Re-verify at your trunk.

The engine accepts `:on-done`, and ANY unknown key, on a `:type :choice` state:
- the state-node key check (the one that raises `:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key`) skips choice states;
- the choice state's own forbidden-key list does not include `:on-done`.

The viz checks the state AFTER `:choice` is desugared to `:always`, so it refuses both, and the two now disagree. The unknown-key half predates PR #10409; the new leaf check added `:on-done` to it.

That is a silent swallow, which spec/Conventions.md forbids: a choice state has no completed compound child, and an unknown key is never read.

## Required correction
- Make the engine's registration check refuse unknown keys on a choice state, using the existing `:rf.error/machine-unknown-node-key`, and refuse `:on-done` there. Reuse the existing leaf rule where it applies.
- Add a row to the engine/viz parity test (tools/machines-viz engine_grammar_parity_test.cljc), as PR #10393 and PR #10409 did.
- Red-first, with the fix removed.
- Check spec/005's choice-state section says what the code does.

implementation/machines/src and implementation/machines/test; the viz parity test row; spec/005's choice-state rows. HOLD: spec/005 and implementation/machines are held by worker xroot-51 (rf2-2n6uv.5.1); dispatch after its PR merges.

Reuse existing unknown-node-key and choice leaf rules in engine validation and add a focused engine/viz parity regression. Coordinate the source Bead, which was in progress at recovery; retain the existing public error conventions.

title: xstate-parity: a parallel region reaching its own :final? child raises no region-local done, so a region body's :on-done never runs (spec/005 says it does)
description:
## What

Worker mengine-v3kl4 found this while applying the root rule to parallel region bodies (rf2-v3kl4). Measured at trunk a21df121cd: the ENGINE never raises the region-local done that spec/005 specifies.

- A region reaching a top-level `:final?` leaf raises no done: `compound-done-paths` returns `[]` for a length-1 path.
- Live probe: region `:x`, with `:on-done {:action :mark}`, reached its final leaf, and `:mark` never ran.

The rest of the system says it works:
- spec/005 (about lines 3468 and 3491) says "a compound region reaching its own `:final?` child raises a region-local `done.state.<region-compound>` that the region's `:on-done` takes";
- machines-viz projects region `:on-done` edges in its chart, Mermaid and SCXML output (`layout_cljs_test`, `mermaid_cljs_test`, `cross_emitter_agreement_cljs_test`);
- the engine/viz parity corpus row `:valid-region-on-done` says both accept it.

So a region body's `:on-done` is accepted and silently never run, which is a silent swallow of a SPECIFIED capability.

## RULING (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance): HONOUR it, per spec/005 and XState parity
The spec is the artefact, and the engine is what is wrong. A region reaching its own `:final?` child raises the region-local done, and the region body's `:on-done` takes it. Refusing the key instead would remove a specified capability.

## Required correction
- Raise the region-local done when a region reaches its own `:final?` child, and run the region body's `:on-done`.
- Settle the TARGET semantics from spec/005 and the viz's existing projection before building. The viz tests read `:on-done :b` as "region :a completes into sibling region :b". If spec/005 does not settle whether a region `:on-done` may target outside its region, or how that composes with the parallel root's own `:on-done` when all regions finish, STOP and report the design choice.
- Keep the parallel root's existing all-regions-done behaviour, and state its ordering against region-local dones.
- Add tests red first, a probe like the one above among them, and keep the `:valid-region-on-done` parity row green.
- Correct spec/005's sentence if its wording is ambiguous; the worker called it ambiguous.

## Fence
implementation/machines/src and test; spec/005 (HOT); spec/009 if a trace row changes. Sequence after rf2-v3kl4 / rf2-7thjw / rf2-wnyaf (worker mengine-v3kl4), which holds the same files.

## Gates
machines `clojure -M:test` with predicted and actual deltas; scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh; tools/machines-viz and tools/xray `clojure -M:test`; clj-kondo plain; mkdocs --strict and check_doc_slugs for spec edits; CLAUDE.md item (e).
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT (mengine2-0u48g, PR #10432): FIXED ==
Reproduced at trunk 910f9a0498: region :x with :on-done {:action :mark} reached its :final? leaf and :mark never ran (compound-done-paths returned [] for a length-1 in-region path).

Fix (implementation/machines/src):
- transition.cljc compound-done-paths: a region body (machine carrying :rf/region) is a compound; a :final? direct child of the body returns [[]], so done-raise-fx raises [:rf.machine/done [<region>]]. The machine root still never raises one (min leaf length 2 without :rf/region).
- transition.cljc pick-done-transition: the empty region-relative done path resolves to the region body itself (node-at cannot return the scope root).
- lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc validate-transition-targets!: the region body's own :on-done targets are checked like its root :on (decl-path [] against the region's :states); cross-region-note also reads a keyword target naming a sibling region.

TARGET SEMANTICS, settled from spec/005 §Parallel regions ("every target declared inside a region ... resolves strictly within that region"; "the region name is not addressable from inside a region"): a region body's :on-done resolves within its region, like the region root's :on. A sibling region's name is refused at registration with :rf.error/machine-unresolved-target (slot :on-done). The viz's reading of :on-done :b as "region :a completes into sibling region :b" is therefore the viz's divergence, reported for rf2-g7bmr; nothing in the engine or spec supports it.

ORDERING against the parallel root: region dones drain inside the macrostep through the parent internal-event queue, FIFO in the order regions raised them; the parallel root's :on-done still fires once afterwards, only if the SETTLED configuration is newly all-final (so a region :on-done leaving its final child holds the root's back). A region born on its final child takes its done at birth.

title: INCOMPLETE: attribution hook self-tests fail under a UTF-8 locale
description:
Audit of PR #10420 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10420), exact merge 539d33aefa15996fab40903188bed0b7f6cead3f. The prose sweep disclosed existing issues; this is a new independently trackable open finding, with existing Bead statuses unchanged.

The implementer reports scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh passes 141/0 in its default locale but fails 10a, 10p and 10q (138/3) under LANG=en_GB.UTF-8, identically at base and head. Those cases exercise emoji-bearing generated-attribution text through the shared message and PR-body guards. scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-commit-attribution.sh:287-295 uses a shell [a-z] range to distinguish a generated marker prefix from prose, under the ambient locale. Source inspection identifies that as a candidate, not a reproduced root cause. No audit rerun is claimed.

Required correction
Reproduce the existing three cases under the reported UTF-8 locale and the passing control locale; identify whether the detector or fixture is responsible and make the intended result consistent. Preserve actual-marker refusal, prose-about-markers acceptance, and quoted diagnostics. If the policy is ASCII-based, make that interpretation explicit at the narrow predicate boundary rather than depending on caller locale. Do not merely skip the failing cases or weaken the guard. This is a distinct portability defect, not a claim that the prose sweep introduced it.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce the existing three cases under the reported UTF-8 locale and the passing control locale; identify whether the detector or fixture is responsible and make the intended result consistent. Preserve actual-marker refusal, prose-about-markers acceptance, and quoted diagnostics. If the policy is ASCII-based, make that interpretation explicit at the narrow predicate boundary rather than depending on caller locale. Do not merely skip the failing cases or weaken the guard. This is a distinct portability defect, not a claim that the prose sweep introduced it.
notes:
VERIFIED STILL PRESENT at 687266bb30 (triage 2026-09-25 19:05 AUSEST; scripts/git-hooks is unchanged between 687266bb30 and c16f8ea546). Reproduced on this machine, Git Bash, GNU grep 3.0:
- `LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 sh scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh` reads "Summary: 138 passed, 3 failed", exit 1. The failures are exactly (10a) "refused but the diagnostic never quoted the line: <robot emoji> Generated with [Cla...", (10p) and (10q).
- Control, same script, same tree, default locale (LANG unset, LC_CTYPE C.UTF-8): "Summary: 141 passed, 0 failed", exit 0. So the determinant is en_GB.UTF-8 specifically, not "a UTF-8 locale": C.UTF-8 is UTF-8 and passes.
ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE, which points AWAY from the detector's [a-z] range at scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-commit-attribution.sh:287-295:
- In the failing 10a run the guard DID refuse (EXIT=1), and the captured stderr shows its diagnostic quoting the line byte-for-byte: "    <U+1F916> Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)".
- What fails is the TEST's own instrument at scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh:2440, `grep -Fq "$t" "$AERR"`, with an emoji-bearing needle.
- Isolated with a Python-written fixture file carrying that exact line: `LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 grep -Fq <needle with U+1F916>` exits 1, and the same command in the default locale exits 0. An ASCII-only needle ("Generated with [Claude Code]") exits 0 under en_GB.UTF-8, and a nonsense needle exits 1.
- So MSYS GNU grep 3.0 under en_GB.UTF-8 cannot match a needle carrying a non-BMP character. This is the same family as CLAUDE.md instrument item (a).
10p and 10q were not isolated one by one, but they are the other two emoji-bearing cases, and 10q's message ("never quoted the trailer") has the same shape.
Surface: scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh (the 10a / 10p / 10q quote assertions). Possible fixes: run those greps under LC_ALL=C, or compare with a byte-level instrument. The detector likely needs no change, but confirm 10p and 10q the same way before deciding. CI runs on Linux grep and is not affected.
== RULING (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance)

Fix the INSTRUMENT, not the guard, unless measurement says otherwise.

1. Confirm that 10p and 10q fail the same way 10a does: the guard refuses and quotes the line, and the test's own emoji-needle `grep -Fq` misses. Show each one isolated.
2. Make the quote assertions locale-independent at that one boundary. Either run those fixed-string greps under LC_ALL=C (a byte-level match, which is what a quoted-diagnostic check means), or compare with a byte-level instrument. Do not skip, soften or delete the three cases.
3. The detector's [a-z] range at scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-commit-attribution.sh (about :287-295): probe it under LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 and the default locale with an uppercase letter and an accented letter.
   - Only if it behaves differently, pin that predicate to ASCII explicitly (LC_ALL=C scoped to the predicate, or an explicit ASCII class).
   - If it behaves identically, leave the detector untouched and say so.
4. Gate: sh scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh reading 141/0 under BOTH LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 and the default locale. It must read 138/3 under en_GB before the change; the red-before is the control. CI (Linux) must stay green.
== WORKER VERDICT (2026-09-25 19:44 AUSEST, PR #10443, branch worker/seedhook-vzlaq, base b49320735c): FIXED (instrument, not guard)

Red before, at base: LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 sh scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh read "Summary: 138 passed, 3 failed", exit 1, failing 10a, 10p and 10q. The default locale (LANG unset, LC_CTYPE C.UTF-8) read "Summary: 141 passed, 0 failed", exit 0.

Ruling item 1: each case was isolated by re-running the guard exactly as the test does and capturing its stderr to a file.
- 10a (commit-message detector): guard EXIT=1.
- 10p (PR-body arm, marker + bare session URL): guard EXIT=1.
- 10q (PR-body arm, marker beside the six prose sentences): guard EXIT=1.
- In all three, a Python byte count finds exactly 1 copy of the marker, U+1F916 included, in the stderr.
- The test's grep -Fq with that emoji-bearing needle exits 1 under en_GB.UTF-8, 0 in the default locale, and 0 under en_GB.UTF-8 with LC_ALL=C.
- Controls on the same files: an ASCII needle ("Generated with [Claude Code](...)") exits 0 under en_GB; a nonsense needle exits 1. The 10p session-URL and "pull request body" greps pass under en_GB.
- So the failing instrument is MSYS GNU grep 3.0 matching a non-BMP needle under en_GB.UTF-8, in the test, at 10a :2440, 10p :2744 and 10q :2929 (base line numbers).

Ruling item 2: those three fixed-string greps, the only sites the emoji needle reaches a grep, now run under LC_ALL=C (a byte comparison). A comment beside AERR says why (commit 6d91410d68). The cases were not skipped, softened or deleted. Under LC_ALL=C the grep still discriminates: it hits the present needle, and misses both an absent-URL needle and an emoji one codepoint away (U+1F917), under en_GB and C.UTF-8 alike.

Ruling item 3: the detector's *[a-z]* case glob (lib/check-commit-attribution.sh, the rule-3 prefix test) was probed under sh (GNU bash 5.2.37) in both locales.
- Probes: a, X, Z, é, É, ñ, the robot emoji, 1 and -. Each was tested at the bare predicate, and end to end through check_commit_attribution on "<char> Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)".
- The outputs were byte-identical across en_GB.UTF-8 and the default locale (cmp 0). Uppercase and accented letters read no-letter in both; the detector end to end exits 0 for a/X/Z (tr folds X to x) and 1 for the rest, in both.
- The probe bites: with bash's globasciiranges switched off, en_GB makes [a-z] match X, é and É. bash has it on by default, which is why the two locales agree.
- The detector is therefore UNCHANGED.

Gate after the change: LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 reads "Summary: 141 passed, 0 failed", exit 0; the default locale reads "Summary: 141 passed, 0 failed", exit 0. CI (Linux) runs the same script in test.yml.
