title: INCOMPLETE: root lifecycle source keys have no macro-stamped source coordinates
description:
PR #10427 fixes root/region action-row addressing, but the source-link part of rf2-wnyaf remains incomplete. format.cljc:407 root-lifecycle-source-key now returns [:entry]/[:exit] or [:regions r :entry]/[:regions r :exit]. The macro stamping implementation is unchanged: core_reg_macros.cljc:418-434 gets its coordinate and inline-code indexes from source-coords/walk-machine-spec and walk-machine-inline-source, whose traversal covers state trees rather than tree-root lifecycle slots. Thus an inline root or region entry/exit row has the right key but still no source-coordinate link. The PR acknowledges this explicitly under Source coords; its new tests assert the key resolves to a function, not that the registered metadata resolves to a link.

Extend the existing source walkers/co-location to the supported root and region lifecycle slots and cover a literal reg-machine or defmachine through registration metadata to Xray source resolution. Preserve production elision and named-action links. This completes the original click-to-source requirement without a new API or broader tracing redesign.
notes:
VERIFIED STILL PRESENT at c16f8ea546 (triage 2026-09-25 19:05 AUSEST; core source_coords.cljc and core_reg_macros.cljc are unchanged between 687266bb30 and c16f8ea546). Checked by reading the code; no JVM was run.
The mayor's framing holds: this is a MISSING link, not a WRONG one. Nothing in the audit shows a row linking to the wrong place.
- Xray side: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/format.cljc lifecycle-source-key (:407) returns [:entry] / [:exit] for the machine root and [:regions r :entry] / [... :exit] for a region body (after PR #10432's c25823855c, from the row's :decl-path).
- Macro side: implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc (:418-434) takes both indexes from rf.source-coords/walk-machine-spec and walk-machine-inline-source. In implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc, both start at (:states spec-form) with path [:states] (:983 and :1160) and recurse only through nested :states. So a root's or region's own :entry / :exit gets no :source-coords and no :source-code, and those rows show no source link.
- Code-read observation, UNMEASURED, and wider than the record's scope: a literal PARALLEL machine keeps its trees under top-level :regions, not :states. Neither source_coords.cljc nor core_reg_macros.cljc mentions :regions (grep: 0 hits for "regions" in either file, against a control of 46 hits for "states" in source_coords.cljc). By that reading, walk-machine-spec and walk-machine-inline-source return {} for a parallel machine, so NO node inside any region is stamped either: state nodes, transition maps and inline :entry / :exit / :guard / :action source. It is still "missing, not wrong", but it covers every region row, not just the root and region lifecycle slots. Confirm with a JVM probe (a literal parallel reg-machine with an inline region-state :entry, then read the registered spec) before sizing the fix.
Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc (walkers) and implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc (stamping core), plus a registration-to-Xray resolution test (tools/xray epoch format / projection tests). Awaiting the mayor's ruling.
== RULING (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance)

FIX IT, at the width the triage note found, if the probe confirms it. Click-to-source is an ergonomics promise. A parallel machine whose region rows carry no source link at all breaks that promise across a whole class of machine, not just one slot, so this is worth doing. It is still "missing, not wrong": nothing links to the wrong place, and nothing new is invented.

1. PROBE FIRST (JVM). Register a literal parallel reg-machine carrying an inline region-state :entry and an inline region-body :entry. Register a literal flat reg-machine carrying an inline root :entry. Read the registered metadata. Record which of these carry :source-coords / :source-code:
   - root :entry / :exit;
   - region-body :entry / :exit;
   - a state inside a region;
   - a transition inside a region;
   - an inline :guard / :action inside a region.
   If the parallel-machine reading is {} as the code read suggests, the scope is the whole :regions tree. If not, narrow the scope to what the probe shows missing.
2. EXTEND THE TWO EXISTING WALKERS (walk-machine-spec and walk-machine-inline-source in implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc) to cover:
   - the machine root's own lifecycle slots (:entry / :exit);
   - top-level :regions. For each region, walk its body's lifecycle slots and its nested :states, emitting paths shaped exactly as the Xray side reads them: [:entry], [:exit], [:regions r :entry], [:regions r :exit], and [:regions r :states ...] for nested states. Take the path shapes from tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/format.cljc lifecycle-source-key and the engine's :decl-path, not from memory.
   Keep the co-location in core_reg_macros.cljc as it is, unless the new paths need it.
3. PRESERVE production elision (source coords and inline source are elided in production builds) and named-action links.
4. No new API, no tracing redesign, and no new slots beyond root/region lifecycle plus the region tree. Root :spawn (landing in PR #10436) is out of scope.
5. TESTS: a JVM test from a literal flat and a literal parallel reg-machine (defmachine too, if it takes a separate path) through registration metadata, asserting a link exists at each path above. Also one assertion that the Xray key (lifecycle-source-key's output) resolves against that metadata. Each must be red with the walker extension removed.
== WORKER REPORT (srccoords-j3qdj, PR #10442)

PROBE (JVM, trunk b49320735c, before the fix): a literal flat reg-machine with inline root :entry/:exit, and a literal parallel one with an inline region-body :entry/:exit, a region-state :entry and a region transition with an inline :guard/:action. Read back through Clojure's reader AND through clojure.tools.reader's indexing reader (map literals then carry positions, as under the CLJS reader). Root [] (flat and parallel), region body [:regions r], state in a region, transition in a region: NO :source-coords and NO :source-code, under both readers. Control on the same run: flat [:states :a] and [:states :a :on :go] carried :source-code (both readers) and :source-coords (indexing reader). So the parallel reading was {} for the whole :regions tree, and the fix was sized to the ruling's full width.

FIX: implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc only (core_reg_macros.cljc needed no change, since its co-location splices whatever paths the walkers return). walk-machine-spec stamps the root map at [] and each region body at [:regions r], and walks each region's :states at [:regions r :states] with the existing walk-states-tree. walk-machine-inline-source keys the root's and each region body's inline :entry/:exit at [] / [:regions r] and walks each region's :states. Those are the enclosing-node paths of format.cljc lifecycle-source-key's keys ([:entry], [:regions r :entry], [:regions r :states s :entry]). The stamps ride the dev arm of the debug-enabled? gate; keyword references add no inline source. title: Flat machine: a vector target commits :state [:b] instead of :b (spec/005 §Snapshot shape says a keyword)
description:
In a FLAT machine, a transition whose target is a vector commits :state as a vector (:state [:b]) where a keyword target commits :b. Found by the docs/machines correctness review (rf2-ahrss, step 2), measured on the JVM at trunk eb53174c3d.

Code: the vector branch of commit-snapshot in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc.
Spec: spec/005-StateMachines.md §Snapshot shape says a flat machine's :state is a single keyword.

A keyword vector is a legitimate absolute-path target form (normalise-candidates), and it is taught for hierarchical machines. For a flat machine, the committed state should normalise to the keyword, or the spec should say otherwise. Low priority: the natural flat-machine spelling is a keyword target.
notes:
ADDENDUM (docs/machines quality pass, rf2-ahrss step 3): the same spelling split appears in HIERARCHICAL machines. A root-level leaf reached with a VECTOR target reads :state [:unauthenticated], in both the pure transition result and the live snapshot. Reached with a KEYWORD target it reads :unauthenticated in the pure result; the live snapshot was not checked for that case. So the committed :state spelling depends on how the target was written, not just on the configuration.
VERDICT (worker flatvec-gk36e, PR #10510): FIXED per the mayor's ruling that the code follows spec/005 §Snapshot shape.

- Reproduced on the JVM: in a flat machine, {:go [:b]} and {:go {:target [:b]}} committed :state [:b], while {:go :b} committed :b.
- Fix: in commit-snapshot (implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc), a vector target whose descended leaf has one element now collapses to its keyword when the machine is flat. A new private flat-machine? helper decides that: no root state declares :states, and the spec is not a parallel region (:rf/region). Hierarchical and parallel machines are unchanged.
- Regression: implementation/machines/test/re_frame/flat_vector_target_state_cljs_test.cljc (dual-runtime). It covers the flat pure and live paths committing :b, a hierarchical [:in :home] staying [:in :home], and a hierarchical root-level [:out] staying [:out].
  - With the fix removed: 3 failures, (not (= :b [:b])).
  - With a naive collapse of every single-element vector: 1 failure, (not (= [:out] :out)).
- Machines JVM suite: 1519/6474 -> 1521/6485, 0 failures.

MULTI-ELEMENT VECTOR TARGET IN A FLAT MACHINE: registration already refuses it with :rf.error/machine-unresolved-target, so it was left as is. This was measured for :on, :always and :after. The pure machine-transition on an unregistered definition still commits [:a :b], but the pure path validates no target at all: an unresolved keyword :zzz commits :zzz the same way.

PARALLEL: parallel.cljc has no vector branch of its own. Region-local transitions run through the same commit-snapshot with the region's synthetic spec, and root region-qualified targets pass a one-element in-region path as a keyword. So a flat region's region-local [:b] target still commits {:r1 [:b]}, before and after the fix; the :rf/region exclusion keeps parallel unchanged, as ruled. Extending the collapse to flat regions is a one-condition change if wanted.

ADDENDUM (hierarchical spelling split): reproduced. In a hierarchical machine a root-level leaf reached by the vector target [:out] commits [:out], and reached by the keyword target :out commits :out. Out of scope under the ruling (hierarchical unchanged). Spec 005 §Snapshot shape says a compound machine's :state is a vector path, so it is the keyword arm, not the vector arm, that departs from the spec there.

description:

Passing re-frame.ssr/hydrate! the frame VALUE that rf/make-frame returns, rather than the frame's id, seeds app-db but SILENTLY SKIPS the hydration-mismatch check: the render-tree fn is never called, and no server hash is stored. The shipped examples pass the id, so they are unaffected. But nothing refuses the value form, and a safety check that silently does not run is the worst failure shape.
Code: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc, hydrate! (about :147) and the frame-target check above it (about :120-145, which compares (:rf/frame-id payload) to target with not=).

MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): normalise, don't refuse. hydrate!'s frame option accepts a frame id OR a frame value, normalised through the framework's existing frame-target->id helper, the same way rf2-74k7f fixed ts/assert-path-equals (PR #10472; test_support.cljc resolve-frame uses rf.frame/frame-target->id). Everything downstream then sees the id: the payload frame-id comparison, the dispatch, verify-hydration! and the render-tree call under the frame's scope. Reproduce first on the JVM. Regression both ways:
- with a frame value, a planted divergence throws :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch, and a faithful payload verifies clean;
- the id form is unchanged.
Show it red with the normalisation removed. Update the hydrate! docstring and docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md's hydrate! entry to say it takes either, if they currently say id only. Check the sibling client entry points in boot.cljc (e.g. streaming-install!, verify-hydration!) for the same id-only assumption, and apply the same normalisation where they take a frame.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #10526 (merged, trunk 1fd7c2aeee). hydrate!, verify-hydration! and streaming-install! now normalise the frame value through frame-target->id, so a frame VALUE and a frame id reach the same frame; the hydrate-page! failure record carries the normalised id. Regressions: implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_hydrate_frame_value_test.clj (JVM) and streaming_install_frame_value_dom_cljs_test.cljs (browser lane, graded by CI). CI 88/88 at head 65d9e00cdc. Worker note: skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/initial-spec.md still names the bare id; it is a historical design record and was left alone.

title: Tier (public or private) for public vars and options with no manifest row or docs entry
description:
MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26), the principle to apply per var:
- a var that exists for tests or tools (http test-support request-chain and canned helpers, in-flight snapshots, seed-*-for-test!, clear-all-*!, interceptors-snapshot) is classified at the IMPLEMENTATION tier in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn and gets a one-line docs entry at that tier;
- a var no caller outside its namespace needs becomes private;
- a documented substrate-author surface (performance entry-id, build-name, mark-and-measure, retain-entries?) is classified public-for-substrate-authors, per its own docstring;
- the two undocumented options (:ssr-blocking-timeout-ms, the resources :timeout-ms spec key) are documented where their siblings are.
HELD with #10504: spec/api-manifest*.edn and spec/API.md are one hot-zone holding, so cluster them into #10504's dispatch.

From GitHub issue #10506 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** decision → task · **Priority:** P3 · **Surface:** `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` (hot-zone holding), the owning source files, and `docs/api/`

These are public in the code but have no `spec/api-manifest.edn` row and/or no docs entry. For each, decide: make it private, or classify it in the metadata sidecar, regenerate the manifest and document it.

- `re-frame.performance`: `entry-id` (its docstring calls it PUBLIC for substrate authors), `build-name`, `mark-and-measure`; the `retain-entries?` goog-define is documented but has no row.
- `re-frame.http.test-support`: `capture-and-run-request-chain`, `run-request-chain`, `emit-canned-*!`, `canned-*-handler`.
- `re-frame.http.managed`: re-exports `clear-all-in-flight!`, `in-flight-snapshot`, `actor-in-flight-snapshot`, `seed-in-flight-for-test!`, `abort-on-actor-destroy`, `clear-all-http-interceptors!`, `interceptors-snapshot`, `default-header-denylist` (`managed.cljc:139-163`).
- `re-frame.ssr`: the CLJS-only `streaming-install!` and `read-server-payload` (`ssr.cljc:79, 156`) have no manifest rows. `pending-error-trace?` and `clear-pending-error-traces!` are now documented in `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md` at the implementation tier.
- Options: `ssr-handler` passes its whole opts map to `drain-blocking-resources!`, so `:ssr-blocking-timeout-ms` works but is undocumented (`pipeline.clj:608`, `ssr.cljc:222`). Resources read an undocumented `:timeout-ms` spec key (`resources/events.cljc:661,1023,1198`).

## Acceptance
- Each item is ruled on, and code, manifest (via the generator) and docs follow the ruling. Gates: `gen --check`, `api-md-check`, `doc-api-check`.

Discovered by: day8/re-frame2#10467, #10468 and #10469.
notes:
== FENCE (mayor)
HELD with #10504 (rf2-kusgs): the kusgs cluster is now HELD — SEQUENCED BEHIND worker/regfx-gzepz (spec/Conventions.md and spec/009 edits). Dispatch together with rf2-kusgs once that PR MERGES.

Applied the ruling per var, by a caller census (git grep with path conversion off, controlled against a known hit):

Callers: views.cljs and substrate/spine.cljs (entry-id), the macro expansion (build-name), fx/router/subs/views and Fresco's collector (mark-and-measure). Member entries added to docs/api/re-frame.performance.md (the coverage gate grades :adapter).
- re-frame.performance retain-entries?: :tooling, beside its sibling enabled? (same kind of :closure-defines flag). DEVIATION from the ruling's "public-for-substrate-authors", which would read :adapter; a one-token sidecar change if the mayor prefers :adapter.
- re-frame.http.managed clear-all-in-flight!, in-flight-snapshot, actor-in-flight-snapshot, seed-in-flight-for-test!, abort-on-actor-destroy, clear-all-http-interceptors!, interceptors-snapshot: :implementation (tests call each through that namespace).
- re-frame.http.test-support capture-and-run-request-chain, run-request-chain, emit-canned-success!, canned-success-handler, canned-failure-handler: :implementation (http and resources tests call them).
- One-line entries for all twelve under a new Framework integration section on docs/api/re-frame.http.md.
- emit-canned-failure!: made private (no caller outside its namespace; its one outside mention is a comment).
- re-frame.http.managed/default-header-denylist: the re-export was removed (no caller anywhere; tests read the home var in re-frame.http.privacy-headers), with managed's now-unused require of that namespace.

title: Spec disagrees with code: :platforms on events, :carriers refusal timing, :initial-events failure routing, :recovery placement
description:
Found by the docs/api review, steps 1-2 (rf2-elnoo, PR #10549, merged 2026-09-26 at trunk a55df1a1e3). Each item is a CLAIM measured by that review; re-verify it at tip before acting.

1. :platforms on EVENTS. spec/011:1507, spec/API.md and spec/001-Registration say :platforms gates events. The router never reads it for events, and spec/Spec-Schemas.md:342 limits it to fx/cofx.
2. :carriers. spec/009:2308 says a malformed :carriers block is refused at registration. It is refused at the next request.
3. :initial-events failures. spec/011:1461 sends them to :error-view; strict construction sends them to :on-error. As a consequence, the default projector's cofx-value-invalid -> 400 path can never fire under the Ring handler.
4. :recovery. spec/010:183 places it in the trace tags; spec/009 and the code put it at the top level of the event.

MAYOR RULINGS (2026-09-26): the CODE is the reference in all four.
(1) :platforms applies to fx and cofx only. Correct spec/011, spec/API.md and spec/001.
(2) Correct spec/009 to "refused at the next request".
(3) Correct spec/011 to route :initial-events failures to :on-error. If the projector's cofx-value-invalid -> 400 branch is unreachable, remove it; if the worker finds a live path, document that path instead.
(4) Correct spec/010 to the top-level placement.
spec/API.md, spec/009 and spec/Spec-Schemas.md are hot zones.

title: re-frame2-pair: server :restore-rejected hint too narrow, and no gate checks tool argument signatures
description:
From GitHub issue #10544 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** bug + gate improvement · **Priority:** P3 · **Area:** `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp`, `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py`

## Gap
Found during the `re-frame2-pair` skill review (day8/re-frame2#10537), which fixed the skill side by hand.

1. **The hint is too narrow.** `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/restore_epoch.cljs:112` names only "not in ring / drain in flight" for `:restore-rejected`. The reason covers all seven restore failure modes (`runtime.cljs:2249-2260`). An agent following the hint misdiagnoses the other five.
2. **Argument drift is ungated.** `check_skill_mcp_drift.py` checks tool names only. The skill's argument table in `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md` had drifted from the descriptor `:input-keys`: a missing `frame?` on six tools, and `get-path` taking `path | paths`. Nothing caught it.

## What to do
1. Make the hint name all seven modes, or point to where they are listed (`skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md` has the table).
2. Extend the drift check to compare `mcp-transport.md`'s argument column with each descriptor's `:input-keys`. Give it a self-test that plants a missing argument and goes red.

## Acceptance
- The hint is accurate.
- The drift check fails on an argument mismatch and passes on the current tree.
- The node lane for `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` is green. It takes the shadow-cljs build lane.

MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): do both.
(1) The :restore-rejected hint names all seven modes, or points at the ops.md table. Pick the shorter hint that stays accurate.
(2) scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py compares mcp-transport.md's argument column against each descriptor's :input-keys, with a self-test that plants a missing argument and goes red.
The tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp node lane takes the shadow-cljs build lane, so rely on CI for it unless the mayor grants the lane.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT (worktree gates-wbx0q, PR #10576, commit "fix(re-frame2-pair): route the :restore-rejected hint ...") — FIXED, both halves of the ruling.

(1) HINT. tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/restore_epoch.cljs: the :restore-rejected :hint now reads "one of the seven restore failure modes tabled in skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md §Time-travel", and says the error trace's :operation names the mode. The ruling asked for the shorter of the two accurate hints, and this is it. The table is the one maintained list. The old hint also filtered the trace read to :rf.epoch/*, which misses unknown-frame (:rf.error/no-such-handler, emitted by emit-error! as :op-type :error). restore_epoch_test.cljs surfaces-restore-rejected-when-runtime-returns-false now asserts the hint names "references/ops.md §Time-travel". It is a CLJS test. The node lane takes the shadow-cljs lane, so it relies on CI.

(2) GATE. scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py gains an arg-signature axis, run by both the default mode and --self-test, both already wired in test.yml, so nothing needed rewiring. The reference is tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn :input-keys, the generated manifest CI drift-checks against the live registry. Each transport-index row's first {...} code span is split on "," and on the escaped "\|", with "?" stripped. Directions: missing-arg (the tool takes a key the row omits and the table does not exempt; the exempt keys are build, max-tokens, cache, mode, modes, epochs-mode, dedup, elision and include-sensitive, per the table's own preamble), stale-arg (the row names a key the tool does not take), and unparsed-arg-signature (a row with no {...} signature). The self-test plants all three against a synthetic manifest whose description carries a decoy :input-keys vector. It also requires the shipped doc to have compared a signature for every manifest tool (30 of 30).

DRIFT FOUND: 1. discover-app's row read `{}` with port only in a trailing parenthetical. The table is fixed to `{build?, port?}`, with the descriptors as the reference. The table preamble's "the arg signatures are hand-kept and no gate reads them" was rewritten to say the gate reads argument names. That sentence sits outside the argument table, which is the only part of the page the brief fenced in. It was edited because it became false.

CONTROLS (restores verified by blob hash): deleting frame? from the live list-handlers row turned the gate to exit 1 naming list-handlers:frame, and it exited 0 after the restore. Emptying the missing-arg detection turned --self-test to exit 1 on the planted missing arg, and it exited 0 after the restore.

NOT GRADED, observed only: the "?" markers disagree with the manifest :required set on describe-image (frame is written as required but is optional) and trace-window (ms is written as required but is not in :required). snapshot {frames, include, path} is written as all-required but none is required. get-path and read-ui are exactly-one-of choices, not schema-required. The ruling covered argument names only.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10576, merged 2026-09-27 at trunk b66ff71e51.
(1) The :restore-rejected hint points at the seven-mode table in skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md §Time-travel, and says the error trace's :operation names the mode. Of the two options the ruling allowed, this is the shorter. The old hint also filtered the trace read to :rf.epoch/*, which missed the unknown-frame mode (:rf.error/no-such-handler). One assertion in restore_epoch_test.cljs pins the pointer, graded by the Node tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp lane in CI.
(2) scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py checks each row of mcp-transport.md's argument table against that tool's :input-keys in tool-descriptors.edn: it catches a missing key, a stale key, and a row with no signature. Deleting frame? from the live list-handlers row turned the gate to exit 1 naming list-handlers:frame; disabling the detection turned --self-test red. Both restores were verified by blob hash. Real drift found: 1 (discover-app now reads {build?, port?}).
PR CI 88/88.

title: Test-suite pruning: implementation/core - events, effects and interceptors sub-area (child of rf2-98kzs)
description:

Frames, images and registration were done under rf2-98kzs.3 (PR #10579), and trace, observability, errors and privacy under rf2-98kzs.4 (PR #10587, merged at trunk 17b681e162).

Its "HOW THIS EPIC RUNS" section carries the mayor's rules: the report shape, the lane, the hot zones, and behaviour preservation. Also read rf2-98kzs.3's MAYOR RULING note: a documented error id stays asserted somewhere, and a verbatim duplicate (same id, identical input) may go.

THIS SUB-AREA: events, effects and interceptors. It covers the test files directly under implementation/core/test/re_frame/ whose names begin with one of these prefixes:
cofx_, fx_, interceptor_, on_, event_, events_, router_, dispatch_, dispatched_, reply_, handler_, effect_, db_, drain_, async_, timer_, flight_, after_, cascade_, trigger_

At trunk 17b681e162 the mayor's regex census found about 80 files and about 540 deftest forms. That is a CLAIM: your stage-1 baseline is the authority. List the files you took, and say if any prefix pulled in a file that belongs to another sub-area.

Nothing outside this file set is yours. The subscriptions sub-area (sub_, subs_, live_, derivation_, subscribe_, path_, reprojection_, cold_) and the examples/smoke/conformance/EP files are later children. The subdirectories adapter/, bench/, substrate/ and views/ are later too.

core runs on three lanes:
- the JVM suite, `clojure -M:test` in implementation/core;
- the node lane, which grades .cljs and .cljc files;
- the browser lane, which grades any -dom-cljs-test file.
A .cljc test that runs on both the JVM and CLJS is not a duplicate. rf2-98kzs.4's PR body is a good model for the report shape: a lane table, per-batch predicted and measured deltas, and a removal ledger naming each covering test.

title: Story recorder drops interactions when a descendant stops propagation
description:
Audit of merged PR #10558, recorder DOM-step deduplication (rf2-5oj7o item 10). Still present at origin/main 384335618a8bfd6fe85528b639bbf2380b9ec78e.

With recording and DOM capture enabled, a descendant button handler calls stopPropagation and dispatches an event. dom_capture.cljs:418-431 opens dom-step-window in the canvas root capture listener, before that handler. recorder.cljc:1103 then suppresses the event unconditionally while that window is open. The step itself is only recorded by handle-click! in the canvas root bubble listener (dom_capture.cljs:462-473, 537-552), which stopPropagation prevents from running. The app acts, but the recording contains neither a click nor a dispatch. Previously the dispatch rail still preserved this interaction. The comment at lines 540-544 incorrectly claims a descendant stopPropagation still reaches the root.

Evidence: all changed recorder source and browser regressions inspected; their positive cases never stop propagation. A Chromium DOM probe using the same capture/handler/bubble ordering gives ordinary click: handled=1, steps=[dom/click]; stopped click with new suppression: handled=1, steps=[]; stopped click without suppression: handled=1, steps=[dispatch]. Probe is a browser event-propagation witness, not a compiled Story integration test: ai/probe-10558-audit-sep23-monitor-1.cjs and .log, exit 0. Source unchanged at current main. No open recorder finding covers this.

Keep the fix local: only discard the dispatch when its replacement DOM step is actually retained, or capture the step reliably before propagation can stop. Preserve the one-interaction/one-replay property and typed-secret redaction.
acceptance_criteria: A browser Story recorder regression with a descendant handler that stops propagation and dispatches preserves exactly one replayable interaction. Show the regression failing on current code; ordinary bubbling clicks still record once and sensitive input values remain redacted. Correct the misleading propagation comment.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #10615 (commit "fix(story): record a DOM step even when a handler stops propagation").

Cause confirmed at trunk b712ee8269: dom_capture.cljs opened the DOM-step window in a capture-phase listener on the canvas root (open-dom-step-window!, lines 426-436), recorder.cljc:1103 skipped every root dispatch inside it, but the step itself was recorded only by bubble-phase listeners (attach-listeners!, lines 537-552), which a descendant's stopPropagation keeps from running. The canvas root [data-test="story-canvas-frame"] is an ancestor of each variant's mount, so this bites React handlers as well as native ones.

Fix (the smaller of the two options): the four step handlers (click/input/change/submit) are registered in the capture phase beside the window opener, so the step is recorded before any handler below the root runs. The misleading comment claiming a descendant stopPropagation still reaches the root is replaced. One consequence handled in the same commit: the element inspector also listens for clicks in the capture phase on the same root and stops its picks there; same-node listeners still run after stopPropagation, and the shell installs the recorder first, so an inspector pick would have become a recorded [:click] step. handle-click! now skips a click the inspector takes as a pick (inspect mode still on, or propagation already stopped), which is order-independent.

Decisive measurements (browser lane, :browser-test, this worktree):
- Regression a-click-whose-handler-stops-propagation-records-one-step: with the fix removed (listeners back to bubble) it FAILED (recorded entries [] instead of [:dom/click]; script [] instead of one [:click] step); with the fix it passes.
- a-typed-password-whose-handler-stops-propagation-records-the-redacted-step: FAILED with the fix removed; passes with it, and no plaintext appears.
- an-inspector-pick-records-no-step: with the guard removed it FAILED in both listener orders; passes with it.
- Controls green throughout: an ordinary click records exactly one :dom/click (click-listener-captures-with-selector, a-click-that-dispatches-records-only-the-click), and the typed-secret redaction rows stayed green.
- Browser base 1141 tests / 6305 assertions green; the fix-removed run 1148 / 6322 with exactly the expected failures; every plant restored and verified by blob hash.
- PR #10615 CI on head 16b320b4b9 (merge onto trunk 1c65672d0a): 88 checks, 0 failed. :browser-test 1148 / 6324, 0 failures (+7 over base, all from the PR's own rows). :node-test 12347 / 65937, 0 failures (+18 = +7 from the PR + 11 from trunk's own new rows).

title: Play runner: a failed dispatch step over a captured exception record reports a message naming nothing
description:
Found by rf2-lxkhh (owner), not fixed there: a coverage PR changes no production code.

`re-frame.story.play.runner-events/dispatch-step-result` builds a failing `:dispatch` / `:dispatch-sync` step's `:message` as `(or (:message rec) (str (:id rec) " " (pr-str (:payload rec)) " failed (expected " ... ", actual " ... ")"))`. That shape fits an `:rf.assert/*` record, but a captured-failure record (`:assertion :rf.error/exception`, built by `re-frame.story.error/captured-failure-record` for a handler / cofx / interceptor exception or an `:rf.error/no-such-handler` refusal) carries neither `:message` nor `:id` at top level: its text is under `[:error :message]`.

title: Coverage gap: decode-cursor's non-map guard is never asserted (mcp-base)
description:
Found by rf2-3h7v2.12 (owner), not fixed there: a pruning PR adds no tests.

`re-frame.mcp-base.cursor/decode-cursor` returns `::malformed` for a token that decodes to well-formed but NON-MAP EDN, through its `(if (and (map? v) (valid? v)) v ::malformed)` guard, so a consumer's `valid?` predicate is never handed a number, vector, keyword or string. No test pins that guard.

The test that names it, `tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/cursor_test.clj` `decode-cursor-non-map-edn-is-malformed-without-consulting-predicate`, says it passes a `valid?` that THROWS on non-map input. Its predicate is `(fn [m] (and (map? m) (pos? (count m))))`, which returns false on a non-map instead of throwing, so every row reads `::malformed` with or without the guard. The CLJS mirror in `cljs_branches_cljs_test.cljs` feeds no non-map token at all.

Measured at the rf2-3h7v2.12 branch: planting `(if (valid? v)` in place of `(if (and (map? v) (valid? v))` in `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cursor.cljc` leaves `re-frame.mcp-base.cursor-test` green (17 tests / 84 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0). A consumer passing a permissive `valid?` (the CLJS suite itself uses `any?`) would then get a bare number or vector back as a cursor payload.

The fix is in the test: make its predicate throw on a non-map (for example `(fn [m] (when-not (map? m) (throw (ex-info "valid? reached a non-map" {}))) (pos? (count m)))`), so the guard's removal turns the four rows red, and confirm that by planting the same fault.

title: Test-suite pruning: tools/ artefacts (one PR per artefact, largest suites first)
description:
MIKE'S INSTRUCTIONS (2026-09-26, verbatim; for tools read "/tools" where the text says /implementation):

for each distinct surface under /implementation, carefully review the unit test suite and reduce unnecessary testing. The aim is a smaller, clearer suite that preserves confidence in important behaviour, not simply fewer tests or a higher coverage percentage.
Work one artefact at a time (propose an order, largest suites first), each in its own worktree and PR, babysat to green. Use background workers as needed. Within an artefact, work in these stages, in order:
1. UNDERSTAND THE SUITE. Map its structure, the behaviours and contracts it protects, and any tests failing today. Read the implementation wherever you need it to judge what a test actually proves. Record the baseline: tests, assertions, runtime.
2. REMOVE DUPLICATION. Find exact and near duplicates: tests exercising the same behaviour, under the same conditions, with the same failure mode. Keep the clearest one and delete or fold the rest. Similar-looking tests may protect different boundaries or regressions; keep those distinctions. A .cljc test that runs on both JVM and ClojureScript is not a duplicate, and neither is a pair covering genuinely platform-specific code.
3. REMOVE LOW-VALUE TESTS. For each candidate, ask: "What plausible bug would this catch that the retained tests would miss?" Candidates are tests that:
- repeat implementation details;
- verify trivial setup;
- assert little of consequence;
- test mock or library behaviour rather than ours.
Give a concrete reason for each removal, and name the retained test that covers its behaviour. Where it is unclear, plant a fault in the code under test and see what goes red: a test that is the only red for a plausible fault stays. Do not delete a test merely because it is small, awkward, flaky or currently failing.
4. IMPROVE ORGANISATION. Group what remains around behaviours or contracts, and fix unclear names. Fold repetitive cases into a table (`are` or a data table) where failures stay readable. Simplify fixtures and helpers where that makes the tests easier to understand. Do not add elaborate abstractions just to cut lines. Always keep:
- tests that pin documentation or spec wording (the *_guide_truth_* and terminology
tests). They guard prose, not code, so they look weak and aren't;
- self-tests of gates and ratchets;
- tests of documented error ids;
- regression tests for real past bugs, unless a retained test demonstrably catches the same failure.
VERIFY as you go:
- Change in small batches. Before each batch, predict the change in test and assertion counts. After it, run the artefact's suite and confirm the counts moved by exactly that much, with everything still green.
- Then run the repository checks CLAUDE.md requires.
- Treat coverage as supporting evidence, never as proof that a removal is safe.
- Before any shadow-cljs run, ask the mayor for the lane.
Proceed wherever the evidence is clear. Keep uncertain cases and say what makes them uncertain. Do not change production behaviour, weaken a retained assertion, or add replacement tests to hold the count up.

== HOW THIS EPIC RUNS (mayor, 2026-09-26)
- ONE CHILD BEAD PER ARTEFACT, created at dispatch time (a child of this epic), each with one worktree and one PR. A very large suite (core, xray, story) may be split into several children by sub-area, each still one PR.
- ORDER: the census below, largest first. Re-derive the counts at the child's own tip; they are the mayor's regex census, not a runner count, and the runner's own baseline (stage 1) is the authority.
- ONE ARTEFACT AT A TIME within this epic. The three sibling epics (implementation / tools / other surfaces) are disjoint trees, so the mayor may run one child from each concurrently.
- SEQUENCING against live work: never dispatch a child onto an artefact whose test directory a live worker is editing, or whose open PR adds tests there. Pruning and adding in one directory collide at merge and can delete a test that was just written. Record the fence on the child.
- THE SHADOW-CLJS LANE is machine-wide exclusive, and most artefacts have a CLJS lane, so every count-verification run on that lane goes through the mayor's grant and queue. Prefer batching CLJS verification; use the JVM lane freely.
- HOT ZONES: implementation/deps.edn and implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. If a child's test-build wiring must change (e.g. a namespace regex or build id), STOP and report; do not edit them in a pruning PR.
- REPORT per child: baseline (tests / assertions / runtime) -> final; per batch the predicted and measured deltas; each removal with its reason and its covering retained test; uncertain cases kept, with why. The removal ledger goes in the PR body, and a summary on the child bead.
- This is behaviour-preserving work: production code is untouched, and CI must be green on the same check count.

CENSUS (mayor, 2026-09-26, trunk 3dd4182af7; deftest plus JS test/it forms per tool, regex count; the proposed order):

Total ~10,460 tests in 708 files.

title: reg-event codemod (M73): --write rewrites CRLF files to LF even when nothing changed (gh-10789)
description:
GitHub issue #10789: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/10789 (opened 2026-10-03T06:28:40Z under mike-thompson-day8). The body below is the issue's, verbatim. Mike's standing rule (2026-10-03): the worker that does this bead also closes issue #10789 as its last act, with a comment naming the PR.

---

The M73 codemod's write mode changes CRLF files even when they contain no event registration or contain only a manually flagged registration. This turns a bounded migration pass into unrelated whole-file changes and increases review and merge-conflict work.

Reproduced with the local codemod at framework revision `6536fae7c3c0ef76231231c0ac508442fe2b6ae7`. Its source and dependency manifest are unchanged from `412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23`.

The [M73 skill recipe](https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23/skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md#m-73--one-event-registration-form-reg-event) recommends `--rewrite --write` and says flagged sites stay untouched. This behavior also conflicts with the migration skill's smallest-correct-diff rule.

Minimal public reproduction, independent of an application:

```python
from pathlib import Path

p = Path("eol-fixtures")
p.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
(p / "no-event-lf.cljs").write_bytes(b"(ns eol-control)\n(def value 1)\n")
(p / "no-event-crlf.cljs").write_bytes(b"(ns eol-control)\r\n(def value 1)\r\n")
(p / "rename-crlf.cljs").write_bytes(
    b"(ns eol-control)\r\n(rf/reg-event-fx :eol-control/event (fn [cofx event] {}))\r\n")
(p / "flagged-crlf.cljs").write_bytes(
    b"(ns eol-control)\r\n(rf/reg-event-db :eol-control/event [(rf/unwrap)] (fn [db event] db))\r\n")
```

With a sibling source checkout:

```shell
clojure -Sdeps '{:deps {day8/re-frame2-reg-event-codemod {:local/root "../re-frame2/migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod"}}}' -M -m re-frame.migration.reg-event-codemod --rewrite --write eol-fixtures
```

Captured exit: **0**. Summary: **3 files rewritten**, with **1 rename**, **0 rewrites**, and **1 flag**.

| Fixture | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| LF, no event | Byte-identical; unchanged |
| CRLF, no event | Changed solely to LF |
| CRLF, accepted rename | Registrar renamed; all CRLF changed to LF |
| CRLF, manual flag | Registration left semantically unchanged, but file changed solely to LF |

Both unchanged-content CRLF controls had two CRLF sequences before the run and zero after it. Their content is equal after normalizing only line endings. No application boot or migration completion is claimed.

[Current source](https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23/migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod.clj): `rewrite-string` returns the zipper serialization; `rewrite-file!` compares it with the original and writes when different. The newline round-trip alone is therefore enough to trigger a write.

Proposed correction:

- Preserve the input file's newline convention and skip files with no accepted source change.
- Make the mixed-ending policy explicit rather than silently normalizing it.
- Cover LF and CRLF no-event, flagged-only and mechanical fixtures in regression tests. For the fixture set above, only the accepted rename file should be reported as changed, and its CRLF should survive.
- Add this byte-fidelity check to the generic M73 skill recipe so agents can detect unnecessary file churn before a broad write pass.

Open and closed searches found no duplicate. Related closed #10546 concerns codemod invocation provenance, not rewrite fidelity.
notes:
== VERDICT (PR #10792, fixes GitHub #10789)
Cause confirmed at source: rewrite-clj's reader reads every CRLF and lone CR as LF (probed: "(a)\r\n(b)\r\n" round-trips to "(a)\n(b)\n", including inside string literals and comments), and rewrite-file! compared that LF serialisation against the raw original, so every CRLF file was "changed" and written back as LF.
Fix (write path only, no new flags, rewrite-string untouched): rewrite-file! compares the rewrite against the original with CRLF/CR read as LF; a file with no accepted change is left byte-identical; a changed file is written with the convention of its FIRST line break (CRLF if that break is CRLF, LF otherwise). Mixed-ending rule, stated in rewrite-file!'s docstring and tested: a mixed file is left alone unless rewritten, and then comes back uniform in its first break's convention.
Reproduction (the issue's four fixtures and exact command): base "3 file(s) rewritten; summary: {:total 2, :rewrite 0, :rename 1, :flag 1}"; branch "1 file(s) rewritten; summary: {:total 2, :rewrite 0, :rename 1, :flag 1}", rename-crlf keeps 2 CRLF / 0 bare LF by byte count, the no-event and flagged CRLF files keep 2 CRLF at unchanged length.
Control: new deftests write-keeps-line-endings and write-mixed-line-endings; with the fix reverted in source the suite reads 8 failures (exit 1), all in those two; restore verified by blob hash against HEAD. Suite 68 tests / 298 assertions exit 0 (base 66 / 286). PR CI: 88 checks, 26 success, 62 skipped, 0 failed, including the codemod JVM job and All required checks passed.
Skill recipe (M73 in auto-call-site-rewrites.md): a dry run's "N file(s) would change" must equal the number of distinct files carrying a rewrite/rename finding; the recipe's pinned sha 8b17cc53 still carries the old comparison, so that check is what exposes the churn there until the pin moves.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #10792 (GitHub #10789): rewrite-file! leaves files with no accepted change byte-identical and writes changed files in their first line break's convention; regression tests red with the fix reverted (8 failures), green with it; issue reproduction now reads 1 file(s) rewritten.

title: re-frame-migration: accept pinned CI checkouts for local/root dependencies in the consumability gate (GH #10816)
description:
skills/re-frame-migration/references/setup.md's consumability done-gate (echoed by runtime-smoke-test.md's done-bar and inventory-and-plan.md) makes repinning every framework/fork coordinate to a pushed Git SHA or Maven version mandatory, on the premise that :local/root always leaves a clean runner without sources. A runner that deterministically provisions the same relative sibling checkout at a reviewed full SHA resolves :local/root unchanged. Allow either route: self-resolving published or pinned-Git coordinates, or deterministic runner provisioning of author-selected relative local roots, the latter needing a reachable reviewed full SHA, head/manifest verification, one source revision across all selected framework modules, containment, fresh selected-basis checks under every active alias, and evidence the framework artefacts are actually selected. Keep every clean-runner compile/test/release/live obligation; unprovisioned machine-specific absolute paths stay a failure case. Update setup, smoke and inventory pointers together. Acceptance: a pinned-sibling relative-root case can satisfy the gate with real selected-library evidence; missing/stale/escaped roots, mismatched revisions and zero-framework selection fail; Git/Maven routes remain valid.

Filed from a consumer migration run. The full body, with evidence links and suggested fix, is on the GitHub issue. Close the GH issue when the PR merges (PR body carries `Closes #10816`). title: M73 codemod: a bare-call rewrite to reg-event must supply a resolvable :refer binding (GH #10851)
description:
GitHub #10851. migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod (re-frame.migration.reg-event-codemod, call-site rewrite ~L1345) renames a bare (reg-event-fx ...) call to (reg-event ...) but leaves the namespace's (:require [re-frame.core :refer [reg-event-fx]]) unchanged, so the emitted call has no binding. With a mixed namespace (one accepted rename plus a flagged custom-interceptor site) the old refer must stay for the held site, so replacing it wholesale is also wrong. Qualified rf/reg-event-fx -> rf/reg-event already works (the control).

Ask: when the namespace proves the registrar comes from re-frame.core, an accepted bare rewrite adds the target binding (reg-event) to that :refer; keep imports still used by unchanged or flagged sites; never silently overwrite an existing conflicting binding; where a safe repair cannot be proved, FLAG the site with an actionable explanation instead of emitting an accepted unbound call. State the binding contract in the M73 recipe (skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md ~L562) and the codemod README.

Acceptance: explicit bare :refer for both fx and db rewrites; a mixed accepted/held namespace; an already-imported target; conflicting or unrelated bindings. Accepted calls resolve through the emitted ns form (the test observes the binding, not only the renamed token); flagged forms and their bindings stay intact; qualified-call behaviour, handler bytes and newline preservation unchanged.

Mayor triage 2026-10-04: valid, action it. The issue carries an executed source-text reproduction at a592708a84 (trunk is a592708a84, no codemod change since), with its own positive control. title: re-frame-migration: M-8 existing-:fx :dispatch-later pass must cover vector and bound arguments (GH #10872)

title: Two inline image entries for one id with the same fn silently merge and drop the second entry's :sensitive
description:
## Bug

An `rf/image` can list two inline entries for one `[kind id]` that share an implementation fn. Assembly then treats them as one registration and keeps whichever came first, so the other entry's metadata silently disappears, `:sensitive` included. The frame constructs normally and its args go unredacted.

The people affected are those relying on the declaration: dev-tool exports, traces and egress projection. This is most likely in stories and test doubles, where inline images are common.

## Evidence

**Where (trunk 475bdcaacf):**
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/image_assembly.cljc:249-268` (`descriptor-coordinate`): an inline descriptor's coordinate is `{:image <id> :inline [section id]}`, so two inline entries for one id in one image have equal coordinates.
- `image_assembly.cljc:278-286` (`same-registration?`): two descriptors are "the same registration" when coordinate and impl are equal. Metadata is not compared.
- `image_assembly.cljc:931-953` (`distinct-by-id`): later descriptors that are `same-registration?` with an earlier one are dropped before `resolve-within-image` checks for collisions.

**Repro (*probed*):** JVM, `clojure -M` from `implementation/core`, plain-atom adapter. Run at HEAD 9b20bf0093, whose `implementation/core` is byte-identical to 475bdcaacf.

```clojure
(def send! (fn [_ _] nil))
(rf/make-frame {:id :probe/inline
                :images [(rf/image {:id :test/duplicate
                                    :registrations {:reg-fx [[:app/send {} send!]
                                                             [:app/send {:sensitive [[:secret]]} send!]]}})]})
(:sensitive (rf/handler-meta {:frame :probe/inline :kind :fx :id :app/send}))
```

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| A1: same fn, plain entry first (above) | constructs; `:sensitive` is `nil` |
| A2: same fn, order swapped | constructs; `:sensitive` is `[[:secret]]` (first entry wins) |
| A3: control, two different fns | throws `:rf.error/image-within-image-collision` |

**Contract:** `spec/002-Frames.md:1060`: "two **inline** entries — `:rf.error/image-within-image-collision`". The conformance index row for `image-within-image-collision.edn` says the same. The existing test `within-image-two-inline-is-malformed` (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/image_assembly_cljs_test.cljc:56-62`) uses two different impls (`::a`, `::b`), so it cannot see this case.

## Expected

Two inline entries for one `[kind id]` in one image fail with `:rf.error/image-within-image-collision`, whatever their impls.

## Fix direction

- Reject a repeated inline `[kind id]` within one image before the general dedupe step.
- Keep the dedupe for what it exists for: one registered (namespace-authored) descriptor reached by two overlapping `:select-ns` globs. The selector already yields an inline descriptor at most once, so inline entries never need deduping.

## Acceptance

- New tests: A1 and A2 both throw `:rf.error/image-within-image-collision`. Both fail at trunk.
- One registered descriptor selected by two overlapping include globs still dedupes and constructs.
- `within-image-two-inline-is-malformed` stays green.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (sol/02 §4, derived from source); probed during the cross-review.
- Related: rf2-3x7nj.5.1 (closed) made inline registrations keep their metadata at the descriptor top level. This bead is the dedupe path, which that fix did not touch. rf2-mn2ht.19 also edits `image_assembly.cljc`, so sequence the two or give them to one worker.
- Standing note: rf2-pk4i6.8 finding #2 (dismissed 2026-09-16) left the generation cache's evict-superseded-revision fix (~6 lines in `assemble-cached`) "worth taking when next in image_assembly.cljc". This bead puts a worker there.
- Hot zones: none.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-frames-registration.md` Insight 13 and A11(a); `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/02-core-registration-images.md` §4.

That worker is the only toucher of spec/002-Frames.md for now. Do not dispatch a second worker onto it until that worker reports.
== FIXED (worker core-images-review, 2026-10-10) == PR #11057 (branch worker/core-images-review), commit 43228c62fd.
Premise held at base 02018bf667: two inline :reg-fx entries for one id sharing a fn deduped in distinct-by-id (same coordinate + same impl), first entry winning, in both orders.
Fix (image_assembly.cljc same-registration?): an inline descriptor never dedupes. The selector yields each inline entry once, so a repeated inline [kind id] reaches resolve-within-image and throws :rf.error/image-within-image-collision whatever the impls. Registered-descriptor dedupe unchanged. No spec change: Spec 002 already says two inline entries collide.
Tests (image_assembly_cljs_test): within-image-two-inline-sharing-an-impl-is-malformed (A1 and A2 orders) and one-registration-matched-by-overlapping-globs-is-selected-once (control; the selector itself yields a registered descriptor once). within-image-two-inline-is-malformed stays green.

title: Skills: structural follow-ups from a week of field-feedback fixes (restated facts drift; per-skill gaps)
description:
Structural follow-ups from a review of one week of field-feedback fixes to `skills/` (filed 2026-10-09 ~12:30 AUSEST, at Mike's request).

## What was reviewed

Every non-test commit to `skills/` from 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-09: 85 commits, excluding the unit-test trimming. Most were fixes for GitHub issues that other AI agents filed after using the skills on real migrations: #10785–#10998 for the two migration skills and Pair, and the rf2-m5q0v review sweep for the smaller skills. Each skill was analysed on its own. The decisive measurements are inline in each child bead, and the key claims were re-checked at trunk 9e84689562.

## The finding that spans skills: restated facts drift

The single biggest structural cause, in every skill that had more than a couple of fixes, is the same. **One fact is written down in several places, nothing ties the copies together, and a fix that reaches one copy leaves the others stale.** The next field report then finds a stale copy, so a fix often needs a second commit to sweep up what the first one missed.

- **re-frame-migration:** 22 of 45 commits were reconciliation between copies, or rework because an earlier fix missed a copy. Eleven issues were literally two statements of one fact disagreeing: #10811 #10816 #10819 #10831 #10848 #10855 #10893 #10908 #10909 #10924 #10927. The skill's own `spec/inputs.md` §6 *requires* a recipe copy per rule, which contradicts `spec/design.md` L1 ("leaves point at the corpus, they don't quote it").
- **re-frame2-pair:** 4 of 5 behaviour fixes needed a follow-up sweep commit (9671842e28 → faf4f6f202; ed389393cf → b2254343ba). A tool behaviour is restated across up to 9 surfaces. One stale claim survives today at `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md:17`.
- **reagent-fresco-migration:** the bridge "doors" are restated 8 times across 7 files. d2f9b09edd was a pure resync, and a copy at `references/catalog-reject.md:127-128` is still stale.
- **setup, re-frame2, xray:** round 2 of the 2026-10-02 review (rf2-m5q0v) mostly found copies that round 1 had missed, within about 3 hours of round 1.

Mechanical gates can't fix this: the existing drift gates pin names and indexes, and each was green while the copies disagreed (e.g. #10908 passed the new INDEX-COVERAGE gate a day after it landed). The fix is **fewer copies**: one owner per fact, summaries link rather than restate, and a copy census before folding any feedback fix.

## Per-skill verdicts

- **re-frame-migration:** structural (duplication, plus search commands presented as complete) → children below.
- **reagent-fresco-migration:** structural (the mixed-renderer tree is never taught as a model; census verdicts are conflated with rule tiers) → children below.
- **re-frame2-pair:** one structural flaw (behaviour restated across many surfaces) and one gap (a stale server is undetectable when its tool contract is unchanged) → children below.
- **re-frame2-xray:** a concrete user-facing bug (the install guide omits the npm peers) → child below.
- **re-frame2-setup, re-frame2:** residual stale copies after two review rounds; folded into the family-rules child.
- **re-frame2-improver, re-frame2-implementor, re-frame2-pair-retro:** healthy refinement; nothing to file beyond the family-rules child's residual copies.

## Existing beads in the same area (not duplicated)

- rf2-2n38e (GH #10998): the migration smoke test treats a legitimately nil subscription as a failure. A small one-off, in the "over-confident diagnosis" class.
- rf2-uyzs7 (GH #10997): Windows Gitlibs cache recovery. The re-frame-migration analyst judged this environment/orchestration rather than migration guidance (it fails `skills/re-frame-migration/spec/improving.md` Bar 1), so it belongs in `re-frame2-setup` troubleshooting or should be declined.

title: reagent-fresco-migration: add node witnesses for the static mixed-renderer claims to the skill fixture (optional)
description:
## Problem

The reagent-fresco-migration skill now makes several claims about how the two renderers interact in a mixed tree, all of them added this week from field reports. They are framework facts, so they can silently go false as Fresco evolves, and nothing executes them. Four of this week's issues (#10825, #10942, #10977, #10978) explicitly asked for an executable check. None was added; the stated reason was that the shadow-cljs lane was unavailable.

## Evidence

- **The skill's only executable evidence** is `skills/reagent-fresco-migration/tests/fixture/…/mig23_cold_start_test.cljs`, a node test that already also covers MIG-14, MIG-22 prop transport and MIG-34.
- **The fixture has hosted such witnesses before:** 1cf9a1d195 and 330a8acec2 (September).
- **The 35 evals are only checked for packaging,** and never run.

## Direction (optional; cheap)

Add node witnesses to the existing fixture namespace. No workflow edit should be needed; confirm the fixture's lane wiring first. Two witnesses:
- **A kept island keeps its keys.** A kept `r/as-element` inside an `h/defview` is lowered by Reagent and keeps its `^{:key}`.
- **Callbacks cross by identity.** A `capture-frame` callback crosses the bridge by identity.

Say in the fixture's README that it is the skill's general witness suite. Also state which claims are deliberately not witnessed because they need a DOM: the mixed-renderer settle (`r/flush` in `flushSync`), and MIG-26 route 3's deferred reactive read.

## Acceptance

title: A {:from-db}-scoped resource sub whose scope resolves nil projects :status :unresolved instead of throwing; retire :rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope
description:
## Bug

A resource subscription whose scope is a `{:from-db …}` resolver throws when the resolver yields nil, for example when nobody is logged in. The sub layer catches the throw, so the view receives `nil` instead of a view-model, and an always-on `:rf.error/sub-exception` is emitted. Logging out with such a read on screen therefore puts `nil` into every mounted view that reads it, plus an error record each. Under SSR, a `:rf.error/sub-exception` projects a 500. Apps must guard every such subscribe with `(when authed? …)`.

## Evidence

Code at 475bdcaacf:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:859-889`: `sub-unresolved-reference!` throws `:rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope`. The resolver is called from `resolve-scope-for-sub` (`:891-947`), and every resource sub reaches that through `subs.cljc:82-119` (`resolve-scoped-key`).
- The thrown message (`registry.cljc:878-887`) tells the developer "the view should render the \"scope unresolved\" state until the resolver's :inputs … appear". No such state exists.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc:406-410`: a throwing sub body becomes `:rf.error/sub-exception`, with the value replaced by `nil` ("Returning nil.").
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:390-404`: `:rf.error/sub-exception` projects a fail-closed 5xx (*read*; the SSR case was not run).
- `docs/resources/errors-and-warnings.md:38` gives the remedy "Resolve only when logged in, or don't subscribe". `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/views.cljs:468-475` follows it with `(when authed? @(subscribe …))`.

Repro (*probed*: JVM, plain-atom substrate, run at 989a1c6d53, whose core and resources trees are identical to 475bdcaacf):

```clojure
(rf/reg-resource-scope :t/session {:inputs {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}}
  (fn [{:keys [username]} _] (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}])))
(rf/reg-resource :t/feed {:scope {:from-db :t/session} :params-schema [:map [:page :int]]}
  (fn [{:keys [page]} _] {:request {:method :get :url "/feed" :params {:page page}}}))
(rf/dispatch-sync [:t/login "jake"])
(def sub (rf/subscribe [:rf/resource {:resource :t/feed :params {:page 1}}]))
(:status @sub)
(rf/dispatch-sync [:t/logout])              ;; (update db :auth dissoc :user)
@sub
@(rf/subscribe [:rf.resource/stale? {:resource :t/feed :params {:page 1}}])
```

Observed:

```
1 logged in, held [:rf/resource q] status => :idle
2 dispatch-sync [:t/logout] => :returned
3 deref held sub after logout (whole value) => nil
5 [:rf.resource/stale? q] while logged out => nil
sub-exception traces: 2   (:rf/resource and :rf.resource/stale?, each "… resolved NIL against the frame db — the scope is UNRESOLVED …")
```

Contract:
- Spec 016 §Subscription-side scope resolution (`spec/016-Resources.md:120`) and the re-keying contract (`:231`) require a "loud, structured error", never a silent `:idle`.
- `:222` says a subscription is "explainable as 'scope unresolved'".
- What a view actually receives is `nil`. Code such as `(case (:status @sub) …)` then fails in render, and a logged-out SSR request returns 500.

## Expected

A logged-out read of a principal-scoped resource yields a defined, renderable value. A missing principal is ordinary application state, not a programmer defect.

## Fix direction

This is Mike's decision, because spec 016:120 makes the throw normative.
- **Recommended (Opus review):** return `{:status :unresolved}`. The scalar projections read accordingly: `:data` nil, booleans false, `:status :unresolved`. Unknown resource ids and malformed policies stay loud.
  - Retire or redefine the `:rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope` row in spec 016's error roster, spec 009's catalogue and `docs/resources/errors-and-warnings.md`.
  - Drop the realworld guard.
- **Alternative:** keep the error. Then correct the message, which points at a state that does not exist. Also document that the sub value is `nil` with a `:rf.error/sub-exception`, and that SSR answers 500.

## Acceptance

- New JVM test, failing before the fix:
  1. Hold `[:rf/resource q]` and `[:rf.resource/status q]` for a `{:from-db}`-scoped resource while logged in, then dispatch a logout that removes the resolver input.
  2. Assert both reads report `:unresolved`, with no `:rf.error/sub-exception` emitted.
  3. Log back in and assert the same held sub re-keys to the new principal's entry.
- Replace `sub-side-scope-fail-closed` (`resources_runtime_cljs_test.cljc:208-212`).
- An unknown resource id still throws `:rf.error/resource-not-registered`.

## Notes

- Origin: Opus review (resources decision 3). Sol 15 adopted it after reading the Opus report, so it is not independent corroboration.
- Hot zones: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (error catalogue row at `:2049`). Sequence this against other beads editing spec 009. `spec/016-Resources.md` is not a hot zone.
- Related (closed): rf2-fn0kx.9, where the route-plan side of the same unresolved condition fails the whole home plan.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/resources.md` decision 3 and action 2.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:58:30 AUSEST at HEAD f678139da9) ==

DECISION: Option A. A resource subscription whose `{:from-db …}` scope reference resolves `nil` reads NO cache entry and projects a value instead of an error. The reference can come from the resource's policy or from a `{:from-db …}` on the payload. The value is `:status :unresolved`, with every other field in its existing empty shape: `:data`, `:error` and `:refresh-error` nil, the derived booleans `false`, and for the infinite family its empty-feed shape with `:status :unresolved`. There is no throw and no `:rf.error/sub-exception`. The error id `:rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope` retires. The causal side does not change: under a nil scope, route planning, event-side ensure/refetch and `:rf.resource/invalidate-tags` still raise `:rf.error/resource-scope-unresolved-reference` and fail closed.

WHY:
- EP-0003 (:870-882) designed the throw for policies a sub can never evaluate, such as a `(route, ctx)` resolver or `:rf.scope/from-caller`. Those were static programmer defects. Registration now admits exactly two shapes (016:86-90), so only one trigger is left: a resolver that returns nil because the app has no principal yet. That is ordinary app state. "Trust the programmer" rules out machinery that treats it as a defect. Today that machinery costs three things, all probed below: a render crash in a naive `case`, a 500 for every logged-out SSR request, and one always-on error record per mounted read on each logout.
- A keeps everything the fail-closed boundary exists for. With no key there is nothing to look up, so the read never touches the global entry, another principal's entry or a previous-key pointer. The write side stays loud. A drops only the part that punishes correct apps.
- A delivers what the design asked for and what the thrown message already promises. EP-0016 :722-724: "Subscription state should be explainable as 'scope unresolved' or an equivalent diagnostic state". 016:222: "a subscription is explainable as 'scope unresolved'". registry.cljc:884-886: "the view should render the \"scope unresolved\" state". No such state exists today.
- Ergonomics. Today every app needs a predicate that mirrors each resolver's nil condition, which is two truths that can drift. The tutorial's resolver returns nil in a third case, a token but no user yet, and needs its own `:auth/restoring?` sub for it. Under A, one `case` arm replaces that predicate. An AI pair finds `:unresolved` where it already looks: the sub docstrings, 016 §Status semantics and the skill. A missing arm fails with "No matching clause: :unresolved", which names the cause. Today's failure is a blank "No matching clause: ".
- A keeps the "idle is not empty" lesson of rf2-kqav8 and does not weaken it. "No identity" and "identified but never ensured" stay distinct values.

REJECTED:
- B: project the ordinary `:idle` empty shape, optionally with a `:scope-unresolved?` flag. This merges "nobody can be named" with "nobody ensured this yet". A naive `case` renders a permanent skeleton for a logged-out user, and correct code still needs the app-level guard. rf2-fn0kx.9's close reason: "A partial failure presenting as success is worse than an error." rf2-kqav8 kept the RealWorld planning-error panel because it is the flagship's "one live demonstration of fail-closed scope as a planning error, of 'idle is not empty'". The flag variant helps only authors who already know to look for it. B saves little code over A, and the spec churn is identical.
- C: keep the throw, fix the message, and document honestly that the view gets nil plus `:rf.error/sub-exception` and SSR answers 500. This is the honest minimum and XS in size. But it classifies a supported resolver outcome as a computation failure, and it leaves a per-view tax on every app with a login. Authors discover that tax only by failing first: a client crash, or a 500 in production. C's one real advantage is a read-side alarm for a resolver that wrongly returns nil, and that alarm survives where it matters (see the cost note below).

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- Three opinions, all A: the bead's own recommendation (from the Opus review; Sol 15 adopted it after reading Opus, so it is not independent), the dossier author, and Codex. The bead carried no mayor recommendation. I agree with both reviewers.
- Codex qualification 1, adopted: nil does not specifically mean "logged out". A resolver can return nil for any app condition. The RealWorld viewer resolver returns nil while a saved token waits for session restore, and gives confirmed anonymous users a concrete anonymous scope. So document `:unresolved` generically: "the scope resolver returned nil, so this read has no identity yet". The app decides what to render, for example a sign-in prompt or a restoring line.
- Codex qualification 2, adopted: 016:111's permanent-skeleton rationale is about a wrong but concrete key, not a missing key, so on its own it does not refute B. The decisive reason against B is that A keeps the two observable situations apart: no identity, and identified but empty.
- Codex marked the SSR 500 as an inference, since it did not run SSR. Settled: I re-ran the dossier's SSR probe at HEAD and it gives [500 200] (see EVIDENCE).
- The dossier left `rf/resource-state` open ("nil is the consistent choice"), and Codex chose nil. Ruled: nil.
- My addition, which neither review raised: the unreachable `:else` branch of `resolve-scope-for-sub` (registry.cljc:936-948) also throws `:rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope`. Make it throw `:rf.error/resource-missing-scope-policy` instead, and drop its "pass :scope on the subscription payload" advice. `:rf.error/resource-missing-scope-policy` is the registration error that names exactly this defect, and the same file already throws it at :850-857. With that change the id retires completely. This is required, not cosmetic. CHECK C of `scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` fails a spec 009 catalogue row with no literal emitter, and CHECK A fails an emitter with no row. So the emitter removal and the 009 row deletion must land in the same PR.
- The real cost, named by both reviews and accepted: a BROKEN resolver (one reading the wrong path) now reads as `:unresolved` on the read side instead of throwing. It is still caught where the fetch happens. With a user logged in, a route plan or ensure under a nil scope fails closed with `:rf.error/resource-scope-unresolved-reference`, and the causal-side `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` trace records `:resolved-nil? true` for Xray. No new warning is added for legitimate unresolved reads.

EVIDENCE (at HEAD f678139da9. The commits since the probe tree 200a67df2d are a beads checkpoint plus tools/docs commits that touch none of the cited files. Since the dossier's tree 2fdf565945, `git diff --stat` over the cited files lists only unrelated edits in resources transport/http.cljc, ssr manifest/response, and spec 009/016 rows elsewhere. The cited sub, registry, memo and ssr.cljc code is unchanged.)
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:859-889`: `sub-unresolved-reference!` throws `:rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope` when `resolve-from-db-reference-pure` returns nil. `resolve-scope-for-sub` (:891-948) calls it for a payload `{:from-db}` (:923-926) and for a policy `{:from-db}` (:931-934). The `:else` branch (:936-948) is unreachable, because registration admits no third shape.
- `subs.cljc:82-130`: `resolve-scoped-key` feeds `entry-for`, and every projection goes through `entry-for` (or `feed-entry-for`, :299-309). The no-entry shapes already exist:
  - `state-sub-fn` :186-190: `{:status :idle :data nil :error nil :refresh-error nil :loading? false :fetching? false :stale? false :has-data? false :previous? false}`;
  - `status-sub-fn` :224: `(or … :idle)`;
  - `infinite-state-sub-fn` :430-436.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc:406-410`: when a sub body throws, the sub layer emits `:rf.error/sub-exception` on the always-on channel and returns nil ("Returning nil.").
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:387-404`: the always-on listener projects `:rf.error/sub-exception` to a fail-closed 5xx, even with `debug-enabled? false`.
- Spec 016:120 makes the throw normative: "a loud, structured error … never a silent `:idle`. The fix the error points at is explicit: pass `:scope` on the subscription payload …". The same rule appears at :89, :222, :231, :235, :697, :699, in roster row :1767 and in resolved decision :1910. Spec 009:2049 is the catalogue row ("Thrown ex-info from the sub"), with recovery `:fix-registration` "pass `:scope` on the payload …".
- Neither hot file moves. `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3144`'s `ResourceEntry` `:status` enum describes durable entries only, and there is no view-model schema. `spec/API.md` names no status set (it has only `resource-state` at :485, which stays unchanged). So the api manifests are untouched too.
- The wrong advice this ruling corrects:
  - `skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md:67`: "an unresolvable scope is a loud `:rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope` (pass `:scope` on the sub payload)";
  - 016:120: "pass `:scope` on the subscription payload";
  - 009:2049's recovery text;
  - `docs/resources/errors-and-warnings.md:38`: "Resolve only when logged in, or don't subscribe";
  - `docs/resources/tutorial/04-scopes-and-guards.md:34` and :45 justify an `:auth/restoring?` root gate with "subscribing to either read is an error";
  - `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/views.cljs:468-475` wraps the feed in `(when authed? @(subscribe …))` for the same reason.
- Probe 1 (client, plain-atom). This is the dossier's script, which I re-ran at 200a67df2d: `cd implementation/resources && java -cp <output of clojure -Spath -M:test> clojure.main probe_client.clj`. Exit 0:
  1. Logged in as jake, entry loaded: `{:status :loaded, :data ["a1" "a2"], :has-data? true}`.
  2. After logout (resolver input removed): `[:rf/resource q]`, `/status`, `/data`, `/loading?` and `/has-data?` are all nil. `(case (:status vm) …)` throws IllegalArgumentException "No matching clause: ". There are 5 always-on records, one `:rf.error/sub-exception` per held sub.
  3. Logged back in: the same held subs read `:loaded` again.
  4. Account switch jake to abel: `{:status :idle, :data nil, :has-data? false}`, with 0 errors.
  Note the asymmetry. Switching from jake to abel gives a clean `:idle`. Switching from jake to nobody gives nil plus five errors, and even the booleans read nil rather than false.
- Probe 2 (SSR), re-run at 200a67df2d. Exit 0:
  - Logged-out request, sub value: nil. Logged-in request: `{:status :idle, :data nil}`.
  - HTTP status [logged-out logged-in] => [500 200].
  - Setup, so a worker can rebuild it:
    - on the `:rf/default` frame, `(rf/reg-resource-scope :t/session {:inputs {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}} (fn [{:keys [username]} _] (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}])))`;
    - `(rf/reg-resource :t/feed {:scope {:from-db :t/session} :params-schema [:map [:page :int]]} …)`;
    - a stub `:rf.http/managed` fx with `{:platforms #{:server :client}}`;
    - two `(rf/make-frame {:id … :platform :server :ssr {:public-error-id :rf.ssr/default-error-projector :dev-error-detail? false}})` frames, with only one logged in;
    - under `(with-redefs [rf.interop/debug-enabled? false] …)`, call `(rf/subscribe-once [:rf/resource q] {:frame f})` in each frame, then read `(:status (:response (rf.ssr/flush-response-result! f)))`.
  - After the fix, the logged-out request must read `:status :unresolved` and answer HTTP 200.
- Codex's independent probe (resources test classpath, plain-atom) agreed. Two held subs read idle. After logout both read nil, with exactly two always-on `:rf.error/sub-exception` records. title: SSR payload accepts maps and sets whose distinct JVM numeric keys collapse in the browser ({1 :i 1.0 :d} emits, then fails client parse)
description:
Filed 2026-10-11 16:27:57 AUSEST at HEAD 82e4037dc7, as a follow-up to the Opus adversarial review (SSR report, decision 3; first found by Sol 28). Evidence below was read at HEAD.

## Problem

The hydration payload's numeric crossing check looks at each number on its own, and nothing looks at a collection as a whole. `re-frame.ssr.payload-policy/check-portable-numbers!` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc:878`, called at :959-960 for `:rf/app-db` and `:rf/runtime-db`) walks values, map keys and set members against `wire/portable-number?`.

On the JVM, `1` and `1.0` are distinct map keys and distinct set members, and so are Long `0` and double `-0.0`. Each passes the per-number rule. The browser reads every number as one IEEE-754 double, so the two keys collapse:

    {:lookup {1 :i 1.0 :d}}   ; allowlisted slice

That slice emits cleanly, and the client's EDN read then fails on a duplicate key, so hydration fails. A set like `#{0 -0.0}` fails the same way.

## How it got here

The only collection-level walk was `numeric-collision` in `re-frame.ssr.manifest`, added by commits c115873690 and ab6af5feef. It guarded the Root Manifest wire, never the payload, and it was deleted along with the manifest in 8323324351. `git grep numeric-collision` over `implementation/` now finds nothing. So this is a gap the payload has always had; it is not a regression of a payload check.

## Fix direction

- Add a collection collision walk to `check-portable-numbers!`. It should fail closed with `:rf.error/ssr-hydration-payload-invalid` and name the partition, the path, the colliding values and the double they share.
- The deleted implementation is at `13834d3115:implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/manifest.cljc` (about lines 450-497), and its dual-host test is in `root_manifest_cljs_test.cljc` at ab6af5feef. Reuse both.
- Check whether the ssr-node `:render-state` wire, which uses `wire/edn-carryable?` per value, has the same gap. If it does, close it there too.
- Spec 011's payload paragraph (about line 86) and §The numeric crossing rule should say that collections are checked as well.

## Verification

- A JVM test with `{1 :i 1.0 :d}` in an allowlisted slice is red before the fix (the payload emits) and green after (the payload is refused, with attribution).
- The CLJS reader rejects the bytes the JVM emitted before the fix.
- A resolving mutation (`{1 :i 2 :d}`) still emits and round-trips.
