title: INCOMPLETE: machine :after validation throws raw host errors instead of a structured refusal
description:
Audit of PR #10457 at 7decbd810451b2694442a40227a7b2f797afed6c. Independent open finding for the engine diagnostic gap reported by the implementer and tracked alongside the separate nil parity issue in rf2-tt83a. It is not introduced by the viz-only change.

Evidence: the implementer ran validate-machine! against non-nil, non-map :after values and measured an ISeq host exception for :after :b and ClassCastException for :after [1000 :b] across the tested positions. At the audited tree, implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:2073-2079 only checks transition entries WHEN the clause is already a map, leaving malformed containers untouched. Downstream traversal uses seq/doseq/destructuring directly, e.g. region/root :after checks at 615/631 and delay traversal at 1601-1604. The viz instead returns machine-bad-after-spec in grammar.cljc:918. Programmers and AI clients therefore get an implementation exception without the normal machine error category or source/slot diagnostic for an ordinary declaration-shape mistake.

Required correction: refuse non-nil, non-map :after at the engine boundary before traversal, across supported declaration scopes, using the existing structured machine error mechanism and a matching viz category (reuse an appropriate category). title: api(ssr): one (ssr/head-model frame-id ?opts) replaces render-head / active-head; retarget ssr-ring lifecycle
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 by the ruling on rf2-kuky.44 (option A, single door). Bead 2 of 2 — blocked on bead 1: the `rf/` copies must be gone first, so there is no façade copy of the new fn to write and then delete. Line numbers at tip 2b6e8a44cf; re-grep before editing._

## Problem

Two public reads answer one question — "what is this frame's head model?": `render-head` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc:128-155`; a keyword-OR-map second argument — the placeful dispatch on type that `spec/Principles.md:30` asks to retire) and `active-head` (`:179-207`; route `:head` → `render-head`, else `default-head`; no route override). Zero app or tool consumers; one framework consumer (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj:178`). RULED: ONE read, `head-model`, defined at home and re-exported from `re-frame.ssr`.

## Why `head-model` and not `head`

The dossier proposed `(ssr/head …)`. That name COLLIDES in ClojureScript: `re-frame.ssr` requires `re-frame.ssr.head`, so the namespace object `re_frame.ssr.head` (carrying `.registry`, `.emit` and the head ns's own vars) exists first, and `(def head …)` in `re-frame.ssr` then emits `re_frame.ssr.head = fn`, clobbering it; the analyzer shipped here (clojurescript 1.12.42, `cljs/analyzer.cljc:1980,3198`) warns `:ns-var-clash` and the runtime breaks. The ruling refused relocating the three-namespace head subtree (the second reviewer's remedy — it breaks the dotted `re-frame.ssr.*` family for a one-word name) and instead names the fn for what it returns: `head-model`, pairing with the existing `head-model->html`. DO NOT name it `head`; do NOT rename `re-frame.ssr.head`.

## Target

```clojure
(ssr/head-model frame-id)                              ; = today's active-head
(ssr/head-model frame-id {:head-id id :route r})       ; = today's render-head; opts map only, no keyword dispatch
(ssr/head-model->html (ssr/head-model frame-id))       ; model -> inner-head HTML (bead 1 lifted it onto re-frame.ssr)
```

ONE selection rule — pin every clause in tests:
1. nil `frame-id` → `:rf.error/no-frame-context` via `require-frame-stamp!` (event `:rf.ssr/head-model`, `:where 're-frame.ssr/head-model` or whichever symbol convention bead 1 settled for the other `:where` values).
2. Resolve the effective route ONCE: `(contains? opts :route)` → that value (an explicit `:route nil` means "no route"); else the frame's runtime-db route slice (`frame-current-route`).
3. `:head-id` supplied → that registration, `:rf.error/no-such-head` if unregistered; else the effective route's `:head` id, if any → that registration, `:rf.error/no-such-head` if unregistered; else `(default-head frame-id)`.
4. The head fn is evaluated against the SAME effective route, so `(head-model f {:route r})` without `:head-id` selects r's head and evaluates it against r.

Return the model and nothing else — no side channel, no HTML mode, no cache. `default-head` stays public; `render-head*` / `route-head-id` / `frame-current-route` stay private (fold or rename as `head-model*`).

## Code

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc`: replace `render-head` (:128) and `active-head` (:179) with `head-model`; rewrite the ns docstring (:8-16); `:where` symbols at `:103,:115,:199`; delete the keyword-or-map branch.

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc`: `(def head-model head/head-model)` beside `head-model->html`.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj:178` → `(ssr/head-model frame-id)`; docstrings `:168,:278,:282`; drop the `[re-frame.ssr.head :as head]` require bead 1 added if nothing else uses it; `pipeline.clj:606` comment.
- SILENT-FAILURE EDGE: `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj:787` guards a check with `(when-let [active (resolve 're-frame.ssr.head/active-head)] …)` — left behind, that check silently stops running. Retarget it to `head-model`, and turn BOTH guards (`:787`, `:796`) into direct calls through a required alias so a future rename fails loudly (the artefact is on the test classpath).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_artefact.cljc:124-125` docstring if bead 1 left it naming `render-head`.

## Tests

- `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj:2724` and the `with-redefs` at `:2815,:2866` → `ssr/head-model` (the var lifecycle now calls); `:847,:2038` comments; `render_hash_tier_test.clj:184`, `ring_streaming_test.clj:1294` prose.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_head_test.clj` (every `render-head :id {:frame f}` / `render-head :id f` → `(head-model f {:head-id :id})`, every `active-head f` → `(head-model f)`), `ssr_teardown_corner_test.clj`, `ssr/test_fixture.clj`, `ssr/head_emit_cljs_test.cljc`, `ssr_head_resolution_no_project_test.clj`, `ssr_keyword_head_contract_test.clj` — enumerate with `git grep -n -E '\b(render-head|active-head)\b' -- implementation/ssr/test`.
- New pins (JVM, and CLJS where the suite is cljc): route `:head` → registered model; no route `:head` → `default-head`; unregistered `:head-id` → `:rf.error/no-such-head`; unregistered route-declared `:head` → `:rf.error/no-such-head`; `{:route nil}` vs absent `:route` differ; `{:route r}` WITHOUT `:head-id` selects r's `:head` and evaluates against r; nil frame → `:rf.error/no-frame-context`; a CLJS compile plus one `head-model` call after ns load (the collision guard).

## Spec / docs / skills

- `spec/011-SSR.md:70` (`active-head` → `head-model`), `:1204` status banner, `:1255-1264` §Default flow steps 3 and 5, `:1266-1276` §`render-head` → §`head-model` (heading AND anchor — check inbound `#render-head` anchors with `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`), `:1286-1287`. `spec/Ownership.md:56`. HOT ZONE `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2127`: the `:rf.error/ssr-head-resolution-failed` row names `rf/active-head` / `rf/head-model->html` — touch only that row text.
- `docs/ssr/head.md:55,76`; `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md` §The head model (`:254` on), `:681,:719`; `docs/ssr/coming-from-nextjs.md:66` if it names the reads; `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md:47-67`; `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:132-133` → one `ssr/head-model` row.

- Regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn` (the `re-frame.ssr.head` `render-head` / `active-head` rows → `head-model`; add the `re-frame.ssr` `head-model` row) and the matching `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` entries.

title: api(observability): configure! {:observability …} process default + frameless/unresolved-owner routing
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 17:23:54 AUSEST by the rf2-kuky.22 ruling (delegated by Mike). RULING on rf2-kuky.22: **A — one production observation door.** This is bead **A1**, SECOND of the fixed chain A0 (rf2-kuky.65) → A1 → A2 (id appended below). The full ruling — the seven routing answers, Codex's three distinctions and how they were weighed, the drift table — is the RULING note on rf2-kuky.22; the dossier is attached to it verbatim. Line numbers below are from the dossier's tip `6d513ba07f` unless marked (desc) = the description's HEAD `6445d0611b`; re-measure at dispatch._

## Problem

Production observation is declared per FRAME only: `:observability` is accepted on `make-frame` / `frame-root` and `configure!` (`core.cljc:2620`) has no such key. Consequences: a multi-frame app restates its Sentry policy on every frame; and three producers emit records with `:frame nil` that NO frame policy can route, so today they reach only the corpus-wide `register-listener! :errors` stream — the door A2 retires. Retiring it before this bead exists opens a gap where those records reach nobody; the ordering A1 → A2 is structural, not a preference.

The frameless producers, verified at tip:
1. `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:804-952` (`no-frame-context-payload` `:834`, `emit-no-frame-context!` `:906`): by construction there is no frame to stamp.
2. The pre-frame SSR hydration-parse arm of `:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload` — `error_emit.cljc:815-830` documents the union shape's `:frame <id-or-nil>` "(the pre-frame hydration-parse FRAMELESS case …)"; the late-bind entry `:error-emit/dispatch-error-record` (`late_bind/directory.cljc:902`) names it.
3. hicasso `compute-sub` errors — `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:221-222`: "`:rf.error/sub-exception` is stamped `:frame nil` BY CONSTRUCTION"; its `watch-recovered-errors!` (`:254-295`) registers on `:errors` for exactly this reason (the per-frame SSR buffer read CLEAN on the failure it exists to catch).

The sink route refuses them by design: `route-error-record!` is a no-op when `:frame` is unresolved, "incl. the FRAMELESS `:frame nil` records" (`observability.cljc:322-324`); `frame-observability` (`:150-157`) returns nil on a nil id; `error_emit.cljc:909` repeats it at the call site.

A second dependency underneath: "project under NO frame" is not expressible today — `elision.cljc:1128` resolves the governing frame as `(or (:frame opts) (rf.frame/resolve-current-frame))`, so an explicit nil falls through to the AMBIENT frame, and `projection.cljc:572-575` seeds `:frame` from the record by truthiness the same way. rf2-kuky.5 makes explicit nil fail closed. This bead is blocked on it.

## Target

```clojure
;; Declared once per process, or per frame — the same closed entry grammar
;; (Spec-Schemas.md FrameSinkEntry, minus :opts per rf2-kuky.17).
(rf/configure! {:observability {:errors [{:sink :app/sentry}]}})       ;; process default
(rf/make-frame {:id :admin
                :observability {:errors [{:sink :app/sentry
                                          :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/public-error}]}})
(rf/register-observability-sink! :app/sentry (fn [projected-record] …))
```

Routing rules — RULED on rf2-kuky.22, implement verbatim:
- **Q1 Precedence, per STREAM.** A frame that declares a stream (even `[]`) uses its own entries for that stream; a frame that omits the stream inherits the default's entries for it. Whole-map replacement is rejected.
- **Q2 Absent vs empty.** `[]` on a frame is the opt-out; `(rf/configure! {:observability nil})` clears the default. Validation reuses `frame_classification.cljc`'s validator (`:205-260` desc) at call time, fail-loud, `:rf.error/bad-frame-classification` with `:where 'rf/configure!` — no new category. NOT an `assert`: rf2-xn13 is closed and the runtime `when-not` / `throw-error!` guard at `core.cljc:2668-2683` is the model.
- **Q3 Frameless (`:frame nil`).** Process default ONLY; projected with the governing frame EXPLICITLY nil → `spec/015:251` case 3 (tree slots `:rf/redacted`, summary ids intact).
- **Q4 Records whose `:frame` no longer resolves** (destroyed frame, dissociated incarnation, exact-incarnation teardown report). Route to the PROCESS DEFAULT under fail-closed projection exactly as Q3; the stale `:frame` id is KEPT in the summary as a diagnostic. NEVER consult any frame's policy for such a record and NEVER re-resolve the stale id — a same-id successor is not the owner (`015:296`). **Producer-seam trap (Codex):** `error_emit.cljc:614` and `dispatch-error-record*` (`:859`) gate the WHOLE late-bound sink call on `route-frame?`, so a fallback added only inside `observability.cljc` is never reached for these records. `route-frame? false` must come to mean "no frame authority — process default still delivers", not "no sink route". Also `frame-observability` (`:150-157`) cannot distinguish "never registered" from "dissociated"; do not add an unresolved-id test that a successor would pass — carry the authority bit from the producer. `capture_frame_reincarnation_sink_route_cljs_test.cljc`'s pin (dissociated id must not reach a same-id successor's sink) STANDS and gains a sibling asserting process-default delivery of the same record under a live, unrelated ambient frame.
- **Q5 Duplicate delivery.** Exactly ONE policy source per record per stream; a sink id present in both the frame's entries and the default's is invoked once.
- **Q6 Raw cross-frame hook.** An explicit `{:sink … :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/local-raw}` entry on the process default (enum member: `projection.cljc:91-97`, `015:264`). A projection profile on the `:rf.observe/*` record — not the substrate record.
- **Q7 Console fallback.** Composes with rf2-kuky.18: a process-default delivery to a REGISTERED sink owns the record; an entry naming an unregistered sink does not.
- Do NOT add an "additive global observer" beside the frame policy to recover corpus-wide parity — that is a third routing model. Q1–Q5 are the model.

## Change list

Code:
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` `configure!` (`:2620`; `:2554-2605` desc) — gains `:observability`; docstring; delegates to a `re-frame.observability/configure!` over a `defonce` default atom; `current-config` is the boot/config area's (rf2-kuky.4), not this bead's — but if `current-config` lands first, the default must show in it.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc` — the default atom + `configure!`; `frame-observability` resolves PER STREAM against the default; `route-error!` / `route-error-record!` / `route-handled-event!` gain the frameless + unresolved-owner arms; the duplicate-delivery rule; a `clear-*` for fixtures beside `clear-observability-sinks!` (fixture-tier, `core.cljc:2184-2194` desc is the pattern — do not export a facade `clear-*`, `Conventions.md:1327-1331`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc` `:614-619`, `:859-865` — the producer seam for Q4 (see trap).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame_classification.cljc` — validator reused at `configure!` time.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc` / `elision.cljc` — nothing beyond what rf2-kuky.5 lands; if .5 has not landed, STOP and wait.

Spec (HOT-ZONE marked):
- `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:270-302` — process default, per-stream precedence, frameless routing, unresolved-owner rule, duplicate rule.
- `spec/API.md` §Configure keys (`:895-935`) + the `:873` row (desc) + §Frame-owned sinks (`:699-706`) — HOT-ZONE. A new `configure!` key is a Spec change by the fixed-and-additive rule (`API.md` §Fixed-and-additive) — additive, fine.

Codex's list: default inheritance vs `[]`; registered / missing / throwing sinks; stale-owner fallback under a live unrelated ambient frame; frameless record reaches the default and no frame's sink.

Docs / skills (after rf2-kuky.21 — .21 owns the teaching ORDER; this bead adds the declare-once form): `docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md` §1 (the `configure!` form beside the frame form), `docs/core/observability.md:481-506`, `docs/core/how-to/configure-dev-and-prod.md:140-143`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/production-observability.md:1-17`, `skills/re-frame2/references/api-cheatsheet.md:153`, `skills/re-frame2/references/privacy-and-elision.md:130-152`, `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` (`configure!` entry).

## Sequencing / hot zone

Blocked by: A0 (rf2-kuky.65 — same `observability.cljc` / `error_emit.cljc` / `Spec-Schemas.md`; A0 first), rf2-kuky.5 (explicit nil fails closed — the real blocker), rf2-kuky.17 (closed entry grammar; same Spec-Schemas region), rf2-kuky.21 (how-to / observability.md / docs/api — same files; .21 first). Worker worktree guard before any edit (`sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh`); gates foreground to completion; no `git stash` — commit, then `git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main`.

## Acceptance

- `(rf/configure! {:observability {:errors [{:sink :s}]}})` + a registered `:s`: an error on a frame with NO `:observability` reaches `:s` once, projected under that frame's classification; on a frame declaring `{:errors []}` reaches nothing; on a frame declaring `{:errors [{:sink :s}]}` reaches `:s` once (Q5); on a frame declaring `{:handled-events […]}` only, its `:errors` still inherit the default (per-stream).

title: api(views): UIx publishes client-root / render! / unmount!; delete the hand-rolled uix.dom root recipe
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from views.md (ref views.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Spec 006 §The client root (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:244-261`) says a browser adapter SHOULD publish a reusable client-root lifecycle — `(client-root)` / `(render! handle tree mount-point [opts])` / `(unmount! handle)` — riding the same Root path and active-root ownership as `render`. The Reagent and reagent-slim adapters do (`implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:142/160/179`, `reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:79/86/102`, backed by the ratom spine's `client-root` / `render-client-root!` / `unmount-client-root!` at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3792-3816`). The UIx adapter publishes nothing of the kind: `re-frame.adapter.uix`'s public surface is `set-hiccup-emitter!`, `use-current-frame`, `frame-provider`, `frame-root`, `use-subscribe`, `use-frame`, `flush-views!`, `wrap-view`, `adapter` (`implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:60-239`), and `make-react-spine` (`spine.cljs:2750`) builds no trio even though its `render` path already owns `createRoot` / `hydrateRoot` and the active-root set (`spine.cljs:1213-1259`). So every UIx app re-invents the recipe the trio was built to delete (rf2-k5r9t): `(defonce react-root (atom nil))` + `when-not @react-root` + `uix-dom/create-root` + `uix-dom/render-root`, and takes a `com.pitch/uix.dom` dependency purely for the mount that the how-to has to warn about (`docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:77-90`). The UIx counter (`examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs:81-112`) is the concrete before/after.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b)

- Hand-rolled root recipe, app-authored: `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs:81-112`, `login/core.cljs:117-141`, `dashboard/core.cljs:350-368` (3 files). Tool-authored: `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_uix/core.cljs:15-34` (the scaffold every new UIx project gets) and `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs:44,56`. The template test `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_emission_test.clj:313-331` PINS exactly one `uix-dom/create-root` call in the emitted `:uix` core — it must move with the recipe.
- Reagent apps: 27 example files use `client-root` + `render!` (`grep -rlE '\(rf.adapter.reagent(-slim)?/client-root\)' examples | wc -l` → 27 at the doc's tip; re-measure).
- `implementation/adapters/uix/deps.edn` already says: shipping source requires only `uix.core`; the shared spine mounts through `react-dom/client`; `uix.dom` is test-only and out of the published pom. So the trio needs NO dependency change — the adapter mounts through the spine, as Reagent does.
- Spine proof of the ratom trio's semantics (the contract the UIx trio must match): `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/adapter_client_root_cljs_test.cljs` (deftests `client-root-does-no-dom-work`, `cold-first-render-creates-once-later-renders-update-the-same-root`, `hydrating-first-render-hydrates-once-later-renders-update`, `unmount-is-idempotent-and-a-later-render-mounts-afresh`, `dispose-adapter-releases-live-handles-once`), `adapter_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (`cold-render-updates-the-same-mounted-node`, `hydrating-render-adopts-the-server-node-then-updates-it`, `destroy-adapter-releases-still-live-handles-once`), and `reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_client_root_cljs_test.cljs`.

## Target API

Published on `re-frame.adapter.uix`, same three names, same shapes and semantics as `re-frame.adapter.reagent` (Spec 006 §The client root: ownership / update / hydration / teardown):

```clojure
(uix-adapter/client-root)                              ;=> inert handle; no DOM work at allocation; defonce-safe, Node-safe
(uix-adapter/render! handle element mount-point)       ;=> nil; first call creates the Root and renders; every later call updates the same Root
(uix-adapter/render! handle element mount-point {:hydrate? true})  ;=> nil; first call hydrates once (Spec 011), later calls update — never a second hydration
(uix-adapter/unmount! handle)                          ;=> nil; idempotent; the Root is in the adapter's active-root set, so rf/destroy-adapter! releases it exactly once and a later render! mounts afresh
```

`element` is a React element built with `uix.core/$` (the spine's `render` slot already refuses CLJS data with `:rf.error/hiccup-on-element-render-slot`, `spine.cljs:1218-1226` — keep that guard on the trio path). `opts` is the same map the spine's `render` takes (`:hydrate?`, and the `:on-recoverable-error` composition rf2-qfz65 installs on the hydrate path, `spine.cljs:1196-1211`); do not invent UIx-only keys.

Before / after (the UIx counter, `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs`):

```clojure
;; before — :81-112
(defonce react-root (atom nil))
(defn ^:dev/after-load mount! []
  (when-let [el (and (exists? js/document) (js/document.getElementById "app"))]
    (when-not @react-root
      (reset! react-root (uix-dom/create-root el)))
    (uix-dom/render-root
      ($ rf.adapter.uix/frame-root {:id app-frame :initial-events [[:counter/initialise]]}
         ($ counter-app))
      @react-root)))

;; after — the same file every Reagent example already has
(defonce app-root (rf.adapter.uix/client-root))
(defn ^:dev/after-load mount! []
  (when-let [el (and (exists? js/document) (js/document.getElementById "app"))]
    (rf.adapter.uix/render! app-root
      ($ rf.adapter.uix/frame-root {:id app-frame :initial-events [[:counter/initialise]]}
         ($ counter-app))
      el)))
```

Implementation shape: lift the ratom spine's `client-root` / `render-client-root!` / `unmount-client-root!` (`spine.cljs:3792-3816`) into a shared helper both spine constructors use, built over each spine's own `mount-root!`-equivalent — for the React spine that is the `render` closure `make-render` returns (`spine.cljs:1213-1259`), which already tracks the Root in `active-roots-cell`. Handle liveness is READ off the active set, never kept in the handle (the rf2-k5r9t rule at `spine.cljs:3786-3791`), so `dispose-adapter!`'s drain releases a live handle's Root once. Expose the three fns from `make-react-spine`'s return map and `def` them on `re-frame.adapter.uix` beside `flush-views!`. Do NOT publish the trio from `re-frame.hicasso.substrate` (also built on `make-react-spine`, `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/substrate.cljs:95`): Hicasso's root goes through its own codec root and gets its handle grammar in views.4.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer. Codex (`view-adapter-ergonomics.md` §Proposed smaller API): "UIx should provide the handle helper instead of teaching a handwritten atom recipe … Retain the already-common `render!` name rather than renaming it merely to settle vocabulary. The first render creates or hydrates the root; subsequent renders reuse it. Hydration remains an explicit first-render mode with its own implementation." Fable adopted both details (keep `render!`; `{:hydrate? true}`); the fable doc's `mount!` rename is withdrawn. Grok: "UIx publishes the trio first — pure addition, deletes the atom/`create-root` recipe."

## Deletion list

- The hand-rolled root recipe (`defonce … (atom nil)` + `uix-dom/create-root` + `uix-dom/render-root`) in: `examples/substrates/uix/{counter,login,dashboard}/core.cljs`, `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_uix/core.cljs`, `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs`, and the teaching copies in `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:168-182` and `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/entry-namespace.md:112-138`.
- `com.pitch/uix.dom` as an APP dependency: drop it from `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_uix/deps.edn` and from the deps table + warning at `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:77-90` and `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/entry-namespace.md:88-97` / `deps-versions.md:48` / `SKILL.md:102` — IF nothing else in the emitted scaffold needs it (verify by compiling the emitted `:uix` scaffold: `template_emission_test.clj` and rf2-eiev's release-boot test `e40f1e3755` cover this). `implementation/adapters/uix/deps.edn`'s `:test` alias keeps `uix.dom` (tests and the docs-pinned component-test recipe use it).
- Nothing on the adapter's existing public surface is removed by this bead (that is views.2).

## Consumers to migrate (counts at tip)

- examples: 3 files (`examples/substrates/uix/{counter,login,dashboard}/core.cljs`).
- tools: `tools/template/.../_uix/core.cljs` (1), `_uix/deps.edn` (1), `tools/template/test/.../template_emission_test.clj:313-331` (re-pin: exactly one `client-root` call, zero `uix-dom/create-root`).
- implementation: `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs` (1) — the adapter smoke `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/spec.cjs` must stay green on the new recipe.
- skills: `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/entry-namespace.md` (root pattern §"The React root pattern" :47-72 already teaches `defonce` + `client-root` for Reagent — make the UIx block the same shape), `deps-versions.md:48`, `SKILL.md:102`; `skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj:279-298` pins entry-namespace.md's `uix.dom` version against the template's `_uix/deps.edn` — update or delete the pin with the dependency.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- **spec (hot-zone):** `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §The client root (:244-261) — the "reference adapters (Reagent and reagent-slim, from the shared ratom spine)" sentence at :254 becomes all three React view adapters; raise SHOULD to MUST for browser view adapters now that the tree honours it (the Hicasso row joins in views.4 — say "the React adapters" here, not "every adapter"); §CLJS reference scope UIx row at :2189 gains the trio in its parenthetical. `spec/API.md` §UIx adapter (:241-253): add three rows (`uix-adapter/client-root`, `render!`, `unmount!`) in the shape of the Reagent rows — grep `client-root` in API.md first: if the Reagent trio has no rows there either, add both sets so the two adapters read alike. `spec/Conventions.md:1821` (`day8/re-frame2-uix` artefact row) gains "the `client-root` / `render!` / `unmount!` root trio". `spec/api-manifest.edn`: three new `re-frame.adapter.uix` rows (`:tier :adapter`, `:owner "006"`) — regenerate with `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen` from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/` (the file's own header says so), then run the drift-check the `api-manifest` job in `.github/workflows/lint.yml` runs (its surface: `spec/API.md`, both `spec/api-manifest*.edn`, `skills/**`, `docs/core/**`, `docs/api/**`).
- **docs:** `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md` (:77-90 deps, :168-192 Step 4 mount, :241 slim comparison), `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:286` ("UIx apps hold a `uix.dom` root themselves" — no longer true), `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md` (add a §client-root / render! / unmount! section mirroring `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.reagent.md:98`), `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md` (add the boot recipe beside :7-24; rf2-tug6 edits :56-66 of the same file — rebase, don't race). `docs/core/testing/views.md:177-182` mounts through `uix-dom/create-root` inside a TEST recipe that `uix_component_recipe_docs_pin_test.clj` holds byte-for-byte to `uix_component_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs`; leave it (uix.dom is a test dep) or switch both halves together — state which in the PR.
- **tests to add:** `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_client_root_cljs_test.cljs` and `uix_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, porting the eight + three Reagent deftests named under Evidence (inert allocation; create-once/update-later; hydrate-once/update-later even when `{:hydrate? true}` keeps being passed; idempotent unmount; `destroy-adapter!` releases a live handle once and a later `render!` mounts afresh; the DOM variants update the same mounted node and adopt a server node). If the shared React suite (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs`) is the natural home, add them there keyed on cfg and run them from `uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs` only.
- **migration README:** no v1-era name changes — no entry.
- **conformance corpus / mcp-conformance:** unaffected (adapter-tier, not a Tool-Pair surface).

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Pure addition on the adapter; deletion only in consumers. Lands BEFORE views.2 (both edit `uix.cljs`, API.md §UIx, the same how-to, the same skill page, the same three examples and `_uix/*`). Hot-zone: `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`, `spec/API.md`, `spec/Conventions.md` — serialise with views.2/3/4/5 and rf2-2vpm. rf2-8urba (deferred) models its Hicasso scaffold on today's UIx `_uix/core.cljs`; after this bead that model is the trio (see the AMEND below).

## Risks

Low. The spine's `render` path already owns `createRoot` / `hydrateRoot`, the active set and the hydration reporter; the trio is a handle over it. One thing to verify rather than assume: the React spine's `render` wraps the tree in a Fragment with the after-render sentinel (`spine.cljs:1235-1247`) — the `:update!` path must render through the same wrapper so a later `render!` reconciles the same top element (a bare tree where the Fragment stood would remount the subtree).

title: api(subs): RULING: reg-sub `:inputs` metadata slot, always-vector delivery; delete `:<-` and two-fn tail
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from subscription-inputs.md (ref subscription-inputs.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`reg-sub` takes one metadata map and one computation fn like every other registrar, then parses a positional dependency language out of its remaining varargs (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:87-170`, `parse-reg-sub-args`, a five-arm `loop`/`cond`). Two grammars declare the same thing — "which upstream queries does this sub depend on" — and they disagree about what a **single** input looks like when it reaches the body:

| Spelling | Lowers to (`:input-kind`) | Body receives | Static edges in `sub-topology` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(reg-sub :id f)` | `:db`, `:input-signals []` | `db` | `[]` |
| `(reg-sub :id :<- [:a] f)` | `:static`, `[[:a]]` | **bare** value of `[:a]` | `[[:a]]` |
| `(reg-sub :id :<- [:a] :<- [:b] f)` | `:static`, `[[:a] [:b]]` | `[a b]` | `[[:a] [:b]]` |
| `(reg-sub :id (fn [q] [[:a]]) f)` | `:parametric`, `:input-fn` | **`[a]`** — a one-element vector | `:parametric` sentinel, no edge |

The spec says `:<-` "is exactly a constant `input-fn`" (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1051`, `spec/API.md:156`, `spec/Conventions.md:1103`) and in the same breath pins that the two deliver differently (006:1020, `spec/008-Testing.md:485-490`, `spec/Principles.md:42`). Both are true at HEAD: the equivalence holds for *which queries are resolved* and fails for *what the body is handed*. That is a calling-convention irregularity on the registrar every app author writes, not two spellings.

## Evidence (verified at HEAD 6445d0611b)

**The four delivery arms, explicit in code:**
- Reactive path `build-and-cache!*` `subs.cljc:1284-1309`: `parametric?` → `make-layer-n-memoised-body … vector-inputs? true` (1292-1295, comment 1284-1291 "even a single realized parametric input is delivered as `[value]`, NOT the bare-value `:<-` convention"); `(= 1 (count input-qs))` → `make-layer-n-single-input-memoised-body` (1303-1306, comment "Delivers the bare value (the v1 `:<-` single-input convention)"); else layer-n vector.
- `subs/memo.cljc` `validate-and-trace` 267-282: `vector-inputs?` → `(body-fn (vec in-vals) query-v)` (270-271); `(= 1 (count input-signals))` → `(body-fn (first in-vals) query-v)` (278-279); the flag is documented at 248-254 and threaded through `make-layer-n-memoised-body`'s 7-arity (701-724).
- Pure path `compute-sub*` `subs.cljc:2068-2098`: `parametric?` → vector (2080-2081); `(zero? n)` → nil (2089-2090); `(= 1 n)` → bare (2093-2094); else vector.
- Tests pin both cells: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_parametric_inputs_test.clj:193-202` (`(fn [[item] _])` for a single parametric input) and 246-252 (`static-single-input-still-delivers-bare-value`, `(fn [n _])`).

**What it does to a programmer, silent in three of four cells:** move a dependency from literal to computed (`:<- [:a]` → `(fn [_] [[:a]])`) and `(fn [item _] (:title item))` now receives `[item]`; `(:title [item])` is `nil` — no error, no trace (`validate-and-trace` only catches throws). Move the other way, or write the parametric habit `(fn [[item] _])` against a single `:<-`, and the bare value hits sequential destructuring: a map/number/keyword throws in `nth` → `:rf.error/sub-exception` → nil (loud in dev, nil in prod); a vector, list, string or nil binds its first element / first character / nil — silent in the value shapes subs most often carry. The same body cannot be shared between the two producers.

**Census** (`node ai/findings/API-review/fable/intermediate/subscription-inputs/census.cjs .`; balanced-form parser over every `(…/reg-sub` in examples/, tools/, testbeds/, docs/, skills/, implementation/; 1782 forms; identical at a3dd39b739 and 948559695f, and HEAD changes no census root):

| Class | `:db` | one `:<-` | many `:<-` | input-fn | of which constant | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| app — `examples/` | 86 | 118 | 20 | 1 | 1 | 225 |
| app — `testbeds/`, `tools/*/testbeds/`, skill fixtures | 72 | 16 | 2 | 0 | — | 90 |
| tool — `tools/*/src/` (all Xray; Story and pair-mcp have no derived subs) | 99 | 31 | 55 | 0 | — | 185 |
| tool tests | 49 | 6 | 2 | 0 | — | 57 |
| docs (code blocks) | 95 | 38 | 8 | 18 | 2 | 162 |
| skills | 22 | 22 | 5 | 15 | 2 | 69 |
| framework tests | 762 | 109 | 41 | 40 | 5 | 956 |

Across every class: 350 single-`:<-`, 135 multi-`:<-` (98×2, 22×3, 7×4, 5×6, 2×7, 1×8 — the wide ones are Xray data subs), 76 input-fn. Of 561 derived subs, 62% are the single-input shape; in the app class **134 of 157 (85%)**. The parametric grammar has **one** app consumer and **zero** tool consumers, and that one is a constant producer — `examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs:358-362` `(fn [_query-v] [[:rf.resource/data {…}]])` — which `sub-topology` (`subs/tooling.cljc:57-118`) reports as the `:parametric` sentinel and Xray's derivation graph draws as no edge (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/derivation_graph.cljs:279`), purely because of the spelling chosen. The one site whose input *count* depends on the query is a framework test: `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/grid/row_total_layer2_dom_cljs_test.cljs:85` (`cols` in the query decides the number of cell queries) — the proof that a parametric body cannot be handed a bare value.

**Three facts the July "power lattice" verdict did not weigh:**
1. The recorded rationale is applied to one mode and abandoned in the other. `Principles.md:42` keeps bare-for-one "preserving the v1 convention". v1's *signal-fn* form also delivered a single signal bare, and v2 already broke that: `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` **M-71 case 3** (:813-825) tells migrators to rewrite `(fn [item _])` to `(fn [[item] _])`. So "preserve the v1 prior" is the reason for the static shape and was overridden for the parametric shape — exactly where the asymmetry lives.
2. The registrar family already spells this declaration in the metadata slot: `reg-flow` `:inputs` (`core_flows.cljc:29-35`, mandatory) and `reg-resource-scope` `:inputs` (`core_resources.cljc:172-173`); `reg-event` carries `:interceptors` there. `reg-sub` is the one registrar whose declaration is positional varargs.
3. The inline-image seam cannot express a derived sub at all: `lower-inline-sub` (`subs.cljc:2466-2514`) forces `:input-kind :db` because the inline tuple `[id metadata body]` "cannot carry" a chain or a two-fn tail; `image.cljc:291` says `:reg-sub → :sub (the layer-1 db-reader form ONLY)`. The restriction exists only because the dependency declaration is not in the metadata map.

## Target API (recommended: option A)

```clojure
(reg-sub id ?metadata computation-fn)

;; metadata may carry :inputs — a literal vector of query vectors, or a pure producer
;; (fn [query-v] -> vector of query vectors); a Var is accepted as today.
;;   absent            → computation-fn is (fn [db query-v] …)                    ;; :input-kind :db
;;   [query-vector*]   → computation-fn is (fn [inputs query-v] …), inputs a VECTOR ;; :input-kind :static
;;   (fn [query-v] …)  → same body shape; inputs realized per concrete query-v     ;; :input-kind :parametric
;; inputs is ALWAYS a vector in declaration / producer order — zero, one or many.
;; explicit {:inputs []} means "no dependencies" (body gets []), not app-db.
```

| Use case (census) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| one upstream (app 134) | `(rf/reg-sub :cart/by-price :<- [:cart/items] (fn [items _] …))` | `(rf/reg-sub :cart/by-price {:inputs [[:cart/items]]} (fn [[items] _] …))` |
| many (app 22, tool 55) | `:<- [:a] :<- [:b] (fn [[a b] _] …)` | `{:inputs [[:a] [:b]]} (fn [[a b] _] …)` — body unchanged |
| chain entry with args (app 29) | `:<- [:rf/machine :auth/flow] (fn [snap _] …)` | `{:inputs [[:rf/machine :auth/flow]]} (fn [[snap] _] …)` |
| parametric (docs/tests) | `(fn [[_ id]] [[:article/by-id id] [:viewer]]) (fn [[a v] q] …)` | `{:inputs (fn [[_ id]] [[:article/by-id id] [:viewer]])} (fn [[a v] q] …)` — body unchanged |
| constant producer (app 1) | `(fn [_] [[:rf.resource/data …]]) (fn [[articles] _] …)` | `{:inputs [[:rf.resource/data …]]} (fn [[articles] _] …)` — body unchanged; the edge becomes static |
| with `:doc` / `:schema` | `{:doc "…"} :<- [:a] f` | `{:doc "…" :inputs [[:a]]} f` |
| referenced body fn | `(rf/reg-sub :x :<- [:a] compute-x)` | `(rf/reg-sub :x {:inputs [[:a]]} (fn [[a] q] (compute-x a q)))`, or change `compute-x`'s first param to `[a]` |
| inline image | not expressible | `{:registrations {:reg-sub [[:cart/total {:inputs [[:cart/items]]} (fn [[items] _] …)]]}}` |

**Deleted:** the `:<-` marker and chain loop; the two-trailing-fn arm; the `vector-inputs?` flag and the bare-value arms in `validate-and-trace` / `compute-sub*`; the `:input-kind :db` forcing in `lower-inline-sub`; the "layer-1 ONLY" carve-out at `image.cljc:291`; the delivery-shape sentences at 006:1020 / 008:485-490 / Principles.md:42; EP-0004 §Single input's second rewrite. **Kept, untouched:** the `:input-kind` / `:input-signals` / `:input-fn` registrar slots (derived from the `:inputs` value's type — `vector?` vs fn-or-Var), so `sub-topology`, Xray (`reactive_panel_subs.cljs:376-422`, `derivation_graph.cljs:279`, epoch view) and pair-mcp `list_subscriptions` (`list_subscriptions.cljs:33-49`) do not move; the `:parametric` sentinel and the static/realized two-level tooling contract (a producer is never executed to fabricate edges); the single-input memo specialisation (`memo.cljc:631-699`, keyed on count, hands `[v0]` on); `:rf.error/sub-input-fn-bad-return` / `-exception`; layer-1 `(fn [db q])` stays bare `db` — it declared no inputs. **Gained:** literal `:inputs` are shape-checked at registration by the existing pure `normalize-sub-inputs` validator (`subs.cljc:395-438`), which today runs only on producer results at first materialization.

## Alternatives weighed and rejected

- **B — keep `:<-`, make one arrow deliver `[v]`.** Fixes the cell, keeps two grammars, and is exactly what Principles.md:42 rejects: every existing single-`:<-` body keeps loading and silently returns nils. Refuted on the recorded rationale's own terms.
- **C — bare value for one input in both modes.** The parametric count is not statically fixed (row-total test above; 006:1053 fixed-topology is per cache entry, not per sub), so the body's argument shape would flip at runtime with the query. Refuted; this is why the asymmetry exists and it is sound.
- **D — delete the parametric mode (zero app/tool consumers).** It is the v2 target of v1's signal-fn idiom (M-71); deleting it makes a common v1 program unmigratable, against Vision C1 — and leaves the positional arrow grammar in place. Refuted.
- **E — named map `{:inputs {:items [:cart/items]}}` + `(fn [{:keys [items]} q])`.** Principles §Name over place keeps single-value cases positional, and flows resolved vector-over-map for v1 with a falsifiable trigger at four-plus inputs (`spec/013-Flows.md:566-573`, 583-585). Adopting a map for subs alone forks the `:inputs` grammar between two registrars. Not now — see the joint question below.
- **Keep as is, record the rejected simplification.** Codex's own fallback: "If preserving existing v1 authoring is non-negotiable, do not ship this as an additive fifth spelling. Keep the current contract and record the rejected simplification instead."
- **A — codex's `:inputs` slot, always-vector (recommended)**, with fable's three refinements: same `:input-kind` discriminator so tools are untouched; literal validation moves to registration; the inline-image seam gains derived subs for free.

## Migration rule (the whole of it)

(a) `:<- q1 … :<- qn` → `{:inputs [q1 … qn]}`, merged into an existing metadata map; (b) `(reg-sub id input-fn f)` → `(reg-sub id {:inputs input-fn} f)`; a producer that is *provably* a literal `(fn [_] V)` (V a vector of literal query vectors, no free symbols) becomes `{:inputs V}`, any other producer moves unchanged; (c) when n = 1 and the body is a literal `(fn [p q] …)`, rewrite `p` → `[p]` (a `{:keys …}` param becomes `[{:keys …}]`); when the body is a reference, wrap it `(fn [[v] q] (f v q))`. Nothing else changes: `:db` readers, multi-input bodies and parametric bodies are byte-identical. **Never reinterpret an arrow registration with its body untouched**: after the deletion, `:<-` or a two-fn tail is a loud `:rf.error/reg-sub-bad-args` at load (the existing error, message re-pointed at `:inputs`). Codex's caution, adopted: the rewrite is **syntax-aware, not regex-shaped** — existing metadata maps, reader conditionals, destructuring and referenced fns need structural rewrites, and an unused/`_`-prefixed producer parameter is not proof the producer is literal (it may deref a Var or call a fn).

## Principles.md:42 vs migration README M-71 case 3

Principles.md:42 fears silent nils from "silently changing that convention". The danger it names is real and is a property of *keeping the spelling while changing its meaning* (option B). Deleting the spelling is what the pre-alpha posture prescribes — a redundant spelling is deleted, not deprecated — and it is what makes the change loud. The parametric half of the same paragraph already accepted `[v]`-for-one (M-71 case 3); the proposal finishes the thought rather than reversing it. Vision C1's mechanical-migration constraint is met — the rule above is what an agent applies — but it is a migration, and it is the one carve-out the migration README currently advertises as preserved (README:25, :3148, :3153 "the static `:<-` forms … are preserved").

Benefit: changing a dependency from literal to computed no longer changes the consumer; adding a second input no longer flips between scalar and vector; one destructuring form; the declaration is a value (`{:inputs …}`) an image carries and a tool reads without parsing an arglist; `docs/core/subscriptions.md:187-189` stops having to teach "the only wrinkle in the syntax".

## Corroboration (two-reviewer)

Codex (`ai/findings/API-review/codex/subscription-inputs.md`, rf2-snkw): "the recommended `:inputs` declaration with always-vector delivery is the strongest simplification in this group … This is not merely dislike of the arrow glyph … An API that makes this refactor preserve the body is meaningfully easier for both programmers and generated code." Codex proposed the target (literal vector or pure producer under `:inputs`; every derived computation receives a vector including zero and one; explicit `[]` is no dependencies; remove arrow chains and the two-fn tail; no named maps, no unpacking modes, no signal DSL) and added two implementation refinements — lower ordinary and inline registrations through ONE dependency-normalization function, and treat the migration as syntax-aware — plus the counterargument above ("this consciously revisits an existing decision … a proposed revision to policy, not a claim that the current implementation violates its spec"). ## Two concrete gains codex left implicit

## The problem

`reg-sub` takes one metadata map and one computation fn like every other registrar, then parses a positional dependency language out of its remaining varargs (subs.cljc:124-170, a five-arm `loop`/`cond`):

| Spelling (subs.cljc:93-96) | Lowers to (`:input-kind`) | Computation fn receives | Static edges in `sub-topology` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(reg-sub :id f)` | `:db`, `:input-signals []` | `db` | `[]` |
| `(reg-sub :id :<- [:a] f)` | `:static`, `[[:a]]` | **bare** value of `[:a]` (subs.cljc:1296-1306; memo.cljc:278-279; compute path 2092-2094) | `[[:a]]` |
| `(reg-sub :id :<- [:a] :<- [:b] f)` | `:static`, `[[:a] [:b]]` | `[a b]` | `[[:a] [:b]]` |
| `(reg-sub :id (fn [q] [[:a]]) f)` | `:parametric`, `:input-fn` | **`[a]`** — a one-element vector (subs.cljc:1284-1294 passes `vector-inputs? true`; memo.cljc:270-271; compute path 2080-2081) | `:parametric` sentinel — no edge |

The spec calls `:<-` "exactly a constant `input-fn`" (006:1051, API.md:156, Conventions.md:1103, EP-0004:248-256) and in the same breath pins that the two deliver differently (006:1020; 008:485-490; Principles.md:42; EP-0004:258-263). Both statements are true at tip, and that is the irregularity: the equivalence holds for *which queries are resolved* and fails for *what the body is handed*. Tests pin both cells (sub_parametric_inputs_test.clj:193-202 `(fn [[item] _])`; 246-252 `(fn [n _])`).

What the asymmetry does to a programmer today, verified against the delivery code:

- Move a dependency from literal to computed — `:<- [:a]` → `(fn [_] [[:a]])` — and the body `(fn [item _] (:title item))` now receives `[item]`; `(:title [item])` is `nil`. No error, no trace, no warning: `validate-and-trace` only catches throws (memo.cljc:389-463). **Silent.**
- Move the other way, or write the parametric habit `(fn [[item] _])` against a single `:<-`, and the bare value is fed to sequential destructuring. A map, number or keyword throws in `nth` → `:rf.error/sub-exception` → `nil` (loud in dev, nil in prod). A vector, list, string or nil binds its first element / first character / nil. **Silent in the value shapes subs most often carry.**
- The same body cannot be shared between the two producers. codex's reading is confirmed exactly, and it is the calling convention, not the spelling, that is irregular.

Three more facts the July "power lattice" verdict did not weigh:

1. **The rationale is applied to one mode and abandoned in the other.** Principles.md:42 keeps bare-value-for-one "preserving the v1 convention". But v1's *signal-fn* form also delivered a single signal bare, and v2 already broke that prior — migration README M-71 case 3 (:813-825) tells migrators to rewrite `(fn [item _])` to `(fn [[item] _])`. So "preserve the v1 prior" is the recorded reason for the static shape and was overridden for the parametric shape, which is precisely where the asymmetry lives.
2. **The registrar already has the regular spelling, for two other kinds.** `reg-flow` declares `:inputs` in the metadata middle slot (core_flows.cljc:29-35, mandatory), `reg-resource` declares `:inputs` there (core_resources.cljc:172-173), `reg-event` carries `:interceptors` there as "the one superset middle-slot shape" (Conventions.md:1122-1124). `reg-sub` is the one registrar whose declaration is positional varargs.
3. **The inline-image seam cannot express a derived sub at all.** `lower-inline-sub` forces `:input-kind :db` because "the inline tuple `[id metadata body]` … cannot carry" a chain or a two-fn tail (subs.cljc:2473-2477; image.cljc:291 "the layer-1 db-reader form ONLY"). The restriction exists only because the dependency declaration is not in the metadata map.

## Simpler elegant target

One registration shape, the family's three slots, one delivery rule:

```clojure
(reg-sub id ?metadata computation-fn)

;; metadata may carry :inputs — either a literal vector of query vectors, or a pure
;; producer (fn [query-v] -> vector of query vectors), a Var accepted as today.
;;   absent            → computation-fn is (fn [db query-v] …)                        ;; :input-kind :db
;;   [query-vector*]   → computation-fn is (fn [inputs query-v] …), inputs a VECTOR    ;; :input-kind :static
;;   (fn [query-v] …)  → same body shape, inputs realized per concrete query-v        ;; :input-kind :parametric
;; inputs is always a vector in declaration / producer order — zero, one or many.
```

| Use case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 2 — one upstream | `(rf/reg-sub :cart/by-price :<- [:cart/items] (fn [items _] (sort-by :price items)))` | `(rf/reg-sub :cart/by-price {:inputs [[:cart/items]]} (fn [[items] _] (sort-by :price items)))` |
| 3 — many | `:<- [:a] :<- [:b] (fn [[a b] _] …)` | `{:inputs [[:a] [:b]]} (fn [[a b] _] …)` — body unchanged |
| 4 — with args | `:<- [:rf/machine :auth/flow] (fn [snap _] …)` | `{:inputs [[:rf/machine :auth/flow]]} (fn [[snap] _] …)` |
| 6 — parametric | `(fn [[_ id]] [[:article/by-id id] [:viewer]]) (fn [[a v] q] …)` | `{:inputs (fn [[_ id]] [[:article/by-id id] [:viewer]])} (fn [[a v] q] …)` — body unchanged |
| 7 — constant input-fn | `(fn [_] [[:rf.resource/data …]]) (fn [[articles] _] …)` | `{:inputs [[:rf.resource/data …]]} (fn [[articles] _] …)` — body unchanged, and the edge is now static |
| with `:doc` / `:schema` | `{:doc "…"} :<- [:a] f` | `{:doc "…" :inputs [[:a]]} f` |
| referenced body fn | `(rf/reg-sub :x :<- [:a] compute-x)` | `(rf/reg-sub :x {:inputs [[:a]]} (fn [[a] q] (compute-x a q)))`, or change `compute-x`'s first param to `[a]` |
| 8 — inline image | not expressible | `{:registrations {:reg-sub [[:cart/total {:inputs [[:cart/items]]} (fn [[items] _] …)]]}}` — falls out of the tuple's middle element |

**Mechanical migration rule (the whole of it):** (a) `:<- q1 … :<- qn` → `{:inputs [q1 … qn]}`, merged into an existing metadata map; (b) `(reg-sub id input-fn f)` → `(reg-sub id {:inputs input-fn} f)`; a producer of the form `(fn [_] V)` becomes `{:inputs V}`; (c) when n = 1 and the body is a literal `(fn [p q] …)`, rewrite `p` → `[p]` (a `{:keys …}` param becomes `[{:keys …}]`); when the body is a reference, wrap it as in the table. Nothing else changes: `:db` readers, multi-input bodies and parametric bodies are byte-identical. A registration still written with `:<-` or a two-fn tail is a loud `:rf.error/reg-sub-bad-args` at load — the existing error, with its message re-pointed at `:inputs`.

**Deletions:** the `:<-` marker and chain loop (subs.cljc:124-135); the two-trailing-fn arm (137-152); the `vector-inputs?` flag and two of the four delivery arms in `validate-and-trace` (memo.cljc:248-254, 267-282) and `make-layer-n-memoised-body`'s 7-arity (memo.cljc:711-724); two of the four arms in `compute-sub*` (subs.cljc:2083-2098); the `:input-kind :db` forcing in `lower-inline-sub` (subs.cljc:2508-2511, replaced by reading `:inputs`); the "layer-1 ONLY" carve-out at image.cljc:291; the 006:1020 / 008:485-490 / Principles.md:42 delivery-shape sentences; EP-0004 §Single input's second rewrite (the body no longer changes between v1-static and v2). **Kept:** `:input-kind` and `:input-signals` registrar slots (derived from the `:inputs` value's type — `vector?` vs fn-or-Var — with `normalize-sub-inputs` now validating a literal at registration rather than first materialization); the single-input memo specialisation (memo.cljc:631-699 — keyed on count, it stays for its allocation profile and merely hands `[v0]` on); `:rf.error/sub-input-fn-bad-return` / `-exception`; `sub-topology`'s `:parametric` sentinel and every tool.

**Alternatives weighed.**

- *B — keep `:<-`, make one arrow deliver `[v]`.* Fixes the cell, keeps two grammars, and is exactly the scenario Principles.md:42 rejects: every existing single-`:<-` body would keep loading and silently return nils. Refuted on the recorded rationale's own terms.
- *C — bare value for one input in both modes.* The parametric count is not statically fixed (use case 6; 006:1053 fixed-topology is per cache entry, not per sub), so the body's argument shape would flip at runtime with the query. Refuted; this is the reason the asymmetry exists and it is sound.
- *D — delete the parametric mode (zero app / tool consumers).* The demand bar has genuinely ruled on it as a *surface people reach for*, but it is the v2 target of v1's signal-fn idiom (M-71), so deleting it makes a common v1 program unmigratable, against Vision's mechanical-migration constraint — and it leaves the positional arrow grammar in place. Refuted.
- *E — named map `{:inputs {:items [:cart/items]}}` + `(fn [{:keys [items]} q])`.* Principles §Name over place (:34) keeps single-value cases positional, and flows resolved vector-over-map for v1 with a falsifiable trigger at four-plus inputs (013:566-571, 583-585). Adopting a map for subs alone would fork the `:inputs` grammar between two registrars. Not now — but the census hands the flows trigger a data point (15 static-4+ subs, 14 of them Xray's), and the vector-vs-map answer should be given once, for `reg-flow` and `reg-sub` together.
- *A — codex's `:inputs` slot, always-vector (recommended, with the three refinements above: same discriminator so tools are untouched; literal validation moves to registration; the inline-image seam gains derived subs for free).*

## Why this is better (ethos)


- **Regularity over cleverness.** A five-arm varargs parser that decides a body's argument shape from the *count of arrows* is cleverness. `reg-sub` becomes the registration family's 3-slot shape (Spec 001; rf2-m90brg) with one declaration key it already shares with `reg-flow` and `reg-resource`; the body has one argument shape per producer-presence, not per producer-arity. docs/core/subscriptions.md:187-189 calls the current rule "the only wrinkle in the syntax. Once you've seen it, you've seen it" — a wrinkle the teaching page has to warn about is a wrinkle the grammar should not have.
- **Data before magic.** `:<-` is a keyword that only means something in arg position 2 or later of one macro; `{:inputs [[:a] [:b]]}` is a value — `(handler-meta :sub id)` returns it, an image carries it, a tool reads it without parsing anyone's arglist. "A vector, or a function of the query that returns one" is the ordinary Clojure data-or-fn idiom, and the same `vector?`-vs-`fn?` discriminator the runtime already uses to choose `:static` vs `:parametric`.
- **One destructuring form.** `[[a] q]` is plain sequential destructuring; there is no framework-specific "one is bare, two is a vector" rule for the programmer or the AI pairing with them to remember, and moving a dependency between literal and computed never touches the body. The rule is one sentence: *if you declared inputs, you get them as a vector.*
- **The recorded rejection, re-read.** Principles.md:42 fears silent nils from "silently changing that convention". The danger it names is real and it is a property of *keeping the spelling* while changing its meaning (option B). Deleting the spelling is what the pre-alpha posture prescribes — a redundant spelling is deleted, not deprecated — and it is exactly what makes the change loud: the old form fails at load with the existing error. The parametric side of the same paragraph already accepted `[v]`-for-one; the proposal finishes the thought rather than reversing it.
- **Honest cost.** The dominant case grows: `:<- [:a] (fn [a _] …)` becomes `{:inputs [[:a]]} (fn [[a] _] …)` — about twelve characters and one bracket pair at each of 134 app sites, and the arrow, which reads well and is loved from v1, goes. **Bother handling?** Yes — this is the one front-porch calling-convention bug in the wave. A single `:<-` hands the body a bare value; a single input-fn hands it `[v]`. Use a syntax-aware rewrite, not a regex — Codex is right that "constant producer" (`_`-prefixed param) is not enough to evaluate a producer at registration; it may close over a binding. - Inline-image derived subs fall out; add an acceptance case, do not treat them as the reason for the change.

This should be high on the implementation order despite a "medium" label. It is the registrar every app author writes.

## Codex Thoughts

**Verdict: worthwhile, and the recommended `:inputs` declaration with always-vector delivery is the strongest simplification in this group.** This is not merely dislike of the arrow glyph. [The parser and delivery paths](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc) distinguish a single static input from a single computed input, so moving the same dependency between those declarations changes the computation's argument. [Memo delivery](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc) implements that distinction explicitly. An API that makes this refactor preserve the body is meaningfully easier for both programmers and generated code.

The inline-image observation strengthens the case: `lower-inline-sub` currently forces `:input-kind :db`, because its three-slot tuple has nowhere to put the dependency declaration. Moving dependencies into metadata removes an actual expressive restriction, not just spelling variation. Keep the existing normalized `:input-kind`, `:input-signals`, and `:input-fn` facts so tools retain static versus query-dependent topology. Do not run a producer speculatively to make its graph appear static.

The alternatives are substantially covered. Keeping the old grammar and changing its meaning risks silent misbinding; making both modes unwrap a singleton gives a query-dependent producer a query-dependent argument type; deleting computed inputs removes useful power rather than redundancy. Named input maps could improve very wide derivations, but adding both maps and vectors now would recreate the choice this review is removing. The honest cost remains that the dominant one-input form becomes longer. The justification is stable meaning and image composability, not fewer characters.

Two implementation refinements matter:

- Lower both ordinary registrations and inline registrations through one dependency-normalization function. Distinguish absent `:inputs` from explicit `[]`; the former receives app-db, the latter receives an empty vector. Preserve function/Var acceptance and source metadata. Keep the single-input memo specialization internally while changing only what it delivers to the computation.
- The migration is **syntax-aware, not safely regex-shaped**. Existing metadata, reader conditionals, destructuring and referenced computation functions need structural rewrites. A producer whose query parameter is unused is not automatically a literal declaration: it may dereference a Var or call another function. Only fold provably literal query vectors into static metadata; otherwise retain the producer under `:inputs`. A lexical census is useful evidence, not that proof.


Focused checks should compare reactive and `compute-sub` results for zero, one and several inputs, including map/vector/nil upstream values, and show the same body working with literal and computed producers. Add one derived inline-image subscription and verify its topology, frame resolution and replacement behavior. Old arrow/two-function registrations should fail clearly, so a half-migrated body cannot silently load.

This deserves priority over cosmetic API pruning. It removes a special calling convention while retaining the underlying power: plain data describes dependencies; a pure function combines their values. That is the Clojure-shaped improvement, without introducing another mini-language.

# Subscription inputs: one dependency declaration, one derived-value shape

Review date: 2026-09-05. Status: proposal only. Tracking bead: `rf2-snkw`.

## Finding

`reg-sub` has a small dependency language hidden in its trailing arguments. [parse-reg-sub-args](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc) accepts these current forms, with an optional metadata map before the tail:

```clojure
(rf/reg-sub :root (fn [db q] ...))
(rf/reg-sub :one :<- [:a] (fn [a q] ...))
(rf/reg-sub :many :<- [:a] :<- [:b] (fn [[a b] q] ...))
(rf/reg-sub :computed
  (fn [q] [[:a] [:b]])
  (fn [[a b] q] ...))
```

Literal and computed inputs are genuinely different capabilities: tools can enumerate the former without running a producer. But they need not be different registration grammars, and selecting a dependency through a function need not change how its value reaches the computation.

Currently a single static input delivers the bare value, while a single parametric input delivers a one-element vector. This is implemented explicitly in the subscription construction/memoization branches in the same source file. Replacing `:<- [:a]` with `(fn [_] [[:a]])` therefore requires changing the handler too. That is a meaningful irregularity, not just two visual spellings.

## Known use cases and empirical evidence

| Use case | Repository evidence | Requirement to retain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read app-db directly, optionally using query arguments | [TodoMVC subscriptions](../../../../examples/core/todomvc/subs.cljs): `:todo/sorted-todos`, `:todo.ui/draft` | The direct `(fn [db q] ...)` case remains simple; parameters alone do not require a dependency producer. |
| Transform one known upstream subscription | Same file: `:todo/showing`, `:todo/todos`; [UIx dashboard](../../../../examples/substrates/uix/dashboard/core.cljs): `:dashboard/selected-range` | One upstream, memoization and ordinary reactive composition. |
| Combine multiple known upstreams | TodoMVC `:todo/visible-todos`, `:todo/footer-counts`; dashboard `:dashboard/visible-metrics` | Ordered inputs, independently tracked upstream values. |
| Use query arguments in a computation with fixed dependencies | TodoMVC `:todo.ui/editing?` | The query remains available independently of input selection. |
| Derive from a resource subscription | [Resources example](../../../../examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs): `:resources.app/first-slug` | The current input function returns a constant one-query vector; this concretely overlaps static inputs. Its computation destructures `[articles]`. |
| Select dependencies using the outer query | [Parametric input tests](../../../../implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_parametric_inputs_test.clj): `:item/title`, `:article/page` | Query-dependent IDs, one or several inputs, and producer order. These are demonstrated by tests, not asserted to be common application patterns. |
| Zero inputs and query-dependent input counts | Same test suite and subscription construction | Empty derived inputs are distinct from an app-db reader; no cardinality-dependent handler convention. |
| A query selects how many upstream cells to combine | [Hicasso row-total test](../../../../implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/grid/row_total_layer2_dom_cljs_test.cljs), `::row-total-l2` | `cols` in the query determines the number of cell queries. This concretely rules out switching between bare and vector delivery by realized input count. |
| Compose derived subscriptions directly into an inline image | [Image grammar](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/image.cljc), `reg-section->kind`; subscription `lower-inline-sub` | Currently impossible: the inline tuple has only one body slot and is forced to an app-db reader. A metadata input declaration can remove that restriction without another tuple grammar. |
| Read framework runtime data or a tool's own reactive state | [Nine states](../../../../examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs): `:todos/items`; [Story coeffects UI](../../../../tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/cofx.cljc): `:story/active-modes` | Do not collapse runtime-backed framework subscriptions or change adapter dependency tracking as part of authoring cleanup. |
| Explain static and realized dependency graphs | [Xray reactive panel](../../../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs), [Pair descriptors](../../../../tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs), [topology tests](../../../../implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_topology_test.clj) | Preserve the distinction between static edges and query-specific realized edges. Never invent a static graph by executing arbitrary producers. |
| Hot reload, disposal, isolation, and snapshot computation | Parametric input tests | Re-registration invalidation, upstream release, frame-local resolution, and agreement between live/snapshot computations must survive. |

## Proposed smaller API

Keep the ordinary app-db reader and the existing metadata position. Give derived dependencies one named slot:

```clojure
;; PROPOSED forms, not supported calls today.
(rf/reg-sub :todo/todos
  {:inputs [[:todo/sorted-todos]]}
  (fn [[sorted-todos] _] (vals sorted-todos)))

(rf/reg-sub :article/page
  {:doc "An article with its comments."
   :inputs (fn [[_ id]]
             [[:article/by-id id] [:comments/for id]])}
  (fn [[article comments] _]
    {:article article :comments comments}))
```

The contract would be:

- No `:inputs`: the computation receives app-db, unchanged.
- `:inputs` containing query vectors: literal dependencies.
- `:inputs` containing a function or supported Var: a pure producer of that same vector-of-queries value.
- Every derived computation receives a vector of resolved values, including zero and one input. Explicit `:inputs []` means no dependencies, not app-db.

Remove arrow chains and the two-unlabelled-functions tail from the target authoring API. Keep optional metadata and source-capturing registration macros. Normalize both input declarations through the same existing registration/inline-image seam. Internally, static versus parametric classification remains useful, as do specialized memoization paths; uniform public values do not require a generic slow runtime.

This is not a proposal for named dependency maps, another signal DSL, explicit dependency objects, or configurable unpacking modes. Adding those would undermine the reduction.

## Additional payoff established by the Fable reread

[Fable's new subscription dossier](../fable/subscription-inputs.md) builds on this proposal, but adds useful evidence beyond concurrence. I checked the following against source:

**Inline images gain expressive power through the same grammar.** `lower-inline-sub` currently hard-codes `:input-kind :db`, explicitly because `[id metadata body]` cannot carry the arrow chain or extra producer function. With dependencies in metadata, an image can express the derived case directly:

```clojure
;; PROPOSED inline registration; derived inline subs are not supported today.
{:registrations
 {:reg-sub [[:cart/total
             {:inputs [[:cart/items]]}
             (fn [[items] _] (reduce + 0 (map :price items)))]]}}
```

This requires updating the shared normalization/lowering path; it is not a capability unlocked merely by changing documentation. Keep the same runtime descriptor and provenance contract, and remove the layer-1-only carve-out for inline subs. That is a concrete power gain from a smaller grammar.

**Literal input mistakes can be caught when declared.** The pure `normalize-sub-inputs` validator already checks the vector-of-query-vectors shape for producer results. Reuse that shape check at registration for literal `:inputs`; keep producer-result checking at materialization. Do not execute producers during registration or require upstream registrations to exist yet. This moves an existing check to the useful phase rather than adding a new validation framework.

**Literal declarations improve static inspection.** The resources example's producer returns a visibly literal query vector. Declaring that vector directly lets topology tools show the dependency statically instead of the `:parametric` marker. Genuine producers retain their realized-query graph. Keep the existing descriptor fields so tools need no new dependency interpreter.

## Counterargument: this consciously revisits an existing decision

[Principles, “Uniform context-map callbacks”](../../../../spec/Principles.md) expressly excludes subscriptions from that family and records why always-vector inputs were rejected: v1-trained single-input handlers expect bare values, and silently changing that convention can produce nils. [Vision](../../../../spec/000-Vision.md) also makes mechanical migration a constraint. This proposal is therefore a proposed revision to policy, not a claim that the current implementation violates its spec.

The reread sharpens that counterargument: [migration M-71, single-signal case](../../../../migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md) already tells v1 users to change a parametric single-input body from `item` to `[item]`. Preserving every v1 calling convention is therefore not the existing policy. The remaining decision is whether to finish that regularization for static derived inputs. Retire the old syntax with a clear registration-time error; do not keep accepting it while silently changing its delivery shape.

My recommendation under the user's pre-alpha elegance posture is to reconsider that tradeoff, but only with an explicit, mechanical migration. Never reinterpret an existing arrow registration while leaving its body untouched. For the new syntax, rewrite a single-static-input handler to destructure `[value]`; where the computation is a referenced function, mechanically wrap it as `(fn [[value] q] (existing-fn value q))`. Root readers and existing parametric/multiple-input computations retain their argument shapes.

The cost is real: the common one-input declaration is longer, and existing projects need a deliberate migration. The benefit is also concrete: changing a dependency from literal to computed no longer changes the consumer, and adding a second input no longer flips between scalar and vector conventions. If preserving existing v1 authoring is non-negotiable, do not ship this as an additive fifth spelling. Keep the current contract and record the rejected simplification instead.

Fable's [census summary](../fable/intermediate/subscription-inputs/summary.txt) reports 118 single-static-input sites in examples and another 31 in tool source, plus testbed/test/doc usage. These are Fable's measured counts, not a census independently rerun here. They make the authoring cost tangible. Use a syntax-aware rewrite; relocate a producer unchanged by default. An unused or underscore-prefixed parameter alone does not prove its body can safely be evaluated early as literal data.

## Why this is more elegant

The input producer answers one question: “Which queries do I depend on?” The computation answers another: “What value follows from their values?” Literal versus computed selection belongs in the first answer, not in an implicit calling-convention change in the second.

That is the useful part of the Clojure ethos here: ordinary vectors, functions, metadata, and composition. It also follows the project's regularity principle without imposing context maps on every function. The programmer still writes an ordinary two-argument function and retains direct access to the query.

## Focused acceptance evidence

Before accepting an implementation, migrate the cited single/multiple/resource examples and one genuine parametric test; verify zero/one/multiple input delivery, live versus supplied-state computation, source capture and inline-image parity, hot reload, disposal, and frame isolation. Check Xray/Pair's static versus realized graph output. A performance comparison should protect the existing single-input specialization. These are bounded checks of preserved behavior, not a mandate to redesign the reactive substrate.

Include one static and one parametric derived subscription authored inline, a malformed literal rejected at registration, and the row-total case with different column counts. Those directly establish the new capability and uniform delivery rule.

function fnParts(s) {

const re = /\((?:[\w.\-]+\/)?reg-sub(?=[\s\n)])/g;

## The problem

`reg-sub` is the one registrar in the family whose declaration is not in the metadata map. `reg-event` carries `:interceptors` there; `reg-flow` carries a mandatory `:inputs` vector there (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_flows.cljc:29-35`); `reg-resource-scope` carries an `:inputs` map there (`core_resources.cljc:146-147`). `reg-sub` instead parses a five-arm positional grammar out of its varargs (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:87-170`, `parse-reg-sub-args`: `:<-` chain loop at 124-135, two-trailing-fn arm at 137-152, single-fn arm at 154-162). Two of those spellings declare the same thing — "which upstream queries do I depend on" — and the spec says so in three places: `:<-` "is exactly a constant `input-fn`" (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1062`, `spec/API.md:156`, `spec/Conventions.md:1109`). But the same pages pin that the two deliver a *single* input differently (`006:1031`, `spec/008-Testing.md:487-492` and `:500`, `spec/Principles.md:42`). Both statements are true at tip, and that is the irregularity: equivalent for *which queries resolve*, different for *what the body is handed*.

| Spelling | `:input-kind` | Body receives | Where the arm lives at tip |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(reg-sub :id f)` | `:db` | `db` | — |
| `(reg-sub :id :<- [:a] f)` | `:static` | **bare** value of `[:a]` | `subs.cljc:1303-1306`, `subs/memo.cljc:278-279`, `subs.cljc:2093-2094` |
| `(reg-sub :id :<- [:a] :<- [:b] f)` | `:static` | `[a b]` | `subs.cljc:1307-1309`, `memo.cljc:281-282`, `subs.cljc:2097-2098` |
| `(reg-sub :id (fn [q] [[:a]]) f)` | `:parametric` | **`[a]`** | `subs.cljc:1292-1294` (`vector-inputs? true`), `memo.cljc:270-271`, `subs.cljc:2080-2081` |

The code is explicit about it. `subs.cljc:1284-1291` comments "even a single realized parametric input is delivered as `[value]`, NOT the bare-value `:<-` convention"; `memo.cljc:248-254` documents the `vector-inputs?` flag that carries the split; tests pin both cells (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_parametric_inputs_test.clj:193-202` and `246-252`, the latter literally named `static-single-input-still-delivers-bare-value`).

### The silent-nil trap, concretely

The delivery arms above mean that moving one dependency between "literal" and "computed" changes the body's argument with no error and no trace (`validate-and-trace` only catches throws). Derived from `memo.cljc:267-282` / `subs.cljc:2080-2094`; not executed in this session:

```clojure
(rf/reg-sub :item    (fn [db _] (:item db)))                              ;; db = {:item {:title "Hello"}}
(rf/reg-sub :title/a :<- [:item]         (fn [item _] (:title item)))     ;; (subscribe-once [:title/a]) => "Hello"
(rf/reg-sub :title/b (fn [_] [[:item]])  (fn [item _] (:title item)))     ;; (subscribe-once [:title/b]) => nil — item is [{:title "Hello"}]
```

The reverse move is loud only for some value shapes: write the parametric habit `(fn [[item] _])` against a single `:<-` and a map, number or keyword throws in `nth` → `:rf.error/sub-exception` → `nil` in prod; a vector, list, string or `nil` upstream binds its first element / first character / `nil` — silent in the shapes subs most often carry.

**Who it hurts.** The app author, on every refactor that changes how one dependency is chosen, and on every second input added (scalar flips to vector). The AI pairing with them, which must remember "one arrow is bare, two are a vector, one producer is a vector" — `docs/core/subscriptions.md:185-189` teaches it as "the only wrinkle in the syntax". The image author: `lower-inline-sub` (`subs.cljc:2481-2512`) hard-codes `:input-kind :db` because the inline tuple `[id metadata body]` has nowhere to put a chain, so `image.cljc:291` restricts inline `:reg-sub` to "the layer-1 db-reader form ONLY" — a derived sub cannot be authored inline at all. Tool authors are *not* hurt: `sub-topology`, Xray and pair-mcp read the registrar slots `:input-kind` / `:input-signals` / `:input-fn`, never the grammar.

## The decision

**Q1 (the ruling).** Which of these does `reg-sub` become?

- **A.** `(reg-sub id ?metadata computation-fn)`; `:inputs` in metadata is a literal vector of query vectors (`:static`) or a producer fn/Var (`:parametric`); declared inputs always arrive as a vector (zero, one or many; explicit `{:inputs []}` → `[]`, absent → `db`); `:<-` and the two-fn tail deleted, old spellings a loud registration error.
- **B.** Keep `:<-`, make a single arrow deliver `[v]`.
- **C.** Bare value for one input in both modes.
- **D.** Delete the parametric mode; keep `:<-`.
- **E.** `:inputs` as a named map with `(fn [{:keys [items]} q])`.
- **F.** Keep as designed; record the rejected simplification.

**Q2 (sub-decision, only under A).** Landing order: **(i)** the in-repo sequence already filed — .46 lands `:inputs` + always-vector + normative spec while `:<-` keeps today's exact delivery behind the existing `vector-inputs?` boolean; .47/.48/.49 sweep in parallel; .50 deletes — or **(ii)** one cut, a single PR carrying parser, delivery, spec and every consumer.

**Q3 (sub-decision).** Vector-vs-map `:inputs`: **(i)** defer to one joint `reg-flow` + `reg-sub` ruling when `spec/013-Flows.md:566-571`'s trigger fires; **(ii)** rule vector now for both; **(iii)** rule map for subs now.
