title: Unit-test pruning: codemod-fresco
description:
Apply the exact requested pruning prompt recursively to migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/test. This is a distinct worker cluster under rf2-0wcq5. Production code remains unchanged except temporary hash-verified fault plants. Push a draft test-only PR, babysit all latest-head checks to green, then mark ready. A measured no-op or unexecuted-file report is valid; do not manufacture changes.

Simplify the unit tests under migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/test. Do not change the code under test. LLMs tend to
write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer
than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction,
and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns
its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could
plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing
it proves.

Stay inside migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/test. Do not edit tests elsewhere. If a deletion relies on a test outside
migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/test to keep covering something, name that test in your report.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines. Confirm a
   runner actually executes each file in migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/test; a file nothing runs cannot be pruned on
   evidence, so report it.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each
   boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests
   refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map:
   promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller
   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/test plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup
  is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate per-platform test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code.
  A single shared test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code
  that no production caller uses.

- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an
  assertion that a later one in the same test implies.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings,
  requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and
  drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.

- Rename a test only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that
  nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter, a skip list or a doc that cites it.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes
  a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised
  failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers
  it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published
  doc or spec claim to the code.

on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a
  simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Dead code and stale docs or spec text go in your report as a
  list, not into your change.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in
the same change. Commit one file or module at a time.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place
  the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code and
  confirm it matches the committed file. One plant per group sharing a cover is enough.
  If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A cover must actually run. A skipped test, a fixture the runner never loads, or a test
  on a lane nothing executes covers nothing. Confirm the runner executes a cover before
  resting a deletion on it.
- Run each test file you touched on its own at least once. Deleting a file can break a
  sibling that relied on it loading something first; give such a file its own require.
- A deletion made under the second question needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in
  the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an
  assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line
  reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Tests outside migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/test that your deletions rely on.
- Dead code, stale docs or spec text, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test
and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters
more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is
not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it
catches that a caller would notice, delete it.

Files that still require slim, at the rf2-47zrp branch:
- `bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/hd8_app.cljs` — requires `re-frame.adapter.reagent-slim`; `?adapter=reagent-slim` arm.
- `bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/hd8_clock_app.cljs` — same, plus the `:slim` arm roster `[:floor :reagent-slim :uix :donor-r1 :donor-r2]`.

- `bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/walk_vs_reagent_app.cljs`.

## Why it was not done in rf2-47zrp

The HD-008 donor arms are measured AGAINST reagent-slim (its `as-element` walk is the donor baseline). Removing the slim arm changes what the HD-008 instrument measures, which is a measurement-design decision, not a mechanical deletion. And `bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco/clock_exit_path.test.cjs` reads the hd8 runners and is held under rf2-hxi3z, so that worker could not touch it.

## Work

Decide the HD-008 instrument's arms without reagent-slim (drop the slim arm and its donor-vs-slim rows, or re-base the donor comparison on stock Reagent), then make the listed files compile under `bench/fresco/shadow-cljs.edn` with no `reagent2.*` or `re-frame.adapter.reagent-slim` require. Sequence after rf2-hxi3z for `clock_exit_path.test.cjs`.

Lineage-only comments elsewhere in the bench that cite reagent-slim as a donor precedent (`front/codec.cljs`, `arm1/*`, `lane*.cljs`, `retention_probe.cljs`, `ssr/entry.cljs`, `amp_merge_clock_app.cljs`) can be tidied in the same pass where they now read as a live adapter.

title: Replace the conformance runner's three hand-kept key rosters with one matcher table tied to the fixture grammar, and shrink the duplicated grammar prose
description:
## Ruling

Once `spec/conformance/fixture-file.edn` is the conformance corpus's one closed grammar (the bead this depends on), the conformance runner's three hand-kept key rosters go. They are replaced by ONE matcher table: exactly one matcher per grammar expectation key, and a test that ties the matcher set to the grammar. No expectation key is ever again "delegated" by name to a runner that picks fixtures by filename. The prose that duplicated the grammar shrinks to narrative plus a pointer, and the unmeasured harness-size promises go. This is the second deliverable of Option C (closed grammar as data plus grade-once), with Goal 2 ruled live but measured; Option D's harness consolidation stays deferred.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. **The rosters are a second, drifting copy of the grammar.** `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:226-239` (`corpus-checked-expect-keys`), `:241-267` (`sibling-owned-expect-keys`), `:279-292` (`implemented-fixture-keys`), with `unknown-expect-keys` (`:269`) and `unknown-fixture-keys` (`:294`) checking only the FIRST level, and only after the capability gate. They were hand-repaired three times in six weeks (rf2-9vbg3, rf2-7yth0, rf2-mn2ht.61).
2. **Delegation by name has already let five channels go ungraded.** `sibling-owned-expect-keys` is "delegated, NOT ignored" (`:249-250`), to "frame-lifecycle / destroy runners" that do not exist (`:247`) and to an SSR runner that loads only `ssr-*.edn` (`implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj:242-252`). Meanwhile `:machine-transition` is realised twice, at `conformance_runner.cljc:940` and `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machines_conformance_test.clj:130`, and neither reads the call record's `:expect-trace` / `:expect-microsteps`.
3. **The prose makes size promises nobody has measured.** "The harness is small (~300 lines per host)" (`spec/conformance/README.md:478`; `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:548`; `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:36`) and "~50 lines" for the DSL interpreter (`spec/conformance/README.md:363`; skill `:51`). The reference harness is 5,547 lines across nine files.

Rejected options: **A** (leave the rosters) keeps the drift and the delegation hole. **B** (one matcher per key, no grammar) is subsumed: the matchers are kept, but tied to the grammar rather than to a fourth hand list. **D**'s test-only `implementation/conformance/` artefact with thin family runners stays DEFERRED, until the next duplicated-harness bug appears or a fourth family runner is proposed. No monolithic harness is needed for this bead.

Supersedes: the hand-kept roster mechanism rf2-mn2ht.61 installed (closed; its fail-loud intent survives as the grammar validation plus matcher coverage), and the implementor skill's "Derive, never transcribe" for the grammar's facts (`skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:12`). No EP is superseded.

NOT decided, and left exactly as it is: whether `:fixture/spec-version`, its README §Versioning floor and its five runner copies are deleted. The two reviews differ and Mike has not ruled, so do not touch any of them here.

## Work

**Code (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc` and siblings):**
- **One matcher table** keyed by expectation key, covering top-level `:fixture/expect` keys AND call-record expectation keys. Each key is graded by exactly one matcher that runs on EVERY fixture carrying it, whatever the fixture's filename.
  - Where an observation needs SSR or flows, the shared runner can host it, since core's JVM test classpath already carries both artefacts (`implementation/core/deps.edn:102`).
  - If a sibling runner keeps a matcher, the coverage check must prove that runner loads every fixture carrying the key.
  - SSR's production-posture evidence stays where it is.
- **A coverage assertion:** the matcher table's keys equal the grammar's expectation keys, top-level and call-record nested. A grammar key without a matcher, or a matcher without a grammar key, fails.
- **A planted-fault check per matcher:** a deliberately wrong retained expectation must fail.
- **Delete:** `implemented-fixture-keys`, `corpus-checked-expect-keys`, `sibling-owned-expect-keys`, `unknown-expect-keys`, `unknown-fixture-keys` and the report lines that print them (`:1857-1860`, `:1922-1960`). Also delete their tests: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj` `unknown-expect-key-fails-loud` (`:231`) and `unknown-top-level-key-fails-loud` (`:246`), and the CLJS leaf `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_corpus_cljs_test.cljs:168-186` (`unknown-top-level-key-fails-loud-cljs`). Rewrite them against the grammar where a positive control is still wanted.
  - On CLJS an unknown expectation key still fails by construction, because it has no matcher.
  - An unknown top-level key is caught by the JVM grammar validation over the same corpus, so the CLJS lane needs no Malli.
- **Small leftovers:**
  - a single `:machine-transition` realiser (drop the second at `machines_conformance_test.clj:130`, or have it delegate);
  - the `:derivation-graph` arm's private one-level `sub-map?` (`conformance_runner.cljc:1363`) replaced by the shared `rf.conformance/submap?`;
  - the core runner's known-skip of `:ssr/hydration-payload` (`:218`), a tag no fixture carries, removed (check `:ssr/render-tree-hash` beside it the same way).

**Prose:**
- `spec/conformance/README.md`:
  - the top-level key, call-op and DSL op tables (§Top-level fixture keys `:40`, §Mode B `:124`, §Handler-body DSL ops `:367`) shrink to narrative plus a pointer at the grammar file;
  - the narrative stays: the modes, the lifecycle, the controlled clock, capability tagging;
  - the 110-row §Fixtures table (`:492`) goes, because each fixture's `:fixture/doc` says the same;
  - the "~300 lines" (`:478`) and "~50 lines" (`:363`) claims go.
- `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:548`: the "~300 lines per host" claim goes.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md`:
  - "Derive, never transcribe" (`:12`) becomes "read the grammar file" for keys, call ops, DSL ops and the capability vocabulary;
  - the dynamic-host-only set and fixture count stay derived at the pin;
  - the "~300 lines" heading (`:36`) and the "~50 lines" claim (`:51`) go.

**What deliberately stays:** `:fixture/spec-version` and everything that reads it; the Python scanner `scripts/check_conformance_fixture_edn.py`; harness file locations; capability tag names.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones:** none. `spec/conformance/README.md`, `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md` and the skill are not hot zones; no `deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn` or workflow change.
- **Depends on:** the grammar bead from this dossier ("Publish the closed conformance fixture grammar..."), wired with `bd dep add`. Also on the coordinator's five-ungraded-channels bug, which the grammar bead already follows.

title: HTTP: replace per-phase handles and split indexes with one stable request record in one registry (behaviour-preserving, prototype-gated)
description:
## Ruling

Rewrite the managed-HTTP request lifecycle so that each `:rf.http/managed` request has ONE stable record for its whole life (issuance, preparation, fetch, backoff, retry, cancellation) in ONE authoritative registry, and changes only through four transitions. It is a behaviour-preserving, prototype-gated refactor: no public API, trace, work-id, reply or hook change. Adopt the result only if the handoff and publication-reconciliation logic disappears while ownership, abort precedence, supersession, restore and exactly-once completion still hold on both hosts; abandon it if equivalent reconciliation grows back. The benefit is a lifecycle that programmers and their AI tools can read as four transitions, and a spec that states behaviour rather than a cell layout; it is not a new authoring capability. The live JVM transport stays: it is a v1 requirement for the reference, so the record needs a JVM realisation. Priority P3, not urgent.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. His instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both the original dossier recommendation and the Codex review chose option B (prototype the one record behind a gate, preserving behaviour) and both keep the live JVM transport.

Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. **One request is tracked by a transfer protocol across split indexes.** There are three process-global indexes, `in-flight` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:107`), `actor-in-flight` (`:113`) and `anonymous-in-flight` (`:143`). Publishing an actor-issued request is "TWO SWAPS OVER TWO ATOMS" with a trailing midpoint reconcile (`registry.cljc:195-271`), a predecessor-only conditional slot take (`:246-258`) and a second scan on the destroy side, `midpoint-actor-handles` (`:754-782`).
2. **Every phase mints a new handle and hands over.** The backoff handle registers first and the predecessor is cleared after it ("CONTINUOUS REGISTRATION", `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1130-1136`), and the shared `finalised?` / `aborted?` cells are threaded across phases in a `:rf.http/retry-handoff` payload (`transport.cljc:1694-1704`). `transport.cljc` is 2,226 lines, 972 of them `;` comment lines, mostly explaining these windows. Spec 014 copies the internals into normative text (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:484` names the `:aborted?` cell, the `:finalised?` CAS, `finalise-success!`, `finalise-failure!` and `maybe-retry!`).
3. **The live JVM transport has a taught consumer.** `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:115-132` fetches its resource live on the JVM from `API_ORIGIN`, and resources lower onto `:rf.http/managed`; Spec 014 ships the JVM transport in the reference (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:26`). The races being removed are between the HttpClient completion or backoff-scheduler thread and the event thread, so the record needs a JVM guard whatever the frame-writer model is.

Rejected options:

- **A, leave it as it is:** correct and heavily tested, but every lifecycle change (`Retry-After`, pluggable backoff, a streaming sibling, a second transport) must first learn the windows, and Spec 014 keeps teaching internals.
- **C, B plus the contract trims bundled** (body-thunk removal, a per-frame work-id sequence, frame-exact aborts from resources, distinct stale reasons): breaking, reaches the `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` and `spec/Conventions.md` hot zones, and throws away this refactor's one strong verification, "same observables, both hosts". Those trims are judged one at a time, later.
- **D, wait and build the record together with the transport seam (rf2-mn2ht.71):** the same end state as one larger change made while someone waits on the seam, and every lifecycle change before then pays today's cost.
- **Dropping the live JVM transport to delete the races:** rejected, because the reference's SSR resource loaders use it (fact 3).

Supersedes no standing ruling or EP. rf2-mn2ht.71 (the deferred `:fixture/transport` conformance seam) stays deferred on its own trigger, and builds on this record when picked up.

**Out of scope, still open:** whether to remove `:body` thunks (`(fn [] …)` bodies) and turn body-encode failures into dispatch-time throws. The two reviews differ there, so it is held for Mike. This bead preserves today's thunk semantics exactly (see Work).

## Work

### The record and the registry (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc`)

- Replace `in-flight`, `actor-in-flight` and `anonymous-in-flight` with one registry atom. Target shape `{frame-id {token record}}`. If repeated frame scans obscure the code, derived projections (for example by `:request-id` or `:actor-id`) are acceptable, provided they live in the same atom and are updated in the same swap; the measure of success is that publication reconciliation disappears, not the number of maps.
- One record per request, published ONCE at issuance with every key, before any cancellation path can reach it:
  `{:token :frame :request-id :actor-id :origin-event :issuance :attempt :url :sensitive? :phase :cancel :abort}`, where `:phase` is `:preparing | :in-flight | :backoff | :done`, `:cancel` is the host cancel for the current phase (or nil) and `:abort` is the abort reason set together with `:phase :done`.
- The token is internal and must distinguish request objects even when frame ids or public work tuples recur. A callback holding an old record must neither retire nor mutate a successor (today's identity-conditional cleanup, `registry.cljc:348-361`, is the behaviour to keep).
- Queries become filters over the one registry: managed-abort and supersede by `:request-id` within the frame, actor destroy by `:actor-id`, frame destroy and epoch restore take the whole frame in one `swap-vals!`. Frame teardown includes anonymous requests, suppresses late delivery and spares any successor under the same public frame id.
- Issuance counters keep their two lifetimes (`registry.cljc:472-570`): named counters evict on terminal completion when unchanged; anonymous counters survive completion until owner teardown.
- The test snapshot helpers (`in-flight-snapshot`, `actor-in-flight-snapshot`) and seed helpers keep their public names and shapes, as projections of the registry.

### The lifecycle (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc`)

Rewrite `run-attempt!` (`:1681-2226`), `maybe-retry!` (`:1349-1457`), `schedule-backoff-handle!` (`:1088-1347`), `finalise-success!` / `finalise-failure!` (`:919-1048`) and `dispatch-aborted!` (`:691-776`) as four transitions, the only writers of the record:

- `send!` — `:preparing` → `:in-flight`; `:cancel` := host cancel.
- `completed!` — `:in-flight` (attempt n) → `:backoff` (retry) or `:done` (reply).
- `fire!` — `:backoff` → `:preparing`, attempt + 1, then `send!`.
- `abort!` — any phase but `:done` → `:done`; call `:cancel`; retire; reply or suppress.

Each transition decides outside the record's guard and commits inside it: the record's monitor on the JVM, a plain `swap!` on CLJS. User code (`:decode`, `:accept`, `:after`, the reply dispatch, a body thunk) never runs under the guard. **Retire** (remove the record from the registry, evict the named issuance counter, detach the external abort signal) runs at exactly one site, replacing today's teardown triple at four sites.

Four boundaries the rewrite must preserve:

1. **Host issuance.** Checking the phase, releasing the guard and later calling `sendAsync` or Fetch would reopen the cancelled-then-sent hole. The phase check, the host send and the publication of its cancel must be ordered against cancellation, as the JVM `issue-lock` / `issue-phase` region does today (`transport.cljc:2166-2200`). Thunk removal would not remove this: two of the three tests in `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_abort_body_prep_race_test.clj` (`:105-173`) use plain string bodies. If send wins, the work may already have reached the server; JDK exchange cancellation is best-effort, and `http_abort_cancels_exchange_test.clj` must still pass.
2. **Outcome commitment.** Decode and accept run before finalisation and may execute user code. A transport completion must not commit `:done` before that classification finishes, and an abort during classification must still win (abort always wins, `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:478-486`). An already-finalised request is not retroactively cancelled (`014:713-721`). Keep response processing (`transport.cljc:1506-1612`) and reply delivery outside the guard.
3. **Identity and retention.** As in the registry section: tokens distinguish request objects, old callbacks cannot touch a successor, the two counter lifetimes are kept, and the sleeping attempt keeps its work identity (`014:486`).
4. **Deadlines and disposal.** Keep per-attempt deadlines covering response bodies (JVM `orTimeout`, `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_jvm.cljc:270-324`; CLJS whole-body deadline, `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_cljs.cljc:147-175`), timeout classification and retry eligibility, real exchange and timer cancellation, and external-listener detachment (`transport_cljs.cljc:307-339`). A single current `:cancel` slot does not by itself prove a timer cannot be armed after retirement; make that ordering explicit.

### Deleted

- The forward-reference cells `handle-holder`, `handle-cell`, `timer-cell` and `cf-holder`; `fired?`; the shared `finalised?` / `aborted?` threading and the `:rf.http/retry-handoff` payload (`transport.cljc:1694-1704`, `:1318-1324`); clear-after-successor (`:1266`, `:1993`) and both post-registration re-checks (`:1327-1346`, `:2023-2026`); per-phase external-signal rebinding (`:1277-1280`, `:2005-2008`) — the signal is bound once at issuance.
- The two-swap publication and midpoint reconcile (`registry.cljc:195-271`), `midpoint-actor-handles` (`:754-782`), the identity dedupe in the sweeps (`:655-662`, `:986-994`), `anonymous-in-flight` as its own atom, `clear-in-flight-in-frame!` and the nil-handle branch of the 3-arity `clear-in-flight!` (`:273-371`).
- The pre-CAS and post-CAS abort sampling in `finalise-success!` (`transport.cljc:919-986`). `issue-phase` and `issue-lock` fold into `send!`'s guarded step.
- The two `interleave!` points no test uses, `:backoff/after-register` and `:maybe-retry/before-schedule` (`transport.cljc:52-78`). The remaining hooks move to transition boundaries.

### Small follow-on edits

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:512-544`, the issue path: mint the token and publish the record at issuance.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_cljs.cljc`: bind the external `:abort-signal` once at issuance; detach it in retire.
- The Xray managed-HTTP testbed calls `rf.http.registry/record-in-flight!` directly (`tools/xray/testbeds/managed_http/core.cljs:223`, `:328`); adjust it and its source-text law test `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/testbed_managed_http_frame_scope_test.clj`.

### Spec 014 (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`, not a hot zone)

- `:484` — replace the implementation paragraph with the observable rule, stating precisely when abort intent is observed and when the outcome commits.
- `:681`, clause 4 — drop "or inside the window before a freshly-issued handle is published".
- `:713` — drop the `:finalised?` CAS name.
- `:894` — drop "the retry mints a fresh handle that bypasses the once-only reply guard" and the "once-only reply CAS" wording; keep the observable claim.
- `:1114` — the `clear-all-in-flight!` row ("Drops both the request-id-keyed and actor-id-keyed in-flight maps") describes the one registry.

### Tests

The cancellation, race, backoff, frame, actor, restore, reply-tail, deadline and exchange-cancel suites keep their observable assertions on both hosts; only their injection points are retargeted to transition boundaries. In `implementation/http/test/re_frame/`: `http_abort_retry_race_test.clj`, `http_abort_body_prep_race_test.clj`, `http_abort_cancels_exchange_test.clj`, `http_abort_precedence_test.clj`, `http_actor_destroy_cancellation_test.clj`, `http_actor_destroy_stale_test.clj`, `http_anonymous_frame_ownership_test.clj`, `http_backoff_cancellation_test.clj`, `http_frame_scoped_cancellation_test.clj`, `http_completion_fence_test.clj`, `http_completion_fence_cljs_test.cljs`, `http_reply_tail_test.clj`, `http_reply_tail_cljs_test.cljs`, `http_jvm_body_timeout_test.clj`, `http_body_prep_failure_test.clj`. The source's own acceptance wording asked both that the interleave seams be deleted and that the suites "pass unchanged"; both cannot hold literally, so the gate is the same observable assertions, on both hosts, with fewer windows.

### Deliberately stays

The args map, the reply envelope, every trace row, the work-id tuple `[:rf.work/http <request-id> <issuance> <attempt>]` (including the sleeping attempt's), `:rf.http/managed-abort`, the late-bind hook names, the public snapshot and seed helpers, `maybe-retry!`'s name (Spec 009 names it in two catalogue rows, so `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` is untouched), and `:body` thunks with today's semantics: invoked in the preparation phase outside the guard, re-invoked per retry, and a preparation failure delivered as `:rf.http/transport` with `:stage :request-prep` (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:207-222`).

### Gate and abandonment

Size L. The reduction is inferred, not measured: about 2,200 lines of lifecycle and index code becoming perhaps 800 to 1,200. Abandon the prototype if the JVM guard needs as many states and re-checks as today, if the transition guards grow back into per-phase handoffs, or if the injection windows do not shrink. On abandonment, record the reason on this bead and file option A's two cleanups instead: delete the two unused `interleave!` points, and rewrite `014:484`, `:713` and `:894` as observable contract.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones:** none. It touches `implementation/http/**`, `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` (not a hot zone, and not the i/crlf file), `tools/xray/testbeds/managed_http/` and one Xray test. It is safe in parallel with anything outside `implementation/http/` and the Xray managed-HTTP testbed.
- **Bead dependencies:** none.
- **Same dossier, still open (`http-one-request-record.md`):** body-thunk removal. This bead does not wait on it. If Mike rules removal, do not run that work in parallel with this bead (both edit `transport.cljc` and Spec 014 §Body encoding). Landing it first removes the CLJS re-entrant-abort-in-thunk window and leaves the prototype one state lighter; landing it after means it edits the `:preparing` step instead. Either order works.
- **Follows this bead:** rf2-mn2ht.71 (the deferred conformance transport seam) and any HTTP transport-seam or stub-transport work from `conformance-fixture-grammar.md`. With a record, the host send is one call with one cancel slot. rf2-mn2ht.71's description cites `014:484` as Spec 014's only "seam" mention; this bead rewrites that line.
- **Should follow this bead, not run in parallel:** any change to `[:rf.work/http …]` from `resource-identity-privacy-and-correlation.md`, because this bead's verification depends on unchanged work ids; and the frame-declared `:http-interceptors` work from `one-registry-top-level-reg.md`, which changes chain capture and retention across retries in the same issue path.
- **Independent of `jvm-one-writer-per-frame.md`:** the races here are between the HttpClient completion thread or the backoff scheduler thread (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj:164-175`) and the event thread, not two writers on one frame, so the record needs its JVM guard whatever that dossier rules.

## Evidence

- **Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:** the three index atoms and two counter maps; the two-swap publication and midpoint reconcile; continuous registration and the retry-handoff payload; the line counts (`transport.cljc` 2,226 lines with 972 comment lines; `registry.cljc` 1,096); the JVM issuance region (`transport.cljc:2166-2200`); the plain-body issuance-boundary tests (`http_abort_body_prep_race_test.clj:105-173`, 173 lines); the Spec 014 lines that name internals (`:484`, `:681`, `:713`, `:894`, `:1114`); the live JVM fetch in the SSR resources example; and the Xray testbed's direct `record-in-flight!` calls.
- **Still needs a run:** nothing was executed. Runtime equivalence on both hosts, the actual line reduction, and the cost of frame scans in the registry are unmeasured; the prototype measures them.
acceptance_criteria:
1. One registry atom in `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc` holds every in-flight managed request (named, actor-issued and anonymous) as one record per request, published once at issuance with its token before any cancellation path can reach it. `in-flight`, `actor-in-flight` and `anonymous-in-flight` no longer exist as separate atoms; any projections live in the same atom and are updated in the same swap.
2. A search of `implementation/http/src/` finds none of `handle-holder`, `handle-cell`, `timer-cell`, `cf-holder`, `fired?`, `:rf.http/retry-handoff`, `midpoint-actor-handles` or `clear-in-flight-in-frame!`, and no midpoint reconcile or per-phase external-signal rebinding remains.
3. The record changes only through `send!`, `completed!`, `fire!` and `abort!`, each committing under the record's guard (the JVM monitor, the CLJS `swap!`); no user code (`:decode`, `:accept`, `:after`, reply dispatch, a body thunk) runs under the guard.
4. Retire (remove from the registry, evict the named issuance counter, detach the external abort signal) has exactly one call site.
5. No path checks the phase, releases the guard and then calls the host send; `http_abort_body_prep_race_test.clj` (including its plain-string-body orderings) and `http_abort_cancels_exchange_test.clj` keep their assertions.

== GATE OUTCOME: ADOPTED (worker, PR #11365, branch worker/http-one-record)

Verdict: the prototype is adopted. None of the abandonment criteria fired.
- The JVM guard is one monitor per record (the record cell itself) around four guarded commits, each checking only phase + attempt. Gone: the finalised?/aborted? cells, the issue-phase CAS and issue-lock, fired?, the four forward-reference cells, both post-registration re-checks, and the pre/post-CAS abort sampling.
- No per-phase handoff grew back: the record is published once at issuance and never replaced; there is no handoff payload.
- The injection windows shrank from five interleave points spread across two handoffs to three, one per transition boundary: :issue/before-send (send!), :completed/before-commit (completed!), :retry/before-attempt (fire!). :backoff/after-register and :maybe-retry/before-schedule are deleted; :backoff/before-register is now :completed/before-commit.

Measured line counts (total / ;-comment lines), trunk dbb2b1a0bd -> branch:
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc: 2226 / 972 -> 1427 / 333
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc: 1096 / 226 -> 641 / 136
- combined: 3322 -> 2068 lines. The four transitions plus send!/run-attempt!/fire!/issue! are about 417 lines.

Shape as built:
- registry.cljc: one atom, {frame-id (sorted-map token record-cell)}. Every query (lookup and abort by request-id, supersede!, actor destroy, both frame sweeps, clear-all) is a filter over it. Actor destroy and the frame sweeps take their records in one swap-vals!. A record the registry aborts leaves the registry whatever its abort-fn does, so a fabricated (seeded) record owes no cleanup.
- transport.cljc: send! (:preparing -> :in-flight), completed! (:preparing|:in-flight attempt n -> :backoff or :done), fire! (:backoff -> :preparing, attempt n+1), abort! (any phase but :done -> :done). Retire (registry removal by token, named-counter eviction, external-signal detach) has one call site, in commit!, when a record reaches :done.
- handlers.cljc calls transport/issue!, which publishes the record with every key, binds the external :abort-signal once (CLJS), then runs attempt 1.

1. completed! also commits from :preparing: a body-preparation failure is attempt n's outcome before any send.
2. The record keeps :abort-fn (its one abort entry point, which every registry query fires and the seed helpers already require) and, on CLJS, :external-abort (for retire's detach), beside the ruling's key list. :abort holds the abort reason.
3. A race-window difference, recorded rather than preserved: an abort that lands while an attempt-2+ failure is being classified used to let that failure's terminal :rf.http/retry-attempt STOP row (:no-recovery) still emit after the abort reply; now the STOP row is emitted only when that failure itself commits.

Found and fixed during self-review (commit 9ae4f9dcd8): the any-frame abort-on-actor-destroy collected frames with keep, which dropped a nil frame, so a record seeded without :frame was never aborted (trunk reached it). That reclassification no longer exists; every abort row now comes from dispatch-aborted!. Line 2322 also still says "the retry mints a fresh handle that bypasses the once-only reply guard". Spec 009 belongs to rf2-fptxd's fence.
- docs/api/re-frame.http.md:528 still says seed-in-flight-for-test! keeps "both indexes" consistent.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc:301 and :723 name run-attempt! and its "(when-not @finalised? …)" guard as where an already-aborted external signal fires. It now fires in transport/issue!, still synchronously inside the issuing fx, so the attribution those helpers implement still holds; only the names are stale.
== SETTLED 2026-10-16 ==
Body thunks STAY. Removing them is not a precondition of this bead, and it is not ruled.

The independent Codex review held that thunks' memory value is unproven, and that changing how preparation failures are reported (dispatch-time throws instead of managed failures) changes the managed-failure contract, which deserves its own decision. title: Examples: rewrite the ':rf/default looks special but isn't' comments to state the app-frame convention
description:
## Ruling

**`:rf/default` is the conventional, documented frame id for a single-frame app, and every teaching surface converges on it.** Today the repo teaches three ids for the same thing: `:rf/default` (examples, scaffold, getting-started, test fixture, migration, pair MCP), `:app` (the guide) and `:app/main` (the skills and parts of the spec). After this ruling the scaffold, examples, guide, skills and spec boot templates all write `:rf/default` for a single-app frame.

It is a NAMING CONVENTION ONLY:

- `frame-root` keeps its REQUIRED `:id`, written out on the page. A missing `:id` still raises `:rf.error/frame-root-missing-id`.
- The runtime still never creates, infers or falls back to `:rf/default`: it is not created by `init!`, not the React-context default, not a lookup tier. A rootless `dispatch` still raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.
- Apps stay free to choose any other id. Descriptive ids stay wherever a passage teaches genuinely independent frames (two roots, per-request SSR frames, stories, embedded widgets).
- Wording constraint: describe it as a shared TEACHING convention, never as an address the REPL or tools secretly expect. Tool-Pair tier 3 resolves any sole app frame whatever its id (`spec/Tool-Pair.md:498`), and the pair guard merely exempts `:rf/default` from reserved-tool classification.
- Matching the app's id and the test fixture's id helps orientation, not test fidelity: the fixture builds `:preset :test` and does not mount the production root, so its `:fx-overrides` / `:interceptors` are not reproduced. Do not claim otherwise.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both the original dossier recommendation and the independent Codex review chose option A (bless the name, keep `:id` required, align the guide and skills) and both deferred B.

**Decisive facts (at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. **The newcomer path fails silently today.** `docs/core/getting-started.md:97` builds the counter with `(def app-frame :rf/default)`. The next guide page, `docs/core/app-db.md:109`, says "call `(rf/app-db-value :app)`", and `app-db-value` returns `nil` for an unknown frame (`spec/API.md:692`). So the instruction returns `nil` on the app the reader just built. Census: `:rf/default` in 41 example files and the template (`tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/core.cljs:17`); `:app` as a frame id across about 67 files under `docs/` (e.g. `docs/core/introduction.md:51`, `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:46` `(def app-frame :app)`); `:app/main` in the skills and spec (e.g. `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/project-structure.md:106`, which tells readers to pick a "descriptively-named" id and calls `:rf/default` "worth picking only for a tiny app or v1 migration").
2. **The spec still calls the id merely ordinary**, at `spec/002-Frames.md:234-249` and `:900-911`, following EP-0002 resolved open issue 4 (`docs/EP/EP-0002-frame-target-resolution.md:1278-1283`). That issue's premise was that "the reservation buys neither migration nor docs clarity", and it no longer holds. Migration rule M-20 rewrites `:re-frame/default` to `:rf/default` (`migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1022`, row at `:1034`), and the guide calls a single-frame app "Type A — only `:rf/default` in play" (`:696`). The test fixture ensures "the conventional `:rf/default` app frame" (`spec/008-Testing.md:196`, `:216`). The pair guard exempts it as "the canonical app frame" (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/reserved_frame_guard.cljs:60-71`).
3. **`frame-root` requires `:id` and fails loud without it** (`spec/002-Frames.md:1696`, `:1746` "There is no `:rf/default` floor"; the shared validator `require-frame-root-id!` is at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/frame_boundary.cljs:143-166`). That stays, so this ruling needs no code change.

**Rejected options:**

- **B (an id-less `frame-root` defaults to `:rf/default`): deferred, not taken.** It hides the REPL address from the source. It also gives `frame-root {}` and `make-frame {}` different meanings for "no id": the conventional frame against a private gensym. And it makes silently joining a shared frame the easy path: a second id-less root replaces the first root's `:fx-overrides`/`:interceptors` and never replays its `:initial-events`. Revisit only with evidence that `:rf.error/frame-root-missing-id` is a recurring stumble.
- **C (examples move to app-chosen ids):** the REPL address varies per app, new apps diverge permanently from M-20-migrated apps and from the fixture default, and the guide would still have to pick one id.
- **D (leave as is):** keeps the three-way split and the silent `(rf/app-db-value :app)` failure.
- **Renaming to a non-"default" `:rf/*` id:** about 2,600 occurrences in about 800 files for a wording nuance, and it loses the v1 echo of `:re-frame/default`.
- **Rootless calls resolving to the sole live frame:** stays closed. A callback captured in a destroyed frame would land in its sole successor.

**Supersedes:** the framing of EP-0002 resolved open issue 4 that `:rf/default` is merely an "ordinary" id. Its substance stands: no privilege, no inference, no floor. This ruling does NOT reopen rf2-78wg or rf2-mhpo; their "there is no `:rf/default` floor" corrections stay true and must survive every rewrite.

**Filed as four beads** (label `dossier-ruling`): the spec bead first, then the guide sweep, the examples comment sweep and the skills sweep, which can run in parallel once the spec bead has merged.

## Work (this bead: the examples comment sweep)

The examples already use `:rf/default` for every app frame (41 files at trunk 89517e8f54, 24 of them `(def app-frame :rf/default)`). No example uses another id for its app frame. Only their COMMENTS contradict the convention, by dismissing the id as "ordinary", "just an id we picked" or "looks special but isn't".

- **Rewrite those comments** to state the convention. Suggested sense, not wording: "`:rf/default` is the conventional app-frame id, the name the guide, the test fixture and migrated apps use. The runtime never falls back to it, so we name the frame here and hand it over explicitly." Keep each comment's existing pointer to `docs/core/glossary.md#frame-identity-is-carried-not-found` or the boot how-to.
- **Known sites** (from `git grep -nE "looks special|ordinary (frame )?id|ordinary frame|no (framework )?privilege" -- examples/` at trunk 89517e8f54):
  - `examples/core/counter/core.cljs:92-96`
  - `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs:94-98`
  - `examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter/core.cljs:87` ("no magic, no privilege")
  - `examples/core/seven_guis/temperature/core.cljs:215-216`
  - `examples/core/seven_guis/crud/core.cljs:244`
  - `examples/core/seven_guis/circle_drawer/core.cljs:340`
  - `examples/core/seven_guis/cells/core.cljs:527`
  - `examples/core/managed_http_counter/core.cljs:316` ("just the id this app happened to pick")
  - `examples/capabilities/routing/routing/core.cljs:180`
  - `examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs:542`
  - Then read the comment beside `:rf/default` in the remaining example files (`git grep -l ':rf/default' -- examples/`) for any differently worded dismissal.
- **Deliberately stays:**
  - every `(def app-frame :rf/default)` and every `:id`/`:frame` value; the SSR boot and several examples rely on the `app-frame` defs;
  - comments saying the runtime never guesses, never falls back, or that there is no floor (they remain true);
  - `with-frame :rf/default` wrappers (see cross-dossier below);
  - `tools/template` (it already uses `:rf/default`, and grep found no dismissive comment there).
- The counter's claim that its boot is "spelled the same" as the boot-and-mount how-to (`examples/core/counter/core.cljs:100-104`) needs no edit. It becomes true when the guide-sweep bead lands.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones touched:** none.
- **Depends on:** the spec bead filed beside it ("Spec: name :rf/default the conventional single-app frame id"). It can run in parallel with the guide-sweep and skills beads.
- **Cross-dossier:** `one-registry-top-level-reg.md` proposes removing thirteen `with-frame :rf/default` wrappers from the examples, in some of the same `core.cljs` files. Sequence the two beads (either order), never in parallel.
- **Gates:** comment-only. No gate covers `;;` lines: the examples compile sweep cannot fail on a comment, and examples are test-free. Verify by hand that the diff touches only comment lines, and say so in the PR body.

## Evidence

Every path:line above was read in source at trunk 89517e8f54, unchanged at 3aaacf1cde. Nothing needs a run.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No example comment dismisses `:rf/default` as ordinary, unprivileged, "just an id we picked" or "looks special but isn't". `git grep -nE "looks special|ordinary (frame )?id|ordinary frame|no (framework |special )?privilege|no magic" -- examples/` returns no line about `:rf/default`.
2. Each rewritten comment says that `:rf/default` is the conventional app-frame id and that the runtime never falls back to it, so the frame is named and handed over explicitly. Each keeps its existing doc pointer.
3. The diff changes only comment lines: every `(def app-frame :rf/default)` and every `:id`/`:frame` value is byte-identical, and no `with-frame` wrapper is added or removed.
4. No test or `*.spec.cjs` file is added under `examples/`.

The next guide page, `docs/core/app-db.md:109`, says "call `(rf/app-db-value :app)`", and `app-db-value` returns `nil` for an unknown frame (`spec/API.md:692`). So the instruction returns `nil` on the app the reader just built. Census: `:rf/default` in 41 example files and the template (`tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/core.cljs:17`); `:app` as a frame id across about 67 files under `docs/` (e.g. `docs/core/introduction.md:51`, `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:46` `(def app-frame :app)`); `:app/main` in the skills and spec (e.g. `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/project-structure.md:106`, which tells readers to pick a "descriptively-named" id and calls `:rf/default` "worth picking only for a tiny app or v1 migration").
2. **The spec still calls the id merely ordinary**, at `spec/002-Frames.md:234-249` and `:900-911`, following EP-0002 resolved open issue 4 (`docs/EP/EP-0002-frame-target-resolution.md:1278-1283`). That issue's premise was that "the reservation buys neither migration nor docs clarity", and it no longer holds. Migration rule M-20 rewrites `:re-frame/default` to `:rf/default` (`migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1022`, row at `:1034`), and the guide calls a single-frame app "Type A — only `:rf/default` in play" (`:696`). The test fixture ensures "the conventional `:rf/default` app frame" (`spec/008-Testing.md:196`, `:216`). The pair guard exempts it as "the canonical app frame" (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/reserved_frame_guard.cljs:60-71`).
3. **`frame-root` requires `:id` and fails loud without it** (`spec/002-Frames.md:1696`, `:1746` "There is no `:rf/default` floor"; the shared validator `require-frame-root-id!` is at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/frame_boundary.cljs:143-166`). That stays, so this ruling needs no code change.

**Rejected options:**

- **B (an id-less `frame-root` defaults to `:rf/default`): deferred, not taken.** It hides the REPL address from the source. It also gives `frame-root {}` and `make-frame {}` different meanings for "no id": the conventional frame against a private gensym. And it makes silently joining a shared frame the easy path: a second id-less root replaces the first root's `:fx-overrides`/`:interceptors` and never replays its `:initial-events`. Revisit only with evidence that `:rf.error/frame-root-missing-id` is a recurring stumble.
- **C (examples move to app-chosen ids):** the REPL address varies per app, new apps diverge permanently from M-20-migrated apps and from the fixture default, and the guide would still have to pick one id.
- **D (leave as is):** keeps the three-way split and the silent `(rf/app-db-value :app)` failure.
- **Renaming to a non-"default" `:rf/*` id:** about 2,600 occurrences in about 800 files for a wording nuance, and it loses the v1 echo of `:re-frame/default`.
- **Rootless calls resolving to the sole live frame:** stays closed. A callback captured in a destroyed frame would land in its sole successor.

**Supersedes:** the framing of EP-0002 resolved open issue 4 that `:rf/default` is merely an "ordinary" id. Its substance stands: no privilege, no inference, no floor. This ruling does NOT reopen rf2-78wg or rf2-mhpo; their "there is no `:rf/default` floor" corrections stay true and must survive every rewrite.

**Filed as four beads** (label `dossier-ruling`): the spec bead first, then the guide sweep, the examples comment sweep and the skills sweep, which can run in parallel once the spec bead has merged.

## Work (this bead: the guide sweep)

**The main acceptance case is convergence.** A reader who builds the counter through getting-started (`:rf/default`) and then follows ANY guide page's REPL or root line must type the same id. Today `docs/core/app-db.md:109` says `(rf/app-db-value :app)`, which returns `nil` on that counter.

- **Scope:** `docs/**` EXCEPT `docs/EP/**` and `docs/design/**` (historical design records, left alone) and `docs/skills/**` (owned by the skills bead). At trunk 89517e8f54, `:app` frame-id hits fall in `docs/core` (46 files, Fresco included), `docs/routing` (8), `docs/api` (5), `docs/ssr` (4), `docs/resources` (3) and `docs/xray` (1). `:app/main` appears in 14 `docs/api` pages, in `docs/core/images.md` and in `docs/xray/api/mount-control.md`.
  - Census commands: `git grep -lE ':app([[:space:])},]|\]|$)' -- 'docs/**/*.md' ':!docs/design/**' ':!docs/EP/**'` gives 67 files and 204 sites, and `git grep -c ':app/main' -- 'docs/api/*.md'` gives 14 files.
  - The `:app` census OVER-counts: it also hits shadow-cljs build ids (`{:builds {:app …}}`, e.g. `docs/api/re-frame.performance.md:9`, `:59`; `docs/resources/tutorial/index.md:74`; `docs/xray/01-installation.md:24`), which are not frame ids and stay.
- **The rule:** where `:app` or `:app/main` names THE app's single frame, change it to `:rf/default`. That covers a `frame-root`/`make-frame` `:id`, `(def app-frame …)`, `{:frame …}`, `with-frame`, `frame-provider`, `app-db-value`, `frame-state-value`, `hydrate! {:frame …}`, `hydrate-page!` entries and REPL lines.
  - Keep a descriptive id where the passage teaches genuinely independent frames: two roots, per-request SSR frames, stories, embedded widgets, a second frame added beside the app's.
  - Keep every non-frame `:app` keyword and every `:app/*` event, sub or view id (`:app/root`, `:app/initialise`).
- **Named sites** (all at trunk 89517e8f54):
  - `docs/core/app-db.md:50` (root `{:id :app …}`) and `:109` (`(rf/app-db-value :app)`);
  - `docs/core/introduction.md:51`; `docs/core/frames.md:103` and `:118`;
  - `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:46` (`(def app-frame :app)`). The counter example claims its boot is "spelled the same" as this how-to (`examples/core/counter/core.cljs:100-104`), and this bead makes that true;
  - `docs/core/run-to-completion.md:65`; `docs/core/events.md:41-43`;
  - `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:33` (the API page's counter hello world uses `:app/main`) and that page's other single-frame `:app/main` sites (`:398-531`);
  - `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:177-258` and `:428`; `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:618` and `:638`; `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:611`; `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md:131`;
  - `docs/ssr/index.md:20` and the rest of `docs/ssr/**`; `docs/resources/concepts.md:202`; `docs/resources/coming-from-tanstack-query.md:63`;
  - `docs/xray/api/mount-control.md:94`, `:151` and `:200` (the inspected host app's frame).
- **Prose:**
  - Any guide sentence that calls `:rf/default` "just an ordinary id", "looks special but isn't" or "a legal frame id you may choose" (e.g. `docs/core/frames.md:118`) becomes the convention statement: `:rf/default` is the conventional app-frame id, and the runtime never falls back to it, so a dispatch outside any frame scope still raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.
  - Say this once per page at most, where the id is first introduced. Do not claim the REPL or tools require the name.
  - Statements that there is no `:rf/default` floor stay.
- **Deliberately stays:** `docs/EP/**`, `docs/design/**`, multi-frame passages, non-frame `:app` keywords. Spec text is the spec bead's job, and skills text is the skills bead's.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones touched:** none.
- **Depends on:** the spec bead filed beside it ("Spec: name :rf/default the conventional single-app frame id"), so the guide's sentences match the ratified spec wording.
- This bead can run in parallel with the examples-comment and skills beads; their directories do not overlap. If one PR is too large, split it by directory (`docs/core` / `docs/api` / `docs/routing`+`docs/ssr`+`docs/resources`+`docs/xray`) into sequential PRs under this one bead.

The nil-on-unknown-frame claim is `spec/API.md:692` ("Returns `nil` for an unknown / destroyed frame"), read in spec, not run. A worker may confirm it at a REPL, but the fix does not depend on it.

title: Spec-Schemas MutationInstance :current-work and WorkLedger keys do not admit the work ids the runtime writes
description:
Two Spec-Schemas resource schemas do not admit values the runtime writes. Both predate rf2-v3ory; found while editing `ResourceWorkId` there.

1. `MutationInstance`'s `:current-work` is `[:maybe ResourceWorkId]`, and `ResourceWorkId` is `[:tuple [:= :rf.work/resource] :keyword :int]` (a read attempt). A mutation instance's current work is `[:rf.work/resource [:rf.mutation <instance-id>] <generation>]`, whose second element is a vector, so the schema rejects every live mutation instance. (Before rf2-v3ory the second slot was `ScopedResourceKey`, a 3-tuple, which rejected it too.)
2. `WorkLedger` is `[:map-of ResourceWorkId ResourceWorkRecord]`, but `re-frame.resources.work-ledger` keys the ledger map by `work-id-id` — the CEDN-1 canonical-bytes string of the work id (it must, because mutation instance ids are caller-supplied values) — and carries the vector on the record as `:work/id`. It also holds mutation records, which `ResourceWorkRecord` (`:work/kind [:= :resource]`) rejects.

Fix: a `MutationWorkId` tuple (or a `WorkId` union of the two) for `MutationInstance :current-work`; `WorkLedger` keyed by the canonical-bytes string with values a union of the resource and mutation record shapes. Spec-Schemas is a hot zone; sequence accordingly. No code schema mirrors these (checked: no `[:= :rf.work/resource]` under implementation/ or tools/).
notes:
== WORKER 2026-10-17 01:20 AUSEST: fixed in PR #11434, commit 6b5c07f5ef ==
Re-derived against work_ledger.cljc and mutation_events.cljc at the PR head. Spec-Schemas gains MutationWorkId ([:rf.work/resource [:rf.mutation instance-id] generation]) and MutationWorkRecord ([:merge ResourceWorkRecord ...] with :work/kind :mutation and :resource/key [:rf.mutation instance-id], which is what mutation_events writes). MutationInstance :current-work is [:maybe MutationWorkId]. WorkLedger is [:map-of :string [:or ResourceWorkRecord MutationWorkRecord]], keyed by work-id-id, the CEDN-1 canonical-bytes string. No code schema mirrors these. The edit sits inside a fenced code block, which no gate inspects, so it was checked by hand; mkdocs --strict 0 and check_doc_slugs 0.
close_reason: Merged in #11434 (f3d2883e08). Spec-Schemas MutationInstance :current-work now admits the mutation work id [:rf.work/resource [:rf.mutation <instance-id>] <generation>]. WorkLedger is keyed by the CEDN-1 canonical-bytes string that re-frame.resources.work-ledger uses (work-id-id), with values a union of the resource and mutation record shapes. Both were re-derived against work_ledger.cljc at the PR head. No code schema mirrors them. CI on 6b5c07f5ef was green.

title: Preserve stale-bundle deletion when the compiler dependency cannot resolve
description: PR #11427 (4dfe096ccd) extracts compile-node-test's delete-before-attempt guarantee into lib/shadow.cjs, but runShadow resolves shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js at lines 512-516 and returns 1 on MODULE_NOT_FOUND before acquiring the lane or removing declared clean outputs at lines 521-524. The old compile-node-test.cjs removed the output before resolving the runner. An existing bundle therefore survives a failed attempt when shadow-cljs is unavailable, allowing a downstream consumer that misses the exit code to test stale code, precisely the failure the wrapper promises to prevent. Focused probe used exact merged helper/wrapper/harness sources and the old wrapper blob bf1bdf47279 in an isolated scratch project, with a preflight proving the compiler could not resolve and a private lock: both wrappers exited 1; baseline stale_bundle_survived=false; merged stale_bundle_survived=true; neither left a lock. No compiler or shadow-cljs build was started. Receipt: ai/pr-audit/11427-stale-output-1.json. Small correction: take the lane and clear declared one-shot outputs before any early compiler-resolution refusal, keeping the existing normalized nonzero result and guaranteed release. Add the missing-runner case beside the existing stale-output/abnormal-verdict tests so a declared output is absent after that failure. Do not widen cleanup beyond declared outputs or clear watch/cache state.

== WORKER SUMMARY 2026-10-16 AUSEST: PR #11435 (branch worker/tooling-lane-classifier), commit "fix(scripts): the build-lane launcher clears a one-shot compile's declared output before it can refuse an unresolvable runner" ==

title: Delete the render and head hash channels and report hydration mismatches by React adoption alone
description:
## Ruling

Hydration mismatches are reported by React adoption alone. Every React-family root (Reagent, reagent-slim, UIx and Fresco) already reports through the spine or Fresco `onRecoverableError` reporter.

Delete these, together with their author-facing surface:
- the body render hash (`:rf/render-hash`, `render-tree-hash`, `verify-hydration!`, `hydrate!`'s `:render-tree-fn`, and the `:ssr {:on-mismatch ...}` and `:detect-mismatch?` knobs);
- the head hash (`:rf/head-hash`);
- both DOM markers (`data-rf-render-hash`, `data-rf-head-hash`);
- the Ring host's `:emit-hash?`.

Describe what remains as REPORTING HYDRATION RECOVERIES, not exhaustive mismatch detection.

There is no framework strict mode and no new comparison engine. CI fails a build by watching the public `:on-recoverable-error` callback.

Accept one loss explicitly: an attribute-only divergence in the root view's own markup loses its re-frame trace, its production record and its strict throw. React's development `console.error` (with a diff) is the signal for that, and React does not patch it.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned, with the instruction:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both recommendations chose option A. Both require the always-on adoption record (rf2-55yio) to land first, and this bead depends on it. Both keep the install ledger's data digest. Both have the testbed rework to cause a real DOM divergence.

Decisive facts, all at trunk 89517e8f54:
- The body hash is one view deep. The canonical walk never calls a view: every fn head serialises to the fixed token `"#fn[]"` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hash.cljc:271-288`). So `[:main [header] [page x]]` hashes as `[:main [#fn[]] [#fn[] x]]`.
- The Ring host omits the hash for any root that resolves to a bare view reference, so the natural spelling `:root-view [(rf/view :app/root)]` "carries no hash" (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj:131-134`, `:198-266`). Strict mode then has nothing to compare.
- Adoption already covers nested divergence. The adapter test hydrates a delegating `app -> layout -> page` root and asserts adoption reports the nested mismatch (`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/adapter_hydrate_root_options_dom_cljs_test.cljs:101-153`).
- No bundled code reads the head hash: "The bundled v1 client stops there — it does not read `:rf/head-hash`, recompute, or compare" (`spec/011-SSR.md:1054`).

Rejected options:
- B (keep the body hash, repaired with symmetric root normalisation and a relabelled recovery): it still misses everything below the root view's own markup, it keeps `:render-tree-fn` and three knobs, and authors would still shape root views for the instrument's sake.
- C (leave as is): it keeps the false `:warned-and-replaced` label on the hash arm (`verify-hydration!` only reports), a head hash with no reader, and the spelling traps.
- A deep hash: it doubles hydration work, cannot evaluate form-2/form-3 local state before mount, and still misses emitter-side differences.
- A framework strict knob on the adoption channel: React has already recovered by the time `onRecoverableError` fires, so the host callback is the right place for CI to fail.

Supersedes:
- the two-tier design of `spec/011-SSR.md` §Hydration-mismatch detection (`:687`);
- the head hash's "post-v1 follow-on" (runtime head-mismatch attribution through `:failing-id`, `spec/011-SSR.md:1056`);
- ssr-hosts Q4 ("should the host normalise a callable-headed root?"). It is moot, because without a hash both spellings are interchangeable.

rf2-tildz is NOT reversed. Its production guarantee moves to the adoption channel in rf2-55yio.

Two findings from the dossier are resolved here:
- **Suspected React dev warning on every correct page.** A static reading of react-dom 19.3.0's development `diffHydratedProperties` (`implementation/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:23077-23731`, reported at `:12910-12912`) says the server-only `data-rf-render-hash` attribute should draw an "attributes didn't match" `console.error` on every hash-stamped Reagent page. It has not been observed, because no test hydrates marker-bearing bytes. The example page omits the marker for exactly that reason (`examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/index.html:27-50`). Deleting the marker removes the cause, and acceptance item 4 pins a clean page.
- **The Xray testbed bakes a fake hash.** `testbeds/ssr_hydration_mismatch/index.html:52` ships `:rf/render-hash "deadbeef"`, and the feature-matrix scenario asserts on `mismatch-server-hash` (`tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs:2101-2126`, scenario entry `:4070-4079`). It is reworked below.

## Work

Code, under `implementation/`:
- `ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hash.cljc`:
  - Delete `render-tree-hash` (`:466`) and the render-tree canonical walk (`canonical-edn-into` `:231`, `canonical-edn` `:371`, and the private helpers only they use, `:115-221`).
  - KEEP `canonical-number` (`:70`), `fnv-1a-32` (`:432`), `canonical-data-edn` (`:506`) and `data-hash` (`:572`). The install ledger uses them (`ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/install.cljc:83-106`).

title: Align Spec 001 flow and HTTP registration ownership with the registrar
description:
Audit of PR #11468 at b3ebeb704455d27ea1c878edb61a266eb6e2ce25: the edited Spec 009 row correctly says reg-flow/clear-flow and reg-http-interceptor/clear-http-interceptor read no frame, but spec/001-Registration.md:206 still gives the opposite normative authoring contract. Its Production elision contract says reg-flow writes a per-frame store with an intentionally empty :flow registrar slot, reg-http-interceptor writes a per-frame middleware store, neither can be selected into an image, and their target is the explicit or ambient frame.

Concrete evidence: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc:85-87 declares :http-interceptor; reg-http-interceptor at 168-185 rejects a :frame key and writes rf.registrar/register!, clear-http-interceptor at 193-198 unregisters that kind, and capture-chain at 245-257 resolves the frame-config :http-interceptors vector through that frame's image/live view. The flows registry is byte-identical to the fully reviewed #11462 owner (blob 4aede58277b7cce0905b4b47278fdb2fa6b87752): reg-flow is a top-level :flow registrar registration, activated by a frame's :flows, not a per-frame definition store.

A programmer or AI following Spec 001 would supply frame targeting that is rejected or conclude these definitions cannot participate in images, contrary to the shipped API. This is registration ownership and image selection, not a wording preference.

Small correction: replace the obsolete frame-owned exception in this paragraph with the ordinary registrar/provenance rules for :flow and :http-interceptor and distinguish top-level definition registration from frame activation through :flows/:http-interceptors. Check the nearby Spec 001 prose for the same now-false exception; no runtime/API change is needed. Validate the edited prose/anchors with the documented docs gates and manual reading.

Complete source beads rf2-4q4lf, rf2-ay9ma, and existing follow-up rf2-hwwmj were read. rf2-hwwmj already records this remaining work and is in progress; it is left untouched. This new open audit bead preserves a separately trackable finding as requested, discovered from the closed rf2-4q4lf review. No application source was changed and no shadow-cljs run was entered.

title: Restore committed flow output claims when a replacement derive throws
description:
Audit of merged PR #11462 (63f3060f00e900e1b450691d1388ada255e6c433), following rf2-s3o2d.

A failed replacement flow can unclassify its still-committed sensitive output. In flows.cljc/run-flows-on-db, the replacement's output claims are installed before evaluate-flow calls its derive. If derive throws, app-db and the memo remain at the old successful event, but the old definition's claims have already been replaced. The failure path does not put them back. registry.cljc/reset-frame-last-inputs-to! (70 onward) also conditions claim restoration on changed memo definition identity, which cannot detect this case: the pass threw before publishing its new memo.

Concrete JVM reproduction on an exact git-archive snapshot of the merged core, flows and epoch sources, using their actual public APIs, adapter, router and wire elider; no stubs or application edits. Register a flow writing :old with :sensitive [[]], seed a frame running it, and confirm elide-wire-value redacts the output. Re-register the flow with either (a) a moved :output-path [:new] and the same mark, or (b) the same output path without the mark, and a derive that throws. Dispatch an otherwise unchanged event. In both cases the event aborts and app-db is unchanged, yet elide-wire-value on the still-committed :old returns the raw AUDIT-ONLY-CLASSIFICATION-SENTINEL instead of :rf/redacted.

Evidence: ai/pr-audit/pr-audit-sol-oct11-11462-failed-claims-2.clj and its .log/.exit. Two tests / six assertions: the initial-redaction and unchanged-db controls pass; both post-abort redaction assertions fail, zero errors, exit 1. No shadow-cljs lane was used. The new schema-rejection-keeps-flow-claims-on-the-committed-output test covers rejection after a successful pass; it does not cover a derive throwing before the memo advances.

Small correction: roll back flow-owned output claims on every aborted pass with the pending-db rollback, independently of whether the memo advanced. Reassert the prior committed rows' claims before propagating a failed pass, preserving other owners' claims. Keep the existing memo and owner model.

Acceptance: a sensitive committed output remains redacted after both a moved-output replacement derive and a declassifying replacement derive throw; app-db stays unchanged. Pin these beside the successful-pass/schema-rejection regression.

Fix (implementation/flows only). run-flows-on-db now catches a failed pass, hands back the output claims of every prior memo row whose definition the pass replaced or dropped, and rethrows. The hand-back is a new registry fn, restore-output-claims! [frame-id prior current]. reset-frame-last-inputs-to! (the router's commit-boundary restore) uses the same fn, so the hand-back now happens whether or not the memo advanced. Claims sit under the flow's own owner identity, so other owners' claims are untouched. The memo and owner model are unchanged.

Regression: flows_rollback_dirty_check_test.clj, next to the flows rollback tests. The core schema-rejection-keeps-flow-claims-on-the-committed-output test stays where it is, because implementation/core is outside this fence.

title: Summarize malformed SSR heads instead of copying their app content
description:
PR #11455 (087f52b0f9a26a4f1f909b99d54c682dbea57f7b) correctly replaces the whole SSR hiccup element with a shape summary, but the malformed-head branch still copies arbitrary app content through :head and the human reason/message.

In implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc, reject-invalid-hiccup-head! takes (rf.error/safe-form (first element)), prints that value with pr-str, and puts it verbatim in :extra :head. safe-form is identity on the JVM and only handles cycles on CLJS. The real emitter routes string, map and vector heads to this branch, so an ordinary malformed rendered vector such as [{:token secret} [:p "child"]] discloses secret in ex-message, :reason and :head before any server-log/error-sink projection. A bad string head does the same. Bounding :element therefore does not bound or remove the private data from the diagnostic.

Owning contract: spec/015-Data-Classification.md:468-474 requires framework render diagnostics to carry a content-free shape summary, explicitly warns against treating an arbitrary app-supplied head as structural, and permits a trusted structural identifier only in a slot the site actually controls. A rejected string/collection head is the offending value, not such an identifier.

Focused probe (exit 0) evaluated the actual merged rejection/shape helpers with the complete merged re-frame.error namespace unchanged, without stubs. Nil-head control and private child content remained clean; a sentinel in each string/map/vector head appeared in both the message and serialized ex-data, while :element was already {:type :vector :count 2}. Evidence: ai/pr-audit/pr-audit-sol-oct11-11455-head-1.clj, .log and .exit. The new ssr_emit_test child-sentinel test uses nil for its malformed head and therefore misses this case. No shadow-cljs lane was entered.

Small correction: on the malformed-head arm, describe the head with diag-value-summary in both the message and ex-data instead of retaining/printing the raw value. Keep useful error id, recovery and shape/count context; known reserved framework head identifiers can retain their separate trusted treatment. Add string/collection-head sentinel regressions asserting neither message nor serialized ex-data contains the sentinel, while the invalid-hiccup-head error and cycle-safe diagnostics remain usable.

title: Conventions says process-level slots have nothing to do with the per-frame registries; registrations live in one process-global store
description: Found by the rf2-pxv4m worker (PR #11477). spec/Conventions.md ~1366 (HOT ZONE) says process-level state mutation outside the registrar touches "implementation-defined slots that have nothing to do with the per-frame registries". title: Spec 002, API and 010 prose still describe flow vacations as a pending queue in the memo (follow-up to rf2-26ehf)
description:
## Defect

Four spec lines still describe flow output-path vacations as a pending queue held in the frame's flow memo. rf2-26ehf (#11497) fixed the same model in router.cljc and spec/013-Flows.md, but these sites were outside its fence.

In the code, a vacation is applied in place to the pending db during the flow pass (vacate-path-in-db in implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc, called from flows.cljc). Nothing queues a vacation, and the memo holds only its evaluation rows.

Stale sites at trunk after #11497:
- spec/002-Frames.md:862: flows release the destroyed frame's flow evaluation memo, "its dirty-check rows together with its pending path vacations".
- spec/002-Frames.md:864: "the dirty-check rows in lockstep with the pending path vacations".
- spec/API.md:900: "its dirty-check rows and pending path vacations".
- spec/010-Schemas.md:195 (row 4): "the restore of transient flow bookkeeping (`last-inputs` / abandoned-path vacations, ...)".

## Change

Restate each site to match the model #11497 used in spec/013-Flows.md:140 and :299. Destroy drops "every memo row it holds". On a rejection, the bookkeeping is "the frame's evaluation memo rows", restored, and the vacations leave with the discarded candidate. Prose only.

## Acceptance

`git grep -n -i -E 'queued vacation|vacation drain|pending path vacation|abandoned-path vacation'` over spec/, implementation/, docs/ and tools/ finds nothing. mkdocs build --strict, check_doc_slugs.py and the api-manifest lint job stay green.

title: Frame-config typo warnings are invisible without a trace listener
description:
Observed while auditing merged PR #11508 at 20efdfae9a117b38bfa7e1da31be57eeaf586eb0. The new frame-key classifier emits the right structured event, but the ordinary development case without Xray, Story or a trace listener still silently ignores a typo.

Behavior: in a dev runtime with no :trace listener, (rf/make-frame {:id :app/example :fx-overides {}}) creates the frame and leaves the misspelled override unused, with no console/JVM warning. With a listener, :rf.warning/unknown-frame-config-key is delivered. The source Bead requested the posture of reg_meta.cljc's unknown-registration-key warning, which also has an unobserved-warning print.

Evidence at the merge: frame.cljc warn-unknown-config-keys! calls rf.trace/emit! and has no other reporting path. trace/tooling.cljc drive-fanout! calls print-unobserved-warning! for an empty listener snapshot (lines 969-973), but that function prints only ids in unobserved-warning-ops (lines 912-943). The set contains :rf.warning/unknown-registration-key and omits :rf.warning/unknown-frame-config-key, so the new warning falls through without printing. Conventions No silent swallow (lines 1193-1195) records the registration-key behavior and requires a warning's fallback set entry and per-surface row to be changed together. The complete rf2-skqan record explicitly confirms the new warning is trace-only and leaves this as an outside-fence follow-up; that source is now closed. The added frame_config_keys_test installs a listener, so its green does not cover this case.

Small correction: add the new id to the existing unobserved-warning-ops set and a frame-config row to Conventions in the same change. Reuse the existing fallback rather than adding a second logger. Add a focused no-listener check that a misspelled key prints once, and a listener-present control that receives the structured warning without a duplicate print; namespaced/known keys and production remain quiet.

Validation: followed the actual emitter, fan-out and print gate, and accepted the author's explicit report of this remaining limitation and the reported listener-based red/green/production-elision tests. No new local test or shadow-cljs run is claimed.
