title: Use change-principal in the Resources tutorial's real sign-in handler
description:
Merged-PR audit #11536, merge f756175334ff8b001cd2b3c2639289f393d5bc29.

The new Spec 016 Changing principal contract applies to login as well as logout and restore: the event clears the departing scopes before replanning, because navigation alone does not clear their cache entries or any app/machine holds. RealWorld's session-established handler implements this. The copyable Resources tutorial still omits it: docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md:222-239, :auth.login-form/submit-success, commits the new user/token and only persists and navigates; Part 4 at docs/resources/tutorial/04-scopes-and-guards.md:95 explicitly says signing in needs nothing extra. Its interactive demo at lines 170-176 now correctly dispatches change-principal, so that demo exercises a stronger sign-in path than the reader has been taught to build.

Following the tutorial leaves the departing viewer's entries cached on sign-in/account replacement. Any non-route owner keeps its hold, so focus/reconnect/poll/invalidation can still refetch that old key after credentials change; the new ensure-load guard only drops an automatic refetch once its entry is absent. The shared principal-change event is what removes the entry, and the real tutorial login never invokes it.

Small correction: in Part 4, extend the inherited :auth.login-form/submit-success handler to resolve the old viewer scope from its pre-transition coeffect db and dispatch [:rf.resource/change-principal {:from [old-viewer] :cause :login}] before the login navigation. Replace the signing-in-needs-nothing paragraph; when Part 5 introduces the session scope, include that departing scope too. Keep the generation guard and classified token payload. The existing rf2-3moeo docs sweep is a suitable owner for this specifically named missed tutorial site.

Evidence: inspected the complete source Bead and rf2-3moeo including their notes and closure/fence state, the actual tutorial handler and caller chain, the updated demo, RealWorld's corrected login handler, and the ensure-load/no-entry guard. The reported four-trigger regressions establish why clearing the departed entry matters; no extra build was needed for this missing event in the documented recipe.

title: Machines: :spawn takes a managed effect directly, retiring one-request child machines and the HTTP machine wrapper
description:
## Problem

Measured at trunk 3959d2a5bf.

`:rf.http/managed` registers as a child machine purely so that a state can spawn it (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/machine_wrapper.cljc`; `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` § Machine-shape wrapper). The boot pattern spawns its own four-state child machine, `:boot/loader`, to perform one request (`examples/patterns/boot/boot.cljs`). So "this state makes a request and moves on when it answers" costs a child machine definition or a wrapper machine.

A replacement must be re-frame-native. `spec/CP-5-MachineGuide.md` rejects XState's actor-logic creators (`fromPromise` and the rest).

## Change

`:spawn` accepts a managed effect directly, for example `{:spawn {:fx [:rf.http/managed {…}]}}`. Settle the spelling.

- The managed effect's uniform reply envelope is the completion, which `:on-done` (and the failure route) reads exactly as they read a child machine's.
- Leaving the state aborts the effect through the abort it already has. No second cancellation protocol.
- Stale replies are suppressed through the existing work-id correlation.
- Delete the HTTP machine wrapper only if no caller remains.

**The bar.** Less authoring than the child-machine form, and no second cancellation protocol. If the prototype misses either, close this bead with the comparison recorded.

rf2-29hkz keeps every statechart feature, so child machines stay; this adds a shorter form for the one-request case.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/005-StateMachines.md`, the `:spawn` contract. **Hot zone.**
- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` § Machine-shape wrapper, and `spec/Managed-Effects.md` if completion-as-spawn is stated there.
- `spec/CP-5-MachineGuide.md`, the actor-logic row.
- The boot pattern and the machine guides.

## Acceptance

- The boot loader is rewritten with the new form, and it is shorter.
- Exiting the state mid-request aborts the request, and a late reply is suppressed.
- Xray's reply-envelope panel still classifies the rows.
- Machines and HTTP suites, and `npm run test:cljs`, green.

## Sequencing

Hot zone: `spec/005-StateMachines.md`. Shares it with the "give `:data` to the user" machines bead (linked as related); sequence them.

Additive. Effort M.
notes:
== WORKER (machines-data-spawn), 2026-10-19 AUSEST: BAR MISSED. No ccm5v code changed. PR #11538 carries rf2-rq6s6 only.

Measured at tip 3c2550942e plus PR #11538.

The bar was "less authoring than the child-machine form, and no second cancellation protocol". The fx form misses both halves, because the child-machine form already exists for the one-request case: the `:rf.http/managed` machine wrapper (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/machine_wrapper.cljc). It is a reg-machine the HTTP artefact registers, so the author writes no child definition.

Authoring, for the boot config fetch:
- today's wrapper form: `{:spawn {:machine-id :rf.http/managed :data {:request {:method :get :url "/api/config.json"} :decode :json} :on-done <fold> :on-error <transition>}}`
- the proposed fx form: `{:spawn {:fx [:rf.http/managed {:request {:method :get :url "/api/config.json"} :decode :json}] :on-done <fold> :on-error <transition>}}`
The difference is `:machine-id :rf.http/managed :data X` against `:fx [:rf.http/managed X]`: the same three tokens, rearranged. The wrapper also composes unchanged under `:spawn-all`, as a child spec's `:machine-id`, which the fx form would have to add separately.

Cancellation:
- The wrapper's request belongs to its own actor. Exiting the state destroys the child, and the actor-destroy contract aborts the request (Spec 014 §Abort on actor destroy). A late completion is dropped by the spawn attempt gate (`spawn-carrier-stale-reason`). Both mechanisms already exist.
- An fx-form request has no actor of its own: the parent issues it. So exiting the state cannot reach it through actor teardown. The engine would have to emit `[:rf.http/managed-abort <request-id>]` per exit, mint a request id per spawn attempt, and translate the reply envelope into the spawn done/error carriers. That is a second cancellation path, and the bead names exactly that as the failing condition.

What the bead's acceptance actually wanted, a shorter boot loader, is available today with no engine change. Point the boot pattern's `:spawn` and `:spawn-all` children at `:machine-id :rf.http/managed` and delete the hand-written `:boot/loader`. I left the example as it is, for two reasons: the packet said to change no ccm5v code when the bar is missed, and Pattern-Boot and the boot skill use `:boot/loader` to teach a hand-written child that "composes unchanged under both spawn forms". Whether the pattern should stop teaching that is Mike's call.

Recommended close reason: not worth doing under the posture. `:spawn {:machine-id :rf.http/managed :data …}` already is the one-request form; an fx-valued `:spawn` saves no authoring and needs a second, exit-time cancellation path.
close_reason:
Bar missed, so no code changed (the prototype was evaluated in PR #11538). The bar was "less authoring than the child-machine form, and no second cancellation protocol", and an fx-form :spawn misses both halves.

- Authoring: the one-request child form already ships. The :rf.http/managed machine wrapper is a reg-machine the HTTP artefact registers, so {:spawn {:machine-id :rf.http/managed :data X …}} against {:spawn {:fx [:rf.http/managed X] …}} is the same three tokens rearranged. It also composes under :spawn-all.
- Cancellation: the wrapper's request belongs to its own actor. Exiting the state destroys the actor, the actor-destroy contract aborts the request (Spec 014 §Abort on actor destroy), and the spawn attempt gate drops a late completion. An fx-form request would have no actor of its own, so it would need per-attempt request ids, an abort on every exit, and envelope translation into the spawn carriers. That is the second cancellation path the bead rules out.

Mayor ruling (2026-10-19, under the posture) on the worker's follow-up question: Pattern-Boot and the boot skill KEEP the hand-written :boot/loader child. It teaches a child that composes unchanged under both spawn forms. :machine-id :rf.http/managed is already available and documented in Spec 014 for anyone who wants the shorter one-request form, so no change is made.

title: A machine's {:rf/sub} recorded fact is projected by the sub's classification on :rf.cofx/generated and in the epoch record, as on :rf.sub/run
description:
Found by the rf2-49k1t worker (PR #11581, merged as f833564d5d). A machine's {:rf/sub query-v :as fact-id} recordable fact has no reg-cofx registration, so `classification-when :cofx` returns nil and nothing redacts it. Its value therefore goes UNPROJECTED onto the dev-only :rf.cofx/generated trace (emitted by deliver-sub-source since #11581) and into the epoch record's :rf.cofx replay token, whereas the SAME value on :rf.sub/run passes through project-sub-tags. A sub fact supplied on a replayed token was already unprojected before #11581.

So a sensitive sub value (classified via the sub, Spec 015) can reach traces and epoch records, and from there off-box tools, unredacted, through the machine fact path only.

Fix direction: project a sub fact by the sub's own classification, the same projection :rf.sub/run uses (project-sub-tags), wherever the fact's value leaves the in-flight token: the :rf.cofx/generated emission and the record token capture folds. Keep the in-flight token raw (the handler needs the real value) and keep strict replay working from a redacted record: decide and state what replay does with a redacted sub fact (a redacted value cannot be re-presented verbatim; the honest options are re-evaluating the sub on replay, or refusing strict replay of that fact with a named error). Pick the simpler correct one and say why.

Acceptance: a sub classified sensitive, used as a machine fact, shows :rf/redacted on :rf.cofx/generated and in the epoch record's :rf.cofx; a non-sensitive sub fact is unchanged and the #11581 real-record strict-replay pin stays green. Tests red first. Gates: core, epoch and machines JVM suites, test-jvm-implementation, npm run test:cljs.

That is the public egress form of a sub's value, defined as the :rf.sub/value a :sub/run trace of the same query carries once projected (project-sub-tags). title: Xray: the schema-source link resolves :resource-params and :mutation-params violations (violation-registration-kind)
description:
Found by the rf2-6x2ts worker (PR #11599, merged as 197dd0dd3f). That PR gave the resource and mutation params path's malformed-schema trace the :where values :resource-params and :mutation-params (Spec 009 :rf.error/malformed-schema row; Spec-Schemas MalformedSchemaTags). Xray's violation-registration-kind in tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs maps a violation's :where to the registration kind its schema-source link resolves; it has no arm for the two new values, so such a row renders its schema source as plain text rather than a click-to-source link (nothing breaks).

Fix: map :resource-params to :resource and :mutation-params to :mutation in violation-registration-kind, matching how its other arms resolve; check at tip that rf/handler-meta {:kind :resource :id <id>} (and :mutation) returns the coordinate the link needs. Add one assertion per family in the epoch view test namespace.

Acceptance: a resource-params and a mutation-params violation row each render the schema-source link. Gate: npm run test:cljs (the Xray epoch view namespace).

== FENCE (mayor): QUEUED. CLEARS WHEN the xray-cofx-path PR (rf2-zirlu, #11597) has merged; that PR edits Xray's epoch view.cljs.
notes:
== FENCE CLEARED + DISPATCH (mayor) 2026-10-21 14:29:43 AUSEST: PR #11597 (rf2-zirlu) merged as 54cf128107. Dispatched to worktree C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/xray-params-link (branch worker/xray-params-link) off origin/main. Reachability of a malformed-schema violation row is checked first; unreachable means a measurement, not a new path.
== WORKER VERDICT (xray-params-link) 2026-10-21 14:34:33 AUSEST: PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD. No change, no PR. Measured at tip 54cf128107.

The `:resource-params` / `:mutation-params` arms would be dead code, because Xray never builds a violation row carrying either `:where`:

1. The params path emits only `:rf.error/malformed-schema`. `re-frame.resources.params/validate+canonicalize` calls the `:schemas/check!` seam with `:tags-only? true`, so the seam emits nothing itself. On a malformed schema the pipeline emits `:rf.error/malformed-schema` (tags `:where :resource-params` / `:mutation-params`) and then throws the domain error. On an ordinary failure it only throws `:rf.error/resource-invalid-params` / `:rf.error/mutation-invalid-params`, with no `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` trace. Spec 009's `:rf.error/resource-invalid-params` and `:rf.error/mutation-invalid-params` rows say the same thing.

2. Xray's violation rows come only from `projection/schema-violation-rows`. It harvests the closed set `schema-violation-ops` = `#{:rf.error/schema-validation-failure :rf.schema/violation}`, which does not include `:rf.error/malformed-schema`. A malformed-schema trace instead lands in `unclassified-error-rows`, an error card that never reaches `violation-block` / `violation-schema-coord`, so `violation-registration-kind` is never consulted for it.

3. JVM measurement (projection.cljc evaluated on the tools/xray base classpath, exit 0):
   - `schema-violation-rows` on a `:rf.error/malformed-schema` event with `:where :resource-params` returns 0 rows;
   - the same with `:where :mutation-params` returns 0 rows;
   - CONTROL: the same event shape under `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` returns 1 row;
   - `unclassified-error-rows` on the two malformed events returns 2 rows.

Third premise (moot): the resource and mutation registrars merge source coords (`rf.source-coords/merge-coords` in registry.cljc and mutation_registry.cljc), so `handler-meta {:kind :resource|:mutation}` would carry a coord if a row ever reached the link.

This matches rf2-zirlu (#11597), which removed the unreachable `:cofx` schema-violation path on the same grounds. If Xray ever turns malformed-schema traces into violation rows, that work adds these two arms along with it.
close_reason: Premise does not hold; no change, no PR. Measured at tip 54cf128107: violation-registration-kind exists (tools/xray .../panels/epoch/view.cljs:5485) with no :resource-params / :mutation-params arm, but no violation row is ever built for those values. re-frame.resources.params/validate+canonicalize calls :schemas/check! with :tags-only? true (the seam emits nothing); on a malformed schema it emits only :rf.error/malformed-schema, then throws the domain error; on an ordinary failure it only throws :rf.error/resource-invalid-params / :rf.error/mutation-invalid-params, with no :rf.error/schema-validation-failure trace (Spec 009's two rows agree). Xray builds violation rows only in projection/schema-violation-rows, which reads schema-violation-ops = #{:rf.error/schema-validation-failure :rf.schema/violation}; a malformed-schema trace lands in unclassified-error-rows (an error card) and never reaches violation-block or violation-schema-coord, so the arms would be dead code. JVM measurement (projection.cljc on the tools/xray base classpath, exit 0): schema-violation-rows on a :rf.error/malformed-schema event with :where :resource-params -> 0 rows, with :where :mutation-params -> 0 rows; control, the same shape under :rf.error/schema-validation-failure -> 1 row; unclassified-error-rows on the two malformed events -> 2 rows. handler-meta {:kind :resource|:mutation} would carry a coordinate (moot). Same reasoning as rf2-zirlu (#11597), which removed the unreachable :cofx path.

title: Resources: delete the single-valued :transport key and the prev-page params while load-prev is deferred
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 deleting options nothing can use:
- the `:transport` registration key, on both `reg-resource` (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc`) and `reg-mutation` (`mutation_registry.cljc`). Its only legal value is the default, now that HTTP is a hard dependency;
- `:prev-page-param` and `:has-prev-page?`, while `load-prev` stays deferred (Spec 016).

Route `:after`, the `:invalidate-timing` variants, `:refetch-populated?`, `:cross-scope?` and `:on-conflict :force` stay. Do not touch them.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e.

**`:transport`:**
- It is a declared resource key (`registry.cljc:34`).
- Every read site falls back to the one built-in: `(or (:transport spec) default-transport)` at `events.cljc:228`, `:545` and `:665`, and `tooling.cljc:121`. `default-transport` is `:rf.http/managed` (`transport.cljc:14-17`).
- `assert-managed-transport!` (`transport.cljc:19-34`) throws `:rf.error/resource-unknown-transport` for any other value at the first load (`events.cljc:413`, `:574`, `:689`). So the key can only restate the default or break the resource.
- `reg-mutation` accepts the same key with the same single value (`mutation_registry.cljc:31`, `:73`; `mutation_events.cljc:878`, `:901`).
- `:rf.resource/registered` copies it as a tag (`registry.cljc:394`).
- Xray's registry row reads it with the same fallback (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/resources_helpers.cljc:511`).

**`:prev-page-param`:**
- It is a declared infinite key (`registry.cljc:37`), checked as a fn (`:109-120`).
- It is derived on every page load (`state.cljc:641-646`, `:696`, `:740`; `events.cljc:1741`).
- It feeds `:rf.resource/has-prev-page?` (`subs.cljc:258-262`, `:346-348`) and `:has-prev-page?` in `:rf.resource/infinite-state` (`subs.cljc:300`, `:310`).
- No event consumes it: `:rf.resource/load-prev` is deferred (`spec/016-Resources.md:1638`, `:2032`).
- `skills/`, `tools/` and `examples/` use neither name.

## Change

**`:transport`:**
- Drop it from `resource-metadata-keys` and `mutation-metadata-keys`. A resource or mutation that still passes it gets the existing `:rf.warning/unknown-registration-key` and registers as before.
- Read sites, resource and mutation alike, use `managed-http-transport` directly. `default-transport`, `assert-managed-transport!` and its call sites go, and `:rf.error/resource-unknown-transport` is retired (reserved, never recycled).
- `reg-mutation`'s missing-`:request` message (`mutation_registry.cljc` around `:73`) stops naming a `:transport` value.
- `:rf.resource/registered` drops its `:transport` tag, and Xray's `request-summary` names `:rf.http/managed`.
- The derivation `:authority` map keeps `:transport :rf.http/managed`, because it describes the remote (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3230-3236`).

**Prev page:**
- Delete `:prev-page-param` from the keys and its check, the entry's `:prev-page-param` slot and `prev-param-for`, and the `:prev-page-param-fn` argument.
- Delete the `:rf.resource/has-prev-page?` sub and the `:has-prev-page?` key.
- `load-prev` stays deferred. When it is built, it brings its param and sub back with it.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/016-Resources.md`:
  - **`:transport`:**
    - the example (`:833`) and the optional keys (`:855`);
    - §Transport (`:1181-1187`): one transport, with no registration key;
    - the error row (`:1846`, deleted) and the resolved decision (`:2003`).
  - **Prev page:**
    - the example (`:1536-1544`);
    - the infinite key list (`:1581`);
    - the entry shape (`:1599`) and the page-success rule (`:1629`);
    - R7 (`:1638`, `:2032`): next-only, with the prepend event and its param deferred together;
    - the subs (`:1655`, `:1671`).
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3134` (`InfiniteResourceArgs`) and the `Authority` comment (`:3230-3236`). **Hot zone.**
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2007`: the `:rf.error/resource-unknown-transport` row is retired. **Hot zone.**
- `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md`:
  - `:transport`: `:88`, `:115`, `:814`;
  - prev page: `:121`, `:730`, `:734`, `:742`, `:756`.
- `docs/resources/errors-and-warnings.md:34` (the retired error).
- `examples/capabilities/resources/infinite_feed/README.md:138` already says `load-prev` is deferred. Leave it, and leave `docs/EP` as history.

## Acceptance

- A `reg-resource` carrying `:transport` or `:prev-page-param`, and a `reg-mutation` carrying `:transport`, warn `:rf.warning/unknown-registration-key` and still register.
- `git grep -n -E "default-transport|assert-managed-transport!|resource-unknown-transport" -- implementation tools` returns nothing.
- `:rf.resource/has-prev-page?` is not a registered sub, and `:rf.resource/infinite-state` has no `:has-prev-page?`.
- Tests updated:
  - `resources_registration_keys_cljs_test.cljc:36`, `:48` (drop both keys from `every-resource-key`);
  - `resources_infinite_registration_cljs_test.cljc:50-51` (delete the non-fn `:prev-page-param` row);
  - `resources_infinite_subs_cljs_test.cljc:63`, `:101`, `:111`, `:155`;
  - `resources_infinite_state_cljs_test.cljc:45`;
  - `resources_infinite_ssr_restore_cljs_test.cljc:46`, `:68`, `:96`;
  - `resources_infinite_load_more_cljs_test.cljc:105`;
  - every test that pins a mutation's `:transport` or `:rf.error/resource-unknown-transport` (find them with `git grep`).
- `git grep -n -E "prev-page-param|has-prev-page" -- implementation tools spec docs ':!spec/findings' ':!docs/EP'` returns only the deferred `load-prev` prose.
- Green: the JVM resources suite, `npm run test:cljs`, the Xray suite, `mkdocs build --strict` and `check_doc_slugs.py`.

## Sequencing

Do this before the work-ledger fold bead, because both edit `registry.cljc`, `events.cljc` and Spec 016. It touches two hot zones (Spec-Schemas, 009).
close_reason: Merged as PR #11602 (rebase, f896f8c1a8). :transport leaves reg-resource and reg-mutation key sets (a registration still carrying it warns :rf.warning/unknown-registration-key and registers); every read site uses managed-http-transport directly; default-transport and assert-managed-transport! deleted; :rf.error/resource-unknown-transport retired (Spec 009 and 016 rows and its ResourceUnknownTransportTags schema deleted; Spec 016 §Transport records it reserved, never recycled); :rf.resource/registered drops the :transport tag and Xray's request summary names :rf.http/managed; the derivation :authority map keeps :transport :rf.http/managed. Prev page: the key, its check, the entry slot, prev-param-for, :prev-page-param-fn, the :rf.resource/has-prev-page? sub and :has-prev-page? deleted; load-prev stays deferred. Premise corrections: the core catalogue conformance ledger pins an exact paired-*Tags count, moved 86 -> 85 in its own commit as its docstring directs; the acceptance grep also hits the new tests, which name the keys by design; extra sites updated beyond the bead's citations (Spec 016 :7, :849, :1207; docs API :107, :207, :320, :611; two further Spec 009 rows), plus spec/Derivations.md, spec/001-Registration.md, migration/from-re-frame-v1/re-frame-query-to-resources.md, the reg-mutation docstring in core_resources.cljc and a gen.clj comment. title: Spec 006 moves Fresco's commit law to Fresco's spec and the per-port notes to the Implementor Checklist
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21, docs only, two moves out of Spec 006, each leaving pointers behind:
- Fresco's commit law (§The six frozen invariants, §Render-batch finalization and §The atomic shell) moves to Fresco's contract home, `implementation/fresco/spec/`.
- The per-port material for the JS cross-compile ports moves to `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md` or an appendix.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e.

`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` is 2,110 lines.

**The commit law is 362 of them:**
- §The six frozen invariants (`:1082-1169`);
- §Render-batch finalization (`:1170-1301`), which includes §The second closer (`:1237`);
- §The atomic shell (`:1302-1442`), with seven H3s.

They state the law "a re-frame-native view substrate" must satisfy (`:1084-1085`, `:1304`). The invariants are cited by ordinal (`:1086-1087`), so their numbering is part of the contract. Fresco's home says root `spec/` takes no product prose and that its own tree governs (`implementation/fresco/spec/README.md`). It holds `authoring-contract.md`, `invariants.md`, `complaints.md` and `server-policy.md`.

**Inbound links to the moved anchors.** The census covered every tracked file outside `.beads/`. As a control, `#adapter-disposal-lifecycle` finds 4 links in 3 files.

- `#render-batch-finalization--the-host-checkpoint-boundary`:
  - `spec/002-Frames.md:1889` and `:1958`;
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2348`;
  - `spec/Runtime-Architecture.md:165`;
  - 006 itself at `:1145` and `:1162`.
- `#the-second-closer-…`: only inside the moved text (`:1178`, `:1215`).
- `#the-atomic-shell` and its seven H3s: none outside 006. The only link inside 006 is `:1085`.

**Prose citations without a link:**
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:3758` cites "Spec 006 §Render-batch finalization" for core's open-drain guard, `:rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch`.
- `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/generation.cljs:2` cites "Spec 006 invariant 5".
- These cite bare ordinals: `frame.cljc:1815`, `subs.cljc:2495` and `:2603`, `collector.cljs:1127`, and two Fresco tests (`reincarnation_cells_cljs_test.cljs:210`, `reincarnation_routing_cljs_test.cljs:146`).

**Three obligations in the moved text are core's, not Fresco's:**
- the open-drain guard (`frame.cljc:3756-3770`);
- the frame install epoch read as evidence (`frame.cljc:1808-1818`);
- the commit-side ref-count attach that does not re-resolve context (`subs.cljc:2488-2497`, "the law is CORE's").

**Per-port material.** The realisations for TS-React and the other cross-compile ports sit at:
- `:180-181`, `:210` and `:345-346`, under each contract function;
- `:453`, the compliance bullet;
- `:1080`, the per-host note;
- `:1718-1730`, the port context table and its discretion paragraph.

Nothing links to `#frame-propagation-across-react-binding-ports` or `#per-host-implementation-notes`.

Normative scope lines are not per-port material, and stay:
- `:11` (the ports are scoped per 000);
- `:534` (every port honours source-coord annotation);
- the packaging pattern at `:2012` and `:2052`.

## Change

1. **Create `implementation/fresco/spec/commit-law.md`** with the three sections.
   - State them as Fresco's commit law.
   - Keep invariants 1-6 numbered as they are.
   - Rewrite links back into root `spec/` as `../../../spec/…` paths.
2. **Leave a pointer in 006 for each section.**
   - Each of the three H2 headings stays, with one short paragraph pointing at the new page. Every inbound anchor above keeps resolving, so `002`, `009`, `Runtime-Architecture` and EP-0032 need no edit.
   - The pointer keeps the sentences that state core's three obligations.
3. **Move the per-port passages listed above** into one section of `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md`, beside F3 Reactive substrate (`:172`). Leave a one-line pointer at each site.
4. **Re-point `generation.cljs:2`** to the new page. Bare ordinals stay correct because the numbering is unchanged.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`. **Hot zone.**
- `implementation/fresco/spec/README.md`: the Files list and the gates table.
- `implementation/fresco/spec/authoring-contract.md:8-16`: the sibling-files sentence.
- `spec/Ownership.md:69`: Fresco's operative-contract row gains the new page.
- `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md`.
- Leave design history as it is (`docs/EP/`, `docs/design/fresco/`, `bench/fresco/`).

## Acceptance

title: Story MCP run-variant ships epoch narrative app-db values (and opt-in trace events) raw off-box; route them through the off-box epoch projector
description:
Found by the rf2-h2fjb worker (PR #11643, merged afbcecdd64). Since the epoch fold (#11642) every dev run records epochs, so Story MCP's run-variant narrative now carries epoch data to an AI host by default:
- each beat's :db-before / :db-after ship app-db values RAW, including slots declared :sensitive?. Measured: the :checks privacy test's sensitive record crosses the wire once epochs are on, which is why that one test still turns epochs off;
- with the new :include-trace-events true opt-in, beats ship raw :trace-events.
The worker reads this as EP-0025's documented fail-open for re-keyed positions, which never showed before because the JVM Story MCP server recorded no epochs.

The pair MCP already sends the same data through re-frame.core/project-egress's epoch projector under :rf.egress/off-box-tool (declared-sensitive slots redact, event and fx args redact, the trace-events projection applies). Story MCP is the same kind of off-box AI surface (Tool-Pair §Direct-read privacy posture; Security.md).

Change: route run-variant's narrative epoch data (the db values and the opt-in trace events) through the same off-box projector the pair MCP uses, with the same trusted-local opt-in if Story MCP has one, so the allow-list in rf2-rq8ou covers it automatically when that lands. Then let the :checks privacy test run with epochs on.

PREMISES ARE CLAIMS: read EP-0025 first. If it deliberately rules that Story MCP narratives ship raw (not merely a known gap), stop and write the options on this bead for Mike.

Acceptance: a declared-sensitive app-db slot reads :rf/redacted in a default run-variant narrative; the :checks privacy test passes with epochs ON; :include-trace-events output crosses the projector; story-mcp, mcp-base and mcp-conformance Story suites green.

EP-0025 check: it does NOT rule that Story MCP narratives ship raw. Its consumer list reads "re-frame2-pair-mcp + story-mcp — every read (app-db, subs, traces, epochs) is projected before it reaches the AI client". Its fail-open covers a FORGOTTEN classification, not an unprojected epoch. So this was a gap, not a ruling, and no options memo was needed.

- Trusted-local opt-in kept: --allow-sensitive-reads plus :include-sensitive maps through mcp-tool-profile to :rf.egress/local-raw. That lifts the app-db axes inside the projection and never bypasses it.

title: Dolt remote push stalls mid-push: no complete bd dolt push since 2026-10-21 20:50, so the git export is the only off-machine copy of the tracker
description:
Split out of rf2-tipmv by its measurement (research worker, note of 2026-10-22 10:54:47 AUSEST). The Dolt remote (git+https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git) has had NO complete push since 2026-10-21 20:50 AUSEST, so the tracked git export is today the only working off-machine copy of the tracker.

Read-only findings:
- The remote is reachable and authenticates non-interactively (git ls-remote exit 0; refs/dolt/data = 9505c4fe).
- A normal push lands two commits seconds apart; 31 did on 10-21. The 21:17 push landed its first commit (21:17:27) and stalled; its second, built locally at 21:17:34, never reached GitHub. The 21:52 and 22:05 retries each built a small (0.2-0.5 MB) upload locally and stopped, so upload size is not the cause.
- 69 leftover staging refs since 08-11 show pushes that never finished go back to August.
- GitHub's API reports the remote at 807,765 KB, but its current manifest references 1.52 GB of table files.

Next step needs a WRITE to the remote: one traced push, bd dolt push with GIT_TRACE=1 GIT_TRACE_PACKET=1 GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1, timed out, its output to a file. The mayor stopped retrying on 2026-10-21 until Mike looks at the remote, so this is HELD FOR MIKE: either run that push, or authorise a worker to run it and read the trace.

Acceptance: a complete bd dolt push, the remote's refs/dolt/data advanced to the local head, and the cause recorded (and fixed if it is ours, for example clearing stale staging refs).
notes:
== HELD FOR MIKE (mayor), 2026-10-22 10:57:02 AUSEST: needs a write to the Dolt remote (one traced bd dolt push) to diagnose; the mayor does not retry pushes there until Mike says so. Clears on Mike's instruction.
== HELD FOR MIKE — STRUCK (mayor), 2026-10-23 03:01:43 AUSEST: the hold above was the mayor's own caution, not a ruling of Mike's.

Re-tested on a method reread:
- CLAUDE.md § Session Completion already sanctions `bd dolt push`.
- One traced push with a timeout is a diagnosis, not a blind retry.
- The worst case, another stall, leaves one more staging ref beside the 69 already there.

Dispatched to a research worker, who is authorised to run ONE traced `bd dolt push` (timeout 30 min) and read the trace. Any DELETION on the remote, for example clearing stale staging refs, stays held for Mike.
== DISPATCHED (mayor), 2026-10-23 03:04:58 AUSEST: zero-edit research worker, no worktree, no branch; authorised for at most two traced, timed-out bd dolt push runs. RE-DISPATCH FENCE: do not put a second worker on this bead until that worker reports.
== TRACED PUSH (research worker), 2026-10-23 03:15:54 AUSEST

PUSH COMPLETED. One traced run: timeout 300 bd dolt push, detached, with GIT_TRACE, GIT_TRACE_PACKET and GIT_TRACE_CURL written to files. It ran 03:10:00-03:13:48 (228 s), exit 0, and printed "Push complete.". GitHub answered "ok refs/dolt/data" twice and "ok refs/heads/__dolt_remote_info__" twice. No second push was needed or run.
- refs/dolt/data before: 9505c4fe (2026-10-21 21:17:27). After: a89c6dd7, whose parent is cbccc082, a parentless root.
- Remote manifest root moved from lmpuuhmu (stale since 10-21 20:50) to rdmnrfpf.

CAUSE: Dolt's git-backed blobstore periodically severs its history, and that push re-uploads the whole database.
- Dolt's go/store/blobstore/git_blobstore.go (module pinned in bd 1.3.1 at dolt 796d07497741) has const maxParentedCommits = 64. Before each manifest commit, Dolt runs git rev-list --count --max-count=65 on the remote tip. At a depth of 64 or more, it runs git commit-tree with NO -p, so the commit is a parentless root, and pushes it with --force-with-lease.
- A root commit shares no ancestry with the remote, so git cannot leave out the objects GitHub already holds. The push therefore sends every table file the manifest references, not the usual few hundred KB.
- Measured in the trace: the remote tip 9505c4fe was at depth 64 exactly, so this run's first commit was a root. pack-objects started at 03:10:16. curl sent 901,154,178 bytes (859 MiB) in one chunked POST, from 03:10:40 to 03:13:21, about 5.6 MB/s. GitHub replied "unpack ok" at 03:13:24. The next commit (parented, depth 1) took 4 s.
- This explains the 10-21 pattern, where the first commit landed and the second never did. The 21:17 session's step 1 was commit #64 and landed. Its step 2 was the first squash. Every retry squashed again, because the remote stayed at depth 64 until a squash landed.
- 66 of the 70 staging commits in the cache (69 old plus this run's) are parentless roots: squash attempts that were killed. Before this run, 65 squash roots had landed on the remote since 08-11, so squashes succeeded while the database was smaller.

PREMISE CORRECTED: the 69 staging refs are LOCAL. They live in the cache repo (.beads/embeddeddolt/rf2/.dolt/git-remote-cache/<hash>/repo.git, as refs/dolt/blobstore/origin/dolt/data/<uuid>), not on GitHub. git ls-remote shows the remote holds only refs/dolt/data, heads/main, heads/__dolt_remote_info__ and HEAD. Nothing needs clearing on the remote. A successful session deletes its own staging ref: this run's was removed, leaving 69. The local leftovers are harmless, and clearing them is optional.

Also ruled out:
- No live bd, dolt or git process named the remote before the push.
- The Codex harness's last audit commit was 10-21 15:22, and its scripts on disk date from September.
- No file over 100 MiB: the largest blob in the tree is 52,428,800 bytes, because Dolt chunks table files.
- Credentials are non-interactive (gh auth git-credential).
- Dolt's post-push git gc --prune=now of the cache took 16 s.
- The store lock queued one worker's bd update from 03:11:49 to about 03:13:48, and then it cleared.

NOT ESTABLISHED: why the 10-21 21:17 attempt, under timeout 900, failed to land the squash in about 878 s. That would mean an upload below about 1 MB/s. The 21:52 and 22:05 retries ran under 300 s, which is marginal. Nothing from that evening survives to settle it.

FOR MIKE:
(1) The next squash is due when the remote reaches depth 64. It is at 2 now, so after about 31 more two-commit push sessions, roughly a day at 10-21's cadence. That push will again upload the whole table set: 859 MiB now, and growing. Under the 300 s guard it fits today with about 70 s to spare at this uplink. A slower link, or about 30% more data, and every retry times out again. maxParentedCommits is a compiled constant with no config knob.
    Options:
    - allow a longer timeout for the one push where the cache's remote tip is at depth 63-64. Check with git --git-dir=<cache repo> rev-list --count FETCH_HEAD after a fetch;
    - shrink the table set (a Dolt gc of the store);
    - raise it upstream with Dolt, or check whether a newer bd/Dolt pushes an orphan commit incrementally.
(2) The 69 local staging refs: optional cleanup, his call.
close_reason:
The push works again, and the cause is measured (research worker, 2026-10-23 03:13 AUSEST).

The push:
- One traced `timeout 300 bd dolt push` completed in 228 s.
- refs/dolt/data moved from 9505c4fe to a89c6dd7. The mayor re-read it with git ls-remote.

The cause:
- Dolt's git-remote code (dolt 796d07497741, under bd 1.3.1) has a compiled-in `maxParentedCommits = 64`.
- Once the remote branch holds 64 commits, Dolt writes the next manifest commit with no parent and force-pushes it.
- That commit shares no history with GitHub's copy, so git cannot skip what GitHub already holds and uploads every table file. Measured: 901,154,178 bytes (859 MiB) at about 5.6 MB/s.

How that produced the stall:
- On 10-21 the 21:17 push's first commit was #64, and it landed.
- Its second commit was the first full upload, and the timeout killed it.
- Each retry, under a shorter timeout, attempted the full upload again.

Not established: why 21:17's 900 s budget was not enough. It would need under 1 MB/s, and no evidence from that evening survives.

The 69 staging refs:
- They are LOCAL, in the cache repo under .beads/embeddeddolt/rf2/.dolt/git-remote-cache/, not on the remote.
- They are harmless, so there is nothing to clear.

The guard is recorded as memory dolt-git-remote-full-upload-every-64-pushes. The next full upload is due in about 31 push sessions. Give that push room (timeout 600, detached, fleet quiet) rather than retrying it under 300 s.

title: Flip re-frame2-pair-mcp epoch tools from whole-record drop to the projected record, keeping :rf.epoch/sensitive? as a label
description:
re-frame2-pair-mcp's history tools stop discarding whole epoch records that carry a sensitivity flag. They ship the record that `project-egress` already produced, with secrets redacted, and keep `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` as a label.

## Ruling

**Decision.** This is the flip to the "redacted skeleton": option B in the decision. Three tools change: `trace-window`, `watch-epochs` and `snapshot :epochs`.
- **Today:** each tool projects each epoch record app-side through `re-frame.core/project-egress` under `:rf.egress/off-box-tool`. Then it DROPS, client-side, any record flagged `:rf.epoch/sensitive? true` or holding a top-level-stamped trace event.
- **After:** the drop goes, and the projected record ships. `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` and the per-event `:sensitive?` stay in the payload as annotations.

The pair server then runs one policy on every epoch path. `dispatch` already ships projected epochs, sensitive or not.

The opt-in is unchanged: the two-key gate `--allow-sensitive-reads` plus `:include-sensitive true`. It still routes THROUGH the projection and widens only the app-db sensitive axis.

**The flag's meaning.** Describe `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` honestly, as "this record contained classified material". It is NOT "this run touched a secret": the rollup fires whenever any declared-sensitive path holds a non-nil value in `:db-before` or `:db-after`.

This is the third of four beads from one ruling.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

**Decisive facts (read in source at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. **The drop blinds the pair for whole sessions.**
   - `sensitive-rollup` is true whenever any declared-sensitive path resolves to a non-nil leaf in `:db-before` or `:db-after` (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc:147-178`).
   - The project's own login example classifies a draft password whose default is `""` (`examples/core/login/model.cljc:450`, `:495-507`), and `(some? "")` is true. So from the first render of the form, every epoch in that frame is flagged and dropped. That includes the submit, the 401 and the machine's move to `:error`.
   - After login, RealWorld holds the JWT at a classified path (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/core.cljs:156`), so every later epoch is dropped too.
2. **One server runs two policies.**
   - The drop is applied at `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljs:161` (`snapshot`) and `:205` (`trace-window` / `watch-epochs`), via `tools/sensitive.cljs` (115 lines).
   - Meanwhile `dispatch` in `:trace` / `:settle` mode returns the projected epoch whether or not it is flagged (`tools/dispatch.cljs:96-136`, `tools/epoch_egress.cljs:296-315`).
3. **The projection already fails closed on what matters** (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:2324-2378`, `:2480-2508`):
   - every trigger-event and trace-event argument becomes `:rf/redacted`, whether declared or not;
   - every effect's `:args` is redacted;
   - unschematized HTTP bodies, error bodies included, are redacted;
   - resource scope values and the runtime-db partition are redacted;
   - declared-sensitive `:db-before` / `:db-after` paths are redacted.

   The drop hides material that is already redacted.

**The accepted tradeoff.** Whole-record suppression also hides undeclared DERIVED copies of a secret while a record is flagged:
- a sub returning `(str "Bearer " token)`;
- an exception message built from a token.

After the flip, those ship in trace views, as they already do through `read-sub` and `dispatch`. That is accepted on the project's author-owned, non-taint-tracking contract (`spec/015-Data-Classification.md:7`; author rules at `spec/Security.md:123-131`). The fixes are `{:sensitive [[]]}` on the sub, and a category-only message.

**Rejected options:**
- **(A) Keep the drop.** The AI pair stays blind in any app with authentication, and `trace-window`'s `:window-excludes-history` advisory (`tools/trace_window.cljs:240-256`) points the agent at `snapshot`, which drops the same records.
- **(C) Also delete the whole-event layer everywhere** (the hoist, the rollup, `rf/sensitive?`, `re-frame.mcp-base.sensitive`). Xray's on-box drop and Story-MCP's assertion drop still consume those signals, and each needs its own ruling.
- **(D) Keep the drop and narrow the rollup to events that touched a secret.** The runs an agent most needs (login, token refresh, logout) stay invisible, and the change alters a signal that other consumers share.
- **Reverse: apply the drop to `dispatch` too.** It contradicts trust-the-programmer and Spec 015's explicit refusal to track taint.

**Supersedes:** no ruling bead or EP. It overturns the pair-server default "drop" stated at `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2822`. The spec rewrite is the fourth bead.

## Work

1. **Pipeline.** In `wire_pipeline.cljs`:
   - Remove the `sensitive/scrub-snapshot-sensitive` step (`:161`) and the `sensitive/strip-sensitive` step (`:205`).
   - Update the pipeline docstrings (`:63`, `:142`, `:198`, `:265`).
   - Delete `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/sensitive.cljs`.
2. **Snapshot `:traces` comes first.**
   - That slice is the one pair slice `project-egress` never walks (`tools/snapshot.cljs:165-193`), so today the scrub is its only off-box gate.
   - Bug rf2-0e0a0 projects or retires it, and this bead depends on that one.
   - Both recommendations allow retiring the MCP slice; Codex prefers retiring it and keeping the in-process trace API.
   - If rf2-0e0a0 has not landed, do not remove the scrub before the slice is projected or retired.
3. **Indicators.**
   - These tools no longer produce `:dropped-sensitive`. It is omit-when-zero per `spec/Conventions.md:794`, so it simply disappears from their envelopes; the slot's definition stays for Story-MCP and `get-app-db`.
   - Re-read `trace-window`'s advisory hint once nothing is dropped, and keep it only if it is now accurate.
4. **Tests.** Turn drop arms into skeleton arms. Each asserts that the distinctive secret is ABSENT, `:rf.epoch/sensitive? true` is PRESENT, and the event id is present.
   - `tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-redaction.cjs`: the OUTER-drop arms. The INNER project-egress arm at `:246-300` stays.
   - `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/sensitive_filter_test.cljs`: convert it, or delete it with `sensitive.cljs`.
   - `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/mcp_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc`: its pair drop arms.
5. **Docs (all off the hot list):**
   - `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md`: `:255`, `:751`, and the `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` / `snapshot` entries.
   - The tool descriptor text in `descriptors_data.cljs`, wherever it mentions the drop.
   - `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/vocabulary.md:93`.
   - `tools/mcp-base/spec/sensitive.md:83`, which describes the pair's custom strip-fn.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): M-17/M-21 fold behaviour-modifying interceptors into chains but never say a v1 interceptor that emptied :queue to abort has no non-throwing re-frame2 equivalent (:rf/skip-handler? skips only the handler)
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Priority 2: a ported guard compiles and runs, but silently lets every event it used to stop run to completion.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-interceptors-subs.md §M-17 (lines 19-49; the "Modifies behaviour?" decision);
- the same file's §M-21 `after` (lines 158-165);
- breaking-changes.md's `->interceptor` row (line 132).

## What it says

- M-17: "If the interceptor was meant to apply to every frame (genuinely cross-frame behaviour modification): replicate in each frame config's `:interceptors` vector."
- M-21 `after`, path 2: "register the behaviour with `(rf/reg-interceptor :my/thing {:after (fn [ctx] ...)})` and reference `:my/thing` from each affected event's (or the frame's) `:interceptors` chain."
- breaking-changes :132: "Author the before/after work with `(rf/reg-interceptor id descriptor)`".

## What happened (generic)

A v1 interceptor can abort the rest of its chain by emptying the context's `:queue`. The v1 executor walks `:queue`, so once it is empty no later `:before` runs and the handler never runs. Apps use this for auth guards and "not ready yet" gates.

re-frame2 has no equivalent that avoids throwing:

- `execute-chain` walks a fixed vector and the context has no `:queue`, so `(assoc ctx :queue [])` does nothing. Later stages and the handler still run.
- `:rf/skip-handler?` skips the handler alone; every other stage's `:before` and `:after` still runs.
- Throwing does abort the chain, but it records an error for every aborted event.

The migration skill and corpus never mention `:queue` aborts or `:rf/skip-handler?`. A guard ported mechanically through M-17 / M-21 therefore lets events through, with no error.

## Evidence

- v1 (re-frame 1.4.3) `re_frame/interceptor.cljc`:112-122: the `:before` walk loops on `(:queue context)` and stops when it is empty.
- re-frame2 implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor.cljc:319-358 (`execute-chain`: a fixed vector; only a captured error short-circuits) and :156-169 (`invoke-before`).
- re-frame2 implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:525 (`(if (:rf/skip-handler? ctx) ctx …)`).
- docs/core/interceptors.md:290-291: "A `:before` can skip the handler by setting `:rf/skip-handler? true` on the context; every `:after` still runs."
- A fixed-string search for `skip-handler` over skills/re-frame-migration and migration/from-re-frame-v1 finds 0 hits. The same instrument hits spec/, docs/ and the re-frame2 skill.
- Observed on a ~170-file app whose SSO design depends on an aborting global interceptor.

## Suggested change

Add a "chain-abort interceptors" row to M-17 / M-21:

1. **Detect** interceptor bodies that empty or replace `:queue`: `(assoc ctx :queue …)`, `(update ctx :queue …)`, `(dissoc ctx :queue)`.
2. **Port** the decision to `(assoc ctx :rf/skip-handler? true)` in `:before`.
3. **Audit** every later stage on the chain (frame and event level), because each one still runs on an aborted event. Where no effect may escape, clear `:effects` in the outermost `:after`.
4. **Say** that throwing is the only full abort, and that it reports an error for every aborted event.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): the test-suite gate warns about a runner crash with no results, but not about a runner whose exit code ignores test ERRORS (9 errors, exit 0)
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main d53a3faf09.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/runtime-smoke-test.md §"The test suite is a THIRD gate the compiler and boot-smoke both miss" (lines 65-72), read with §"Required to finish is not required to run" (line 61).

## What it says

- :72: "the first fixture `:before` throws on the undefined v1 var, and the runner reports **"No test results found"** — a runner crash with zero results, not a failed assertion."
- :61: record each gate's "terminal outcome".
- The leaf never mentions exit codes: a search for "exit code" or "exit 0" finds nothing.

## What happened (generic)

cljs.test counts failures (an `is` that is false) separately from errors (a test that throws). On a ~170-file app's migrated test build, the runner reported 9 errors and exited 0. Any gate that reads the exit code counts that run green, and that includes CI and the "terminal outcome" a worker records.

A migration produces mostly errors rather than failures. Here, 8 of the 9 were `:rf.error/no-frame-context` thrown from code under test.

## Suggested change

Add to the third-gate section:

> Read the runner's own totals (tests, assertions, failures AND errors), not only its exit code. Once per project, prove that the exit code catches an error: add a throwaway test that throws, run the suite, and confirm a non-zero exit. title: skill(re-frame-migration): orchestrating §5's single post-sweep gate has no route for a unit held for human review, which hides every other unit's compile errors until it lands
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 62a62c7472.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/orchestrating-a-large-migration.md:

- §5 "The all-or-nothing single compile gate" (lines 95-104);
- §4 "Wave sequencing" (lines 85-93).

## What it says

- :97: "the project does not compile until the whole sweep lands."
- :102: "Green comes at ONE post-sweep gate. Once all waves have landed and the broken add-ons are gone, you run the consolidated compile of the whole tree … Errors surface together; trace each to its unit, fix, recompile the whole tree."
- :104: "do not let a worker spin trying to compile a tree that cannot yet compile."
- §4 orders units by id publication. Nothing orders the units inside a wave.

## What happened (generic)

§5 assumes that every unit lands in the sweep as soon as its diff is ready. Some units are HELD instead: the diff is done, but the unit waits for a human decision. Examples are a security-sensitive unit awaiting sign-off, or a Type B batch awaiting the author. While such a unit is held:

1. The one compile gate cannot run, because "all waves have landed" never becomes true.
2. Every other unit's compile errors stay invisible. They surface only when the held unit lands. By then the other units' owners (workers or agents) have often finished and gone, so "trace each to its unit, fix" has nobody to hand an error to.
3. If the held unit was dispatched late in its wave, its review also starts late, and the whole sweep waits on it.

§4 and §5 do not mention this case. The leaf has no notion of compiling before every unit lands, so the natural reading is to wait.

## Evidence

- The quotes above.
- `git grep -n -i -E "held|convergence probe|early convergence|awaiting review|sign-off"` over orchestrating-a-large-migration.md finds one hit, :15 ("a disposition needs no sign-off", about the Phase-0a gate). The same search over SKILL.md and sequencing.md finds only Type-B site holds (SKILL.md:65 and :150, sequencing.md:52). None of these covers a unit held out of the sweep. The control "consolidated" finds 4 hits in orchestrating.
- rf2-5w8nu's change (now on main: "Land the sweep on a sweep branch; it reaches the trunk once") does not cover the case either. A unit PR still "merges on its §5 deliverable", and nothing addresses a unit that cannot merge yet.
- Observed on a ~170-file app whose fan-out included a security unit held for sign-off.

## Suggested change

Add to §5:

> A unit held out of the sweep (awaiting a human review or sign-off) blocks the single gate and hides every other unit's errors. Do not wait for it. Run an **early convergence probe**: in a scratch worktree, merge the sweep tip and the held unit's branch locally (push nothing), then run the consolidated compile. Triage each error to its owning unit while that owner is still reachable. Repeat as units land. Like sequencing.md's first compile, the probe is a diagnostic: it need not pass, and it gates nothing.

Add to §4:

> Dispatch a unit you expect to be held FIRST in its wave, so that its review runs in parallel with the other units rather than after them.

Related: rf2-5w8nu (the sweep branch) and rf2-0fne3 (wave 2 gated on the frozen id contract).

comments.text:
More evidence from the same downstream migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main d53a3faf09: orchestrating-a-large-migration.md §5 :97 and :104 read as quoted above. rf2-5w8nu's change (635fc6bee1) does not touch them.

The early convergence probe has now been run, and it shows that §5's premise is stronger than the tree:

- With 11 of 14 units plus the held unit merged locally into the sweep tip (in a scratch worktree, nothing pushed), the dev build COMPILED. The test build failed on exactly one in-flight unit's leftover require.
- So :97 ("the project does not compile until the whole sweep lands") and :104 ("do not let a worker spin trying to compile a tree that cannot yet compile") hold only while a compile-breaking surface remains: an add-on that :refers a removed var, or an off-contract require. Once the units that remove those surfaces have landed, the tree compiles. From then on the probe is no longer a diagnostic that "need not pass". It is a real gate, with real errors that each belong to a unit.
- runtime-smoke-test.md:61 already states the general rule: "Run each gate as soon as its inputs exist, and never hold a runnable gate behind an unrelated pending one." §5 as written contradicts that rule for the compile.

Suggested addition to the change above:

- Replace "does not compile until the whole sweep lands" with "does not compile while a compile-breaking surface remains".
- Have the plan name the units that remove those surfaces (the add-on drops and conversions, M-0, M-1).
- Run a combined dev + test compile as soon as those units land, and triage each error to its owning unit.

The held-unit probe above then becomes one instance of that rule rather than an exception. Getting past shadow's first missing namespace in such a compile is filed separately as rf2-x8clx.

Observed on a ~170-file app.

title: O-16 companion: escalation case 2 omits the plain lowering for an :events predicate that tests one fixed event id plus its payload (an exact :on key with a :guard)
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

migration/from-re-frame-v1/async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md (the O-16 companion), §Explicit escalation cases, case 2, "Rules with `:events` as a predicate fn" (lines 260-282).

## What it says

The case offers three escalation paths:

- (a) "restructure the upstream dispatches so the events carry distinguishing ids";
- (b) "use a namespace or total wildcard (`:job/*`, `:*` …) whose `:guard` runs the predicate";
- (c) "hold the flow for the author's design decision".

## What happened (generic)

The most common predicate shape is "this one event id AND a test on its payload", for example `(fn [[id p]] (and (= id :job/status) (= :failed (:status p))))`. That lowers directly to an exact `:on` key with a `:guard`:

```clojure
:on {:job/status {:guard :failed? :target :failed}}
```

This is clearer than a wildcard and needs no upstream change. The companion's own worked example already uses exactly this shape (an exact key plus `:guard :this-run?`, line 186), but case 2 does not offer it. So a migration either reaches for a wildcard (path b) or escalates a flow that needed neither.

## Evidence

Companion :260-282 (the three paths) and :186 (exact key with a guard). Observed on a ~170-file app's boot design unit.

## Suggested change

Add a path (a') ahead of (b): "When the predicate fixes the event id and tests only the payload, use that exact `:on` key with a `:guard` that reads `:event` from its context map." Keep (b) for predicates that span several ids.
